strings.text: Cosette's at the resort setting traps on the beach, and you fall into one because of your curiosity. Luckily, Willow helps you out just in time. You chat with Willow on the beach, and she offers to teach you to swim.
Perfect. Not a soul in sight. Now's my chance.
Intel says the target's around here...
Found it! The Automatic Vending Artifact!
Strawberry milk, sea salt lemon soda, iced coffee...==W== They look great, but...
I'm here for this! Summer Limited: Fruity Aurora Fizz!
You can't get this anywhere else! Only this one Automatic Vending Artifact in the whole resort carries it! I came all the way out here for this drink!
And the name's basically "Aeloria"!==W== One sip and maybe I'll be as strong as Lady Aeloria...?
Since no one's around, these fizzes are all mine!
But a night walk on the beach listening to the waves... That's actually pretty nice.
Huh? Did a shadow just dart by?
Why is there an unopened drink on the sand? Did someone drop it...?
They're perfectly spaced out... Like a trail meant to lead me somewhere...
Two more...==W== With a pattern like this, could it be...
Huh? The ground feels weird here...
Gotcha at last, you rotten thief!
I knew it! Leave out some bait, and a sneak like you can't resist.
I should be asking you that.
No, no, no... I set this trap for the villain. How'd it catch ==SEX4==?
Ugh, this ruins the whole plan...==B== Huh? Wait.
Hold on...==W== Now that I think about it, I actually caught ==PLAYER_NAME==?!
If I bring ==SEX4== back now, Lady Aeloria will be thrilled!
Ugh... But then I won't catch the thief...==W== What do I do...?!
Cosette's mumbling something... I can't make out a word.
Cosette? Can you let me down?
Shush! I'm thinking about something important!
Why am I the one getting yelled at?!
What's that noise? Are you there?
Oh no, someone's coming...==B== I'll get caught if I stay!
I-I'll let you go this time!
Haha... Fancy seeing you, Willow. Couldn't sleep either?
I actually came to find you. You were gone a while, and I got worried.
Anyway... Why are you hanging upside down from a coconut tree? You look awfully calm. Did you sneak out to play some strange game?
I'm trying a new workout routine! I made a slight miscalculation, and ... one thing led to another.
And here I thought that girl kidnapped you.
Yes, though I only caught her running away.
It's alright. I'm sure you had your reasons, ==PLAYER_NAME==.
Since it's your "workout," I won't pry.
Thanks, Willow.==W== By the way... Could I ask a favor?
Could you get me down? I'm getting dizzy...
Oh? Is your workout session over already?
Heh, I'm teasing. You looked so amusing up there, I had to enjoy the view for a moment.==W== Let's get you down.
Willow has a surprisingly wicked streak...
Phew...==W== Good to be right-side up again.
So...==W== Do you have any other plans tonight?
Since neither of us can sleep, why not keep me company? We could chat under the moonlight.
The ocean is peaceful at night.
It is. Feels like we're the only two people left in the world.
Just the two of us, huh...
I haven't properly thanked you yet.
For the trouble you went through to trick me into this vacation.
Laru got the tickets, the prize thing was your idea...
And Iori played along. It's obvious this was carefully planned.
Going to such lengths, all to get me to rest...
But I had a great time. Thank you.
Really?! I'm glad. That's all that matters.
Heh... Then as a thank-you, how about I teach you to swim?
You stayed on the beach while everyone else was in the water, right?
At first I thought you didn't want to get in. But then it hit me.==W== ==PLAYER_NAME==, you're not much of a swimmer, are you?
Well, it's not that I can't swim at all, but I can barely keep myself from sinking.
Seeing everyone else swim effortlessly, I felt a little embarrassed to join in. Besides, wading in the shallows was fun enough.
The way you looked at the ocean... Your gaze was full of longing.
Willow takes my hand and leads me to the water. Her grip is firm—insistent, even—but somehow, I don't mind.
The water's shallow here, and we have the beach to ourselves. It's the perfect place to practice.
Alright. It'd be a shame to come all this way and never get in.
Oh, fair warning: I'm a strict teacher. Brace yourself, Boss.
P-Please go easy on me, coach...!
That's it. Relax. Gently kick your legs. Don't force it.
Don't fight the water. Imagine you're embracing the sea.
Take your time. There's no rush. I've got you.
Moonlight spills across the water, shimmering quietly with the ripples.
The night water is cold, but Willow's hands are warm.
Guided by her warmth, I let go, until I finally embrace the sea...

param: Cosette's at the resort setting traps on the beach, and you fall into one because of your curiosity. Luckily, Willow helps you out just in time. You chat with Willow on the beach, and she offers to teach you to swim.
Perfect. Not a soul in sight. Now's my chance.
Intel says the target's around here...
Found it! The Automatic Vending Artifact!
Strawberry milk, sea salt lemon soda, iced coffee...==W== They look great, but...
I'm here for this! Summer Limited: Fruity Aurora Fizz!
You can't get this anywhere else! Only this one Automatic Vending Artifact in the whole resort carries it! I came all the way out here for this drink!
And the name's basically "Aeloria"!==W== One sip and maybe I'll be as strong as Lady Aeloria...?
Since no one's around, these fizzes are all mine!
But a night walk on the beach listening to the waves... That's actually pretty nice.
Huh? Did a shadow just dart by?
Why is there an unopened drink on the sand? Did someone drop it...?
They're perfectly spaced out... Like a trail meant to lead me somewhere...
Two more...==W== With a pattern like this, could it be...
Huh? The ground feels weird here...
Gotcha at last, you rotten thief!
I knew it! Leave out some bait, and a sneak like you can't resist.
I should be asking you that.
No, no, no... I set this trap for the villain. How'd it catch ==SEX4==?
Ugh, this ruins the whole plan...==B== Huh? Wait.
Hold on...==W== Now that I think about it, I actually caught ==PLAYER_NAME==?!
If I bring ==SEX4== back now, Lady Aeloria will be thrilled!
Ugh... But then I won't catch the thief...==W== What do I do...?!
Cosette's mumbling something... I can't make out a word.
Cosette? Can you let me down?
Shush! I'm thinking about something important!
Why am I the one getting yelled at?!
What's that noise? Are you there?
Oh no, someone's coming...==B== I'll get caught if I stay!
I-I'll let you go this time!
Haha... Fancy seeing you, Willow. Couldn't sleep either?
I actually came to find you. You were gone a while, and I got worried.
Anyway... Why are you hanging upside down from a coconut tree? You look awfully calm. Did you sneak out to play some strange game?
I'm trying a new workout routine! I made a slight miscalculation, and ... one thing led to another.
And here I thought that girl kidnapped you.
Yes, though I only caught her running away.
It's alright. I'm sure you had your reasons, ==PLAYER_NAME==.
Since it's your "workout," I won't pry.
Thanks, Willow.==W== By the way... Could I ask a favor?
Could you get me down? I'm getting dizzy...
Oh? Is your workout session over already?
Heh, I'm teasing. You looked so amusing up there, I had to enjoy the view for a moment.==W== Let's get you down.
Willow has a surprisingly wicked streak...
Phew...==W== Good to be right-side up again.
So...==W== Do you have any other plans tonight?
Since neither of us can sleep, why not keep me company? We could chat under the moonlight.
The ocean is peaceful at night.
It is. Feels like we're the only two people left in the world.
Just the two of us, huh...
I haven't properly thanked you yet.
For the trouble you went through to trick me into this vacation.
Laru got the tickets, the prize thing was your idea...
And Iori played along. It's obvious this was carefully planned.
Going to such lengths, all to get me to rest...

Really?! I'm glad. That's all that matters.
Heh... Then as a thank-you, how about I teach you to swim?

strings.text: The next day, you hear that some visitors were attacked here and that this resort is said to be haunted, which is apparently why very few people come here. That's when you run into the Treasure Hunters again...
Ugh... Too bright. Is it morning already?
Can't beat the beach. The sun's gorgeous, but I can barely keep my eyes open...
Well, my eyes are closing anyway... Guess I'll catch a few more minutes.
No, no, no! This is a disaster!
I forgot the supply list! I haven't planned out the guild's next steps, and nothing's written for our itinerary!
Wait, hold on...==W== Was Loxy's ceiling this high?
Phew... What a relief. I can finally relax.
You're amazing, Iris. Running the guild even in your sleep.
It's not like I wanted to... All I remember is trying to balance the books, and the numbers wouldn't add up.
The more I tried, the more panicked I got, until I literally shot up in bed.
But it's fine now. I'm going back to bed to make up for every lost minute.
<size=50>I've had it! I am not spending another day in this dump!</size>
I want a refund! I'm packing my bags and leaving right now!
Ugh, so loud... What's going on out there?
You want me to calm down?! I went to grab a drink and got attacked out of nowhere!
And those eyes! Two green lights popping out of the pitch black—who wouldn't be terrified?!
Attacked? Green lights? Sounds like something wild happened...
A tourist was attacked...==W== Cosette set up traps on the beach last night. Could she be involved?
Could be a misunderstanding...==W== But if she caused this, I can't look the other way.
Anyway, we'd better go check it out.
Agreed. If someone's in trouble, we can't ignore it. Besides... I'm not letting some random incident ruin our trip.
Count me in! I want to know what's going on!
Let's split up and ask around then.
Iris, if you're still tired, feel free to stay here and rest.
Like I could sleep now...==W== What if you all leave and I get attacked by some weird creature...==W== Eek!
The sooner we figure this out, the sooner I can relax!
Excuse me, sorry to interrupt. We arrived yesterday and heard someone got attacked this morning. Is that true?
Yeah, seems so...==W== I heard a shadowy figure with scissors attacked someone last night.
I saw it too! I was walking back from the woods the other night and felt something behind me.==W== I turned around and saw two glowing eyes the size of lightbulbs staring out from the dark!
Are you sure those were eyes and not actual lightbulbs?
Yes! Two giant eyeballs, two moving eyeballs!
Way too many strange occurrences lately. I don't even want to stay here anymore...
I'd pack up and leave if I were you. It looks peaceful now, but who knows what's lurking around after dark.
Ugh... That gives me the creeps.
Don't worry, Iris. If a monster shows up, I'll take it down.

You guys hunting the resort urban legends too? Perfect timing! We were debating whether to stake out the woods for Terror Scissorhands tonight, or wait by the beach for the Human-Eating Vending Artifact.
Wait, you're not here for the rumors?
We're regular tourists. But those rumors sound fascinating. Could you tell us more?
You bet!==W== This resort has gotten popular with thrill-seekers lately. Most folks come strictly for the legends.
The top three are the Gaze in the Dark, Terror Scissorhands, and the Human-Eating Vending Artifact.
Hu-Human-Eating Vending Artifact? That sounds intense...
I heard there's a Human-Eating Vending Artifact here. It tosses out drinks to lure people in, and sometimes you can hear chewing from inside. People say the drinks are made from the victims' blood.
Then there's Terror Scissorhands. That one's popular too. The most widely told version goes like this—
Years ago, this resort had a hardworking gardener. He couldn't stop working even after his death, so he turned into a vengeful spirit. Every night, he'd wander the grounds with giant shears.==W==
As for the Gaze in the Dark, there are tons of theories. The funniest one is that it's a Bouncing Fairy Light that escaped a Monolith...
Have you seen any of those yourself? Not hearsay, but with your own eyes.
Not personally. Plenty of people swear they're real, but no one has concrete proof.
That's why I've decided to skip sleep for a few days. I'm bound to catch at least one in the act!
Strange rumors? News to me. I'm on vacation, just here to relax.
Have you heard any strange noises at night? Or noticed anything unsettling?
I'm out cold the second it gets dark, so I don't remember a thing.
By the way, is that girl with you?==W== She's been staring at us this whole time.
Oh no. Did they find my bait again?!
D-Don't panic. Lady Aeloria said the key to any mission is staying calm...
Calm down... Calm... Ca—==W== WAAAH! I can't stay calm at all! I'm out of here!
Hey, wait! I need to ask you something!
Can't get answers from Cosette now. Better head back and regroup with everyone.
Once we regroup, we trade what we'd learned.
So this resort has a bunch of weird rumors going around, and actual suspicious incidents to back them up. That about right?
Besides the thrill seekers who came for the scary stories, regular guests have been drying up. That's why the place feels so dead.
The stories sound awful, but when you ask around, barely anyone has seen the monsters firsthand.==W== The rumors just snowballed, getting wilder every time. And here we are.
If Cosette's been using drinks to set traps, then the Vending Artifact rumor probably started with her.
But what about the Gaze in the Dark and Terror Scissorhands? No way she's behind those too.
We've got a good handle on what's happening, but the cause of those legends is still a mystery.
Then let's ask the people who'd know best.
I walked past the service center earlier. Looks like the staffer handling all the complaints is back at her desk.
Sorry to bother you, but I have a couple of questions—
Sure, how can I help you...==W== Wait! You... You're?!
Huh? Aren't you from...==W== Oh, you're working here now.
Crap. Of all the people to run into right now.==W== Talk about bad luck walking through the goddamn door.
Screw it. We're striking first!==W== Everyone, get 'em!
Hey, wait!==W== Why are you attacking us all of a sudden?!

strings.text: It turns out that the "ghost" is a hermit crab wearing an Automatic Vending Artifact that trashes the resort. And Cosette is on its back too! You and your friends decide to track it down and rescue Cosette.
Why can't you just give us a break? We kept our heads down this time, working an honest job. Why are you still coming after us?!
That's rich coming from you.==W== You threw the first punch.
So ... you aren't here to mess up our job?
We were just looking for someone to ask about the rumors. Unless you're up to something shady again?
No! We've been busting our tails day and night, trying to save up for our travels.
Oh... Okay. I thought you might be the ones behind the urban legends.
No kidding! We're the victims here!
Working here was tough, sure, but business was booming. Good revenue meant good bonuses, and the owner paid out.
Then, out of nowhere, weird rumors started circulating. Gaze in the dark, shadows, Scissorhands... And they keep getting wilder.
I imagine those rumors hit business pretty hard.
You bet. Business completely tanked! People would check in for the night and demand a refund by morning. Others would cancel their reservations the second they heard the stories.
Sure, we get a few thrill-seekers looking for living urban legends, but that amounts to nothing.
The crowds kept shrinking and that really brought the resort owner down. He eventually gave up on running the front desk and shoved the whole staff into hunting down those supernatural incidents.
At this rate, we're going to fail our performance reviews and lose our jobs!
But those stories didn't come from nowhere. Something has to be going on here.==W== Have you witnessed anything strange yourselves?
Well... We aren't supposed to go around spreading rumors.
Don't worry, we're here to help. Whatever you tell us stays between us. We aren't looking to cause trouble.
Cap...==W== Maybe we should tell them? It's not like we have any better options.
Alright...==W== We did run into some weird stuff.
Lately we keep hearing this click-clack noise at night, and getting the feeling that something's watching us from the dark.
Every night, massive drag marks are carved on the beach, and we have to rake them over before sunrise so that the guests don't freak out.
But the weirdest thing of all is that Automatic Vending Artifact.
Oh, I heard about that one! The Human-Eating Vending Artifact, right?!
Sounds like somebody exaggerated that story. But we did see the Artifact move on its own.
I saw it clear as day! That Automatic Vending Artifact was sliding slowly toward the ocean.==W== By the time I hunted it down to the water, it had vanished!
But here's the kicker. Every time we went back to check on it, the Artifact would already be back in its original spot.

Strange as it was, it wasn't hurting anyone, so we let it be. Then this morning, a guest came screaming that he got attacked while buying a drink. When we went to check the scene after finally calming him down...
The Automatic Vending Artifact had somehow vanished into thin air! Poof! No trace left behind.
Cosette was digging traps on the beach last night... Could that be connected?
Shadows, eyes, drag marks in the sand, and a roaming Automatic Vending Artifact.==W== It seems these clues are all connected.
Cap... Maybe we should tell them about that other thing?
Well, besides all that, something else caught our eye. A tiny girl with white hair showed up at the resort recently.
We figured she was just another tourist. But she started hiding in corners a lot. We have no idea what she is up to.
First thing this morning I caught her lying on the beach, muttering about how she will definitely catch someone this time. I tried asking what she was doing, but she panicked and bolted.
White hair, tiny...==W== Are they talking about Cosette?
Aaah! What is that?! Keep away!
A hermit crab wearing an Automatic Vending Artifact. And it's trashing the place.
How did those two things even get stuck together?!
Wait... The person chasing it looks like...
Stop right there!==W== Give me back my drinks!
Hey! That's the girl I was telling you about!
Why on earth is she chasing a hermit crab...?
... Wait, never mind that. No time to stand and stare. We need to clear the area now.
Everyone, keep moving! Stay calm and clear out of the crab's path immediately!
Hold up! Is that the missing Vending Artifact on its back?!
Oh crap, it is! We're done for. There goes our entire paycheck...
The giant hermit crab is berserk, thrashing==RT==its claws and tearing through the resort.
We can't reason with it. In that case—
Wait, Willow... You aren't going to—
Willow charges straight at the rampaging crab.
A heavy thud echoes as her mechanical arm==RT==smashes into its head.
... Classic Willow. She doesn't pull her punches.
Waaah! You might as well give up! I'm not letting go until you return my drinks!
... How are you worrying about drinks right now?!
Wait a minute! This hermit crab...
Could it be the legendary Treasure-Bearing Hermit Crab?!
Yes! Look, I have my senior's old notebook right here. It's all right here!
It's a massive hermit crab found only in the ocean. Its tough shell, smooth with a bizarre luster, is priceless to collectors!
Because of that, countless treasure hunters have spent their lives chasing it down.
But it doesn't have a shell on its back...
Word is, a few months back, a rich tycoon hired a crew of Trekkers to catch this thing. They tracked it for a whole week and finally cornered it...
But it slipped away at the last second. No one's seen it since... Rumor has it, fragments of the shell were even seen floating on the water back then.
It must have fought so hard when they cornered it that it lost the treasure it was carrying!
So now it's back, burning with resentment, to take revenge on humanity!
I'm serious. Think about it! That shell was its pride and joy, and the greedy humans just took it. That's enough motive for revenge.
Attacking humans wasn't enough to satisfy its rage anymore, so it started to target human valuables. And what's the biggest prize in this resort?
... That Automatic Vending Artifact with special drinks?
Spot on! That Artifact dispenses an exclusive drink you can't get anywhere else. Half the tourists come here specifically for it. It's practically a local landmark.
The crab figured it was a human treasure and snatched the whole thing.
I SAID==W== GIVE IT BACK!==W== NOW!
The hermit crab dives into the ocean with Cosette still clinging desperately to its back. A massive geyser of water sprays up, and they vanish into the churning waves.
We have to go after her!
But they're in the ocean. How are we supposed to chase them?
But please, you gotta bring back that Automatic Vending Artifact too!
And here I thought you were being generous. Turns out it's all about the Artifact...
Course I care! That's no cheap knockoff with some staff hiding inside. It's a genuine Automatic Artifact wished straight out of the Monolith. It costs a fortune!
The resort owner dropped serious coin on it. If we don't bring it back, we're packing our bags for sure!
But look at it, it's completely busted. Even if we do get it back, it probably won't work anymore.
Dead or alive, I need a body!==W== If it's broken, we can figure out a way to fix it. If it's gone for good, we'll have nothing left!
Please, honored Boss... You gotta help us.
... Alright. Rescuing Cosette is priority one.==W== We'll do our best to bring that Artifact back with us too.
Fantastic! I expect nothing less from the Boss who always ruins our plans. You are the real deal!
That doesn't sound like a compliment...
Enough chatter. Everyone to the boat. We need to catch up to them!

Waaah! You might as well give up! I'm not letting go until you return my drinks!
... How are you worrying about drinks right now?!
Wait a minute! This hermit crab...
Could it be the legendary Treasure-Bearing Hermit Crab?!
Yes! Look, I have my senior's old notebook right here. It's all right here!
It's a massive hermit crab found only in the ocean. Its tough shell, smooth with a bizarre luster, is priceless to collectors!
Because of that, countless treasure hunters have spent their lives chasing it down.
But it doesn't have a shell on its back...
Word is, a few months back, a rich tycoon hired a crew of Trekkers to catch this thing. They tracked it for a whole week and finally cornered it...
But it slipped away at the last second. No one's seen it since... Rumor has it, fragments of the shell were even seen floating on the water back then.
It must have fought so hard when they cornered it that it lost the treasure it was carrying!
So now it's back, burning with resentment, to take revenge on humanity!
I'm serious. Think about it! That shell was its pride and joy, and the greedy humans just took it. That's enough motive for revenge.
Attacking humans wasn't enough to satisfy its rage anymore, so it started to target human valuables. And what's the biggest prize in this resort?
... That Automatic Vending Artifact with special drinks?
Spot on! That Artifact dispenses an exclusive drink you can't get anywhere else. Half the tourists come here specifically for it. It's practically a local landmark.
The crab figured it was a human treasure and snatched the whole thing.
I SAID==W== GIVE IT BACK!==W== NOW!
The hermit crab dives into the ocean with Cosette still clinging desperately to its back. A massive geyser of water sprays up, and they vanish into the churning waves.
We have to go after her!
But they're in the ocean. How are we supposed to chase them?
But please, you gotta bring back that Automatic Vending Artifact too!
And here I thought you were being generous. Turns out it's all about the Artifact...
Course I care! That's no cheap knockoff with some staff hiding inside. It's a genuine Automatic Artifact wished straight out of the Monolith. It costs a fortune!
The resort owner dropped serious coin on it. If we don't bring it back, we're packing our bags for sure!
But look at it, it's completely busted. Even if we do get it back, it probably won't work anymore.
Dead or alive, I need a body!==W== If it's broken, we can figure out a way to fix it. If it's gone for good, we'll have nothing left!
Please, honored Boss... You gotta help us.
... Alright. Rescuing Cosette is priority one.==W== We'll do our best to bring that Artifact back with us too.
Fantastic! I expect nothing less from the Boss who always ruins our plans. You are the real deal!
That doesn't sound like a compliment...
Enough chatter. Everyone to the boat. We need to catch up to them!

strings.text: You borrow a boat to track down the hermit crab. Unfortunately, your boat veers off course in a storm and hits a reef. When you regain consciousness, you find yourself on an unknown island with Willow.
We scraped together everything we had for this boat. We'll let you take it just this once. Keep her in one piece!
Our future is in your hands! You have to get that Automatic Vending Artifact back!
Okay, okay, we hear you. That's the third time you've said that.
Cap, bad news! Another guest is complaining. You need to go deal with it!
She sure can run. Are complaints that scary?
They can definitely be a headache.
Even someone as reliable as you gets complaints?
Anyway, back to business. Before we head out, does anyone here know how to sail?
I played a sailing arcade game at the Monolith once.
Err... I drove Loxy into the water once. Does that count?
I've been out on the water before and know the basics,==W== but...
... In that case, I'll take the helm.==W== ==PLAYER_NAME==, can you assist?
There's nothing you can't do, Willow.
I had some basic training in Sailstead, but I'm no expert.==W== A seasoned sailor would be ideal, but this is an emergency. We can't afford to wait.
Hold on tight, everyone. We're heading out.
Reporting. No sign of the target.
That hermit crab we ran into looks like a monster called a Stomper Crab.
They move in a straight line and need to surface for air from time to time.
So as long as we keep heading in the same direction, we should be able to track it down.
The wind's picking up...==W== And those clouds in the distance worry me a little.
The weather changes fast at sea. We need to stay sharp.
This rain is pouring. I can't see a thing...
Iris!==W== Everyone, grab something and hold on!
Another massive wave slams into the hull. The ship is tossed high into the air before crashing back down. The mast shakes violently, throwing the bow off course.
From somewhere below comes a sudden, sharp crack.
The mast eventually gives out against the gale,==RT==snapping in two with a deafening crack.
The rope jerks violently in my hands. I'm yanked off the deck==RT==and plunged into the sea before I can even react.
Don't try to get up yet. Are you dizzy? Does anything hurt?
I'll live... Feels like my insides got tossed around by the waves. Swallowed half the ocean, too. I'm full enough to skip lunch today.
You're still cracking jokes. That's a good sign.
Yeah. I scouted the area while you were out. No sign of human life anywhere.
I'm sorry...==W== Pulling you to shore took everything I had. I don't know what happened to the rest of them...
Let me try Heartlink. My phone can reach anyone, no matter how far away they are.
Weird, the screen's dead. Don't tell me it broke...
Tyrant, I must correct a misconception. The Throne never breaks.
Water has breached the device. It is currently inoperable.
That's the exact definition of broken!
Let me reiterate. The Throne never breaks. It is merely temporarily out of service.
I also do not appreciate being wet.
Some Priest you are... Fine, you're dismissed.
Ahaha... So, fun fact, my phone hates water...==W== It's not going to be any help right now.
So even you can't reach the others, huh...
Don't worry. They're all pros. They can handle whatever gets thrown at them.
True... We need to focus on keeping ourselves safe.
Let's find shelter from the rain. Once we rest up, we'll figure out a way to call for help.
Let's stop here for a bit. Wait right here.
Soon, Willow returns carrying branches, vines, and massive leaves. A blade pops from her prosthetic, and she expertly cuts the materials to pitch a makeshift tent.
That blade's spinning fast... Oh, her prosthetic has a built-in auto-saw...==W== Makes sense...
Wait! You have an auto-saw in your arm?!
When Sparkla built this for me, I told her I needed to handle complex situations. So, she packed an entire multi-tool kit inside.
She even added a propeller. I thought it was overkill, but it definitely came in handy today.
Yep. Otherwise, no way I could have dragged you through those massive waves to this island on my own.
It's still warm from running at max power. If you're cold, you can hug it to warm up.
I'm good. Appreciate the offer, though...
Hehe. By the way, how are you holding up?
I'm okay, just a little drained.
Then let's rest a bit longer. We'll head out once you get some energy back.
I scouted the area earlier. No signs of large beasts or monsters.
But we're too low down here. Higher ground is safer. Next up, we should try to find a cave or something to take shelter.
Even when things look bad, I feel safe with you around, Willow.
The deserted island before us is unfamiliar and dangerous.
But Willow's smile makes it easy to believe there's always a way forward,==RT==no matter how bad things get.

strings.text: In the pouring rain, Willow's prosthetic malfunctions from overuse. She is upset about something in her past, while worried about being a burden to you. You tell her that you can "be her hand"...
We need shelter fast, or hypothermia will set in.
I follow Willow, stumbling through the mud as we push further inland.
Why? Is it dangerous out here?
The rain loosens the soil. Even flat ground can give way to a mudslide.
If the dirt looks discolored or feels soft underfoot, step back immediately.
She stays ahead of me the entire way, tearing through vines==RT==and snapping branches to clear a path.
Tossing aside heavy logs and rocks with ease... Willow is incredible.
The riverbed is the fastest route, but with rain like this, getting near the water is...
Huh? What makes you ask that?
Your left arm is looking stiff...==W== And you look pale. Are you feeling sick?
It's nothing. I'm fine. Don't worry about me. The priority is finding a place for you to rest.
Stop making this about me. You need rest too. If something happens to you, what am I going to tell the others? Your health matters.
... I suppose you're right.==W== I'll keep that in mind.
Maybe it's the exhaustion from the storm, or constantly watching our step in the mud... We haven't gone far, but it feels like we've been walking for hours.
Hold on. The ground up ahead looks off. Let me check it out—
Wait,==W== Willow! Did you hear that—
A deafening roar shakes the air as a torrent of mud and rock==RT==tears down the slope. The ground beneath our feet gives way.
Willow lunges toward me. She grabs a dangling vine,==RT==trying to swing us both out of harm's way.
... At least, that was the plan.
The wet vine slips through her stiff fingers.
Losing her grip, Willow lurches off balance,==RT==falling toward the ravine below.
Mud, branches, and water cascade down the slope. Over the deafening roar,==RT==I grab Willow's hand and hold on with everything I have.
The world spins as we tumble down the slope,==RT==only stopping when we slam into a tree trunk.
Ugh... I'm okay. What about you?==W== Your arm...
I'm fine... But my prosthetic is completely dead.
I pushed it too hard clearing the path and drained its energy. The spare Neo Solution is still on the boat.
You warned me, but I was too impatient to listen.
I was supposed to keep you safe. Instead, I messed up and dragged you into danger...
I swore I'd never make this mistake again. And then I did.
If anything happens to you, how could I face the New Star Guild?
Everyone worked hard to give me this awesome arm... Yet I still made the same mistake.
It's cold metal. It never gets tired, never gets hurt. It's supposed to be stronger than my real arm.
Why... Why does it hurt this much?
I don't know the details of your past, but you didn't drag me down.
If you hadn't caught me when we fell, I'd be fish food by now.
I did what you would have done—risked my neck to help a friend. You have nothing to apologize for.
Willow, thank you for saving my life. I want to show my gratitude, not accept an apology. Those are two different things.
So stop beating yourself up. Okay?
You didn't save me just because you have a fancy mechanical arm.
It was your wits, your experience, and your guts.
As long as you're safe, I'm happy. And since that arm is out of commission...
Let me be your left hand from now on.
Just tell me what needs doing. Boss me around like I'm your actual hand!
Clearing paths, moving rubble, helping you walk... I'm on it.
And if something's too much for me alone, we'll figure it out together.
You've been holding it together for so long. Why not lean on me for a change?
Thank you. I'll leave the heavy lifting to you then, my "left hand."
Phew... Finally a dry spot to wait out the rain.
Caves like this make perfect dens for large monsters. Let's not deliver ourselves as takeout.
Fair point...==W== Hey, Willow? Come check this out.
Old barrels, crates, shipwreck pieces ... and scattered seashells...
Looks like someone else washed up here before us.
Maybe. Those weird scratches on the planks are a bit concerning...==W== But right now, we need to focus on scavenging what we can.
I find a clear patch of ground, pick out some planks as Willow directs, and try to start a fire.
Start with the fine shavings for kindling. Once the flame is steady, add the bigger pieces bit by bit.
Leave some gaps for airflow, or it'll choke and die.
Yeah, that's it. Good job.==W== Ah... I'm coming back to life. It's so warm.
This left hand of yours did a good job, huh?
It did. At this rate, I'll end up spoiled rotten.
Would that be so bad? You could use the rest.
Yeah, good idea. Let's stay close.
Not only that.==W== You helped me pull myself together when I was panicking.
It might seem like a given to you... But it means everything to me.
Then let me thank you too. Thanks for always looking out for me, Willow.
I wouldn't have made it this far without the survival skills you taught me.
Heh... It's the least I could do. Part of being a senior is showing newcomers the ropes.
Speaking of which, Noya mentioned you used to be an amazing Trekker. Is that true?
That's a huge stretch. I was a Trekker for a couple of years, that's all.
I'm glad I haven't forgotten the experience. At least it came in handy today.
Then why join the Trekker Association? With your skills, you'd be a legend by now if you kept going.
Hmm... Why, indeed.==W== I realized I wasn't cut out for that life. I'm better off working behind the scenes.
I still climb the Monolith occasionally, but I can't charge in headfirst anymore, chasing nothing but freedom and dreams...
Why is Willow wearing that look on her face? What happened in her past...
Did warming your phone by the fire bring it back?
Hello? ==PLAYER_NAME==?!==W== Thank goodness, I finally got through!
Are you okay? Is Willow with you?
Yeah, a huge wave washed us ashore on a deserted island.==W== We're fine thanks to Willow. How about you guys?
We drifted on some wreckage for a bit, then we got rescued!
We'll come find you. Stay safe until we get there.
Hearing their familiar voices, I breathe a sigh of relief. After checking in, Willow gives them our approximate location.
We understand the situation. Try not to worry, we have navigation experts with us. We will find you.
The storm is too rough out there now. Once the weather clears, we'll come get you. Take care of yourselves in the meantime.
Don't worry. With Willow here, we'll be fine.
We finally got through. Hearing everyone is safe takes a weight off my shoulders...
Yeah. Now we sit tight and wait for rescue.
The cave falls silent, save for the comforting crackle of the campfire.
We huddle together in the warm glow.==RT==Just as I'm drifting off to sleep, I hear Willow whisper.
Those hands that caught me...==W== They're really dependable.

strings.text: You and Willow are finally out of danger, and your friends have arrived by boat to get you. Just as you're about to leave, you run into the hermit crab, who has made the island its home...
I'll hold them off! Go first, Willow!
No! The captain trusted me to keep you safe. I'm not leaving you behind!
It's okay, I've got this. Find somewhere safe and wait. I'll be right behind you!
I'm sorry, Willow...==W== The doctors did everything they could, but they couldn't save your left arm.
I see...==W== No wonder I feel much lighter. What about her? How is she?
She's still in surgery. But the doctors say ...==W== she might never wake up.
... She did this to save me.
Bad dream? You looked like you were hurting...
... No, I'm fine. How long was I out?
It's morning. I checked outside, and the rain stopped, but...
I keep hearing this weird sound... I can't make out what it is.
A weird sound? Could it be...
Willow presses her ear to the ground and listens intently. A moment later, she gets up to inspect the cave entrance.
... We need to move. There's going to be another landslide.
And it'll be worse this time. The soil here is naturally loose. Now that it's soaked...==W== It's bound to give way.
Let's fall back to the beach. If we get buried here, Noya and the rest couldn't dig us out even if they tried for weeks.
... Yeah, that would be a nightmare.
A deep rumble echoes from inside the island. The ground near the entrance that seemed solid moments ago suddenly caves in, sending wet soil sliding down.
Huff...==W== Huff...==W== We should be safe here, right?
Keep your guard up. The landslide is worse than I thought...==W== We need to get further away from the mountain...
But we're out of beach. Where else can we go?
I follow her gaze. Not far offshore, a flat stretch of reef breaks the surface.
If we make it out there, the landslide can't reach us.
That's a lot of open water... I guess we're swimming.
No.==W== You wouldn't suggest it unless you knew I could make it.
Wait, why are you holding my hand?
Well, I'm helping you swim across, aren't I?
I... I wasn't going to ask for help.
Your mechanical arm is dead. Swimming one-handed is going to be rough.
I'll be fine. It takes more energy with one arm, but I can manage...
Right now, I'm your left hand. Let me help.
Besides, my swimming coach was a pro. You might doubt me, but you can't doubt her.
...==W== Okay. I'm counting on you, my left hand.
Relax...==W== Don't fight the water. Embrace it.
Willow holds my shoulder while I paddle forward. For all my big talk, I still need her kicking with me to make any headway.
Pace yourself. The current is with us here. Once we reach that reef, we can catch our breath.
The dawn water is freezing,==RT==and the wind keeps howling.
But somehow, having Willow right here beside me==RT==feels incredibly safe... It's hard to explain.
<size=32>Now I get why Noya and the others trust you...</size>
Huff...==W== Haa... We finally ...==W== made it...!!
The moment my feet hit solid ground, I collapse onto the sand. Willow sits next to me, hugging her knees with a soft smile.
You're amazing...==W== Willow...==W== I'm half dead...==W== And you barely broke a sweat...
Come to think of it, being stranded out here with you isn't the worst thing.
Shipwrecked, stranded, and almost buried alive twice...==W== Are you kidding? This is a complete disaster!
But if you feel that way, then I guess my struggling was worth it.
I ... have something from my past I want to share.==W== Will you listen?
I was ... in an accident a long time ago.==W== It cost me my left arm.
It's the kind of memory I should never forget. But somehow, I did. I have no idea what actually happened that day...==W== No matter how hard I try, I only get blurry pieces.
Back then, I was supposed to protect a junior in the guild...
But instead, the person I was guarding took a fatal blow to save me...
Ever since then, I promised myself I would never repeat that mistake.
I refuse to be a burden. I can't drag my team down. It's my duty to take care of everyone else, and never the other way round.
Well, as you can see...==W== I still ended up showing you this helpless side of me.
Back in the woods, for a second, I felt like I was right back in the past...==W== Back to being dead weight. The one who needed saving.
But when you offered to be my left hand...==W== I realized something.
Like I've always wanted to support you, you just wanted to lend me a hand.
To you, I'm not a burden. And you're not a burden to me either.
We're just two people leaning on each other right now...
I'm glad that ...==W== you're the one by my side at a time like this.
Yeah...==W== I feel the same way.
Looks like our little castaway adventure is finally over.
Yeah. It's coming to an end.
==PLAYER_NAME==! Willow! Thank goodness we finally found you two!
Are you okay? Are you hurt anywhere? Do you feel alright?
We're both fine. Willow took great care of me.
Looks like your arm can finally work again, Willow.
Yeah. Looks like Boss can finally step down from ==SEX3== left hand duties.
Well, out of a job again. Not sure if I should be happy or sad about that.
Out of a job...? What does that mean?==W== Whatever! We can catch up on all that once we get back!
Oh, by the way, ==PLAYER_NAME==. We brought someone you know with the rescue boat...
Ugh...==W== Give it back...==W== Give...==W== Give me back my drinks!
Everyone, we need to calm this hermit crab down first!

param: You and Willow are finally out of danger, and your friends have arrived by boat to get you. Just as you're about to leave, you run into the hermit crab, who has made the island its home...
I'll hold them off! Go first, Willow!
No! The captain trusted me to keep you safe. I'm not leaving you behind!
It's okay, I've got this. Find somewhere safe and wait. I'll be right behind you!
I'm sorry, Willow...==W== The doctors did everything they could, but they couldn't save your left arm.
I see...==W== No wonder I feel much lighter. What about her? How is she?
She's still in surgery. But the doctors say ...==W== she might never wake up.
... She did this to save me.
Bad dream? You looked like you were hurting...
... No, I'm fine. How long was I out?
It's morning. I checked outside, and the rain stopped, but...
I keep hearing this weird sound... I can't make out what it is.
A weird sound? Could it be...
Willow presses her ear to the ground and listens intently. A moment later, she gets up to inspect the cave entrance.
... We need to move. There's going to be another landslide.
And it'll be worse this time. The soil here is naturally loose. Now that it's soaked...==W== It's bound to give way.
Let's fall back to the beach. If we get buried here, Noya and the rest couldn't dig us out even if they tried for weeks.
... Yeah, that would be a nightmare.
A deep rumble echoes from inside the island. The ground near the entrance that seemed solid moments ago suddenly caves in, sending wet soil sliding down.
Huff...==W== Huff...==W== We should be safe here, right?
Keep your guard up. The landslide is worse than I thought...==W== We need to get further away from the mountain...
But we're out of beach. Where else can we go?
I follow her gaze. Not far offshore, a flat stretch of reef breaks the surface.
If we make it out there, the landslide can't reach us.
That's a lot of open water... I guess we're swimming.
No.==W== You wouldn't suggest it unless you knew I could make it.
Wait, why are you holding my hand?
Well, I'm helping you swim across, aren't I?
I... I wasn't going to ask for help.
Your mechanical arm is dead. Swimming one-handed is going to be rough.
I'll be fine. It takes more energy with one arm, but I can manage...
Right now, I'm your left hand. Let me help.
Besides, my swimming coach was a pro. You might doubt me, but you can't doubt her.
...==W== Okay. I'm counting on you, my left hand.
Relax...==W== Don't fight the water. Embrace it.
Willow holds my shoulder while I paddle forward. For all my big talk, I still need her kicking with me to make any headway.
Pace yourself. The current is with us here. Once we reach that reef, we can catch our breath.
The dawn water is freezing,==RT==and the wind keeps howling.
But somehow, having Willow right here beside me==RT==feels incredibly safe... It's hard to explain.
<size=32>Now I get why Noya and the others trust you...</size>
Huff...==W== Haa... We finally ...==W== made it...!!
The moment my feet hit solid ground, I collapse onto the sand. Willow sits next to me, hugging her knees with a soft smile.
You're amazing...==W== Willow...==W== I'm half dead...==W== And you barely broke a sweat...
Come to think of it, being stranded out here with you isn't the worst thing.
Shipwrecked, stranded, and almost buried alive twice...==W== Are you kidding? This is a complete disaster!
But if you feel that way, then I guess my struggling was worth it.
I ... have something from my past I want to share.==W== Will you listen?
I was ... in an accident a long time ago.==W== It cost me my left arm.
It's the kind of memory I should never forget. But somehow, I did. I have no idea what actually happened that day...==W== No matter how hard I try, I only get blurry pieces.

strings.text: Together, you beat the hermit crab, rescue Cosette, and get the Automatic Vending Artifact back. Before leaving, you enjoy the view of the island on the beach with Willow... But this summer tale is to be continued.
Stop! Give me back my drink!
Sob... My head's spinning...==W== My Automatic Vending Artifact... My drink...
So you're crying over that drink...==W== Guess you're alright then...
Looks like she's just a bit dizzy, nothing serious. She just needs some rest.
But it's seriously deformed. Can it actually be fixed...?==W== Fine, let's take it back first.
What a surprise. We were out here to catch the hermit crab but ended up running into the artifact.
Maybe it's not simply a coincidence...
Willow, do you remember the barrels and shells with scratches in the cave?
Of course I do... Ah, so the scratches were left by the hermit crab?
I guess it has taken that cave as its home... It's been living on this island all the time...
And by following its trace, we happened to discover the location of its home.
Anyway, now we've found Cosette and the Automatic Vending Artifact, our job's done here. We should celebrate!
The seas were quite rough just now. I think we should double-check the condition of our boat before we set off. Let's take a break in the meantime.
Hey, if it isn't Shia!==W== Karin's here too?
Hello, Boss. Feels like we just saw each other not that long ago...
So you two are the "old friends" Iris talked about.
Yep.==W== We heard about your trouble at sea, and my first thought was, "Again...?"
Well, you look great now, and that's reassuring.
Thanks to you. I mean it. Thank you for coming to help us out.
S-stop that! You're giving me goosebumps! We just did what we had to do.
Alright, enough chit-chat. I've got work to do!
I'll let you know when we're ready to go. You can relax for a bit.
Cosette is doing well, and the Automatic Vending Artifact has been fixed. Now all that's left is to wait...
Wait, where's Willow? She was here just now... I need to find her.
Not far from where the boat docks, there is a shallow cove with crystal-clear water embraced by surrounding rocks.
I didn't see you at the boat, so I got a bit worried.
Ah... I thought I should wash up real quick before getting on board. You know, I've got sand and mud all over my feet...
It would be very disrespectful to soil their boat like that.
I step closer to Willow.==W== The cool seawater laps at my ankles, and it feels so nice.
Sweet view... Wonder why I never noticed it.
Yeah... Well, I did, just didn't have the time and mood to enjoy it...
Now that we can finally take a break, I just have to take it all in.
Standing in the water, Willow carefully rinses off every bit of mud and sand on her.
As the sun shines on her, the water droplets streaming down her hair and shoulders glisten like diamonds.
What? Why are you staring at me?
Nothing... It's just...==W== You look somewhat different from the usual you.
You've always been so considerate and reliable. It feels like you can take care of everything perfectly.
And that makes me ...==B== very dependent on you. "Just follow Willow's lead," and I know everything will be fine.
Are you saying you find me less reliable now?
No, no! That's not what I meant...
I'm just not used to seeing you like this.
Like, usually, you'd be saying something like "Watch your step!"
You know, it's pretty slippery here, and I could trip.
Guess I'm really enjoying the present here.
Not worrying about anything, or planning the next step. Just stand here in the water, listening to the sounds of the waves and feeling the coolness of the water...
It is the first time I've seen Willow so relaxed...
This is incredible... Us standing here in the breeze, looking out at the sea...
It feels like we are actually on vacation, with all our worries left behind.
That sounds wonderful...==W== I can be here by your side as long as you wish.
Well... Looks like we'll have to save our vacation for next time.
Next time... Hehe, make sure to keep your word!
Let's go. Don't keep them waiting.
He's very weak now...==W== Be careful while you move!

strings.text: Intrigued by rumors of the Monolith at sea, Leafia wants to set sail to investigate. Horizon recommends two experienced seafaring Trekkers to her—Shia and Karin.
You want to investigate the Monolith in the sea?
That's right.==W== A fisherman got rescued from open water a few days ago.
Ever since they pulled him out, he's been muttering the same thing on loop like he's sleep-talking: In the sea... A Monolith...
Ah, that.==W== I heard the guy was barely coherent when they pulled him in, babbling pure nonsense. We figured it wasn't worth sending a team out over an unconfirmed rumor.
But what if he did see something?
If there's an uncharted Monolith out there, we need to put it on the map. Rumor or not, I have to see it for myself.
I figured you'd say that. Officially, I can't assign you people or resources. But if you want to poke around on your own time, I'm not stopping you.
One thing though, Leafia...==W== Have you ever sailed the open ocean?
That means you have to help me figure it out.
You always ask for favors like you're owed them.==W== Fine, I can't talk. Lucky for you, I saw this coming.
I'll hook you up with two experts. If you want to get out on the water, they're your best bet.
Oh, and when you see them,==W== see if you can ask when they'll finally drop by. My special expert seats are gathering dust over here...
This should be the spot.==W== Horizon mentioned Fluflas in swimsuits... Ah, there they are!
Excuse me, are you two...==W== Whoa!
Mm... Smells like paper and ink, with a hint of sunshine and soil...
Wh-What are you doing?! Who goes around sniffing people the second they meet?!
Shia! Why do you always do this to new people?! I told you it freaks them out!
How else am I supposed to confirm she's the one Horizon sent without getting a read on her scent?
Normal people start by asking for a name!
Yeah, starting with a name feels a bit safer...
Hehe, sorry for the scare. But identity confirmed.
Nice to meet you. I'm Shia, and this is Karin. We're seafaring Trekkers. If it involves the sea, we handle it.
And you must be Leafia. The surveyor who hauled a massive bag of tools all the way from Sailstead on a wild goose chase for a sea Monolith that might not even exist.
Sounds like Horizon already filled you in on me.
But to be polite, let me do this right. I'm Leafia, with the Trekker Association.
I'm hoping you two can help me head out to sea and look into those sea Monolith rumors.
Most people would write that off as a hoax or back out. Not you. You showed up hauling a giant pack.
I'm warning you now, surveying at sea is no joke. Underestimate the ocean, and you will pay for it.
I'd never. That's why I came to you.
Horizon said you two are the best seafaring Trekkers around. Real experts. I figured with you, I'd be in good hands.
Is she okay? Did I say something weird?
Heh, looks like Karin's tail is pointing straight up.
Shia! Am not!==W== Ahem... Anyway, I believe you're serious about this. And you don't look like a scammer who'd steal our boat and sell it.
That's low. Why would I do something like that?
Heh, Karin's cautious. But once she trusts you, she'll take good care of you.
Shia! You don't have to tell her all that!
A-Anyway... We're curious about the sea Monolith too.
So you think there really is a Monolith in the sea?
Mm.==W== A few months ago, a mysterious light appeared out on the water. People said it was the glow of a sea Monolith.
Turns out it was a glowing whale skeleton. But after that, we checked some old records and found quite a few stories about a sea Monolith.
The sea is full of unknowns, but this kind of rumor doesn't surface from nowhere.
As seafaring Trekkers, we want to understand the ocean better too. Unveil its secrets.
Perfect. When do we set sail?
Right, I get it. There's a ton of prep work before we can set sail, right?
Like inspecting the hull, checking the sails, stocking up on water and food, and plotting a course based on currents and wind patterns...
All that matters, but there's something even more important.
Something more important? Is it...==W== I've heard fishermen offer a prayer to the sea before heading out...
Not our thing.==W== Priority number one is getting you a swimsuit!
Huh? Did I hear that right? Maybe I need more sleep.
You heard right! Let's go, we need to get you a swimsuit!
B-But aren't we here to investigate the sea Monolith? What's a swimsuit got to do with that?
A lot! You can't seriously plan to go out in those clothes. If they get wet, not only will you be miserable, you'll barely be able to move!
A swimsuit is essential gear! Light, breathable, nothing to hold you back.==W== And the best part? Put on the right one, and you'll feel like diving right into the ocean!
Come on, don't look so horrified. You asked for our help, so we're doing our job: making sure you're prepped for the sea!
I can't believe I'm in a swimsuit... Can't focus at all... This feels wrong...
Huh? That person crouching by the water...==W== Is that Karin?
Hmm... You look the part, but you seem tense. Does it not fit?
No, you picked great. I'm just not used to walking around in this...
But for the mission, I'll get through it... I'd even dance in the street in this.
You don't have to go that far! You take things way too seriously...
In the field, unexpected things happen. If you can't adapt fast, the work won't get done.
Right... Well, for today, take it easy.
I know you're itching to hit the water right now, but we're not leaving till tomorrow morning. Save your energy.
As if.==W== Horizon told us in her letter. She said you'd be eager enough to swim there yourself, and begged us to hold you back.
Alright.==W== If we aren't going out today, what are you doing crouching out here?
Y-Yeah! Since it's our first time meeting, I figured I'd dig up some clams and have Shia cook a nice welcome dinner.==W== Is... Is that a problem?!
No, not at all. I just didn't expect you to go out of your way for me. It's a nice surprise.
What do you mean go out of my way?! Y-You're a guest, and we're sailing together. Of course I'd look after you!
Too bad the beach is dead today. I've been out here forever and barely found a thing.
Oh no... What am I supposed to say?
That compliment strategy Mikan taught me is way too complicated. My mind is completely blank. I can't remember a single thing.
Maybe I should just stick to the clams...
Um... Are razor clams hard to find?
Not really. You just focus and listen for any movement under the sand.==W== Oh... I think there's something here.
Karin brushes aside a thin layer of sand, revealing a tiny crab underneath.
Looks like it got stranded at low tide and dried up in the sun. Poor thing didn't have the strength to crawl back, so it buried itself in the sand to hide.
Karin bends down, carefully picks up the limp little crab, walks to the water's edge, and gently sets it back into the sea.
There you go. Head on home.
That's amazing... How could you tell it was a crab just from the sound?
Shia and I have lived by the water for years.
Where the shells wash up at low tide, which rocks the crabs hide under, what fish swim into the shallows... I know all of it with my eyes closed.
Wait, do you want a blindfolded demonstration?==W== You're on! Challenge accepted!
No, I'm genuinely impressed. You know this ocean better than I expected, Karin.
Yeah... Now I see why Horizon sent me to you.
You're not only expert seafarers. You actively feel and understand the sea.
If there is a Monolith out in the sea, I know following you will lead us right to it.
Hmph. Guess you have good eyes.
Since you're singing my praises, I guess I have to show off a little and blow your mind!
Get ready to see what a reliable seafaring Trekker looks like!

That compliment strategy Mikan taught me is way too complicated. My mind is completely blank. I can't remember a single thing.
Maybe I should just stick to the clams...
Um... Are razor clams hard to find?
Not really. You just focus and listen for any movement under the sand.==W== Oh... I think there's something here.
Karin brushes aside a thin layer of sand, revealing a tiny crab underneath.
Looks like it got stranded at low tide and dried up in the sun. Poor thing didn't have the strength to crawl back, so it buried itself in the sand to hide.
Karin bends down, carefully picks up the limp little crab, walks to the water's edge, and gently sets it back into the sea.
There you go. Head on home.
That's amazing... How could you tell it was a crab just from the sound?
Shia and I have lived by the water for years.
Where the shells wash up at low tide, which rocks the crabs hide under, what fish swim into the shallows... I know all of it with my eyes closed.
Wait, do you want a blindfolded demonstration?==W== You're on! Challenge accepted!
No, I'm genuinely impressed. You know this ocean better than I expected, Karin.
Yeah... Now I see why Horizon sent me to you.
You're not only expert seafarers. You actively feel and understand the sea.
If there is a Monolith out in the sea, I know following you will lead us right to it.
Hmph. Guess you have good eyes.
Since you're singing my praises, I guess I have to show off a little and blow your mind!
Get ready to see what a reliable seafaring Trekker looks like!

strings.text: The rough seas leave Leafia severely seasick on her first voyage. After some healing and conversation, Leafia and Karin discover how much they have in common. Just then, a Vending Artifact appeared on the water...
The next morning, Leafia, Karin, and Shia set sail.
The boat glides out of the harbor into the morning breeze, the water deepening into a richer blue the further they go.==W== Leafia stands at the rail, lost in the horizon.
The paper, ink, and sun-dried cotton are still there, but now there's sea salt and mist ...==W== and a hint of nervous excitement.
Heh, looks like Leafia's taken to the sea.
W-Why are you sniffing me again?!
That's how Shia is. She gets close and sniffs people she finds interesting...
I see...==W== But Karin, why are you grinding your teeth? Do you have a toothache?
Ahem... Never mind. Go back to watching the sea.
You look like you can't get enough of it. Don't tell me this is your first time out here.
First time this far out. The view is nothing like the ocean I'm used to.
When I look at the water from land, my brain defaults to practical things. Are there reefs nearby? How do I map out this coastline?
But out here on the boat, I get it. It's a completely different perspective from drawing maps.
... The wind, the waves, the deck rocking under my feet. It all feels incredibly real.
You can't capture the sea on paper, after all.
I spend most of my time traveling overland. Mountains, rivers, cities, roads. Mapping those isn't hard.
But out here, there's nothing but water. No landmarks, no borders. Even directions feel fuzzy.
It looks empty, but I can't shake the feeling something is hidden underneath.
The sea's a liar.==W== It looks calm on top, but whirlpools and reefs are waiting underneath. One minute it's clear skies, the next it's a storm.
The farther out you go, the wilder the water gets. And the weather stops making sense.
I see... I guess your experience is what keeps us safe out here.
To understand the sea, looking isn't enough. You have to listen to the wind, smell the air, feel the pull of the waves...
Take today. The breeze is fresh and clean. Perfect weather.==W== But if the air turns damp and heavy, with a murky saltiness to it, then the weather is about to turn.
And the water's color. See how it changes? That tells you a lot.==W== Depth, currents... Whether there is something hiding below.
That sounds complex... You'd never catch that staring at a chart.
Obviously. You can't capture a seafaring Trekker's experience on paper.
Fair point...==W== That only makes me want to figure it out.
How charts capture all those changes... How seafaring Trekkers navigate and avoid danger out here...
Would you two teach me more about sailing?
Of course. If you want to learn, I'll teach you everything I know.
Thank you. I'm counting on you, Shia.
<size=30>Hmph... I could teach her that. Why is she glued to Shia...
Hehe. Karin is reliable, too. If you ever get confused, go ask her. She'll patiently explain it all.
Got it. I look forward to your lessons, Professor Karin!
P-Professor?!==W== Hmph! Well, since you asked nicely, I suppose I can make an exception!
As the boat pushes deeper into the ocean, the shoreline shrinks until it vanishes. The waves grow rougher, relentlessly rocking the hull.
Yet even in the violent swells, Leafia stands perfectly upright on the deck.
Huh... You're handling this well. First-timers usually hurl their lunch by now.
Wait! Why is your face so pale?!
I need to ... record ... the wave cycles...
Forget the records! Look at the state of you!
Actually... Maybe there is a small problem...==W== Blurgh!
Looks like you're seasick, Leafia.==W== Here, sit down. Don't force yourself.
O-Okay... I get it now... Real ocean waves and map contour lines are two completely different things...
They looked so similar a minute ago... At least before the dizziness hit... Both so elegant...==W== Blurgh...
See? What did I tell you?
I-I was only taking a deep breath...
Since when does a deep breath make your soul leave your body?!
W-What is this? Why is it so dark and murky...?
This is the Splash Heartbeat secret seasickness remedy! Shia's own formula. It'll fix you right up.
What's with that face?!==W== Shia and I tested this improved version extensively! It might look==W== a little gross... But it works like magic!
Leafia takes the bowl of liquid, with its questionable color and indescribable smell, and falls silent. Then, as if surrendering, she squeezes her eyes shut and downs it in one gulp.
It tastes like seaweed, ginger, and mint all fought to the death inside my mouth... Leaving behind this unspeakable sour bitterness...==W== Ugh, I think I'm going to hurl...
Is it that awful...? This is the most normal-tasting version we have...
No, wait, forget the taste! How are you feeling?!
I think I feel a little better...==W== But I also want to throw up even more now...
If even the special remedy didn't help... You must be severely seasick.
Leafia, if it's too much, we can still turn back.
You need to know your limits at sea. Getting sick your first time this far out is totally normal. And it would be a shame if this ruined the ocean for you.
If we turn back now, I won't be able to rest either.==W== We came all this way, I can't give up halfway.
If I quit now, I'll be leaving another huge blank spot on my map. I'll definitely regret that... Let's keep going.
Alright, your call. Karin, take Leafia down to the cabin. I'll take the helm and keep us steady.
Let's move, maphead. Keep standing here and you'll be best friends with the deck.
Well? Feeling any better after a break?
A lot better... Thanks for taking care of me.
What choice did I have? If you passed out alone down here, Shia would worry herself sick.
You do take good care of me, Karin.
Wh-Where did that come from?! Don't say stuff like that.
Sigh... I will never get what goes on in that head of yours.
You dragged yourself out here for a rumor that might not even be true. Even in this state, you refuse to turn back.
And in the end, we might not find a thing.
If there's an unrecorded Monolith out here, the entire map needs to be redrawn, and we'd have to survey the Monolith.
And if there's no Monolith, I can honestly mark the map as empty and know for sure.
Is all this trouble worth it just to fill out a map?
Because this is what I do.
If a place hasn't been explored or mapped, I want to see it for myself.
But the maps we have now are detailed enough, aren't they?
Looking complete doesn't mean they're accurate. Rivers shift course, mountains crumble, forests expand.
And Monoliths reshape the land around them.==W== A map from a few years ago could be entirely useless today.
That's why I need to survey every inch of Nova myself. I want the best data to draw the most precise maps.
Wiping every patch of fog and blind spot off the map. That's been the Trekker Association's goal since day one.
But going by your logic, a perfect map today will be outdated in a few years. What's the point?
Then I'll go back and check it again. I'll keep updating the map until it reflects every change.
True accuracy comes from constant correction.
Seriously, maps have hijacked your brain.
People used to ask me why I was obsessed with being a seafaring Trekker.
They asked if the hardship was worth it. Some even said I wasn't cut out for the sea.
The more they said that, the more I refused to quit.
You chase blank spots on a map, I chase the waves. At the end of the day, we're both pursuing what we believe in.
I guess to everyone else, we're both stubborn weirdos.
I'll take that as a compliment.
Hmph, don't get cocky. Survive this voyage first, then we'll—
Karin! Leafia! Come out here and look at this!
There's something strange in the water.
Huh... What is that thing? It's blue and square.
Am I seasick enough to hallucinate? Why is there an...

strings.text: The three stumble upon the New Star Guild drifting at sea. Learning that you and Willow are stranded on a deserted island, Karin and Leafia work together to deduce a safe path to carry out the rescue.
... Is that actually an Automatic Vending Artifact?
Oh my. I've never seen an Automatic Vending Artifact make deliveries at sea. What a sight!
Who's supposed to use it out here?!
Since we're all curious, let's sail over and take a look.
Gone? Look closer. The waves might be hiding it.
Ugh, my eyes are burning from staring, but I don't see a—
Wait! There's a piece of driftwood out there, and people are hanging onto it!
What?! Quick, we need to save them!!
Cough... Cough... This seawater is awful...==W== Worse than the pain of missing a clearance sale...
Hang in there, Iris... Hold tight and don't let go...
Wait, isn't that the New Star Guild?==W== Hey! Are you okay?! Can you hear me?!
W-We're saved...==W== Thank goodness. Please tell me this isn't another hallucination...
Whoa, an actual boat! I'm not seeing things, it's a real, moving boat!
Do you have the strength to climb a rope?==W== Forget it, I'm coming down.
Give me your hand. Good, keep your weight low... Cling to me like an octopus and whatever you do, don't let go. Got it?
Next!==W== Hurry up, there's no time to be polite!
Eek, you sound so mean...==W== But you're a lifesaver, Karin. That's what I love about you...
Wh-who cares what you love?! Get on the boat already!
Sitting on solid ground...==W== I never knew it could feel this amazing...
Everyone, get some rest. If you aren't feeling well, don't tough it out. Let us know.
Thanks. I never thought we'd bump into you out here. What are the odds?
I didn't expect to be fishing you out of the ocean either. How did you end up drifting out here?
We hit a storm and the ship struck a reef...==W== Willow was with us at first, but she got separated from us when she jumped in to save ==PLAYER_NAME==...
The waves were too rough to swim in... We clung to some boards and drifted all the way here.
What do we do? What if something happened to them...
Easy. Don't panic. Let's get the facts straight first. There might be clues.
Shia's right.==W== Where were you approximately when the storm hit? And what were the wind and currents doing at the time?
How long were you drifting? Did you spot any islands, reefs, or obvious landmarks? And...
Wait, wait. That's too many questions at once...
Ugh... I guess we have to lay out our whole streak of bad luck, huh?
That's right. The more detail the better. Don't leave anything out, no matter how small.
The New Star Guild recounts their entire voyage in detail.
So that's the gist of it. When I fell in, I think I saw an island, but I honestly can't remember which direction...
... I think I can help. With this map, I can figure out the rough coordinates.
So you set out from the resort near Port Bellin, heading southeast...
Leafia pulls a map and scratch paper from her bag, spreads them on the deck, and starts scribbling furiously.
She was practically puking a minute ago, but the second she pulls out a map, her eyes light up...
Hmm... Still missing some key data.
Karin, can you estimate their ship's speed? We'll also need to factor in the wind and currents along the way...
You're asking the right person. Leave it to me.
Karin crouches beside Leafia, the two quickly trading notes...
We're right here. Backtracking from how they drifted and for how long...
Add in the distance they sailed from the resort...==W== They must have separated somewhere around here.
I recall seeing a few small islands in these waters.
Let's start our search in this area, then.
Amazing! You figured out the location fast!
I only have a general direction. To narrow it down, we actually need to ... go there ...==W== and check...==W== Blegh...
The second I look up from the map, the nausea hits me again...==W== I'm ... gonna go hug it and lie down for a bit.
Hello? ==PLAYER_NAME==?! Thank goodness, I finally got through!
Karin, Shia! We finally reached ==PLAYER_NAME== and Willow! They're stranded on a deserted island.
I ran the numbers again using Willow's intel. This is the spot.
Oh, I know that place! Ugh...==W== Why did it have to be that island...
What's wrong? Is there a problem with it?
The island itself is fine, but the surrounding waters are full of hidden reefs. They churn the currents into a total mess, making it a nightmare to sail through...
And I'm not making excuses because I can't handle it! On a clear day, Shia and I could tackle the worst routes without breaking a sweat!
But it's getting dark, and the wind and waves are picking up...
Trying to force a landing in these conditions is too risky.
Understood. I trust your expertise. We'll wait for the sea to calm down before we go pick them up.
Shia, port twenty degrees...==W== Five more. Hold her steady.
Starboard ten. Ease off the throttle.
Why go starboard? The left looks completely clear.
We can't. There's a crosscurrent over there. It would drag us off course and send us straight into the reefs.
Reefs? I don't see any reefs.
Little Karin uses her ears. She can pick up on hidden dangers even in choppy waters like this. We're in good hands.
I-It's nothing special! My ears wouldn't mean a thing without Shia's steering. She's the one navigating us through this mess...
Horizon definitely sent us the right seafaring Trekkers.
Ahem...==W== You bet they did! We are professionals.
I see movement on the island ahead.
Those two on the beach... That has to be ==PLAYER_NAME== and Willow, right?
Mmm... They just look like two blurry dots to me...
==PLAYER_NAME==! Willow! We're here to pick you up!
The boat barely touches the shore before the three New Star Guild members dive into the water.
Slow down! The boat is still moving!
Let them go, Karin. You know how eager they are to see their friends.
Fair enough...==W== Well, as long as they are safe, I can finally catch my breath.
Ugh...==W== Give it back... Give... Give me back my drinks!
Um... Doesn't that look like the Automatic Vending Artifact we saw floating in the ocean earlier?
Isn't this supposed to be a touching reunion after surviving a crisis?==W== Why...
... Why is there a hermit crab running around wearing a Vending Artifact?!

strings.text: On the return voyage, the rumored Monolith suddenly appears, but it is impossible to approach. Prompted by Cosette and guided by the hermit crab, you decide to risk sailing into the depths of the whirlpool...
Ah... I could get used to this peace and quiet.
We hit a few bumps along the way, but hey, we're finally back together!
Oh, speaking of which, how come Amber's phone is the only one working? Mine is still dead.
I stuck it between two Tawny Nightingale pieces, said a prayer, and waited for it to dry.==W== Shia taught me that.
The wood shavings in Tawny Nightingale probably help absorb the moisture. But uh...==W== Are they safe to eat after soaking up all that water?
Sure is lively out here. Looks like everyone is holding up fine. Well...==W== Almost.
Looks like those two are having a rough time.
It's a body constitution thing. Nothing we can do to help.
Sorry for the wait! Shia and I whipped up an improved batch of seasickness remedy. This will cure them for sure!
Here, drink this while it's hot. You'll feel better in no time.
Whoa... A bubbling dark mystery goo.==W== Oh yeah, that looks completely safe.
This is medicine?! No way, I hate medicine...==W== Blegh...
Hey now! Hang on! Don't throw up in the cabin!
Pretend it's a special drink exclusive to this ship. You won't find it anywhere else in Nova.
Special and exclusive?==W== Ugh... F-Fine.==W== I-I'll drink it!
... Was it bad enough to knock her out?!
Ah... I added some sleep-inducing herbs to help them rest. Might have overdone it...
It's alright. Let's let them sleep it off.
Leafia's seasickness is brutal as always. She knew how her body would react, but she insisted on coming anyway.
Yeah, she was dead set on finding that Monolith in the sea. She begged us to bring her along.
She's actually doing a lot better now. She couldn't even stand earlier. She was sprawled out on the deck like a puddle of mud and we couldn't pry her off.
Ah, are you talking about that rumor?
A week ago, a fisher was rescued near Port Bellin. He got caught in a storm, drifted into the open ocean, and claimed that a Monolith appeared right on the water.
He was delirious when they found him, though. Everyone assumed that the Monolith was a hallucination from the trauma.
But you can't prove it's a hallucination without checking for yourself. Besides...
Leafia said she'd be fine finding absolutely nothing. She only wants to chart the truth on her map.
Are we heading out to look for it now?
Leafia decided that getting you back safe is the priority. As for the Monolith, it can wait.
So that's "the Monolith in the sea"...
Wait, what do you mean it suddenly appeared?
Exactly what it sounds like! The horizon was empty a second ago, and then a Monolith popped out of nowhere!
Look who's cured. One mention of the Monolith and she springs back to life.
So what's the move? Do we keep heading back, or...
Are you kidding? It's right in front of us! Obviously we—==W==uh...
We made it this far. We might as well check it out.
Please don't worry about us. The Monolith was your main goal.==W== We'd feel awful if you turned back on our account.
Besides, I bet everyone here is dying to see this mystery Monolith up close. Right?
If we ignore it, we'll all be lying awake tonight regretting it.
Yeah! I know I wouldn't sleep a wink!
Let's get closer and see what we can find out.
The boat changes course and heads straight for the mysterious Monolith on the horizon.
Something feels wrong.==W== We're heading right for it, but the distance isn't closing.
Weird. The heading is dead on and the current isn't pushing us off course. Yet we aren't making any ground at all.==W== Tch.
Maybe it isn't a real Monolith.
Right! That explains everything.==W== If it's a mirage, we'll never close the gap. The actual structure isn't even there.
So it is an illusion. What the fisher saw was indeed a hallucination...
We hit something! Hold on tight!
Was it a reef?==W== No, there shouldn't be any rocks out here!
Look in the water! Is that...
Why does it keep ramming us?!
Maybe it's mad==W== because we took the Automatic Vending Artifact...?
A-And it tracked us all the way out here to attack us?!
That doesn't make sense. Stomper Crabs are docile. They don't attack unless they're backed into a corner.
Plus, look at it. It doesn't look angry... It looks more like ...==W== anxious?
You can tell what a crab is thinking?
It's written all over its face.
Besides, it looked thrilled when that Artifact fell off earlier.
I'm staring a hole through it and I still see absolutely nothing.
Shia wrestles the helm to dodge the crab. The creature is relentless, refusing to back off.==W==
Maybe... it isn't trying to sink us. It's forcing us off course.==W== Is it trying to steer us somewhere?
What is that sound? That doesn't sound right.==W== What's going on?!
The calm sea rips open, churning into a massive whirlpool. An eerie light pulses deep within the vortex, like a giant eye watching from the abyss.
Shia, turn the wheel! We're done for if we get sucked in!
I can't! The current is too strong. She won't turn!
We have to abandon ship.==W== Karin, lower the lifeboat! We need to move!
If a ship this size is trapped, how will a lifeboat help?
Lifeboats accelerate faster. If we drop it now, we can still outrun the pull!
Shia, get everyone to safety. I'm staying behind to try and steer us clear.
Stop being stubborn, Karin! Did you forget Grandma's number one rule?
<size=50>"Never pick a fight with the sea!"
I know! But if we abandon it, the ship is going to be torn apart...
This is Grandma's ship. She left it to you!
It's safe underneath the whirlpool... We'll be fine even if we get sucked in.
Are you out of your mind? How is that even possible?!
I-I swear it's true... I've been down there before.
Karin, I can smell that she's telling the truth.==W== I think we can trust her.
If Shia says so...==W== If it's really safe down there... Then maybe...
Make the call, Karin. We trust you and Shia.
Shia, ride the current straight into the eye of the whirlpool. It's our best shot at keeping the ship in one piece.
You got it! Leave the wheel to me.
Brace yourselves, everyone! We're diving straight in!
