strings.text: The girls of the New Star Guild, who are going broke, bring you, an amnesiac, up another Monolith, where their wish brings forth an Artifact, something both familiar and alien to you.
Hey, Ir<r=Ayame></r>is! How's the person who came out of the box?
Pulse and temperature are normal. Breathing's steady, too.
That's good. Oh, and that tune just now—wasn't that the one Aunt Allie used to hum? What made you think of it?
I was just remembering something. Once when I was little, I fell and hurt myself, and Aunt Allie sang that song to me. The pain just ... vanished, like magic.
So I figured if I sang it now, maybe it would help this person feel better too...
We took a Wishing Box from the Monolith, and when we opened it, you were inside.
Hi there! I'm No<r=Seina></r>ya. Nice to meet you!
And that one up on the car is Am<r=Kohaku></r>ber!
And Ir<r=Ayame></r>is is the one who explained everything just now!
By the way, are you alone? No teammates with you?
Hey, No<r=Seina></r>ya. Maybe ease up on the questions, yeah?
Oh, my bad! I was just so surprised, you know?
I mean, the box opened and there you were, fast asleep. Ir<r=Ayame></r>is even said, "Maybe it's a humanoid Artifact!" and started inspecting you from head to toe.
Ahem! I was just checking if you were a person or an Artifact, that's all!
I-I swear I didn't do anything weird!
Then hey, do I look familiar to you? I get the feeling we've met before, somewhere.
Before? If I'd met someone as cute as you, I definitely wouldn't have forgotten.==W== Sorry, nothing's coming to mind.
Huh!? C-Cute!? Aww, come on now! Don't just say stuff like that out of nowhere, it's embarrassing!
I don't think I said anything that strange...
Anyway, I don't remember my name, or your face, or why I was in that box.
Well, for us, it's kind of an occupational hazard.
Amnesia? The way you say that makes it sound really common.
That's because being a Trekker and losing your memories kinda go hand in hand.
Trekkers climb Monoliths, make wishes with the Wishing Boxes, and receive powerful Artifacts.==W== But in return, a part of their memory is taken by the Monolith.
Your situation is exactly what that looks like. Ideally, we'd send you straight back to the city, but...
We can't leave empty-handed either, so we're on our way to another Monolith.
So ... we're really sorry,==W== but we'd appreciate it if you could travel with us for a bit.
There are a lot of monsters around here, too, so it's not exactly safe staying behind in the car alone. But don't worry. We'll protect you!
We'll take down any monsters or Stellaroids that come our way.
Doesn't seem like much of a choice. Heading to this so-called Monolith might help me get some memories back anyway.
But about what you just said—
If you make a wish, you could end up with amnesia like me, right?
Ahaha... Well, I'd be lying if I said I wasn't scared.
But honestly, right now, what's scarier than memory loss is the fact that we have no money to survive another day!

strings.text: In your dream, you are called "Tyrant." You awake as an amnesiac Trekker in a vehicle rolling into the City of a Thousand Monoliths. The girls vow to help you restore what you've forgotten.

<size=47>==RT====RT==Emor's legions suffered ten tragic defeats, powerless against the Tyrant's bewitching magic.==RT====RT==But divine intervention brought clarity. The Tyrant lost their dark powers upon stepping into Emor, and was brought to judgment.==RT====RT==From that day, the Tyrant ceased to exist, and the God of Grace's bounty flowed equally to all Novians.</size>==RT====RT==<size=47>—Chronicles of New Nova, by Virigia</size>
A whiff of gunpowder drifts on the evening breeze.
Crumbled buildings and shattered banners litter the landscape.
Hordes of soldiers storm the City of a Thousand Monoliths, reducing the magnificent city to ruins.
Yesterday's sovereign now sits, a prisoner on a frigid throne...
awaiting some fortunate soul to claim the head of ==SEX5==.
It's because I have betrayed you…
You've got the wrong person. I'm no Tyrant.
Maybe you lost your memory, but it's okay. Happy days ahead surely await you.
I turned against the Tyrant's army...
Which led to our dream being shattered.
That is to say... The story we've been trying to write ends today.
Even if you don't think of yourself as "Tyrant"...
As long as everyone believes that you are...
Then that is who you are, and no one else.
Do you see that incredibly bright star?
People give their wishes over to that star.
Because, then, when their wishes don't come true...
"Well, I did the best I could, but my lucky star didn't shine on me."
But dreams don't come true just because we wish for them. Life's not that easy.
But we're so pathetic that we can't really face our life without fooling ourselves like that.
And that's exactly why ... you don't need to become a wishing star.
No one ever gets different results by doing the same thing over and over again.
Goodbye, Tyrant. I'm glad we had this final talk.
But, if... If fate would guide us once more…
Let's meet again under a starless sky.
D-Don't go! I have questions for y—
I wake up staring at the unfamiliar sunroof of a caravan.
Right. I was rescued in the desert.
I climbed the Monolith with them. Now we're heading to the city.
I take a cup from Iris.==W== The warm drink soothes my throat and calms my nerves.
I can't say if it was a nightmare, really.==W== But thanks, I feel better now.
In the dream... Someone called me "Tyrant."
Wow, that's ancient. Like something out of a children's storybook.
With a gesture that feels strangely familiar, Iris flips her notebook sideways and points to a phrase.
In fact, we don't speak of this word anymore. It's an ancient one.==W== Now, everyone just says "Boss."
It means the absolute strongest Stellaroid inside a Monolith.
That old word ... represented a world destroyer, the one taken down by warriors...
So, even the sound of the name had to go.
Wait, the Tyrant was like that?
I thought the Tyrant's whole deal was conquering every Monolith. Isn't that kinda cool?
You didn't finish the story, Noya. The Tyrant planned to demolish every Monolith after conquering them.
No Monoliths means no Artifacts—how's that not world-ending?
Iris nuzzles her wished-for Recording Artifact.
Relax. Losing all the Artifacts wouldn't be the end of the world.
We pawn off most Artifacts anyway. It's not like we use them.
True, but the money from selling Artifacts is what pays for the Lucky Oasis' repairs!
Yes, and it's also the name of our home.
Right. This is more than just our ride—it's the home we built ourselves.
The three of us all grew up in the same orphanage. Every single bolt and plate on the Lucky Oasis was put there by us ...==W== well, mostly Noya.
Oh, and you can call it Loxy!
You built this all by yourself? That's amazing, Noya.==W== But if you wanted a ride, why not just wish for one from some wishing box?
Hehe! This is how Trekkers roll! Just wishing for stuff is lame. Wish for parts, then build something awesome by hand!
Hey Iris, Loxy's rattling a bit. Think we can splurge on some grease after we sell our loot?
And my gun ... needs a magic recharge...
Pretty urgent, I see...==W== But the answer is no.
We're flat broke. Every last coin's gotta go to critical stuff. "Pretty urgent" isn't going to cut it.
After we grab essential supplies, my numbers say we'll have just enough for one Soul Stone.
Soul Stone... Oh yeah, let's do it!
Soul Stone... You mean the four-pointed star-shaped stone you are wearing?
It's a stone bound to your soul that stores magic.
Spells and Artifacts drains a lot of power, so you need to store some in the stone first.
Plus, the Grace Imperium keeps records of every single Soul Stone ever crafted.
That way, when we get you a new one, your name and identity should pop right back.
Thanks...==W== But no amount of flattery is moving your shopping plans up the list.
But that is expensive... I don't wanna be a burden.
All Trekkers are sworn to help those who've lost their memories.
'Cause who knows? Tomorrow, we could be the ones drawing a blank.
Just roll with it. It's not everyday Iris is this generous!
Check it! We're here—the City of a Thousand Monoliths!
Noya steers the vehicle into a sprawling, bustling city.
Wow, it's been two years since we left.==W== This place is as lively as ever.
Maybe we should stop by the Ash Orphanage to see Aunt Allie... No, we have to sell the Artifacts first.
So the City of a Thousand Monoliths ... wasn't destroyed.
Was it really ... just a dream?
In the distance, stars embedded in towering white spires that stand in silent sentinel.

And my gun ... needs a magic recharge...
Pretty urgent, I see...==W== But the answer is no.
We're flat broke. Every last coin's gotta go to critical stuff. "Pretty urgent" isn't going to cut it.
After we grab essential supplies, my numbers say we'll have just enough for one Soul Stone.
Soul Stone... Oh yeah, let's do it!
Soul Stone... You mean the four-pointed star-shaped stone you are wearing?
It's a stone bound to your soul that stores magic.
Spells and Artifacts drains a lot of power, so you need to store some in the stone first.
Plus, the Grace Imperium keeps records of every single Soul Stone ever crafted.
That way, when we get you a new one, your name and identity should pop right back.
Thanks...==W== But no amount of flattery is moving your shopping plans up the list.
But that is expensive... I don't wanna be a burden.
All Trekkers are sworn to help those who've lost their memories.
'Cause who knows? Tomorrow, we could be the ones drawing a blank.
Just roll with it. It's not everyday Iris is this generous!
Check it! We're here—the City of a Thousand Monoliths!
Noya steers the vehicle into a sprawling, bustling city.
Wow, it's been two years since we left.==W== This place is as lively as ever.
Maybe we should stop by the Ash Orphanage to see Aunt Allie... No, we have to sell the Artifacts first.
So the City of a Thousand Monoliths ... wasn't destroyed.
Was it really ... just a dream?
In the distance, stars embedded in towering white spires that stand in silent sentinel.

strings.text: Novians need a Soul Stone to use magic, but the Grace Imperium has no record of you. The key on you, however, opens an ancient safe.
After selling the Artifacts, we find ourselves at a large complex.
This is a Soul Shop run by the Grace Imperium, a place that crafts Soul Stones.
Please rest your hand here for about five minutes.
While you wait, try thinking of something that makes you happy, or a really important moment in your life.
But I don't have any memories to begin with.
The only "important" thing I can think of is ... that moment when they found me.
Oh, don't worry. It's not required to make a Soul Stone. It's just that, you know, people say focusing on those memories makes for a higher-quality Soul Stone.
Thanks... This whole process is incredible.
The box you're touching has Water of Grace in it, straight from the God of Grace.
The Water of Grace resonates with your soul, and then it crystallizes into Soul Stones of all different sizes and colors.
Wow. Iris sounds more like the clerk than the actual clerk.
Alright, you can take your hand away now. And this, from the box, is your...
Wha...? What?!! The Water of Grace ... it didn't crystallize!!!
We are so sorry. We've run a full diagnostic, and your constitution is ... well, it's highly unusual. Your body is immune to magic.
That's right. You might not have known, but your body can't use magic. Without magic, your soul can't resonate with the Water of Grace, so no Soul Stone can be made.
I'm sorry. It's extremely rare, but this condition does exist.
We also couldn't find any past records of you making a Soul Stone, so we don't know if you were born this way.
Born this way ... or did my memory loss from the Monolith do this to me? Who was I before all this?
I get it. It's not your fault. If it can't be done ... then let's just forget about it.
All of you went to so much trouble ... for nothing. I'm sorry.
Hey, don't apologize! Maybe the Water of Grace here just expired. Let's try another Soul Shop!
I've never heard of Water of Grace expiring...
I'm really sorry we couldn't be more helpful. ==W==Bastelina, would you see our guests out?
Hmm, do you guys not find it strange?
Someone with no magic, trekking through the desert alone, climbing a Monolith, and hiding in a wishing box guarded by Stellaroids... It just doesn't add up.
I can't remember how I got to the Monolith, either. Maybe someone else brought me there. That would make sense.
I just wish I could find someone who knew me before all this.
I'm Bastelina, a super-duper cute intern here at the Grace Imperium Soul Shop.
If you don't mind my asking, are you suffering from memory loss? A pretty bad case?
Yes. It happened in the Monolith. I can't even remember my own name.
I bet you've also forgotten where this key came from.
Come to think of it, I do have a key on me.
That key was already on you when we found you. We don't know what it's for, either.
My internship is actually in the Grace Imperium Vault. I'm just helping out at the front desk today by chance.
If I'm not mistaken, that key you've got is—
—the key to the highest level security safe in our shop.
This is the actual Grace Imperium Vault? So many safes...
I can't believe we're allowed in here. This is where the Senators and top executives stash their secrets!
Who would dare to mess with the Grace Imperium? They're the biggest company in Nova.
An ... an alarm! Did we touch something we weren't supposed to?
Whoops, my bad! I forgot to feed my Artifact tamago!
It scared me to death! ==W==Can you please turn that game off?!
Somehow, even without my memories, I feel at ease with them.
It's off. Hey, where'd Bastelina go? She just disappeared.
She's looking for the security safe for us.
I have a security safe in a place like this? What kind of person was I before?
See? I knew you weren't some ordinary Trekker. Anyone who has a safe here must be someone amazing.
I hope you're right. I hope I can find something in there that can tell me who I am.
I've found it. This way, please.
We follow Bastelina deeper into the vault.
The air has a faint, musty smell, as if time itself has stood still.
Your key opens Safe #1, the oldest one in the shop.
I only started my internship last month, so I'm not sure why you're linked to this specific safe.
What's this? Some kind of Artifact?
Ooh, it's so sparkly and pretty.
A phone? Since when do phones look like this?
Can't even fold it! Where's the number pad?
As far as I can remember... You use it like this.
This is the messaging app everyone uses—Heartlink. Your name's gotta be in there if you ever used it.
This is ... my face? ==W==And bellow should be my name... Sounds familiar.
So glad I could help! Now that you have your name, your memories will start coming back.
If you press your finger on it, you can see people you've contacted before and their messages. You might be able to recover more memories.
Touch the screen and enter Heartlink
ÎÒèñ ëîðòý, Î ñàí ìîñô äî ïåñò.==RT==Î ëîâå õîó, ==PLAYER_NAME==.
Uh... There's a message. ==W==I can't make sense of it at all—except for my name.
That's it, there's no one else who's ever contacted me.
Oh, um... Is there something wrong with the communication magic on this phone?
Oops, that's my phone. My supervisor's calling, one moment.
Yes, the customer just opened Safe #1. ==W==Special instructions? Got it. On it right away.
Um ... d-did I just hear "special"? Please tell me she's not going to charge us storage fees.
Storage here probably costs a fortune. There's no way we can afford that...
Ahem, thank you for waiting. So sorry, but could I ask for just a moment more of your time?
My supervisor just told me there's an important file in the archives for whoever opened Safe #1. My colleague is bringing it over now.
And don't worry, this isn't about a fee. The safe was paid for a long time ago.
Oh, th-thank goodness... I seriously thought we were about to go broke...
The file's here already? That's fast.
That green RV outside, that's yours, right?
You need to get outside. Now.
Someone's trying to tow your ride away!

strings.text: Suspicious debt is pinned on the New Star Guild. Your vehicle, also serving as your home and shelter, is seized by the greedy Creta Trading as repayment.
Chief Feagin! The ride's all strapped up and ready.
Careful with the paintjob! Any scratches come straight outta your paychecks.
Thick wooden beams are lashed to the Lucky Oasis's frame.
Heave on three! One ... two ... LIFT!
A dozen hired hands shoulder the beams, raising the vehicle steadily.
Hey! What do you think you're doing with Loxy?
This has to be a mistake. Why are you hauling off our wheels?
We're just hired muscle. You gotta ask our client about the details.
What's this? Coffee break already? Seems like you're costing me too much?
What do you care if the owners are here? I'm the one signing your checks!
R-right, understood! We'll get it back up.
So you're the crook behind this?
Excuse me? Who are you calling a crook, you filthy gutter rats?
I am Feagin, CEO of the Creta Trading. I'm sure you've heard of the name. Now step aside if you know what's good for you.
N-Noya, hold on! She's a CEO! We can't win this!
Chief or not, thieves are thieves, and that means trouble.
Amber, get ready for a fight.
Woah, hold your fire! We're putting it down!
There's just no reasoning with your kind.
Well ... I don't know all the details, but you can't blame them for being upset. You can't just take someone's vehicle like that.
Huh? And who are you supposed to be?
I'm Bastelina, an intern with the Grace Imperium.==W== You must be ... Chief Feagin of the Creta Trading?
Hmph. Finally, someone with half a brain.
With all due respect, Chief, even for a CEO,taking a vehicle without permission is still theft. It's a crime.
And since this is happening in front of the Soul Shop, Grace Imperium has a duty to protect its clients.
I must insist you stop this immediately. Otherwise, I'll have to call the Sentinel of Dawn.
My, my, aren't you a brave one?
That's right. The vehicle is collateral for a debt, which makes it the property of the Creta Trading.
What?! We built Loxy with our own two hands! How can she be yours?
The borrower ... it's the Ash Orphanage?!
Read it and weep. It's all there in black and white.
Two years back, Ash Orphanage took a 10-billion-Dorra loan from us. Twenty-year term, 20% APR, monthly payments.
No way! Aunt Allie would never take out a loan that big!
Exactly. Aunt Allie always prioritize the children's well-being. She would never do something so reckless.
Or maybe it was for the sake of those children that she had to keep borrowing?
Even if that's true, this is all so sudden.==W== We'll look into this and make sure to settle things with you properly.
We're not going to run off, I swear. So, please, could you return our vehicle for now?
When was the last time you all were in Emor?
One year and ten months ago, the Ash Orphanage closed its doors. Director Allie and the kids vanished.
The money they owed us? Poof. Gone.
So, it's nothing personal, but any property with even a whiff of Ash Orphanage on it? It's ours now.
But ... but Loxy ... We built Loxy with our own hands...
I already looked into it.==W== A lot of the parts for this vehicle came from the orphanage's warehouse.
The contract is perfectly clear. We are to impound any item that includes orphanage property.
Does that loan contract really carry that much weight? Can such an unfair clause actually be enforced?
But an aggressive approach like this is bound to cause problems.
And you lot—former orphans—are jointly responsible for the debt.
Consider this your introduction to the real world. Think of it as paying tuition.
Hey now, why the long faces? Cheer up!==W==This car, plus the orphanage and its land, must be worth at least 20 million.
That brings this month's remaining balance downto a measly 833,333 Dorra!
So, there you have it. Come pay us at the Creta Trading once you've got the fund.
Point out the holes in Feagin's story
Hmm? And who might you be?
I'm their Guildmate, but I'm not from the orphanage.
And I think you're trying to scam my friends.
Oh, really? You have any idea what you're doing?
Better have proof, or I'll sue you for everything you're worth.
Bastelina, could you remind me how long we were inside the Soul Shop?
Let me see ... around thirty minutes.
In just thirty minutes, you found our car in this huge city,==W== recognized parts from two years ago, and hired all these guys to move it?
S-so what? I've had my eye on you for days. It's called being prepared!
That's a lie! We just got back to Emor this morning!
And besides, you didn't even recognize them as the owners at first, did you?
Something's not right. There has to be more to this story.
Hey, we've got other jobs to get to. We hauling this thing or not?
Haul it! Ignore these vagrant Trekkers! Extra pay if they try anything.
Ma'am, we're run ragged. That up-and-down wore us all out.
What? Are you serious? Why is everyone so useless...?
W-what do you think you're doing?
Like I said. Leave the car with us.
If there's a real debt, we'll honor it.
No, no way.You lot, get back to work!
The Imperial Guard ... What are they doing here?
Good thing I paid extra for their protection.
Quick, get that RV out of here!
Iris restrains Noya and Amber as they try to rush a wall of silver-clad knights.
All we can do is watch the Lucky Oasis disappear.

strings.text: Homeless but undeterred, you rally to investigate the debt and reclaim your vehicle. Before you leave, you give your food to a girl fainting from hunger.
Iris' fingertips shimmer, freezing the rain around us into tiny ice beads that swirl to form a growing ice orb at her chest.
50,009, 50,010 ... No, no, it's not enough! This will NEVER be enough!
It's probably the shock of it all.==W== We finally get back to Emor only to find the orphanage closed, Aunt Allie missing, Loxy taken, and now we're drowning in debt.
Indulging in despair ... won't fix anything.
We may have lost something precious, but we gained a new friend. No reason to be sad about that.
You saw right through those Creta creeps ... You knew they were actually after our ride all along.
Whoa, slow down. I'm the one without memories here, remember?
You've gotta have some idea what our next step should be, right?
Our next step ... We were targeted the moment we entered the city. Creta Trading clearly wasn't after the money.
That brilliant deduction that cornered Feagin? Only you could've pulled that off!
Noya's exaggerating ... but the way Feagin was talking...
Are they after our ride? Is the orphanage hiding some secret?
50,200 ... At this rate, making 830 thousand Dorra will be a piece of cake...
Hehe, at this rate, I'll have 830 thousand in no time!
Is there any way to snap her out of this?
Talk her down, or wait it out. She'll get over it soon. If you want to speed things up, distract her with something she likes.
Comfort Iris by getting her to solve problems
Iris, we're definitely getting the Lucky Oasis back.
Nothing happened.==W== Okay, time for a different approach...
Look, the ride's gone, we're drowning in debt...==W== Maybe we should just ditch this whole Trekker thing for good.
I've lost my memory, and Noya and Amber ... they aren't exactly cut out for city life.
So let's just bail. If we never come back to Emor, they can't stick us with that crazy debt, can they?
W-what was I just doing? Did someone say something about disbanding the guild?
You heard wrong.==W== We were just talking about lunch.
I just ... I figured if I could collect 833,333 raindrops, a solution would come to me.
She really went off the deep end.
I'll give her something to chew on.
A girl is collecting rainwater. She gathers 800 drops a minute, but 10 drops evaporate every hour.
How long will it take her to collect 833,333 raindrops?
This crazy math should get her mind off counting actual raindrops.
Ahem.==W== Anyway, the point is, some things just take time.
It was a bit of a stretch, but at least it got her attention.
The orphanage closed, Aunt Allie's gone, the Lucky Oasis was towed, and we have those awful monthly payments.
It's just ... so much is happening at once ... I panicked.
But if I take the time to think, there must be a solution. We just haven't found all the variables for the equation yet!
Whew. Her logic is one of a kind, but at least she's got some fire back.
Convince Iris? Not a chance. Just go with the flow.
Minutes tick by. Iris stands frozen at the edge of the bridge, still fixated on the falling rain.
Huh? Why'd she stop? Don't tell me she's finally broken down...
It's okay. This means she's about to snap out of it.
Noya, Amber, ==PLAYER_NAME==, could you give me a hand?
I'm fine.==W== Was I acting strange?
Iris is so obsessed about our health that no matter how out of it she is, she always comes to her senses at mealtime to make sure we eat.
What a weirdly specific habit ==W==... So I was worried sick for nothing?!
By the way, anything that can hold water?
Alright. Amber,==W== melt this ice ball and filter it. That should give us clean water.
Amber expertly shoots a gout of flame from her gun. They've clearly done this a million times.
Even when she's in despair, she's still looking out for the Guild.
Speaking of which, Iris, you can use water magic, right? Why not just make some water?
Oh, well ...==W== most of my magic pulls from nearby water or moisture in the air. Without the rain...
I'd have to use the water from my own body. I guess it would look like I was creating it from scratch...
Oh, I get it. So, Iris-brand water...
That's just weird and you know it!
I don't see what the big deal is.
I can do with it too.
That is NOT the point! Stop being so agreeable!
Their life on the road is rough for sure.
Amber caught some fish, and I found some mushrooms. Let's get a fire going for grilled fish and mushrooms.
Hold on. It's not a real meal without proper staple food.
Iris rummages in her hat and fishes out a banknote.
I've got 10,000 Dorra left. If we get the cheapest Tawny Nightingale bread, there'll be enough for lunch and dinner for the four of us.
Whoa, I thought we were broke.
We are. This is the emergency fund I've been saving up.
Iris saved it. Skipped a slice of bread every meal.
Whenever things look dire, Iris pulls another rabbit out of her hat.
Hey, I can't just conjure up funds forever!
This is barely enough to last us through tomorrow. We need jobs and a place to crash, and fast.
Let's just bust into that corporation and rescue Loxy!
I know how you feel, but that's a terrible idea.==W== If we get caught, we're finished.
Not fair! They're the ones who stole our ride!
Feagin is the CEO of the Creta Trading. Companies, their staff, and Trekkers like us... We're not treated the same.
Why? What's the big deal with this "CEO" title Feagin uses?
Companies are blessed by the God of Grace, stamped with the Seal of Grace and all.
They run cities, command soldiers—some even have private armies.
They're the closest to the Gods. They only answer to their own rulebooks, not common decency.
A CEO is a company's leader. Even if they break the law, they can usually get away with it by paying a fine.
They can just do whatever they want? Don't people ever push back?
It's always been this way. I guess you could say everyone's just used to it...
Nova was once ruled by emperors and nobles, but companies muscled them out. Now, noble titles are just really old, fancy names.
What really matters is becoming a big shot in a company, or joining their senate. That's true glory.
Just because things have always been this way ... doesn't make it right.
I still think finding a Wishing Star in the Monolith is the ultimate glory.
City folk and Trekkers just see things differently.
I see things more like Noya does ... Maybe I used to be a Trekker.
Even so, we can't just take this lying down.
Maybe we should poke around the Ash Orphanage? Might find something.
Agreed! I'm sick of being used like this!
Rain's letting up. Let's eat, then head out.
I was scouting the bridge ... and I found someone passed out.
That's not the point. It's strange for someone to be sleeping out here like this. What if she's a spy from the Creta Trading?
Probably got nowhere to go, like us.
You hear her stomach growling? She must have fainted from hunger.
I feel bad leaving her here, but let's just leave her some food and get to the orphanage first.
I'm not that hungry. She can have half of my share.
Before we leave, I set down my saved bread and fish beside the sleeping girl.

param: Homeless but undeterred, you rally to investigate the debt and reclaim your vehicle. Before you leave, you give your food to a girl fainting from hunger.
Iris' fingertips shimmer, freezing the rain around us into tiny ice beads that swirl to form a growing ice orb at her chest.
50,009, 50,010 ... No, no, it's not enough! This will NEVER be enough!
It's probably the shock of it all.==W== We finally get back to Emor only to find the orphanage closed, Aunt Allie missing, Loxy taken, and now we're drowning in debt.
Indulging in despair ... won't fix anything.
We may have lost something precious, but we gained a new friend. No reason to be sad about that.
You saw right through those Creta creeps ... You knew they were actually after our ride all along.
Whoa, slow down. I'm the one without memories here, remember?
You've gotta have some idea what our next step should be, right?
Our next step ... We were targeted the moment we entered the city. Creta Trading clearly wasn't after the money.
That brilliant deduction that cornered Feagin? Only you could've pulled that off!
Noya's exaggerating ... but the way Feagin was talking...
Are they after our ride? Is the orphanage hiding some secret?
50,200 ... At this rate, making 830 thousand Dorra will be a piece of cake...
Hehe, at this rate, I'll have 830 thousand in no time!
Is there any way to snap her out of this?
Talk her down, or wait it out. She'll get over it soon. If you want to speed things up, distract her with something she likes.
Comfort Iris by getting her to solve problems
Iris, we're definitely getting the Lucky Oasis back.
Nothing happened.==W== Okay, time for a different approach...
Look, the ride's gone, we're drowning in debt...==W== Maybe we should just ditch this whole Trekker thing for good.
I've lost my memory, and Noya and Amber ... they aren't exactly cut out for city life.
So let's just bail. If we never come back to Emor, they can't stick us with that crazy debt, can they?
W-what was I just doing? Did someone say something about disbanding the guild?
You heard wrong.==W== We were just talking about lunch.
I just ... I figured if I could collect 833,333 raindrops, a solution would come to me.
She really went off the deep end.
I'll give her something to chew on.
A girl is collecting rainwater. She gathers 800 drops a minute, but 10 drops evaporate every hour.
How long will it take her to collect 833,333 raindrops?
This crazy math should get her mind off counting actual raindrops.
Ahem.==W== Anyway, the point is, some things just take time.
It was a bit of a stretch, but at least it got her attention.
The orphanage closed, Aunt Allie's gone, the Lucky Oasis was towed, and we have those awful monthly payments.
It's just ... so much is happening at once ... I panicked.
But if I take the time to think, there must be a solution. We just haven't found all the variables for the equation yet!
Whew. Her logic is one of a kind, but at least she's got some fire back.
Convince Iris? Not a chance. Just go with the flow.
Minutes tick by. Iris stands frozen at the edge of the bridge, still fixated on the falling rain.
Huh? Why'd she stop? Don't tell me she's finally broken down...
It's okay. This means she's about to snap out of it.
Noya, Amber, ==PLAYER_NAME==, could you give me a hand?
I'm fine.==W== Was I acting strange?
Iris is so obsessed about our health that no matter how out of it she is, she always comes to her senses at mealtime to make sure we eat.
What a weirdly specific habit ==W==... So I was worried sick for nothing?!
By the way, anything that can hold water?
Alright. Amber,==W== melt this ice ball and filter it. That should give us clean water.
Amber expertly shoots a gout of flame from her gun. They've clearly done this a million times.
Even when she's in despair, she's still looking out for the Guild.
Speaking of which, Iris, you can use water magic, right? Why not just make some water?
Oh, well ...==W== most of my magic pulls from nearby water or moisture in the air. Without the rain...
I'd have to use the water from my own body. I guess it would look like I was creating it from scratch...
Oh, I get it. So, Iris-brand water...
That's just weird and you know it!
I don't see what the big deal is.
I can do with it too.
That is NOT the point! Stop being so agreeable!
Their life on the road is rough for sure.
Amber caught some fish, and I found some mushrooms. Let's get a fire going for grilled fish and mushrooms.
Hold on. It's not a real meal without proper staple food.
Iris rummages in her hat and fishes out a banknote.
I've got 10,000 Dorra left. If we get the cheapest Tawny Nightingale bread, there'll be enough for lunch and dinner for the four of us.
Whoa, I thought we were broke.
We are. This is the emergency fund I've been saving up.
Iris saved it. Skipped a slice of bread every meal.

strings.text: You find the girls' childhood orphanage gone, replaced by the Ashwind Clan. The moment they hear you're from the orphanage, they draw their weapons.
Are we just going to walk along Waterways?
Emor's Waterways link up all seven Monoliths in the city.
This way, we avoid all those twisty little streets down below. It's the fastest way to the orphanage!
If it's so convenient, why isn't anyone else using it?
It's high up and really dangerous. One slip, and it's a long way down.==W== I think only Trekkers are reckless enough to use this path.
Hey, c'mon, this way! There's a shortcut that way, I think.
Bridge out ahead ... Noya, this shortcut's a bust. Head back.
Relax, I'm not going to fall.
This is the shortcut! Just worried you won't jump!
Hold on tight, ==PLAYER_NAME==. I've got you.
As it turned out, we aren't actually jumping to the ground. The wreckage had formed a makeshift staircase that we simply walk down.
Huff ... huff ...==W== Noya, a little warning next time, okay?
I thought you knew. We found this shortcut when we were kids!
You're the only one who'd call this a shortcut.
Out of the way. We don't mess with kids.
Get Minova out here! I'm gonna show her who rules this street!
Keep Cap's name out of your mouth!
I can take out you slowpokes with one hand tied behind my back!
Big talk! Let's start by shutting you up to force Minova out!
A gang of menacing women lunges at the red-haired girl, but she spins, dodging their attacks with ease.
Minova ... That name rings a bell.
Huff, puff ... Can't even lay a hand on her.
What's that skateboard thing? Come down and fight like you mean it!
Hey, it's not my fault you're slow.
(Coughs and chokes) Can't ... breathe!==W== You dirty cheater!
"Dirty"? All's fair in a street fight.
That's custom chili-pepper smoke. Better wash up quick, or your eyes and throat will be screaming for days.
Fine, you win this round! You won't be so lucky next time!
Hah! Come back whenever you want! We'll just kick your butts again!
Alright everyone, you can resume business as usual.
Once the two gang members leave, people start gathering.
Thank the stars! My veggies were about to hit the compost heap.
Those thugs were posted up here since sunrise, scaring off every last customer.
Those kids seem pretty well-liked. Don't seem like bad guys at all.
We need to get back to the orphanage, fast. We have to track down clues about that bizarre loan.
Hey, you! Where'd you come from? Why are you skulking around?
Fresh meat. Are you with that other crew? Quick, tell Sis Vollara!
No, no, no! We're just regular Trekkers!==W== Not suspicious at all, I swear!
Sis Vollara, these guys are acting real shifty.
Just my luck! Why does the worst possible thing always happen?!
Hey there! We're the New Star Guild, just a group of Trekkers. By the way, your moves back there were sick!
Hmph! Gotta say though, the compliments are music to my ear.
Incredible, Noya can strike up a conversation with anyone...
So, what brings Trekkers to a place like this?
That's true ... only locals come this way.==W== Oh! I'm Neuvira, and this is my older sister...
I'm Noya.==W== This is Iris,==W== and that's Amber.==W== And this one ... Hmm, what's the best way to introduce you?
"==PLAYER_NAME==, a Trekker suffering from memory loss." That's how I usually introduce myself, but dealing with a gang member like this, a more memorable name might go over better. So...
B-Boss? Like, the ultimate villain from fairy tales who tries to destroy the world?
Huh! Now that's a name with some real guts.
Boss, huh? I like it! Sounds totally badass!
Taking on the world. I like that.
Uh-oh ... Now we sound like the villains.
Oh, right! We're looking for the Ash Orphanage.
The Ash Orphanage? It shut down years ago.
What business do you have with it?
Uh-oh. Is it me or is the vibe suddenly off?
We're surrounded. Get ready to fight.
W-Wait a minute! We grew up there! We just wanted to see the old place.
The place did close down two years ago. But how are you gonna prove who you are?
You're the fourth group this week to show up claiming you're from there.
What? Fourth? B-but we really are!
Hmph. Heard enough.==W== You look suspicious, so beat it!

strings.text: The fight sparks an alliance. Minova, the Ashwind leader, reveals that they only pose as a gang to protect themselves from Creta Trading.
Heh, same to you. Still, can't believe we lost a three-on-one fight.
This was a blast, though. I'll let you get one last word in before I flatten you.
The Ground Vipers? The Eta? Or the Crowns?
No, no! That's our guild's name.
Careful, Cap. This week alone, we had some guy claiming to be a Senator from the Grace Imperium.
So, that makes me wonder if you're really Trekkers at all.
We really used to be kids there.
Yo, Vollara, Neuvira. You recognize these faces?
Nope. No one their age on the orphanage records.
Cap, just say the word. I'll get all of 'em to come back.
Was that battle just a stall tactic?
It's a turf war! Anything goes, it ain't about honor.
Everyone we've run into in this city is so impulsive.
Can't we just talk this out?
Talk? With a crew I can't trust? Save your breath.
Wait, Sister Minova! I know them.
Whoa, it is Rainea! Long time no see! How've you been?
How do you know her? Are you for real...?
I really know them—before they left, they used to take us climbing on the Waterway.
See? Told ya we were telling the truth!
Uh… we’ll apologize properly. But before that, allow me to reintroduce myself.
I’m Minova, head of the Ashwind Clan. Pleased to meet you.
We were completely out of line.
Minova and Ashwind members kneel before and kowtow to us, their attitude entirely reversed.
No, please, there's no need for such formality.
No way! We gotta make this right!
Whoa ... Amber, check it out. They're all bowing to Iris ... Guess we should start calling her "Lady Iris" now, huh?
Shouldn't accepting your apology be enough to settle this?
Then please, ==PLAYER_NAME==, you handle it.==W== I'm ... really bad at this.
Me? Fine ... I suppose someone has to break the stalemate.
Understood. On behalf of my companions, your apology is accepted.
It was our fault for attacking you. So, as a token of our sincerity, I will personally guarantee your safety for as long as you're in Emor.
The orphanage is now a gang hideout ... Having her on our side could be useful.
What Noya and the others think?
Phew.==W== Thanks for being cool about this.
So, what caused this whole misunderstanding anyway?
"Senators from some companies," "children who grew up in the orphanage" ... We've had a parade of phonies showing up with all sorts of titles, sniffing around and asking questions.
I don't know what their angle is, but my priority is protecting the kids of the Ashwind Clan.
Ah, so you thought we were just another group of impostors.
Rainea, how many kids are left at the orphanage? Do you have any idea where Aunt Allie went?
Oh ... um, Aunt Allie ... she's missing.
Do you remember anything about when she disappeared?
I-I don't know. That night ... I snuck out to catch fireflies...
I was scared I'd get in trouble, so I slept under the bridge where you all used to take me. When I came back the next morning ... the orphanage was empty. Everyone was gone.
Later, thugs started showing up on this street and taking over the orphanage house.
But then Miss Minova showed up—she was still in her school uniform—and chased them all away. She started the Ashwind Clan to protect us.
And now I'm a member of the Ashwind Clan, too!
Look how proud she is ... The Ashwind Clan. So Minova's not a villain after all.
So all the kids here are...
Yep. A bunch of strays with nowhere else to go.
Why would she go to such lengths for a bunch of strangers?
Is this her idea of ... justice?
Um, sorry to ask, but ... Minova, you aren't by any chance that kid, are you? The one everyone's parents compared them to?
The genius who made it out of the Ash District. First kid from here to get a scholarship to the Platinum Academy in ten years. You were practically a legend.
You've done your homework ... Yeah, that's me.
You want to know why I came back here and started a clan instead of living it up in the Gold or Silver Districts, right?
You could've joined a major company...
Sounds pretty suspicious, I get it. From where you're standing, I'm just the squatter who took over your home.==W== You've got every right to be wary.
No ... that's not what I meant.
Miss Noya, Miss Iris, Miss Amber, now that you're not fighting with Miss Minova anymore. I'm gonna take a little nap now.
The clan kids look completely wiped out, like they pulled an all-nighter.
(Yawns) Cap, Neuvira and I are gonna grab some rest too.
Take care of yourself too, cap.
Yeah, you guys go ahead. I'll be fine.
Minova? What is going on here?
Come with me. We need a different spot for this conversation—I'll tell you everything.
Not a bad view, huh? I love coming up here to catch the breeze around this time.
Tell me about it. We practically lived up here when we were kids.
Amber would snooze in the corner, while I'd lean against the pillar reading.
And Noya would just sit on that railing over there, staring at the Monolith for hours.
The Monolith's always been special to me.
You guys are pretty tight, huh?
Always have been. Laughed together, cried together, fought like crazy ... and for the last two years, we've been traveling together.
Two years huh ... I was just a student at Platinum Academy back then.
Like Iris said, I was one of the lucky ones from the Ash District. My grades were good enough to get me noticed by the Platinum Academy, who gave me a full scholarship.
It's in the Gold District.==W== The school was overflowing with Artifacts you could use anytime you wanted.==W== Nothing like here, where a school's lucky to have one or two.
I studied intensely and worked my way up to become the first-ever Ash District kid to run the student council of Platinum Academy.
I thought that would be my ticket to the sky—flying out of Ash District and leaving my old life in the dust.
It was raining all day, so nobody wanted their shoes shined.
Like I give a damn about the rain! No customers? Then go steal something! Mug someone!
But Aunt Allie said we mustn't be bad.
She told us that once we resorted to wrongdoings, it'll become a habit.
Hey, you little runt trying to mock me in your sneaky way?
Besides, who cares what Allie said? Didn't she ditch this worthless orphanage and run off in the middle of the night?
This is our turf now, so you play by my rules.
Quit your damn crying! It's annoying! Maybe a beating will finally get it through your thick skull!
My fists flew before my brain caught up. I went straight for those two punks.
Nah, I got my butt kicked instead. Only good thing was that the kids managed to bolt.
When I got home, I looked in the mirror and saw a bruised-up kid staring back at me.
I was an orphan, just like them. Lived on the same streets, never knew where my next meal was coming from.
And if I ever scraped a little coin together, some thug would just rob me of it.
Well, well, if it ain't the little songbird who flew out of the Ash District.
What's the matter? Got so used to your platinum cage you forgot where you came from? Wouldn't wanna get those fancy clothes dirty, now would you?
He was right. I'd completely forgotten who I was.
I cared far too much about that piece of clothing I wore.
The first book I ever read came from Aunt Allie.
The orphanage couldn't take everyone, but its street was the safest one in the Ash District. You could sleep under a bridge there and your stuff would be safe.
Aunt Allie would lend me books from the orphanage. I didn't get a scholarship because I was smart. I got it because someone was watching my back.
Ah, so that explains why books on the shelf kept disappearing and reappearing. You were the one borrowing them.
Yeah, I was practically an orphanage kid myself. Too bad I didn't get to meet you guys back then.
It's not too late. Here, let's swap numbers.
I thought I'd made it out of the Ash District all on my own. Turns out, I just never noticed the people holding an umbrella over my head.
When one bird flies the coop, that's escaping. When the whole flock takes off? That's really soaring.
After Aunt Allie and the orphanage were gone, I figured it was my turn to hold the umbrella for the kids.
Fighting wasn't my thing, but I studied every martial arts book in Platinum Academy's library.
Gang life was foreign to me, but I watched every Monolith gang movie in Platinum Academy's collection.
So I picked up a bat, put on the outfit I made myself, pretended to be the toughest badass, and kicked down the door of the old orphanage the gangs were squatting in.
Next thing you know, the Ashwind Clan was a thing. And I ended up with a bunch of kids hanging around ... I used to be one of them.
Thank you ... for protecting a place that means so much to us.
Don't thank me. I was just...
Nothin' can stop the wind from blowin' through the Ash<r=Ashwind Clan> District</r>.
Sounds pretty badass, right? In reality, it's just a place where a bunch of us strays look out for each other.
Me, Vollara, Neuvira, and the other older kids ... we couldn't protect this street by ourselves, not if we play by the rules anyway.
We have to look scary and act overly aggressive just to barely keep the gangs at bay.
Truth is ... they're all good kids.
So ... does this mean we're friends?
It's simple! You want to protect the orphans in the Ash District, so do I. We're fighting for the same thing, and we've already fought side-by-side. That practically makes us battle buddies!
Haha! So we skipped right past "friends" and went straight to "battle buddies," huh?
I like the sound of that. Let's make it official, then.
Phew ...==W== turns out she's not scary at all.
Alright, enough about me. We need to talk about the kids.
As Trekkers, how do you deal with the side effects from climbing the Monoliths?
Yeah, all the kids in the clan are exhausted because they were forced to climb the Monoliths.
To be precise, they were forced to retrieve Artifacts on a regular basis.
Could it be the same for Rainea?
It wasn't just her. Nine times out of ten, any street kid in the Ash District had gone through the same thing before they joined us.
Even after they stop climbing, they're still ... out of it. Completely drained.
They forced literal kids to climb the Monoliths?! What kind of monster would do that?
Ugh ... Creta Trading ... Not a name I was hoping to hear again anytime soon.
Huh? You know about the Creta Trading too?
Iris explains how Creta Trading took Lucky Oasis==RT==using orphanage loans as an excuse.
So they make a habit of these shady practices?
After the orphanage disappeared, Feagin started rounding up orphans.
She'd spew all this garbage about how it's "only natural for children to pay their parents' debts." And you wanna know what they used as "proof"?
A worthless piece of paper. No name, no date, nothing.
A scrap of paper? How is that legally binding?
==PLAYER_NAME==, the Creta Trading is a company. Regular folks can't question them.
That's company privilege. They're blessed by the God of Grace, after all.
Just like what they did to us. I don't know if they're more greedy or just plain crooked...
Nothing good ever comes from putting power in the hands of people who don't deserve it.
Well, good thing you all showed up. Maybe something good can come out of this mess after all.
The scent of thread? What does she mean?
Now I get it.==W== The orphanage's debt, the Ashwind Clan's problems, the New Star Guild's predicament ... it's all connected. Which means...
You're right! Since the root of our problems is the corporation, we should team up to take them down!
The Creta Trading. A common enemy.
Heh. Guess this means we're more than just battle buddies now. You could say we're partners in crime.
"Partners in crime," huh ... Still, teaming up with the Ashwind Clan is a smart move. They know this area inside and out.
So, Creta Trading is forcing you to work off the debt by climbing the Monolith and making wishes for them?
The kids in the Ashwind Clan ... they're beyond exhausted. Just how hard has the Consortium been pushing them?
Wait ... don't tell me they were forced to make a wish today!
Relax. For the past few months, it's just been me, Vollara, and Neuvira making runs to the Monolith.
The other kids don't go anywhere near it. Once you're in the Ashwind Clan, I make sure nobody can push you around anymore.
If that's the case, why are Rainea and the others still in such bad shape?
I wish I knew ... Something's gotta be wrong with the way the wishes are being made.
We followed Feagin's instructions to the letter, but who knows if any of it is right. We're not Trekkers, so we're just fumbling in the dark here.
Sitting here brainstorming won't get us anywhere. What if—
Tomorrow, let's hit the Monolith with Minova and find out what Feagin is really up to.

param: The fight sparks an alliance. Minova, the Ashwind leader, reveals that they only pose as a gang to protect themselves from Creta Trading.
Heh, same to you. Still, can't believe we lost a three-on-one fight.
This was a blast, though. I'll let you get one last word in before I flatten you.
The Ground Vipers? The Eta? Or the Crowns?
No, no! That's our guild's name.
Careful, Cap. This week alone, we had some guy claiming to be a Senator from the Grace Imperium.
So, that makes me wonder if you're really Trekkers at all.
We really used to be kids there.
Yo, Vollara, Neuvira. You recognize these faces?
Nope. No one their age on the orphanage records.
Cap, just say the word. I'll get all of 'em to come back.
Was that battle just a stall tactic?
It's a turf war! Anything goes, it ain't about honor.
Everyone we've run into in this city is so impulsive.
Can't we just talk this out?
Talk? With a crew I can't trust? Save your breath.
Wait, Sister Minova! I know them.
Whoa, it is Rainea! Long time no see! How've you been?
How do you know her? Are you for real...?
I really know them—before they left, they used to take us climbing on the Waterway.
See? Told ya we were telling the truth!
Uh… we’ll apologize properly. But before that, allow me to reintroduce myself.
I’m Minova, head of the Ashwind Clan. Pleased to meet you.
We were completely out of line.
Minova and Ashwind members kneel before and kowtow to us, their attitude entirely reversed.
No, please, there's no need for such formality.
No way! We gotta make this right!
Whoa ... Amber, check it out. They're all bowing to Iris ... Guess we should start calling her "Lady Iris" now, huh?
Shouldn't accepting your apology be enough to settle this?
Then please, ==PLAYER_NAME==, you handle it.==W== I'm ... really bad at this.
Me? Fine ... I suppose someone has to break the stalemate.
Understood. On behalf of my companions, your apology is accepted.
It was our fault for attacking you. So, as a token of our sincerity, I will personally guarantee your safety for as long as you're in Emor.
The orphanage is now a gang hideout ... Having her on our side could be useful.
What Noya and the others think?
Phew.==W== Thanks for being cool about this.
So, what caused this whole misunderstanding anyway?
"Senators from some companies," "children who grew up in the orphanage" ... We've had a parade of phonies showing up with all sorts of titles, sniffing around and asking questions.
I don't know what their angle is, but my priority is protecting the kids of the Ashwind Clan.
Ah, so you thought we were just another group of impostors.
Rainea, how many kids are left at the orphanage? Do you have any idea where Aunt Allie went?
Oh ... um, Aunt Allie ... she's missing.
Do you remember anything about when she disappeared?
I-I don't know. That night ... I snuck out to catch fireflies...
I was scared I'd get in trouble, so I slept under the bridge where you all used to take me. When I came back the next morning ... the orphanage was empty. Everyone was gone.
Later, thugs started showing up on this street and taking over the orphanage house.
But then Miss Minova showed up—she was still in her school uniform—and chased them all away. She started the Ashwind Clan to protect us.
And now I'm a member of the Ashwind Clan, too!
Look how proud she is ... The Ashwind Clan. So Minova's not a villain after all.
So all the kids here are...
Yep. A bunch of strays with nowhere else to go.
Why would she go to such lengths for a bunch of strangers?
Is this her idea of ... justice?
Um, sorry to ask, but ... Minova, you aren't by any chance that kid, are you? The one everyone's parents compared them to?
The genius who made it out of the Ash District. First kid from here to get a scholarship to the Platinum Academy in ten years. You were practically a legend.
You've done your homework ... Yeah, that's me.
You want to know why I came back here and started a clan instead of living it up in the Gold or Silver Districts, right?
You could've joined a major company...
Sounds pretty suspicious, I get it. From where you're standing, I'm just the squatter who took over your home.==W== You've got every right to be wary.
No ... that's not what I meant.
Miss Noya, Miss Iris, Miss Amber, now that you're not fighting with Miss Minova anymore. I'm gonna take a little nap now.
The clan kids look completely wiped out, like they pulled an all-nighter.
(Yawns) Cap, Neuvira and I are gonna grab some rest too.
Take care of yourself too, cap.
Yeah, you guys go ahead. I'll be fine.
Minova? What is going on here?
Come with me. We need a different spot for this conversation—I'll tell you everything.
Not a bad view, huh? I love coming up here to catch the breeze around this time.
Tell me about it. We practically lived up here when we were kids.
Amber would snooze in the corner, while I'd lean against the pillar reading.
And Noya would just sit on that railing over there, staring at the Monolith for hours.
The Monolith's always been special to me.
You guys are pretty tight, huh?
Always have been. Laughed together, cried together, fought like crazy ... and for the last two years, we've been traveling together.
Two years huh ... I was just a student at Platinum Academy back then.
Like Iris said, I was one of the lucky ones from the Ash District. My grades were good enough to get me noticed by the Platinum Academy, who gave me a full scholarship.
It's in the Gold District.==W== The school was overflowing with Artifacts you could use anytime you wanted.==W== Nothing like here, where a school's lucky to have one or two.
I studied intensely and worked my way up to become the first-ever Ash District kid to run the student council of Platinum Academy.
I thought that would be my ticket to the sky—flying out of Ash District and leaving my old life in the dust.
It was raining all day, so nobody wanted their shoes shined.
Like I give a damn about the rain! No customers? Then go steal something! Mug someone!
But Aunt Allie said we mustn't be bad.
She told us that once we resorted to wrongdoings, it'll become a habit.
Hey, you little runt trying to mock me in your sneaky way?
Besides, who cares what Allie said? Didn't she ditch this worthless orphanage and run off in the middle of the night?
This is our turf now, so you play by my rules.
Quit your damn crying! It's annoying! Maybe a beating will finally get it through your thick skull!
My fists flew before my brain caught up. I went straight for those two punks.
Nah, I got my butt kicked instead. Only good thing was that the kids managed to bolt.
When I got home, I looked in the mirror and saw a bruised-up kid staring back at me.
I was an orphan, just like them. Lived on the same streets, never knew where my next meal was coming from.
And if I ever scraped a little coin together, some thug would just rob me of it.
Well, well, if it ain't the little songbird who flew out of the Ash District.
What's the matter? Got so used to your platinum cage you forgot where you came from? Wouldn't wanna get those fancy clothes dirty, now would you?
He was right. I'd completely forgotten who I was.
I cared far too much about that piece of clothing I wore.
The first book I ever read came from Aunt Allie.
The orphanage couldn't take everyone, but its street was the safest one in the Ash District. You could sleep under a bridge there and your stuff would be safe.
Aunt Allie would lend me books from the orphanage. I didn't get a scholarship because I was smart. I got it because someone was watching my back.
Ah, so that explains why books on the shelf kept disappearing and reappearing. You were the one borrowing them.
Yeah, I was practically an orphanage kid myself. Too bad I didn't get to meet you guys back then.
It's not too late. Here, let's swap numbers.
I thought I'd made it out of the Ash District all on my own. Turns out, I just never noticed the people holding an umbrella over my head.
When one bird flies the coop, that's escaping. When the whole flock takes off? That's really soaring.
After Aunt Allie and the orphanage were gone, I figured it was my turn to hold the umbrella for the kids.
Fighting wasn't my thing, but I studied every martial arts book in Platinum Academy's library.
Gang life was foreign to me, but I watched every Monolith gang movie in Platinum Academy's collection.
So I picked up a bat, put on the outfit I made myself, pretended to be the toughest badass, and kicked down the door of the old orphanage the gangs were squatting in.
Next thing you know, the Ashwind Clan was a thing. And I ended up with a bunch of kids hanging around ... I used to be one of them.
Thank you ... for protecting a place that means so much to us.
Don't thank me. I was just...
Nothin' can stop the wind from blowin' through the Ash<r=Ashwind Clan> District</r>.
Sounds pretty badass, right? In reality, it's just a place where a bunch of us strays look out for each other.
Me, Vollara, Neuvira, and the other older kids ... we couldn't protect this street by ourselves, not if we play by the rules anyway.
We have to look scary and act overly aggressive just to barely keep the gangs at bay.
Truth is ... they're all good kids.
So ... does this mean we're friends?
It's simple! You want to protect the orphans in the Ash District, so do I. We're fighting for the same thing, and we've already fought side-by-side. That practically makes us battle buddies!
Haha! So we skipped right past "friends" and went straight to "battle buddies," huh?
I like the sound of that. Let's make it official, then.
Phew ...==W== turns out she's not scary at all.
Alright, enough about me. We need to talk about the kids.
As Trekkers, how do you deal with the side effects from climbing the Monoliths?
Yeah, all the kids in the clan are exhausted because they were forced to climb the Monoliths.
To be precise, they were forced to retrieve Artifacts on a regular basis.
Could it be the same for Rainea?
It wasn't just her. Nine times out of ten, any street kid in the Ash District had gone through the same thing before they joined us.
Even after they stop climbing, they're still ... out of it. Completely drained.
They forced literal kids to climb the Monoliths?! What kind of monster would do that?
Ugh ... Creta Trading ... Not a name I was hoping to hear again anytime soon.
Huh? You know about the Creta Trading too?
Iris explains how Creta Trading took Lucky Oasis==RT==using orphanage loans as an excuse.
So they make a habit of these shady practices?
After the orphanage disappeared, Feagin started rounding up orphans.
She'd spew all this garbage about how it's "only natural for children to pay their parents' debts." And you wanna know what they used as "proof"?
A worthless piece of paper. No name, no date, nothing.
A scrap of paper? How is that legally binding?
==PLAYER_NAME==, the Creta Trading is a company. Regular folks can't question them.
That's company privilege. They're blessed by the God of Grace, after all.
Just like what they did to us. I don't know if they're more greedy or just plain crooked...
Nothing good ever comes from putting power in the hands of people who don't deserve it.
Well, good thing you all showed up. Maybe something good can come out of this mess after all.
The scent of thread? What does she mean?
Now I get it.==W== The orphanage's debt, the Ashwind Clan's problems, the New Star Guild's predicament ... it's all connected. Which means...
You're right! Since the root of our problems is the corporation, we should team up to take them down!
The Creta Trading. A common enemy.
Heh. Guess this means we're more than just battle buddies now. You could say we're partners in crime.
"Partners in crime," huh ... Still, teaming up with the Ashwind Clan is a smart move. They know this area inside and out.
So, Creta Trading is forcing you to work off the debt by climbing the Monolith and making wishes for them?
The kids in the Ashwind Clan ... they're beyond exhausted. Just how hard has the Consortium been pushing them?
Wait ... don't tell me they were forced to make a wish today!
Relax. For the past few months, it's just been me, Vollara, and Neuvira making runs to the Monolith.
The other kids don't go anywhere near it. Once you're in the Ashwind Clan, I make sure nobody can push you around anymore.
If that's the case, why are Rainea and the others still in such bad shape?
I wish I knew ... Something's gotta be wrong with the way the wishes are being made.
We followed Feagin's instructions to the letter, but who knows if any of it is right. We're not Trekkers, so we're just fumbling in the dark here.
Sitting here brainstorming won't get us anywhere. What if—
Tomorrow, let's hit the Monolith with Minova and find out what Feagin is really up to.

strings.text: The New Star Guild climbs a Monolith for Creta Trading to free exhausted children drained from their climbs. You discover the new method Feagin is using to make wishes.
The next morning, we visit Feagin and offer to retrieve the Artifact from the Monolith for her.
Unexpectedly, Feagin leads us into the Monolith==RT==without giving us a hard time.==RT==However...
The city Monoliths are a breeze to climb. Found the wishing box in no time.
All the Stellaroids are frozen, and there are no mechanisms or traps anywhere. Safe as can be.
Are outer Monoliths not like this?
Yeah, the Monoliths we usually climb are packed with Stellaroids. Those in this place? Feels like browsing a gift shop.
So only companies get access to places like this ... Is this the so-called blessing bestowed upon companies by the God of Grace?
Heh heh ... I only let you in because you seemed so eager to work off your debt. I expect a little gratitude.
She can't say anything nice, can she?
Would you specify your Artifact requirements? We'll do everything we can to wish for precisely what you need.
If you could provide us with the specifications, we'll do our best to wish for something that meets your needs.
Specifications? Hmph. The Chalk Consortium has no need for such crude methods.
You're right. The more specific the image, the higher the chance of getting the Artifact you want.
But everyone's imagination is different, isn't it? Seems inefficient.
Just take this card, place your hand on a wishing box, and recite the prayer. See? Simple, right?
So I don't need to think of anything specific?
Not really. Just follow my instructions.
Though doubtful, Iris does as she's told.
O mighty God of Grace, please hear our prayer...
As soon as she finishes, the box opens. Inside is an Artifact for communication.
Yep, that's exactly the communication Artifact I was after.
You good, Iris? You seem a little off.
I'm ... fine. Just ... a little drowsy.
I wonder if Noya and Amber noticed? Iris looks just as drained as Rainea did.
But ... we have zero clue about what Artifact we're wishing for ... How does that even work?
Trade secret. Your job is just to donate memories—I'll handle the Artifact selection.
You're fast climbers, not like those other kids who just break down crying. It'd be a shame to let your talents go to waste.
Ever consider working for Creta Trading?
Look, I get it. You guys probably hate me.
You're climbing the Monolith in place of those Ashwind Clan kids today, instead for cash.
At least you're self-aware. Anyone who takes Loxy away is unforgivable in my book.
What did you expect me to do? I can't just write off debts, can I?
I'm the one making a huge concession here. You said you wanted to work, and I readily agreed, didn't I?
A "concession"? How about you start by giving Loxy—the Lucky Oasis—back to us?
Technically, "giving it back" isn't the right term ... How about this: sign an employment contract with me, and I'll let you use the Lucky Oasis, free of charge.
And once you're under contract, I'll naturally pay you a salary. 300 thousand Dorra a month per person. What do you say?
For the five of you, that's 1.5 million Dorra a month. Even after your paying off your debt, you'll still have more than enough left, right?
Our debt isn't Minova's responsibility. For the four of us, that's 1.2 million a month. Minus the 830 thousand for the debt ... we'd have over 300 thousand left.
Even cheap bread costs 10 thousand Dorra a day here. We'd be working our tails off for crumbs.
But it's a chance to get our vehicle back. Feagin is a shrewd negotiator. That CEO title isn't just for show after all.
One more thing, with expert climbers like yourselves, I'd be willing to wipe all those parental debts out for the orphanage kids.
With you climbing the Monoliths, I'll have no more need for them.
Wipe it out? So you're saying you'll leave those kids alone from now on?
Look, I didn't force those kids up the Monoliths for kicks. I just wanted them to get a taste of what real work feels like.
Using the kids as leverage ... This is a trap we have no choice but to walk into.
Uh ... Amber? Iris? What do you think?
Weighing our options, we have no reason to refuse. Iris and Amber nod, and we sign an employment contract with Feagin.
Excellent. Now that you're officially employees, please continue with your work.
We've made our wish for the Artifact already.
Yes, you did. But I never said you were only wishing for one.
Keep climbing. At least one wish per person!
I'm ... so exhausted ... I can barely move my legs ... What was the magic formula for ice arrows again ... It's gone.
How many wishes did we actually make today?
T-Ten ... That shouldn't even be possible...
Yeah ... but now I get it. This must be why Rainea and the kids are still in such bad shape. They were forced to do this over and over again.
You're right ... Having your memories stripped away multiple times in one day must put an incredible strain on you.
The physical toll is bad enough, but enduring this repeatedly ... it could completely erode your spirit.
In the worst cases, you lose all your memories and your soul suffers severe damage. For someone to recover from that, like you did, ==PLAYER_NAME==, is a one-in-a-million miracle.
Most people just become empty shells, living on mechanically.
Tch ... You can't be serious. I'm going for a walk.
Minova tries to hide her emotions as she heads for the door.
Ah! I was just ... I was just speculating! It's not like that's guaranteed to happen!
Sorry, it's my fault for making such a claim. I'll go check on her.
I'll go see how Rainea's doing.
Noya and Iris also leave, and the room falls silent.
Amber seems to be holding up okay.
Should I ask her about it? But ... Amber doesn't seem to enjoy talking.
Amber holds her phone against mine, back to back. A prompt appears on my phone screen.
（此处有新功能 图标安装，打开，弹出提示——）
Amber tilts her head in confusion and presses her phone against mine once more.
Don't tell me ... you forgot how to use your phone?
Maybe this went a little too far.
I guess ... I have no other choice.
Amber's fingers wrap around my index finger, forcing it to move across the screen.
S-Sorry! I'm sorry! I took the joke too far!
Phew, finally added you as a friend.
You had a question for me before, didn't you?
What was it? I'll answer anything I know!
You made wishes today too, right? How are you holding up?
I'm just a liiitle low on energy.
But I'm fine! Wanna explore the Waterway Bridge together?
Were you ever in Emor before you lost your memory, ==PLAYER_NAME==?
Maybe you did, and even took photos on the Waterway.
She doesn't look "low on energy" at all.
Come to think of it, Amber's been glued to her phone since we left the Monolith.
You really love that phone, don't you, Amber?
Yeah, phones are super fun! I like talking through my phone—it's faster, plus I can keep track of conversations better.
I also love taking photos with it, anytime, anywhere!
When I'm feeling down, my phone always cheers me up.
I wish I could get a phone with a big screen like yours, ==PLAYER_NAME==!
Maybe the kids have taken a harder hit because...
Leave it to someone with more experience
I should check with Minova and Iris. If everyone's experiencing this, it might confirm my suspicions.
If professional Trekkers can't figure this out, what chance do I have with my amnesia? Probably just my thoughts running wild. I should stay out of it.
Can't think straight anymore. I was right on the verge of figuring it out.
Can't think on an empty stomach.

strings.text: Iris and Minova later recover by discussing magic. It gives you an idea: creating more fun memories could heal the children.
The power of a water spell equals the magic energy you channel in, plus or minus whatever's used or gained when it changes state.
Right. The First Law of Water Magic. I remember now.
O mighty God of Grace, I follow the axioms you have granted, beseeching the destined result written in your laws—
Where did Iris and Minova go...?
Huh? I think I heard something ... Let me go check it out.
That's a textbook ice arrow, with minimal magic consumption.
Phew ... Thank you.==W== I never imagined the legendary Minova would be giving me magic lessons.
Don't sweat it. What's the point of hitting the books if you never use what you learn?
Not sure what went down between them, but they seem to be on good terms now.
There's something I'd like to ask you two.
What do you usually do after climbing and wishing?
...You mean right after we get back from a Monolith?
I study ...==W== I don't have a gift for magic, so I have to memorize all the formulas just to be able to cast anything.
I have to work twice as hard so I don't hold everyone back.
Same here, pretty much. I always drag myself to class the next day.
Class? I figured you'd be the type to skip. You know, play the delinquent.
I'm not—what makes you call me a delinquent? Uh...
...Anyway, you need to be smart to land a good job in companies these days.
That's why I study hard. So I can teach the others in the Ashwind Clan what I learn.
Thinking about your crew's future ... That's admirable.
Wh-What?! It's not that deep! And stop calling me admirable...
It's just a guess, but I have a feeling this hypothesis is right.
Please rest your hand here for about five minutes.
While you wait, try thinking of something that makes you happy, or a really important moment in your life.
I can't believe that pointless conversation actually turned into a lead.
I was wondering something else. What do Vollara, Neuvira, and the children do after their climbs?
How should I know? That's their business.
But ... they're probably exhausted. I doubt they do anything at all.
That's the issue right there! These kids need more mental homework.
Are you serious? What are you talking about, ==PLAYER_NAME==? I'm completely lost.
Trekkers climb Monoliths, make wishes with the wishing boxes, and receive powerful Artifacts. ==W==But in return, a part of their memory is taken by the Monolith.
I got that right, didn't I?
Yes. Making multiple wishes in a single day is dangerous because memory loss puts a huge strain on your mind and body.
Mm ... even if you push yourself, twice is the absolute limit. It's standard Trekker practice to rest properly afterward, to give your mind and body time to recover.
Rest when you're tired. That's obvious.==W== But ... what does "rest" actually mean to all of you?
A healthy diet and proper sleep.
Yeah, that'll help your body recover, but it does nothing for mental exhaustion.
When you rescued me, you gave me the best food and the most comfortable bed. But my head was in a fog for days.
Back then, I thought it was because I'd climbed a Monolith right after waking up, or maybe because of that weird dream...
But that wasn't it. The real reason, I suspect, is that my mind never had a chance to recover from the memory loss.
Now that you mention it ... you were pale when you woke up from that dream. Just like the kids.
Exactly. But later, after I started making new memories with you all, I slowly started to feel better.
So, here's my hypothesis: to heal a wounded mind...
...you have to create new memories to replace what was lost.

The kids have stopped climbing, but the important memories they lost are still gone. Holed up in their rooms all day, they're not making any new, interesting memories either, which is why they're in a daze.
If we can help them create new, powerful memories, they might not get the old ones back, but at least ... they could start living their lives again.

Hmm, your theory has merit, ==PLAYER_NAME==. Children don't have that many important memories to begin with, so losing a bunch at once would definitely take its toll. It's like trying to solve a problem after forgetting all the key formulas.
The logic seems to hold up ... but if it's that simple, how come no one's thought of it before?
Most Trekkers don't push themselves that hard.==W== And aside from the Creta Trading, no one else would force children to climb and make wishes.
True. Alright, ==PLAYER_NAME==, your suggestion is worth a shot. So we just need to help them make new memories, right?
I told you. The whole reason I go to school is so I can teach everyone else. There's only one thing to do.
Yea, why? Iris, you can join the class too.==W== No, wait, your fundamentals are already solid.
How about you teach with me?
Me...? I-I don't think I can.
Noya and Amber trust you completely, and you work so hard. I think you'd be great.
Besides, since it's your first time, it might be an even more memorable experience for the kids.
Just ... don't laugh if I'm terrible at it.
No way. I'd never laugh at someone for trying their best.
That's it! Class is in session tomorrow!

Right. The First Law of Water Magic. I remember now.
O mighty God of Grace, I follow the axioms you have granted, beseeching the destined result written in your laws—
Where did Iris and Minova go...?
Huh? I think I heard something ... Let me go check it out.
That's a textbook ice arrow, with minimal magic consumption.
Phew ... Thank you.==W== I never imagined the legendary Minova would be giving me magic lessons.
