Just think!==W== No writing out long requests, no reciting complicated prayers. You just hold a card, offer a memory, and make a wish.==W== Isn't that incredible?
Memories are also a form of information. Vita will replicate memories the Monolith demands during your wish-making, then hand over those copies while you keep your originals.
Can ...==W== it really work like that?
Tricking the Monolith ...==W== no, technically we're not tricking it. The Monolith does get the memories, even if they're copies. Info is info, and a copy works just as well as the real thing.
Huh...? Is that really what happened? So this is ...==W== the power of the Tyrant Development System, or rather, the power of this phone...
With this kind of power, I really could rule the world like the legendary Tyrant.==W== That explains why this phone is called the "Throne," huh?
Indeed. To be precise, these are your powers as the Tyrant. The "Throne," the Development System, and Vita—we all serve you. Please use us as you see fit.
I don't get the mechanics, but it sounds pretty amazing! Are you saying we're immune to amnesia?
That's correct in simple terms. Moreover, anyone who has made a soul trade with you will be considered part of the Tyrant Accord and can access this benefit.
Finally ...==W== no need to log everything on the phone.
Yes, it's great for us, but ...==W== if word leaks about this power, every Trekker and company across Nova will be after our seal!
Guys, this has to stay under wraps. Not a word to anyone, understood?

Lady Iris is quite meticulous, but Vita too would recommend the same. Until you have established an army of true loyalists, Tyrant, everything about the "Throne" and the system must be kept absolutely confidential.
You're right about this. These secrets stay between just us.
Don't worry. Already working on wiping it from my memory.
By the way, Vita, if each chess piece has its own unique power—
That king piece we got with the phone...
Why am I in the White Room all of a sudden...==W== Did we crash the ride? Is everyone okay?!
Please don't be alarmed, Tyrant. This isn't the actual White Room—it's a simulated space Vita created inside your head with the king chess piece's ability.
As the king piece holds abilities of the utmost significance, Vita would strongly advise that our following discussion remain private—for your ears only.
A virtual space created by the king piece? Are you saying ...==W== entering the White Room is the king piece's power?
Allow me to clarify. Its creation ability extends beyond virtual spaces. The original "White Room" itself was constructed by the king piece.
So that place ... was made by the king piece as well?
That's right. It's a power known as "Player"—the king piece on the board represents the "Player," and as such, one can occasionally "undo a move."
Since you've already been to the White Room, you must be aware of its unique nature.==W== That place is ...<size=55> the convergence of time and space in the Monolith.
If you happen to lose your life unexpectedly, you'll return there for a second chance. The two Monolith divine messengers ...==W== or shall I say, employees, will be there to assist you.
So I can't tell anyone else about this ...==W== can I?
I'm afraid not. The ability of this room cannot be manipulated at will. Choosing to forfeit your life will not initiate its function.
Moreover, if any third party besides you and Vita learns of this, the room will cease to function. Though even this safeguard isn't entirely foolproof.

This is precisely why Vita is communicating this to you within the realm of your mind. Plus, Vita has implanted a subtle mental barrier in your consciousness to prevent you from mentioning this to anyone else.
For your protection, please handle everything regarding the White Room with utmost discretion. Vita trusts you will exercise good judgment.
You're very considerate. Thank you.==W== Or maybe you just doesn't trust me enough? ...==W== Just kidding.
Looks like the White Room is just a fallback option. What you're really saying is ...==W== I shouldn't make a habit of depending on it.
All of Vita's actions serve one purpose—to aid you in growing into a mighty Tyrant.
这里往下是过去没有触发过BE的分支
Huh? What is this ... place?==W== Hello—Noya? Iris? Amber?
Tyrant, this is a simulated White Room that Vita has created in your mind. We're having this conversation via your thought right now.
Vita?! ... White Room? What's that supposed to be?
It appears you've successfully evaded all threats. Your wisdom never ceases to amaze Vita.
Please cut to the chase. Weren't we having a regular conversation? Why are you making it so complicated all of a sudden?
Let Vita explain. You inquired about the power of the king's piece. ==W==Due to its significance, this must remain confidential, even from your subordinates.
The seal carries a power known as "Player." The king piece on the board represents the "Player," and as such, you occasionally have the right to "undo a move."
Undo a move? You mean ...==W== I can start over?
Correct. However, it only works for accidental deaths. Choosing to forfeit your life will not initiate this function.
Unlike in my simulated space, should you meet an unfortunate end and enter the White Room, two divine messengers of the Monolith ...==W== or employees will be here to guide you. They look like this—
Although it's possible to start over, hmm ...==W== I'd prefer staying alive. Let's keep this as a backup plan.
I concur, Tyrant. Prudence serves us well.
Moreover, if any third party besides you and Vita learns of this, the room will cease to function. Please be sure to note this.
I see. This mental communication must be to keep everything under wraps.

This is precisely why Vita is communicating this to you within the realm of your mind. Plus, Vita has implanted a subtle mental barrier in your consciousness to prevent you from mentioning this to anyone else.
For your protection, please handle everything regarding the White Room with utmost discretion. Vita trusts you will exercise good judgment.
Back ...==W== from where? You seemed lost in thought—you good?
Was that entire conversation just a few seconds in real time? If I can't tell anyone about the White Room...
My bad, I was just spacing out.
These chess pieces sure are something else.
How should I explain it to them?
After all, it's a precious ability. If sharing it means losing it, I should keep quiet about it.
So we can make wishes without losing our memory now. I'm not fully convinced...==W== But if it really works, that's quite a game-changer.
Coming back to life after dying...==W== It's so unrealistic...
They'd just worry if they knew everything, plus I literally "cannot" tell them. Might as well put it out of my mind.
Making wishes without losing memories ...==W== sounds almost too good to be true...
Assuming it works, we can be more at ease when making wishes from now on.
==PLAYER_NAME==, same for you—no more memory wipes! Oh, oh, why don't we wish for some super-rare Artifacts? Just to test it out, ya know!
I get where you're coming from ...==W== but we should be cautious. Maybe start out with smaller wishes?
"Implanting a subtle mental barrier in the consciousness"...==W== Is such a thing even possible? What if I try to say "White Room" out loud?
I-It won't come out. Then how about I write it down?
Ugh, my mind's gone blank... How to spell the word again...?
Tyrant, prudence serves you well. Testing it yourself is better than blindly trusting Vita.
What are you talking about? What's with the "whi"?
Ahem, "while," I mean, while it's still daylight, we should work on our plans.
Nearly blew it there. Guess there's seriously no way to mention the "White Room" to others...
So, we're heading to Philae next, aren't we?
Right. The trip should take roughly a week, even on the Lucky Oasis.
Fingers crossed we uncover something. I'm really concerned about Aunt Allie and the kids.
No sweat! Little Bastelina even hooked us up with an information broker.
It's actually information.==W== There's an info broker in Philae named Serena. She might know something about what you're after.
Think she'd have info on the orphanage? Or the Boss Accord?
Possibly. If Serena doesn't know, it's unlikely anyone does.==W== She might even have intel on that Nocturn Eterna officer you encountered.
Oh, oh,==W== and get this—the broker Serena has this quirk of playing mind games.
So she might challenge you to play some games ...==W== hehehe. Best of luck when that happens.
What kind of games are we talking about?
Heehee, I'm not sure. Could be anything, but—
That's the only hint I can give you.
Bastelina seems pretty sure about this. Finding Serena should give us the leads we need on the orphanage.
Yeah, let's climb some Monoliths during our trip. We need to raise more funds.
==PLAYER_NAME==, feel free to chat with me anytime on the road.
Hehe, I'll get going and take the wheel, Tyrant. Give me a shout if you need anything!
You don't have to use that title...
Why not? It's pretty awesome, right? Don't you all agree?
Well, using "Boss" seems more appropriate for official matters, considering our positions as employees of "Boss Accord."
I'll just use the name saved in your contacts.
Under the azure sky, the small Lucky Oasis cruises across the endless grasslands.==RT==Vita falls silent, retreating to the depths of the phone until I would summon her again.
The wheels of fate began to turn—slowly, but irreversibly.
Still need five more souls for the first mission.
Should I really continue to collect ...==W== even more souls?
That fifth soul in the phone ...==W== who did it belong to?

strings.text: After reaching Philae, you learn about the Big Three. It is said that the United Harvest has posted an enormous bounty for them, and one of them was already taken down by a hunting squad a week before.
Ugh, my heart nearly leaped out of my chest.
I've got good news and bad news. Which do you wanna hear first?
Good news. It's always better to wake up to good news than bad.
The good news is, we've made it to Philae!
Outside, the usually empty forest path is snarled with "traffic."
The Lucky Oasis is boxed in by monster-drawn wagons and bizarre Artifact vehicles.
In the distance, a seemingly endless sprawl of houses crests the horizon.
Yep. Come on, take a look.
Outside, the once-deserted forest path is now swarming with Trekkers on foot, inching past your gridlocked vehicle.
Yup, that's the good news. We've reached Philae.
Ugh, Neither. My morning sleep is sacred.
Outside the window, a monster with two trunks deftly plucks a piece of fruit from Amber's hand.
Huh? Nah, Amber's just making friends with the monster pulling the cart next to us. This is Philae. And we're stuck.
And there's your good news and bad news: Philae is right there, but we're not going anywhere.
So this is Philae? It's even busier than I imagined.
No, Philae is still a ways off. This is just the Trekker camp outside the city.
All these people in such a huge camp are Trekkers?
Trekkers usually set up camps near hot spots. Makes things easier.
Over time, they turn into these huge hubs for finding commissions, trading Artifacts, and forming guilds.
But since there's no Monolith nearby, I'm not sure why this place is so crowded.
I see. So this is the Trekkers' lifestyle.
By the way, what exactly is a "hot spot"?
Different Monoliths drop different kinds of Artifacts.
The ones with the best loot draw the biggest crowds. We call 'em "hot spots."
So the opposite would be "cold spots," right?
Why's Iris suddenly looking so serious?
Something's not right. This camp is huge, and the nearest Monolith is half a day away, yet more people keep pouring in.
It has to be...==W== There's a commission here with an insane payout!
We can't miss out on this!==RT====PLAYER_NAME==, Amber—our money problems are over!
Hey, you guys wondering why it's so packed?==W== I can fill you in!
Everyone's here for the Big Three!
The Big Three? Is that some kind of ... ==B==monster commission?
Oh, never heard of them?==W== You must be new in town.
...==W== A few months back,==W== three super nasty monsters nested in the forest near the Monolith,==W== blocking the path.
Nobody in Philae can get to the Monolith for Artifacts, and without Artifacts, you can't make a living, right?
So a big local corp—United Harvest—stepped up.
They posted a monster bounty. Any Trekker who can neutralize the beasts gets to split a ridiculous pile of Dorra.
That's why this place blew up.
Yeah, y'know, neutralize. Just get 'em out of the way. Beat 'em, capture 'em, whatever works. Each one's worth 500 million Dorra.
You bet! Way out of a rookie's league like me, though.
I heard a hunting squad with over a hundred Trekkers tried ...==W== and failed. Miserably.
I'll just stick to the small fry in the forest. You still get paid for clearing those out.
Thank you for telling us. We didn't catch your name.
I'm Eleanor! Just a rookie Trekker, still learning the ropes!
I guess I got a little carried away. It's just so exciting to finally share some intel with seasoned pros like you!
What's happening? Why is everyone suddenly looking over there?
Oh! I think that's the Trekkers who took down one of the Big Three! They're back from a scouting run.
What?! Someone actually beat one of them?!
You betcha! Blade of Jade was captured last month by the squad she led.
Ohh! Lady Nazuka! Over here! Please, just look this way!
It's still hard to believe though... A quiet girl like her managed to capture Blade of Jade...
Huh? What are you, a hater? Are you saying she didn't take down Blade of Jade herself?
Whoa, hey, stop putting words in my mouth! And stop glaring at me like that!
That thing was seriously tough. I was helping the new squad, and I couldn't even stand on my feet when it flapped its wings.
Heh! See? That's why Lady Nazuka's the best!
Even that witch from Scarlet Sights Media showed up to cover it. The whole Continent is gonna know her name soon!
I hope I can be famous like her someday...
Well, see ya! I'm off to train!
Eleanor vanishes into the crowd, full of energy. As the expedition departs, the onlookers start to drift away.
Huff ... huff ... Finally made it through.
Can't believe it took longer to drive Loxy through that mess than for you to walk.
So, what was all the commotion about?
Some amazing Trekker named Nazuka. Apparently, she led a team that took down a monster with a 500 million Dorra bounty.
Five hundred mil, huh?==W== Alright, let's get going.
Sure, it's a lot of cash. Enough to keep Loxy in parts for a lifetime.
But I'm more interested in Star Pluck. Monster hunting isn't really my thing.
Yep! It's said that if you defeat the final, hidden boss Stellaroid in a Monolith, you'll find the Wishing Star it guards ... and it can grant any wish!
That's just an urban legend, though.
So what? It's the romance of the adventure that counts!
Anyway, let's hurry and find that info broker Bastelina told us about. I already got directions to the Trekkers' House.
Um ... Noya? Are you positive this is the right way?
Totally! Don't worry, I got perfect directions back at camp.
How am I supposed to not worry when the forest is closing in on us?!
Amber, can you see anything from up there?
Sitting atop the vehicle, the girl's keen eyes seem to catch a flicker of movement.
Thought I did... It's gone now.
(Phew ... that was close. I was certain I had masked my presence completely.)
(The New Star Guild...==B== They're not to be underestimated.)
(Hmph. But the likes of you can't possibly stand in the way of Nocturn Eterna.)
(As the fixer of Nocturn Eterna, I will clear away any obstacles in the path.)
(Especially you, Boss. I will definitely find a chance to kidnap you...!)

strings.text: The Hidden Lord in the Forest
Following the clues, you arrive at Serena's location. Here, you meet a girl who calls herself the "Lord of the Prize Claw". She is engaged in an intense claw machine competition with Amber.
Wait ... this is it? This shack?
Hey, the greatest Trekkers always live in places like this.
Like in those Stella Dramas, you know? The little green swordmaster hiding out in a spooky cave.
But Bastelina said ...==B== the info broker was staying at the Trekkers' House.
Trekkers' Houses are supposed to be outposts for the Trekker Association, places to help Trekkers and hand out commissions.
What happened here?==RT==This path is totally overgrown. No one's used it in forever.
Quit overthinking it! Only one way to find out—let's go!
You dummy! You'll give them a heart attack.
Ahem... Pardon the intrusion. We're the New Star Guild...==W== It's empty?
Hm, the inside's actually pretty clean. It looks like someone lives here after all.
Shhh! This is the crucial moment...
In a dim corner of the lobby stand several prize claw machines. The girl who spoke is hunched over one of them.
She grips the joystick, her focus absolute as the gleaming silver claw descends toward its prize.
The claw seizes a plushie of a black-and-white penguin named Sherlock—a common sight in the Monoliths.
Could she be...?==B== No, doesn't seem likely.
Excuse me ... are you a swordmaster?
Noya, reality is not a Stella Drama.
A-Anyway, we're the New Star Guild. Terribly sorry to barge in like this.
We're looking for an information broker named Serena.
Yeah, well, bad news: she's not here. She's not one for public appearances.
But lucky for you, I know how you can find her.
Oh, thank goodness! Could you take us to her, please? About the price...
Hmm, okay. But first, you have to play with me... Er, I mean, pass my trial! Can't just help any random crew that wanders in, you know.
Ooh, I get it! It's just like in the stories! To meet the legendary hermit, you have to defeat their loyal guardian first!
S-Sorry! Apologies for Noya...==B====RT==So, about this trial...
This, of course! A prize claw duel! You each control a claw, and whoever snags the most plushies before time's up wins.
Sounds like a real challenge, huh?
She just wants someone to play with, doesn't she?
Whoa, I've never seen Amber get this excited about anything.
Knew you couldn't resist! See? Your friend is already raring to go♪
Hmph. Oh, I get it now! You weren't looking for Serena at all. You came for ME!
You must've heard stories about the Hidden Lord of the Prize Claw and came looking for a challenge, right?
Okay, looks like we're not getting any answers until we play along.
Show her what you're made of
Since Amber wants to play, might as well go along with it.
Fine, we accept your challenge. But if we win, you have to take us to Serena.
You do realize you're challenging the Lord of the Prize Claw, right? Finding Serena is nothing. If you beat me, I'll do anything you want.
Haha, I knew you'd be the challenger! Come on, have a seat.
The Lord hops beside Amber and works the controls with expert flair. She deftly maneuvers the claw and, in one swift motion, snags a crocodile plushie.
Hmph. See that? Pure skill. If you want to surrender now, I won't blame—
Wha—wait! How are you so fast?!
In the blink of an eye, a trio of new plushies appears at Amber's feet.
Oh, playing the lethal, silent type, are we?
Fine! Then I'll just have to show you the true power of the Hidden Lord!
Well, if this is what it takes to get her to cooperate...
Besides, Amber seems really into it, so what's the harm?
Alright, you're on. But can we get a feel for the machine first?
But of course. A true challenge demands a level playing field.
Oh? Someone's confident. Just so you know, these machines aren't like those in the Monoliths.
These are custom-tuned. The claw tension is extremely delicate. A rookie could try a hundred times and still—
Huh? Ha ... that's just luck. Beginner's luck. It'll run out soon, and then...
And that makes three and four.
Amber is a prize claw prodigy!
Hmph... Heheheh! How very interesting. A worthy opponent appears at last...
Then allow me, the Hidden Lord of the Prize Claw, to utterly CRUSH that confidence!
I was just marveling that some mortal would dare challenge ME, the great Boss ... and with such a childish game.
And so, I must ask you:
Are you prepared to offer your soul?
When you issue a challenge, you must wager your very soul.
Heh heh ... Let the games begin! My champion, the Panther of Darkness, shall teach you a lesson!
And so, in the name of gathering intel, a fierce and secret war was waged.
You think you can beat ME? Sorry, pal. I was born to win!
There is no "defeat" in the vocabulary of the Hidden Lord of the Prize Claw! Not now, not ever! RAAAAAAAGH!
All that yelling, and for what?
Th-This time only counts because the claw's tension was off!
And the prize placement was all wrong! Plus, it's ... really windy today!
Hours flew by in a blur.==RT==The final score was 109 to 58, a landslide victory for Amber.
... This has to be ... yeah, a dream. A total nightmare.
Huh? My prize collection! All the plushies I wished for from the Monoliths, the ones I gathered one by one... Why are some missing?!
Ahaha... Oh. So this isn't a dream after all. Whatever. A loss is a loss. I'm not a sore loser or anything...
From the mountain of prizes at her feet, Amber picked out a single orange cat plushie.
This is the only one I want.
… Are you pitying me? I don't need charity from the winner—!
Though I'm unwilling to accept it, the Lord of the Prize Claw is no more. From now on, I will live as Nazuna, just a regular member of Petal Bloom...
So, uh... Amber?==RT==The title is yours now.
Why?! Aren't you coming after the title?!
We've been saying that all along...
I... I'm completely defeated. Um... you must be Trekkers from another city, right?
I see. Well then, if you haven't settled on a place to stay yet, you're welcome to stay here.
Actually...==B== Serena is just out on business. She'll be back in the evening.
That would be too much trouble for you. This is your place after all.
No worries. Though it looks a bit run-down, this used to be the Trekkers' House of the Trekker Association in Philae—It was always meant to be a resting spot for Trekkers.
Besides, no Trekkers have come here recently at all. Otherwise, we wouldn't be so free to do whatever we please.
So this is a Trekkers' House... But how did it end up like this?
Well...==W== Um, I'll explain everything properly once everyone gets back tonight.

She grips the joystick, her focus absolute as the gleaming silver claw descends toward its prize.
The claw seizes a plushie of a black-and-white penguin named Sherlock—a common sight in the Monoliths.
Could she be...?==B== No, doesn't seem likely.
Excuse me ... are you a swordmaster?
Noya, reality is not a Stella Drama.
A-Anyway, we're the New Star Guild. Terribly sorry to barge in like this.
We're looking for an information broker named Serena.
Yeah, well, bad news: she's not here. She's not one for public appearances.
But lucky for you, I know how you can find her.
Oh, thank goodness! Could you take us to her, please? About the price...
Hmm, okay. But first, you have to play with me... Er, I mean, pass my trial! Can't just help any random crew that wanders in, you know.
Ooh, I get it! It's just like in the stories! To meet the legendary hermit, you have to defeat their loyal guardian first!
S-Sorry! Apologies for Noya...==B====RT==So, about this trial...
This, of course! A prize claw duel! You each control a claw, and whoever snags the most plushies before time's up wins.
Sounds like a real challenge, huh?
She just wants someone to play with, doesn't she?
Whoa, I've never seen Amber get this excited about anything.
Knew you couldn't resist! See? Your friend is already raring to go♪
Hmph. Oh, I get it now! You weren't looking for Serena at all. You came for ME!
You must've heard stories about the Hidden Lord of the Prize Claw and came looking for a challenge, right?
Okay, looks like we're not getting any answers until we play along.
Show her what you're made of
Since Amber wants to play, might as well go along with it.
Fine, we accept your challenge. But if we win, you have to take us to Serena.
You do realize you're challenging the Lord of the Prize Claw, right? Finding Serena is nothing. If you beat me, I'll do anything you want.
Haha, I knew you'd be the challenger! Come on, have a seat.
The Lord hops beside Amber and works the controls with expert flair. She deftly maneuvers the claw and, in one swift motion, snags a crocodile plushie.
Hmph. See that? Pure skill. If you want to surrender now, I won't blame—
Wha—wait! How are you so fast?!
In the blink of an eye, a trio of new plushies appears at Amber's feet.
Oh, playing the lethal, silent type, are we?
Fine! Then I'll just have to show you the true power of the Hidden Lord!
Well, if this is what it takes to get her to cooperate...
Besides, Amber seems really into it, so what's the harm?
Alright, you're on. But can we get a feel for the machine first?
But of course. A true challenge demands a level playing field.
Oh? Someone's confident. Just so you know, these machines aren't like those in the Monoliths.
These are custom-tuned. The claw tension is extremely delicate. A rookie could try a hundred times and still—
Huh? Ha ... that's just luck. Beginner's luck. It'll run out soon, and then...
And that makes three and four.
Amber is a prize claw prodigy!
Hmph... Heheheh! How very interesting. A worthy opponent appears at last...
Then allow me, the Hidden Lord of the Prize Claw, to utterly CRUSH that confidence!
I was just marveling that some mortal would dare challenge ME, the great Boss ... and with such a childish game.
And so, I must ask you:
Are you prepared to offer your soul?
When you issue a challenge, you must wager your very soul.
Heh heh ... Let the games begin! My champion, the Panther of Darkness, shall teach you a lesson!
And so, in the name of gathering intel, a fierce and secret war was waged.
You think you can beat ME? Sorry, pal. I was born to win!
There is no "defeat" in the vocabulary of the Hidden Lord of the Prize Claw! Not now, not ever! RAAAAAAAGH!
All that yelling, and for what?
Th-This time only counts because the claw's tension was off!
And the prize placement was all wrong! Plus, it's ... really windy today!
Hours flew by in a blur.==RT==The final score was 109 to 58, a landslide victory for Amber.
... This has to be ... yeah, a dream. A total nightmare.
Huh? My prize collection! All the plushies I wished for from the Monoliths, the ones I gathered one by one... Why are some missing?!
Ahaha... Oh. So this isn't a dream after all. Whatever. A loss is a loss. I'm not a sore loser or anything...
From the mountain of prizes at her feet, Amber picked out a single orange cat plushie.
This is the only one I want.
… Are you pitying me? I don't need charity from the winner—!
Though I'm unwilling to accept it, the Lord of the Prize Claw is no more. From now on, I will live as Nazuna, just a regular member of Petal Bloom...
So, uh... Amber?==RT==The title is yours now.
Why?! Aren't you coming after the title?!
We've been saying that all along...
I... I'm completely defeated. Um... you must be Trekkers from another city, right?
I see. Well then, if you haven't settled on a place to stay yet, you're welcome to stay here.
Actually...==B== Serena is just out on business. She'll be back in the evening.
That would be too much trouble for you. This is your place after all.
No worries. Though it looks a bit run-down, this used to be the Trekkers' House of the Trekker Association in Philae—It was always meant to be a resting spot for Trekkers.
Besides, no Trekkers have come here recently at all. Otherwise, we wouldn't be so free to do whatever we please.
So this is a Trekkers' House... But how did it end up like this?
Well...==W== Um, I'll explain everything properly once everyone gets back tonight.

strings.text: At night, the members of Petal Bloom gather together. Serana plays a game with you, challenging you to find the "real her." You see through her trick and initiate the conversation about information trading.
No, not me! P-Please, don't look at me.
Ugh, Serena always loves to play these little "games" ...==W== Heh, can't say Idon't, though.
Serena is one of them... The green-haired girl says she's Nazuna, but she could be lying.
Hmm ... which one of these three is the real Serena?
This whole situation started five minutes ago.
Nazuna, I wished for a new plushie at the Monolith and...==W== Oh, do we have visitors? How unusual.
Greetings. We're Trekkers of the New Star Guild.
Eek—! S-s-strangers?! I'm so sorry, wrong house!
Relax, you're at the right place... Long story short, they're looking for Serena.
Let me introduce you.==RT==The tall one is—
Hold on, Nazuna. Don't introduce us just yet.
If I'm not mistaken, you're the Boss from the Boss Accord Staffing Corporation, aren't you?
I am. Words of my company have already reached Philae?
I couldn't say if it has. I was simply asked to give this letter to you.
A letter? The sender must have known I was coming.
Greetings, Boss.==RT==I am standing right before you. You have one chance to guess who I am.==RT==Choose wisely, and you may ask me anything.==RT==—Serena, Pluvia Month 10th.
A letter from six days ago... Interesting. Though this is all very strange, it sounds like all I have to do is find the real Serena.
So, ==PLAYER_NAME==? Time to make your choice.
Oh, and for the record, she doesn't actually care about winning or losing. She'll show herself even if you're wrong, so no pressure.
I doubt it's meaningless, though... This is likely some kind of test.
I think the pink-haired girl is the most suspicious. She claims she was just delivering the letter, but what if she wrote it herself? It's the perfect way to deflect suspicion.
"Serena" is just a codename, right? That means even Nazuna could be our target.
That's true, I can't rule her out...
That's why my gut says it's the timid, white-haired girl.
Why her? Someone that shy could never be an information broker.
No, no, what if that's just a front? The perfect cover to hide her real skills.
I don't know why she'd hide them, but it's not impossible, right?
Serena likes games. Nazuna likes games.
You all make good points, but I don't think it's any of them.
What? But the letter said, "I am standing right before you." Besides us, they're the only other people in the room.
Oh, I get it! ==PLAYER_NAME== thinks Serena secretly swapped places with one of us.
I doubt she'd infiltrate our group. Given her love for games, she wouldn't resort to a cheap trick like that. There's no fun in winning if you cheat.
Which brings me to my conclusion. Remember what Bastelina told us?
That's the only hint I can give you.
If we believe her, then Serena must be in this room somewhere, and she isn't cheating.
Since she's playing fair, she must have given us some kind of clue.
The letter says, "I am standing right before you"... It never said she had to be one of those three people.

In that case, my answer is this: Serena isn't one of the three people in front of me. She's hidden somewhere in this room, but still within my line of sight as I read the letter. Which means the most likely spot is...
The words are barely out of your mouth when an old cloak on the wall suddenly billows, taking on a human shape.
You blink, and a girl is standing silently by the wall, as if she has been there all along.
Impressive, Boss. You saw through my little game far quicker than I anticipated.
It's a pleasure to finally meet you. I am Serena.
To every question in this world, I hold the answer.
With Serena's identity revealed, the once-quiet Trekkers' House now hosts a simple but delicious dinner.
Alright, now that everyone's here, let's do some proper introductions.
This weirdo who's always hiding her face under a hood is Serena, the one you all came to see.
She looks a little shady, I know, but that's just her. Don't worry about it.
Protecting one's own safety is only natural. Being an information broker tends to make you a few enemies, you know<size=60>♪
Um ... was I not being subtle enough?
That's why I was trying to gloss over it!
Anyway, about my guild, the Petal Bloom—this is our tall one, Kaede. She's a pro at everything from commissions to logistics. Our guild would fall apart without her.
About that letter—Serena asked me to give it to you last week. She said the Boss would be the next person to arrive at the Trekkers' House. We honestly weren't trying to mess with you.
Serena ... knew we'd be here six days in advance?
But we drove straight here. That has to be the fastest way to travel. How could she possibly have known?
And this white-haired girl is Fuyuka. She's our newest member, just joined last month...
Fuyuka? Fuyuka, where did you go?
Fuyuka isn't trying to be rude. She just has a hard time with people.
To put it simply, she's incredibly shy. Seeing so many strangers at once must've completely drained her social battery.
She just needs to go tremble in a corner for a bit to recharge. She'll pop back out when she's ready.
Our turn! We're the New Star Guild, also known as the Boss Accord Staffing Co.!
The very ones who crushed the Creta Trading, halted the Monolith Meltdown, destroyed a giant Stellaroid, and saved the Waterway and the city.
Crushed the Creta Trading... You took down an entire company?
But Serena, where did you hear that? If Scarlet Sights Media ran a story on us, Nazuna and others would've heard about it already.
Oh, no. Their cross-city report won't be out for another week. As an information broker, it's my job to be faster than any journalist.
Heh. You certainly live up to your reputation.
In that case, let's get back to our deal. The location of the orphanage ... You know where it is. What's your price?
Whoa, ==PLAYER_NAME==, hold on. Didn't she say we could ask anything if we found her?
She did. But the letter never said she'd answer all your questions.
In other words, the game isn't over yet ... is it?
My, my. You really are something, Boss ... I think I'm starting to like you.
Truthfully, I never had to meet you at all. So, letting you ask me questions is already a generous discount.
So it's a simple transaction. We just have to pay your price.
See? Talking to the smart ones saves so much time.
I know everything about your question, including the reason behind it. And anything I don't know yet, I can find out easily enough.
But you will do something for me: defeat one of the two remaining Big Three and restore the Petal Bloom to their former glory.
Huh? Serena? What are you talking about—
Hey, Serena, stay out of our business!
The Petal Bloom Guild used to be a force to be reckoned with.
You met a mighty Trekker back at the camp, didn't you? Lady Nazuka, the one who led the expedition against the Blade of Jade.
She used to be a member of this very guild.
Dammit! Don't bring up that traitor!

strings.text: Nazuna and her group parted ways with Nazuka due to a hunting mission. Serena asks for your help with Petal Bloom. In the end, you all agree to a pact: to make Fuyuka a "Trekker Hero."
Ugh...==W== Help...!==W== My leg's hurting so much... I can't move...
No...==W== I don't want to die... Someone, please ... help me...
Just hang on! I'll get you out of here!
Kaede, how's it looking on your end?
Too many wounded. We can't treat them all here. We have to carry them out of the forest.
Easy for you to say. We're surrounded by three very dangerous monsters.
Kaede, get people to safety! I'll hold the three of them off!
That's insane! They tore through all these people in an instant. You can't take them on alone—
A green whirlwind tears through the forest. The Garden of Parasite's massive canopy thrashes wildly, blocking the Blade of Jade's dive and blinding the Spirit of Brutality.
Trees, split. Let the mountains tremble!
Oh, wild spirits, let more than the leaves quake!
Stride forth through this dense wood,==RT==and cast out the beasts that bar our way!
After her brief chant, the storm surges into a towering green wall, sealing the monsters away from the wounded Trekkers.
Heh, just in time. I managed to get those three giant monsters all grouped up for you.
Think you can take them all out in one shot?
My magic will only hold them for a short time. You must evacuate the wounded. Now.
You've got no sense of humor, you know that? You and Kaede get everyone out. As Captain of the Petal Bloom, I can't just leave you to die.
Captain, this is not the time to argue. My magic is ill-suited for evacuating the wounded. Only your skills are fit for this task.
Kaede, let's move! These people can't wait any longer!
Is there anyone else who can still stand? Cover our retreat with me!
Nazuka, just hold out until we're clear of the forest! As soon as we're out, you fall back immediately, you hear me?
Don't worry, Captain. I have no intention of dying today.
We made a promise, remember? We're going to climb every Monolith in the world, together.
And that was that. The first hunting squad, completely wiped out by the Big Three.
One flies, one spits poison, and one has a hide tough like stone. A trio like that would be tough for anyone to handle.
But wait ... why did you call Nazuka a traitor? It sounds like she saved you all by covering your retreat.
The first hunting squad was organized by a handful of guilds on a volunteer basis. We were among them.
Just like Nazuna said, we ran into all three of those monsters at once. The other Trekkers were caught completely by surprise. A lot of them were hurt.
Nazuna and I got off with minor injuries, so we helped escort the others out of the forest.
Nazuka, who bought us time to escape, made it back safely, too.

However, the Trekker Association's House in Philae was saddled with the responsibility for the failure of the hunt, and was forced to withdraw from Philae after being sued against by United Harvest—==W==the largest local corporation.
The once bustling House now fallen into disrepair, with only us left to guard the place for them.
The Trekker Association was actually expelled...==W== So that's why the bounties for the Big Three were issued by United Harvest.
But Nazuka wasn't the same after that day.
First, she started putting distance between us—me and Kaede.
Then, she quit the Petal Bloom. She and that Claire girl got backing from United Harvest and organized a new squad.
Kaede and I tried to talk to her, but all we got was corporate double-talk...==W== As if all the time we'd spent adventuring together meant nothing.
Did something happen after Nazuna's group retreated? Or is there more to the story?
The way I see it, she decided you were dead weight and dumped you for a better team.
It's simple. A month after that new squad was formed, Nazuka led her own team and took down the Blade of Jade.
One success, one failure. Sounds like the only difference was the people involved.
That's bullshit! We were fighting three of them at once!
Proper reconnaissance, luring and separating your targets, using superior numbers ... that's all part of battle, isn't it?
Serena's words are harsh, but it's hard to argue with her. Looking purely at the results, Nazuka clearly did better after leaving Petal Bloom.
So, how about my little proposal? Seems perfectly reasonable, wouldn't you say?
I trust you have no objection to me telling Nazuna and her friends the full story of how you defeated the Creta Trading?
There's no reason to hide what we did in Emor. Words are bound to reach Philae eventually.
Wonderful. Then allow me to begin...
In an instant, the great hall of the old Trekkers' House became Serena's personal stage.
She recounted our adventures in Emor in painstaking detail,==RT==as if she had been there herself, an invisible shadow at our side.
Just who is this Serena? She even knows the exact details of how we infiltrated the Creta Trading.
Would a simple information broker ... really expose a client's secrets like this? Or does she have other plans?
Noya, Iris, Amber. What do you think? Can we handle the last two commissions?
A giant boar and a huge man-eating plant... They can't be tougher than that giant Stellaroid on the Waterway, right?
Noya, you are not ramming it with Loxy!
If we take them on one at a time, we should be able to win.
If everyone else is on board... Helping them in exchange for information from Serena seems like a reasonable trade.
So? This is your chance to borrow the power of the Boss—
Aren't you the least bit curious why Nazuka left you?

Just think. If this group can take down one of the remaining two monsters and prove their strength... Nazuka, as a key figure in the new squad, would have no choice but to cooperate with you to defeat the final one.
That would be your chance to speak with her as an equal.
I don't care why she left, and I have no intention of dragging her back to Petal Bloom.
Let the "impressive" new squad handle the Spirit of Brutality and the Garden of Parasite.
I have no desire to "revive the guild." I'm perfectly happy just playing the claw machine every day.
Kaede? What do you think? You've been quiet this whole time.
After that failed expedition... I realized I'm just not cut out to be a Trekker. I ... was actually planning to look for a job at United Harvest.
What?! Why? What's wrong with being a Trekker?!
Such a blunt refusal. Looks like Serena's out of moves.
Heh. So Petal Bloom really is a lost cause. Boss, might I propose an alternative deal?
Sure. It's better not to force them.
Then I ask you to take this promising young Trekker and mold her into ... no, not just the Camp ... the hero of all Philae.
H-Huh? Eh? M-Mold ... me ... into a hero?
Waaah! N-No way! I can't do that! It's too embarrassing! I'll die! I'll literally die of a heart attack!
Hey, Fu ... Fuyuka ... you're holding on too tight ... can't breathe ... I'm a goner...!
Nazuna is obsessed with prize claw, and Kaede is busy looking for a job...
So, having the Boss help this newcomer grow seems like a fine idea, no? Or are you going to reject that as well?
We've ... we've tried training with her a few times ... but it didn't really work out.
But perhaps the next time's the charm! Little Fuyuka, how about you let Boss here help you? The choice is yours.
<size=35>Eeeeeek! I-I'm so soooorry!==RT==A lowly peon like me shouldn't even be looking at a person of your stature! My sincerest apologies!
She seems terrified. Am I really that scary? Ouch ... that kind of hurts.
B-But ... Fuyuka, you can't keep going on like this. You'll just keep holding everyone back.
Boss ... runs a whole company... Someone that powerful has to be able to help me with my problems. This is ... this is a chance to change.
A chance to change? What's she muttering about now...?
U-Um ... B-Bo ... Bobb! I'm so sorry, so sorry! I messed it up at the most important part, I'm so, so sorry!
It's fine, don't worry about it. Please, continue.
<size=40>I want your help! I want you to help me become just like Nazuka—the le-<r=legit>legend</r> of this Camp!

We made a promise, remember? We're going to climb every Monolith in the world, together.
And that was that. The first hunting squad, completely wiped out by the Big Three.
One flies, one spits poison, and one has a hide tough like stone. A trio like that would be tough for anyone to handle.
But wait ... why did you call Nazuka a traitor? It sounds like she saved you all by covering your retreat.
The first hunting squad was organized by a handful of guilds on a volunteer basis. We were among them.
Just like Nazuna said, we ran into all three of those monsters at once. The other Trekkers were caught completely by surprise. A lot of them were hurt.
Nazuna and I got off with minor injuries, so we helped escort the others out of the forest.
Nazuka, who bought us time to escape, made it back safely, too.

However, the Trekker Association's House in Philae was saddled with the responsibility for the failure of the hunt, and was forced to withdraw from Philae after being sued against by United Harvest—==W==the largest local corporation.
The once bustling House now fallen into disrepair, with only us left to guard the place for them.
The Trekker Association was actually expelled...==W== So that's why the bounties for the Big Three were issued by United Harvest.
But Nazuka wasn't the same after that day.
First, she started putting distance between us—me and Kaede.
Then, she quit the Petal Bloom. She and that Claire girl got backing from United Harvest and organized a new squad.
Kaede and I tried to talk to her, but all we got was corporate double-talk...==W== As if all the time we'd spent adventuring together meant nothing.
Did something happen after Nazuna's group retreated? Or is there more to the story?
The way I see it, she decided you were dead weight and dumped you for a better team.
It's simple. A month after that new squad was formed, Nazuka led her own team and took down the Blade of Jade.
One success, one failure. Sounds like the only difference was the people involved.
That's bullshit! We were fighting three of them at once!
Proper reconnaissance, luring and separating your targets, using superior numbers ... that's all part of battle, isn't it?
Serena's words are harsh, but it's hard to argue with her. Looking purely at the results, Nazuka clearly did better after leaving Petal Bloom.
So, how about my little proposal? Seems perfectly reasonable, wouldn't you say?
I trust you have no objection to me telling Nazuna and her friends the full story of how you defeated the Creta Trading?
There's no reason to hide what we did in Emor. Words are bound to reach Philae eventually.
Wonderful. Then allow me to begin...
In an instant, the great hall of the old Trekkers' House became Serena's personal stage.
She recounted our adventures in Emor in painstaking detail,==RT==as if she had been there herself, an invisible shadow at our side.
Just who is this Serena? She even knows the exact details of how we infiltrated the Creta Trading.
Would a simple information broker ... really expose a client's secrets like this? Or does she have other plans?
Noya, Iris, Amber. What do you think? Can we handle the last two commissions?
A giant boar and a huge man-eating plant... They can't be tougher than that giant Stellaroid on the Waterway, right?
Noya, you are not ramming it with Loxy!
If we take them on one at a time, we should be able to win.
If everyone else is on board... Helping them in exchange for information from Serena seems like a reasonable trade.
So? This is your chance to borrow the power of the Boss—
Aren't you the least bit curious why Nazuka left you?

Just think. If this group can take down one of the remaining two monsters and prove their strength... Nazuka, as a key figure in the new squad, would have no choice but to cooperate with you to defeat the final one.
That would be your chance to speak with her as an equal.
I don't care why she left, and I have no intention of dragging her back to Petal Bloom.
Let the "impressive" new squad handle the Spirit of Brutality and the Garden of Parasite.
I have no desire to "revive the guild." I'm perfectly happy just playing the claw machine every day.
Kaede? What do you think? You've been quiet this whole time.
After that failed expedition... I realized I'm just not cut out to be a Trekker. I ... was actually planning to look for a job at United Harvest.
What?! Why? What's wrong with being a Trekker?!
Such a blunt refusal. Looks like Serena's out of moves.
Heh. So Petal Bloom really is a lost cause. Boss, might I propose an alternative deal?
Sure. It's better not to force them.
Then I ask you to take this promising young Trekker and mold her into ... no, not just the Camp ... the hero of all Philae.
H-Huh? Eh? M-Mold ... me ... into a hero?
Waaah! N-No way! I can't do that! It's too embarrassing! I'll die! I'll literally die of a heart attack!
Hey, Fu ... Fuyuka ... you're holding on too tight ... can't breathe ... I'm a goner...!
Nazuna is obsessed with prize claw, and Kaede is busy looking for a job...
So, having the Boss help this newcomer grow seems like a fine idea, no? Or are you going to reject that as well?
We've ... we've tried training with her a few times ... but it didn't really work out.
But perhaps the next time's the charm! Little Fuyuka, how about you let Boss here help you? The choice is yours.
<size=35>Eeeeeek! I-I'm so soooorry!==RT==A lowly peon like me shouldn't even be looking at a person of your stature! My sincerest apologies!
She seems terrified. Am I really that scary? Ouch ... that kind of hurts.
B-But ... Fuyuka, you can't keep going on like this. You'll just keep holding everyone back.
Boss ... runs a whole company... Someone that powerful has to be able to help me with my problems. This is ... this is a chance to change.
A chance to change? What's she muttering about now...?
U-Um ... B-Bo ... Bobb! I'm so sorry, so sorry! I messed it up at the most important part, I'm so, so sorry!
It's fine, don't worry about it. Please, continue.
<size=40>I want your help! I want you to help me become just like Nazuka—the le-<r=legit>legend</r> of this Camp!

strings.text: Despite being powerful, Fuyuka struggles to cooperate with others. It turns out that the reason behind is a past traumatic experience. Fuyuka intends to offer you her soul first, but you, however, have other plans.
That should be ...==W== all of them.
Whoa! You took out all those monsters by yourself? Awesome!
Nice work, Fuyuka. Here, have some tea and take a little break.
Heh ... heheh ...==W== Thanks. I've still got a long way to go before I'm on your level.
For day one of Fuyuka's special training, we've ventured deeper into the forest, past the Trekkers' House.
The plan is to gauge her current skill level while taking out some of the smaller monsters.
When faced with monsters, Fuyuka doesn't hesitate. Her slender arms conceal a surprising strength, allowing her to clear out entire groups in a flash.
Get it together, Fuyuka. You can't keep this up. You'll just drag everyone down... You're going to end up abandoned...
Strange. With that kind of strength, why is she so insecure?
Whoa, looks like a tough one up ahead! Let me give you a hand, Fuyuka!
I've got its attention! Your chance, Fuyuka!
Ah, wha—?! I'm so sorry, I'm so sorry! You gave me the perfect opening and yet I missed! I'm really, really sorry!
Hey, it's fine! No big deal. Just calm down and aim for the next one!
Huh? Her punches have slowed down.
The monster cocks its head, apparently deciding Fuyuka is the easier target.
Fuyuka throws a punch, but with noticeably less force. She takes the full brunt of the monster's charge.
I'll hold it! Amber, end it!
I... I'm fine. I'm sorry, I just ... I dragged everyone down again.
Don't worry about it. Everyone has off days.
But it's not just on my off days. It's ... every day. Whenever I team up with people, this happens.
It's true. When Noya was distracting the monster, Fuyuka's movements seemed hesitant.
Hmm... When I was kiting it, did you pull your punch because you were afraid you'd hit me?
Yes. These gauntlets... They explode on impact.
And when it charged at you, you went easy on your punch for the same reason?
Mhm... I've ... made that mistake before.
Three months ago. At a Monolith.
Hss—damn, that hurts. Her punch took down the Stellaroid, alright... And took us down with it.
Is this really the time for jokes?! You're seriously hurt. Can you even stand?
I... I don't think I can make it.
Hey, you! White-haired rookie! Look what you've done! Who the hell knocks a Stellaroid back into their own teammates?
I-I didn't mean to...==W== There was nobody behind it when I swung.
Still making excuses? People are hurt because of you!
What good is an apology going to do? Pay for it.
You're fired. And before you leave, you're covering medical bills, lost wages, emotional distress compensation, and gear repair costs. That'll be 5 million Dorra.
5... 5 million?! I don't have that much!
B-But ... it really is my fault that people got hurt... I don't have the money right now, but I'll work commissions to pay you back. I promise, I'll pay every last Dorra!
That's more like it. Here's some free advice.
With your "skills"? Find another line of work. You're not cut out to be a Trekker.
So... that's what happened.==W== After that, I could only take commissions alone. My body just freezes up when other Trekkers are around.
I had to sell everything to pay the debt. Thank goodness Nazuna and Kaede took me in. Otherwise, I'd be out on the streets.
Something about that team ...==W== doesn't add up.
On a Monolith climb, you have designated attackers and support. The support team doesn't engage without orders, let alone wander into the attacker's line of fire.
You were attacking the Stellaroid, Fuyuka, so you were the attacker. The support members running wild were the ones at fault.
Of course it wasn't Fuyuka's fault.
Nazuna...! Wh-what are you doing here?
You're one of the Petal Bloom. I had to make sure this Boss here wasn't trying to steal your soul.
Heh, sounds like you're a good senior to have. Since you know what really happened, why not fill us in?
I've told Fuyuka this before...==W== She ran into a crew of scammers who prey on newbies.
They set new Trekkers up to fail—or just fake a mistake—so they can shake them down for cash.
There are crooked Trekkers?! Where are they? I'll expose those jerks!
Wish I knew.==W== That crew wanted to join the expedition team we were forming, but their rep was so bad we said no.
But ... word is they followed us anyway. Not a single one made it back.==W== End of story.
A month later, Fuyuka couldn't find them to pay them back, so she came to the old Trekkers' House. That's how we met.
Sounds like they got what was coming to them.
See, Fuyuka? That "accident" has nothing to do with you. It was just a setup by some lowlifes. Just be yourself and fight how you know you can.
I... I know it was a scam, but ...==W== I can't get that image out of my head—of him lying there. I'm terrified that next time, it'll be for real.
The incident was three months ago. She met Nazuna and Kaede a month ago.
So she lived with that guilt for two whole months. No wonder this messed with her head so much.
A quick chat isn't going to fix this. I need to figure out a real plan.
Please, be honest with me... Can that Boss really fix what's wrong with me?
I feel so bad, making everyone go through all this trouble just for me...
Relax, Fuyuka. We're talking about Boss here. Or perhaps ... I should call ==SEX4== Tyrant.
A little hang-up like yours is nothing to ==SEX4==.
B-But... ==SEX1== wore such a grim look after watching me fight this morning.
If you're that worried, there's a foolproof method. With this, you'll never have to worry about hurting a teammate again.
R-Really? Is there actually a way?
Surrender your soul to the Boss.
Just give control of your body to someone else. Become a puppet. That way...==W== If anyone gets hurt, it's not on you.
Become ...==W== Boss's puppet? Let Boss control my body... That way, I couldn't... I couldn't possibly hurt anyone.
I understand, Miss Serena. Thank you.
That said, I must warn you. Being a puppet isn't exactly a good thing, you know.
I know. But if this fixes my weakness, I can finally fight beside everyone.
I-I want to be a Trekker! I want to fight with my friends! I'm so tired of climbing Monoliths all alone.
Ah... My apologies. I spoke out of turn. I underestimated your resolve, Fuyuka.
Since this is your decision, you should do it. I think ...==W== you should trust your own instincts.
Good luck. I'll be rooting for you.
After dinner, I'm just about to go looking for Fuyuka when I feel an anxious gaze on me from behind the sofa.
Y-Yes, it's me! Um, I-I-I... I was hoping I could talk to you for a moment, um ... Boss.
Good timing. I was just looking for you.
Y-You were? Oh, then ... please, you first.
I've figured out how we can solve your problem.
Oh... Boss... Are you here to take my soul?
Your soul? What? That's not part of the plan.
The solution I came up with is—
Since it's a pain in the heart, it must be resolved from within.
"Habit is second nature," and what you lack is precisely the experience of cooperation.
Stubborn illnesses require strong medicine. I must prepare some "special" methods.
I saw some stress-relief methods in a Monolith; I should let Fuyuka try them.
As long as she relaxes and stops thinking about "harming her squadmates," her problem should be solved.
Rather than avoiding a difficulty, it's better to face it.
I just need to let her adapt to fighting alongside her friends through extensive training. Hmm... For safety, I'll need to limit her power a bit.
There's no time for slow methods. The way to deal with one trauma is to create an even bigger one to overshadow it.
Heh heh, I have a good idea!

strings.text: You introduce meditation and talk therapy to Fuyuka, but the results always go awry. Just as you are feeling troubled, you encounter a witch, Mistique.
In psychotherapy, meditation is a pretty basic tool.
A calm mind is the key to controlling your emotions, and through them, your body.
Sit however you're comfortable—cross-legged, on the ground, in a chair, or on a cushion.
Relax your body, clear your mind, and picture a calm, still lake.
I'm just going by what I remember from a book in the Monolith. Hope it works.
Close your eyes. Follow me. Breathe out ... then in.
Find a rhythm that feels natural to you.
Keep it up, and you should start to feel like you're observing yourself from a distance.
No need to apologize. All that matters is learning to manage your feelings.
And honestly, you're a fast learner. You're already getting the hang of it.
Good. This should help build her confidence.
Um... So, how many times a day should I==W== ... do this?
The important thing is not to force it. Just go at your own pace and don't overdo it.
You don't have to be sitting, either. You can do it anytime, anywhere—even on a walk.
I ... I get it! I'll practice as hard as I can, I promise!
Well, I hope this helps. We'll see how she is tomorrow.
Hey, it's okay. You're not hurt, and that's the important part.
I was about to ask you the same thing. Heard this was because of that meditation you taught her?
N-no... It has nothing to do with ==PLAYER_NAME==...
I'm just so dumb. I got too focused on the meditation practice and zoned out during a fight. A monster ended up chasing me all over the place.
My bad. Guess I jumped to conclusions.
Looks like meditation just isn't her thing.
Fuyuka, let's try a different approach today.
I'm so sorry...==W== After you spent all that time teaching me...
Don't sweat it. Different methods work for different people. Besides, knowing how to meditate is a good skill to have—it might come in handy later.
Have you ever tried just ... talking to someone about your troubles?
You don't have to start with strangers. Just try with the people around you.
The Petal Bloom, Serena, any of us... You can talk to whoever you feel comfortable with.
But ... wouldn't I just be bothering?
They might be concerned at first, but teamwork is built on trust.
Learning to communicate is the first step toward growing stronger.
R-Right...==W== When you put it like that, it makes sense.
If you're worried about what to say, you can even practice by talking to an object first.
It's all about mastering your own feelings.
Um ... ==PLAYER_NAME==, do you think you could try and help Fuyuka?
I'm really worried about Fuyuka lately.
For the past two days, she's been talking to the tree outside.
Oh no... This is probably because of me.
Okay...==W== Besides talking to the tree, has she tried talking to you?
Guess talking to objects isn't giving her the courage she needs.
Thanks for letting me know. I'll go have a chat with her.
That's a relief. We're so close that it's actually hard for me to bring certain things up.
==PLAYER_NAME==! What weird thing did you teach Fuyuka this time?!
What is it now? Is she still talking to the tree?
Worse! She's talking to my doll now! C'mon, look!
Mmm ...==W== hehe, is that so...?==W== That's ... fun...
I see...==W== Well, then ... I'll tell you something about me...
Do you think some invisible monster possessed the doll and put a hex on her?
No, it's a type of ...==W== therapy. Seems this method isn't for her, either.
Ugh, talk therapy's a bust. Maybe I should go to a Monolith and check for other treatments?
But the path to the Monolith is blocked by monsters right now. What a pain.
Hey, Trekker! Hold on a moment!
If I'm not mistaken,==W== you're the Boss, aren't you?
I am. Can I help you...?
Heheh~ No need to be so guarded. I'm Mistique, a witch from Scarlet Sights Media. A real pleasure!
Sorry, but I'm not looking to get my fortune told, buy a potion, or curse anyone right now.
Ah ...==W== huh? What sort of fairy tale have you been reading?
Witches are long past that line of work. These days, we feast on the truth.
And you, my dear,==W== look like the most delectable morsel of all.

Hey, Trekker! Hold on a moment!
If I'm not mistaken,==W== you're the Boss, aren't you?
I am. Can I help you...?
Heheh~ No need to be so guarded. I'm Mistique, a witch from Scarlet Sights Media. A real pleasure!
Sorry, but I'm not looking to get my fortune told, buy a potion, or curse anyone right now.
Ah ...==W== huh? What sort of fairy tale have you been reading?
Witches are long past that line of work. These days, we feast on the truth.
And you, my dear,==W== look like the most delectable morsel of all.

strings.text: You attempt to restrict Fuyuka's great power through weighted training, but this instead causes her strength to double and makes it even more difficult to control. While you're feeling troubled, you encounter a witch, Mistique.
Is she gonna be okay? Fuyuka looks like a wreck.
All of us staring is probably making it worse. Her nerves seem totally shot.
I'm sure the Boss's got a plan.
The first step for Fuyuka is just getting used to having other people around during a fight.
Teamwork is too much to ask right now. Let's start with her adjusting to an audience.
Everyone's watching...==W== I have to do my best...
She's too hung up on us watching. She can't focus.
Ugh...==W== Why can't I ever do this right...?
Everyone's staring...==W== I'm so nervous...==W== My body just won't listen to me...
If I stay like this, when will I ever be able to fight alongside them...
Yeah, you can see it on her face.
We're making her nervous, and when she's nervous, she makes mistakes. Then she feels useless, and it just spirals from there.
She gets this flustered just from an audience.
Alright, new plan. Let's tackle this at the source.
Fuyuka's afraid of hurting us in battle, right? So let's find a way to keep her power in check.
(sob) I'm so sorry. I totally locked up,==W== just 'cause people were watching... I'm more useless than shrubshrew droppings...
Don't be so hard on yourself. It's alright. I have a new training idea.
Here. Try strapping these to your arms and legs.
Yep. It's a simple idea. This way, your strength will be held in check.
So even with people around during a fight, you won't have to worry about hurting them.
I get it. I'll try to throw a real punch without holding back.
Um... ==PLAYER_NAME==? Do you have a second? I'd like to talk about Fuyuka's training.
Is something wrong with the training? Or do you think it isn't working out, Kaede?
No, it's working great. It's just... I guess you could say it's working a little too well...
Whoa... What a punch. Was that one of her special moves?
Nope. Just a regular old punch.
Cough, cough... She took down a whole tree in a single hit.
Fuyuka, the logging commission's finished. Let's head back.
Instead of coming closer, Fuyuka takes a few steps back.
D-don't come any closer!==W== Ah, um...==W== Sorry, I didn't mean it like that... I just... It's safer for you all if I keep my distance...
She's been like this for a while now. She won't even come back to the Trekkers' House anymore.
So, has Fuyuka learned to control her strength?
Control it? It's the exact opposite. She's stronger than ever.
I see...==W== Wait, she got stronger?
(sob) It's all my fault. For the first few days, the sandbags made my punches feel heavy, like my power was being held back...
But ...==W== since yesterday ... I can't even feel the weight anymore. My punches are just faster and harder.
Looks like the resistance training actually built up her strength and skill.
That... That usually takes two or three months to get used to!
Hee hee~ Our Fuyuka just lacks confidence. Truth be told, there's little she can't do when she puts her mind to it.
Yeah, well, whatever the result, at least she got stronger. The training wasn't a total bust.
Well, that's a positive way to look at it...==W====RT== But if sandbags won't work, I need a new plan.
After Nazuna and Kaede take Fuyuka back, I stand alone in front of the felled tree, racking my brain while I wait for it to be hauled away.
This Fuyuka problem is tough. If mental conditioning and weighted training don't work...
Someone... Can someone give me a hand?
Huh? Sounds like it's coming from under the tree...
No, that's impossible! We cleared the area before the tree fell. There's no way someone's trapped under there—
Huff ... huff... Thank you so much. If it weren't for you, I'd probably be dead.
I'm more amazed==W== that you survived in the first place...
The name's Mistique! I'm a witch with Scarlet Sights Media. You can call me anything you like!
Alright, Miss Mistique. How'd you end up pinned under the tree?
I'm not really sure myself.==W== I was taking a little nap in the branches, and the next thing I know, the tree fell.
Best not to tell her what happened...
So, uh...==W== What brings you out here, Mistique? Since you call yourself a "witch"... Are you gathering potion ingredients?
Potion ingredients? Oh, please. We witches are way past that stuff. I'm here to...
What is it? Is there something on my face?
Wait a minute... You wouldn't happen to be the Boss from the Boss Accord Staffing Company, would you?
Oh my goodness! I can't believe I ran into you here★ It was totally worth the trip all the way from Flavio!
I heard your stories in Emor, so I zipped over on my broom, but I missed you! Then I heard you went to Philae, so I chased you here, but I still couldn't find you. I was starting to freak out★
Yup! We witches just live to uncover secrets and feast on the truths within. And you...==W== You smell absolutely delicious.

strings.text: You attempt to boost Fuyuka's courage through fear. You disguise yourself as a monster, but instead attract a real monster... You are indeed successful, but the cost is your own life.
Uh... Um... Are you sure it's really okay for me to just ... do nothing?
Yep. Just go about your day like you normally would.
But...==W== Sorry, I don't mean to question you, Boss. It just ... doesn't feel like this will fix anything.
Don't worry. Have a little faith.
A real personality shift requires a real scare. If I warn her, it'll ruin the surprise.
Though, I gotta admit, pickin' on our sweet junior feels a little mean...
That's a separate matter. C'mon, let's hide. Lemme see...
Hehe, that corner. Totally hidden, easy to miss. No one'll ever think to look there.
Is this really gonna solve the problem, though?
One jump-scare won't cut it... But a few should toughen her up.
Oh, I get it! Like when you pull a tooth, you distract the patient so they don't feel the pain.
Shhh, quiet! Fuyuka could be back any second.
What is everyone doing hiding back here?
I've been crouching here ever since I got back...
This spot is small and out of the way. It feels safe. People usually don't notice it...
I-I can play, too...==W== Oh, or ... am I in the way?
N-No, we were just trying to find a quiet spot to talk! Ahaha.
Fuyuka knows this place better than we do. She practically invented hiding here. This wasn't well-thought-out huh?
Guess it's back to the drawing board.
A rustling drifts from the nearby trees, like wind whispering through leaves.
I pull on the Spirit of Brutality disguise Noya spent days making for me and wait for my target.
I look like a real beast. Fuyuka's gonna jump out of her skin...
Whoa, this thing's got some serious tunnel vision.
Gotta deal. Fuyuka's almost here. Time to focus on the scare.
Ah, shoot... Got so hung up on the disguise, I forgot to practice the roar. Okay, gotta pinch my nose, like this—
But ... it's too close to the Trekkers' House. If it attacks... O-Okay... I'm scared, but I've gotta stop it here. For everyone.
At least I'm alone. No one else'll get hurt.
In and out, in and out... I'll be fine. If any monster shows up, I'll just punch it into orbit...!
What's keepin' her? It's not that far.
Oh, she's trying to sneak up behind me. Clever girl. Too bad I heard her.
What did I just touch? Are these ... giant ... teeth...?
The next instant, a massive force flings me into the sky.==W==
The last thing I see is ...==W== a beast of unbelievable size.
Sorry! I'm sorry!==W== It's all my fault—I hesitated, I was scared! That's why I'm too late!
Fuyuka's iron fist hammers the beast, the shockwave ripping a whirlwind through the trees.
This time, her strike veers around me on the ground, landing dead-on.
No, that's not it! Boss, are you okay...!?==W== Boss, wake up!
Dear Tyrant. You actually pulled it off.
One punch, thrown in a rage, took down that massive beast in a heartbeat. The girl you chose is truly one of a kind.
"Chose" is a stretch. More like I got saddled with her...==W== Wait, did that thing actually send me flying?
Precisely. Your act was so convincing, the Spirit of Brutality mistook you for a rival trying to claim its turf.
Hold on—the Spirit of Brutality?! Can't believe I ran into one of the Big Three out there...
Regardless, you ought to be pleased. You were right next to the beast, yet her punch didn't even scratch you. Seems her inner conflict is resolved.
You put your life on the line to help her work through her issues? How selfless! ==W==(sob)
This is ... a lot. You're making this super awkward.
So she can only unleash her true power when she's pushed to the edge, huh...
Hah... Only someone with that kind of talent is worthy of serving me.
And getting to see you two again...==W== Yeah, I suppose I should be glad.
Ah, it's an honor just to be in your thoughts, Tyrant.
I mean, we only get to see you when you're at death's door! Can't even say "drop by again soon." It's killing me~
Right, I'm heading back. Got things to take care of.
Until next time, Tyrant. While I can't say "hope to see you soon," we'll be waiting for our reunion♪
We'd love to meet her at the Monolith sometime.
This whole time-hopping thing ... never gonna get used to it.
This time... Let's try a different method.

strings.text: Following the witch's suggestion, you decide to have Fuyuka confront her past. Fuyuka confesses that she was once looked down upon by Claire of the new squad. Nazuna is enraged and decides to stop wallowing.
Phew! This cake is a lifesaver. I totally needed this.
Here, Boss, you gotta try some.
Weren't you gonna "eat the truth"? How'd that turn into eating cake? This whole thing seems pretty suspicious.
Not at all! This is just my standard sugar fix★==RT==A witch runs on sugar, you know.
Ugh, my brain was complete mush after a week of eating Tawny Nightingale on the road.
Besides, cafe interviews are totally normal, right? You gotta sit down somewhere nice to get the real story.
An interview? So, you're a reporter?
A reporter? I remember it means ...==W== someone who records things?
Hehe<size=60>♪<size=37> It's funny people still use that old word. It's kinda what we do, but a witch is a witch.
Hmm... So I guess I can think of a "witch" as a "reporter" ... but why is my memory of them so different?
Like you said, herbs, curses, fortune-telling ... that's all ancient history. Mmm, not that I can't do it...
But these days,==W== a witch's job is to fly around, hunt down big scoops, and spread the word.
Got it. That explains why you're here.==W== So, where's this "Flavio" place you mentioned?
That's the "city of entertainment," always shrouded in mist!==RT==It's the hub where all of Nova's news gets traded.
So, trust me, digging for intel out here ...==W== is a huge waste of time.
Finding an orphanage? Pfft, that's nothing. In Flavio, you'd get a lead on that in a second.
Oh? Then you know where it is?
Well...==B== I didn't hear you were looking for it 'til I hit Emor. And this isn't Flavio—flying all the way back now would be pointless.
But ... if you give me an exclusive interview, I'll definitely make it worth your while★
I can handle pretty much anything, like tidying up your vehicle, taking you for a spin in the sky...
An interview, huh... Some public promotions for the guild couldn't hurt.
Besides...==W== There is something she could help me with.
Witches zip around Nova on brooms, right? So you must know the ropes.
Mhmm! Lookin' for a guide? I've hit up most cities in Nova, and I know Philae like the back of my hand.
No, I was actually wondering if you've ever dealt with something like this.
I leave out Fuyuka's name and alter the details so Mistique won't recognize her, then lay out the situation.
Hmm...==W== Sounds like you've already tried the right things.
Well, it's different for everyone. I once interviewed someone who got over it with some "experiential therapy."
Exactly! 'Cause I literally just made it up. It's not, like, official or anything★
Long story short—a certain Stellaroid chased her as a kid, and she's been scared stiff of 'em ever since...
Even after becoming a Trekker, she still couldn't handle that kind of Stellaroid. The moment she saw them, she couldn't stop trembling.
Then one time, she got cornered by one in a Monolith and had to fight. Guess what happened?
Nope! Lost and ran away! But the fear ... poof, gone. During the fight, she realized it wasn't half as scary as she'd imagined...
She even got the feeling that she could totally win next time.
So, confronting one's fear head-on...==W== That makes sense.
What feels like a huge deal right now ... sometimes it just fades.
Hee hee, so I was a pretty big help, right? Does that mean I snag the exclusive interview with the Boss?
You wanna know more about how Fuyuka got scammed?
Yeah. Like, why'd she join that phony guild to begin with?
That part's no secret; we all know why. But ...==W== why are you asking me and Kaede behind her back?
I'd have asked her myself if I could.==W== But I can't just go dredge up painful memories.
Mmm... I get why Nazuna feels weird talking behind her back...==W== But the Boss has a point. It should be fine to tell ==SEX4==, right?
You're right. Okay, I'll tell you. Fuyuka was just desperate to become a Trekker.
Can't anyone just become a Trekker if they want to?
"Anyone who leaves a city is a Trekker"—that's how the saying goes. But by real Trekker standards, you gotta climb a Monolith, make a wish, and beat a tough monster to earn the title.
So it's not that simple. Lots of newbies don't know the ropes, and that's how frauds take advantage.
But you said Fuyuka climbs Monoliths by herself. Wouldn't that make her a "real Trekker" by now?
Yes, that's true. But Fuyuka herself...
I-I'm so sorry. I didn't mean to worry everyone.
Fuyuka, what are you doing hiding under the table?
N-Nothing... It's just that it feels safe being so small and tight in here... Hehe, and ... the living room is so quiet at night.
Great. I was trying to hide from Fuyuka, and we end up in the same spot...
I'm sorry...==W== We discussed your past without permission. We didn't mean any harm...
N-No, it's fine! I know Boss means well for me. It's all because I was too weak...
I finally got on a team and I still couldn't get it right...==W== Someone like me trying to be a Trekker... It was probably a mistake from the very beginning—
On that point, I must say you're mistaken. The very first Trekker legend speaks of climbing the Monoliths and adventuring all alone. That proves you don't need a team to be one.
Just as when they first met, Serena's cloak billows out from the coat rack, revealing her form.
You just ... hang out on a coat rack all day?
My, my. Prying into a lady's secrets is quite rude. Besides, this little chat isn't about me.
Fuyuka, did someone say something to upset you?
I find it hard to believe someone with your dream would give up so easily. More importantly, I'm afraid your grasp of history is a bit flawed.
Lone-wolf Trekkers are rare, certainly, but history has seen its share of famous ones.
To climb the Monoliths alone and become famous...==W== That's incredible.
Okay... I'll tell you all what happened. It was from before I joined the Petal Bloom.
No. I can't let you join the new hunting squad.
But ... you haven't even seen me fight.
I know who you are. The Trekker who decked her own teammate.
I've heard things about that crew. I even suspect it wasn't your fault. But that's not the issue.
If you can't even control your own fists, you could hurt an ally at any time.
In my book, anyone who can't work with others has no right to be a Trekker. They're just dead weight.
And let's just say you can control your fists. If you get framed and don't fight back—or worse, don't even realize you're being framed...
Then you're just naive. That means you're weak, and you're still dead weight.
Besides, word's already gotten around camp. We're facing a massive, dangerous monster. I can't have people doubting the person fighting beside them.
So, the answer's no. If you get it, go home.
Claire, the vice-captain of the new hunting squad...==W== She practically knew Fuyuka was framed...
Oh, so that's the kind of person our vice-captain is. Won't take the slightest risk. How interesting.
Vice-Captain Claire's logic holds up, and her reasons are solid... But still...
For someone so sharp, rejecting Fuyuka without even testing her skills... I feel like there's more to this.
Fuyuka's trauma isn't just from the Monolith climb. It's from everyone judging and blaming her after. To fix the root of the problem, we need to—
ARGH! I can't take any more of this!
S-Sorry, Nazuna senpai... I didn't mean to drag up something so awful, wasting everyone's time...
It's your attitude! "Sorry"? Fuyuka, what'd you do wrong? You really need to ditch this habit of apologizing for everything!
And every last one of those people from the new hunting squad is spouting the same damn nonsense!
And since we're on the topic—I told you Nazuka used to live here, right? The traitor.
She said almost the exact same thing before she left—
Huh... She did? I had no idea.
I didn't wanna get you all worked up. That day, I tried to stop her from leaving...
Nazuka, why are you leaving? We're more than halfway done with our research on those monsters...
Once we figure out all their patterns, we can definitely beat them.
You don't have to do a thing.
I'm starting a new hunting squad.==W== And it has no room for the weak. Goodbye.
I was so mad. I'm still so mad. I have never gotten over it.
Eek—?! Nazuna senpai, please, calm down!
You are NOT weak. And neither is anyone in the Petal Bloom!
We're gonna finish those last two commissions!
And we're gonna show those smug jerks who underestimate the Petal Bloom what we can really do!
