strings.text: The Grace Imperium fast-tracks the auction for the Philae Monolith's next decade of usage rights. Grand Inspector Matilda explains United Harvest's past and its current crisis, and officially asks for your help.
"Early Bidding Opens for Philae Monolith Usage Rights"?! This is huge!
Whatcha reading, Iris?==W== "Monolith Usage Rights"? What does that even mean?
You know how there are "City Monoliths" managed by companies? Besides the "Wild" ones we usually climb?
Yeah. Only company employees or hired Trekkers get to touch those. Freelancers like us are stuck with the wild ones out in the boonies.
Technically ... we are employees. Of Boss Accord.
Hey Iris, does that mean we can climb the City Monoliths now?
Of course not! We don't have usage rights from the Grace Imperium, and we certainly haven't purchased any climbing permit from a licensed company.
Rights, permits... It's all gibberish to me.
Listen, Monoliths are divine gifts for the Novians.
And the Grace Imperium manages all Monoliths==RT==on behalf of the God of Grace.
They lease the City ones to companies, which require==RT==specific clearance to enter.
Being an employee alone isn't a free pass.
The Grace Imperium... The shop that sells Soul Stones? Are they really that big a deal?
They aren't just a shop! They're a massive conglomerate controlling the magical energy supply for all of Nova.
Since they hold the keys, they sell usage rights to companies, usually in ten-year contracts.
But after Darcia's stunt here in Philae, the Grace Imperium doubts United Harvest can manage the branch. So, they're auctioning the next ten-year contract early.
That auction process is what they call a "tender."
You make it sound so complicated. Basically, whoever throws the most Dorra at them wins, right?
It's not just about money. There are conditions.==W== Anyway... That's big company business. Small-time Trekkers like us wouldn't even be allowed in the building.
The familiar click of heels approaches the door as a cool, composed voice interrupts the conversation.
United Harvest's Philae branch must win this bid.==W== And to do that, we need to rely on the Boss's wisdom.
Boss. Everyone. Thank you for holding down the fort while I was gone.
Perfect timing.==W== I don't know the details yet, but this bidding war sounds like a headache...
I have a fair idea of the situation. Leave it to me, Boss.==W== In the meantime, I've brought a guest.
Boss, I've heard so much about you. It is an honor. I am Matilda, Grand Inspector for United Harvest.
My apologies for the sudden intrusion, but I must ask... Would you be willing to lend us a hand?
Matilda and I sit opposite each other on the office sofas, leaving the executive seat empty.
Grand Inspector Matilda, thanks for uncovering the mastermind behind the banquet attack—and for making the trip to Philae. I know how tired you must be.
I'm happy to help if I can...
But you mentioned United Harvest? Honestly, I doubt someone like me has much to offer to a company of that size.
I meant what I said. As it stands, United Harvest needs the power you possess. But before I explain, I'd like you to hear a story.
Are you familiar with the name Samuel?
Rings a bell... I've definitely heard it before somewhere.
Trekkers' House. On the wall. The old man with the white beard.
Oh! He's the legendary Trekker who conquered a dozen Wild Monoliths. They say he's the reason there aren't any "uncharted Monoliths" left in Nova.
Precisely. Sixty years ago, after discovering the very last uncharted Monolith, he finally returned home to Philae.
Philae was a quiet farming town back then.==RT==Though it had a local Monolith...
The Monolith only yielded mediocre Artifacts.==RT==No company even bothered bidding for the rights to use it.
Samuel sank his life savings into it and took out a massive loan==RT==from Deepsea Finance.
He used a shell company to secure a ten-year lease==RT==through an old Trekker contact.
Folks thought he'd lost it. Why trade a peaceful retirement for a worthless Monolith?
He braved the Monolith alone and brought back Artifacts==RT==no one had ever seen and didn't even know how to use.
After demonstration, they finally understood—they were seed==RT==chambers, automated harvesters, and powder that helps crops thrive.
With those Artifacts, Samuel grew the finest wheat and vegetables in Philae.
Then, he simply gave those superior seeds to the local farmers.

He organized a fair-price system so farmers wouldn't undercut each other during a surplus, and no one would starve during a bad harvest. Slowly, food shortages gradually eased in cities around Philae.
Ten years later, he founded United Harvest using a Seal of Grace he'd been saving. Soon, affordable grains and produce were flowing down the river to every neighboring city.
The grain trade built Philae, turning a tiny settlement into the city you see today.
Wait, you mean ... the legendary Samuel founded United Harvest?!
That can't be right. Everything I've read says it started in New Orelian, bankrolled by a bunch of fruit merchants.
Sigh... History is cruel. Such a monumental legacy, quietly swept under the rug.
Nyx, Firenze. You both work for United Harvest. You must know Samuel's name.
Yeah. Actually, almost all United Harvest employees know about him.
But the official story is ... he was a terrible manager who nearly bankrupted the company.
Supposedly, the business only took off after the New Orelian merchants bailed him out, transforming United Harvest into a corporate giant.
Hmph. The Senate certainly works hard when it comes to revising history.
Samuel founded United Harvest with a single vision: affordable, quality bread for every person in Nova.
He poured his profits straight back into the land—expanding fields, building greenhouses, and improving seeds and irrigation.
But Firenze isn't entirely wrong. Five years in, unprecedented storms hit Philae. That year went down as one of the worst harvests in history.
The company's finances tanked. To save the farms and his workers, Samuel sold his shares to the New Orelian merchants and moved the headquarters there.
Flush with new cash, United Harvest spread its farms and storefronts to every city. Better yet, their food was cheap and top-tier.
Eventually, people stopped buying from anyone else. A natural market shift, I suppose.
Are we talking about the same company? That doesn't sound like the United Harvest we know at all.
Yeah. That business model sounds a lot like ... well, the ideal version of the company Firenze has been fighting for.
Undercut the market using deep pockets and endless supply. Sure, the customers win at first.
But once they're the only option left on the shelf...
Fast forward thirty years. United Harvest had become the largest grain and food supplier in all of Nova.
The Senate decided it was time to reap the harvest. Only they weren't after wheat—they wanted Dorra.
United Harvest gutted their product lines. Low-margin goods were axed, while top sellers saw their production costs slashed and retail prices hiked.
But wouldn't that ruin the flavor? They'd lose their customer base... Wait, no. They still have bustling shops in every city. Unless...
Wait, what? Am I the only one lost here? Boss, do you know what they are talking about?
The food industry demands massive, long-term investment for thin margins.
By the time United Harvest started hiking prices, they had a thirty-year head start. No ordinary farm could ever compete with roots that deep.
Once they secured a monopoly, they could inflate prices unsupervised. People had no choice but to buy from them.
Spot on. That is the reality of their monopoly.
People have to eat. As long as the bread isn't entirely inedible ... they'll keep buying it. Eventually, they'd even get used to the taste.
Tell me, my brilliant Boss... What do you make of United Harvest's success story?
Blinded by greed. They'll rot from the inside out eventually.
Nobody meant any harm, yet everyone will end up losing.
Boring. Spare me the corporate whitewashing.
Without a single competitor breathing down their neck, quality and fair pricing go out the window. They're free to strong-arm the market.
But people aren't fools. Whether it's the drop in quality or the soaring prices, public patience will run dry.
Keep this up, and it's only a matter of time before some new force—internal or external—tears them down.
Samuel had a noble vision, but he ignored the risks. As a result, the company became completely dependent on outside money.
Profit drives the economy. No matter who funded them, they were always destined for this outcome.
Customers naturally want the best products at the lowest prices. There's nothing wrong with that.
Samuel's dream matched those demands perfectly, creating a fragile cycle.
Nobody realized this setup would ultimately benefit no one.
But look at the outcome... The Senate is rolling in cash. Isn't that a happy ending? Sounds like a total win!
True. Though even the Senate must know they're bleeding the system dry.
Otherwise, nobody would resort to assassinations over the Philae branch's director seat.
United Harvest is clearly tearing itself apart.
Grand Inspector, you left out one crucial detail:==W== the Seal of Grace.
Sure, United Harvest expanded through massive production and deep pockets.
But you're likely the only agricultural firm in Nova holding a Seal of Grace.
A Seal of Grace lets you raise an army—but not every company chooses to do so.
Why would United Harvest, a food company, command a formidable private legion? Surely it isn't just for show. No. It must be because...
There are external forces standing in opposition to the company. Probably more than just a couple.
Meanwhile, your internal issues are boiling over. That assassination attempt at the banquet proves it.
You hit the mark. Without Samuel's guidance, United Harvest has been morphing into a monster over the decades, a greedy monster whose only concern is the Dorra in its own pockets.
The Senate fractured into warring factions. Nobody cares about the company's future anymore. Anyone who did was devoured by the rest long ago.
They don't even bother checking if the soldiers' wages are paid on time. They have no idea they're sitting on a massive powder keg.
So that's the mess you're dealing with.==W== Honestly, I'm even more certain now that there is not much I can do to help a giant like United Harvest.
My guild's a company, and so is United Harvest. Under the Seal of Grace's authority, we stand on equal footing. No one outranks anyone here.
The only real difference is that we're Trekkers.
But I don't see how our time in the field can be much help when it comes to running a corporate empire.
People rarely see their own worth. It seems like you haven't realized the true nature of the power you hold.
This may sound odd, but as proof... Gibel Corregio, the senator who orchestrated your assassination attempt, is already in custody.
You caught him?! But you just arrived in Philae. How'd you even pull that off so fast?
We have Boss to thank for that.
Good day, Grand Inspector Matilda. I've been expecting you.
Cosson? Thought you and your people were supposed to be retreating to Port Goldfinch.
That was the plan. But en route, I received a transmission from the Senate. They've given me a temporary mandate to represent the company at the Monolith bidding here in Philae.
Sounds like they really trust you.==W== Give it a few years, and you might be the talk of the Senate.
You flatter me. But clinging to power after a defeat is hardly "elegant." Once I return, I intend to resign my seat and focus on rebuilding the legion.
Rebuilding the legion? Are you sure? You've always obsessed over elegance, and life in the barracks is anything but.
If our military were truly "elegant," we wouldn't have suffered such a humiliating defeat over unpaid wages. The whole thing was a total farce.
Fair point. Let me make you a promise, then. To help you regain that "elegance," the Compliance Department will give you our full support.
I appreciate it.==W== But the main reason I waited was to hand this individual over to you.
You traitor! You're handing me over to Compliance? My friends in New Orelian will have your head for this, Cosson!
"Friends" in New Orelian, huh? Good to know. We'll just round them up right along with you.
Matilda?! What are you doing here?!
One more thing. Please tell the Boss and Lady Firenze that with you away from New Orelian, the Senate is moving fast. They're tabling an emergency motion today—
What are they thinking? If that branch closes, food supply will drop by ten percent. That's not just a shortage. It's a continental crisis.
They can't skim off the top in Philae, so they lose nothing killing it. Plus, they'll make a fortune hoarding the rest.==W== Typical inelegant behavior, wouldn't you say, Grand Inspector?
But the Senate backed Gibel. He was handpicked by them to run the Philae branch next.
Gibel, you orchestrated an assassination while under the Senate's wing. This is a slap in their face.==W== Are you planning to cross the New Orelian merchants?
That isn't the point, Grand Inspector. This is about what's elegant. Dragging everyone down for his own petty ambition... It's pathetic.
Besides, our main force only survived that massacre because the Boss commanded those Intelligent Plants with such ... undeniable elegance.
It's only right. When the Boss shows such consideration, we must respond with equal elegance.
Understood. You're putting a lot of faith in the Boss.==W== I'll make sure ==SEX== knows.
Just look at the people you've won over. Cosson who fought you, the Goodwind assassin who targeted you...
Firenze and Nyx who trust absolutely no one... Even Darcia holds you in high regard.
Boss, you possess something United Harvest lost long ago: the power to earn people's trust.
Please, help us. Let's save the Philae branch and keep Samuel's dream alive.
I was going to do that anyway.==W== Firenze is my ally, and I have friends in Philae. But more importantly—
Food is a necessity. Even a one-percent shortage can drive prices up until they're high enough for one percent of the population to starve. I can't just stand by and let that happen.
Our first priority now is figuring out how to halt the Senate's resolution... Do you have any strategy?
Honestly, I'm stuck. If I were in New Orelian, I could stop them... But they knew that and waited for me to leave before striking.
I'm in Philae now, and even with a witch's help, I can't get back to New Orelian in time. The Senate has me in checkmate. That's why I'm turning to you...
It's not checkmate yet. If you can make it to that meeting, you can turn the tide—correct?
Don't worry. I have a very reliable friend over in New Orelian.

param: The Grace Imperium fast-tracks the auction for the Philae Monolith's next decade of usage rights. Grand Inspector Matilda explains United Harvest's past and its current crisis, and officially asks for your help.
"Early Bidding Opens for Philae Monolith Usage Rights"?! This is huge!
Whatcha reading, Iris?==W== "Monolith Usage Rights"? What does that even mean?
You know how there are "City Monoliths" managed by companies? Besides the "Wild" ones we usually climb?
Yeah. Only company employees or hired Trekkers get to touch those. Freelancers like us are stuck with the wild ones out in the boonies.
Technically ... we are employees. Of Boss Accord.
Hey Iris, does that mean we can climb the City Monoliths now?
Of course not! We don't have usage rights from the Grace Imperium, and we certainly haven't purchased any climbing permit from a licensed company.
Rights, permits... It's all gibberish to me.
Listen, Monoliths are divine gifts for the Novians.
And the Grace Imperium manages all Monoliths==RT==on behalf of the God of Grace.
They lease the City ones to companies, which require==RT==specific clearance to enter.
Being an employee alone isn't a free pass.
The Grace Imperium... The shop that sells Soul Stones? Are they really that big a deal?
They aren't just a shop! They're a massive conglomerate controlling the magical energy supply for all of Nova.
Since they hold the keys, they sell usage rights to companies, usually in ten-year contracts.
But after Darcia's stunt here in Philae, the Grace Imperium doubts United Harvest can manage the branch. So, they're auctioning the next ten-year contract early.
That auction process is what they call a "tender."
You make it sound so complicated. Basically, whoever throws the most Dorra at them wins, right?
It's not just about money. There are conditions.==W== Anyway... That's big company business. Small-time Trekkers like us wouldn't even be allowed in the building.
The familiar click of heels approaches the door as a cool, composed voice interrupts the conversation.
United Harvest's Philae branch must win this bid.==W== And to do that, we need to rely on the Boss's wisdom.
Boss. Everyone. Thank you for holding down the fort while I was gone.
Perfect timing.==W== I don't know the details yet, but this bidding war sounds like a headache...
I have a fair idea of the situation. Leave it to me, Boss.==W== In the meantime, I've brought a guest.
Boss, I've heard so much about you. It is an honor. I am Matilda, Grand Inspector for United Harvest.
My apologies for the sudden intrusion, but I must ask... Would you be willing to lend us a hand?
Matilda and I sit opposite each other on the office sofas, leaving the executive seat empty.
Grand Inspector Matilda, thanks for uncovering the mastermind behind the banquet attack—and for making the trip to Philae. I know how tired you must be.
I'm happy to help if I can...
But you mentioned United Harvest? Honestly, I doubt someone like me has much to offer to a company of that size.
I meant what I said. As it stands, United Harvest needs the power you possess. But before I explain, I'd like you to hear a story.
Are you familiar with the name Samuel?
Rings a bell... I've definitely heard it before somewhere.
Trekkers' House. On the wall. The old man with the white beard.
Oh! He's the legendary Trekker who conquered a dozen Wild Monoliths. They say he's the reason there aren't any "uncharted Monoliths" left in Nova.
Precisely. Sixty years ago, after discovering the very last uncharted Monolith, he finally returned home to Philae.
Philae was a quiet farming town back then.==RT==Though it had a local Monolith...
The Monolith only yielded mediocre Artifacts.==RT==No company even bothered bidding for the rights to use it.
Samuel sank his life savings into it and took out a massive loan==RT==from Deepsea Finance.
He used a shell company to secure a ten-year lease==RT==through an old Trekker contact.
Folks thought he'd lost it. Why trade a peaceful retirement for a worthless Monolith?
He braved the Monolith alone and brought back Artifacts==RT==no one had ever seen and didn't even know how to use.
After demonstration, they finally understood—they were seed==RT==chambers, automated harvesters, and powder that helps crops thrive.
With those Artifacts, Samuel grew the finest wheat and vegetables in Philae.
Then, he simply gave those superior seeds to the local farmers.

He organized a fair-price system so farmers wouldn't undercut each other during a surplus, and no one would starve during a bad harvest. Slowly, food shortages gradually eased in cities around Philae.
Ten years later, he founded United Harvest using a Seal of Grace he'd been saving. Soon, affordable grains and produce were flowing down the river to every neighboring city.
The grain trade built Philae, turning a tiny settlement into the city you see today.
Wait, you mean ... the legendary Samuel founded United Harvest?!
That can't be right. Everything I've read says it started in New Orelian, bankrolled by a bunch of fruit merchants.
Sigh... History is cruel. Such a monumental legacy, quietly swept under the rug.
Nyx, Firenze. You both work for United Harvest. You must know Samuel's name.
Yeah. Actually, almost all United Harvest employees know about him.
But the official story is ... he was a terrible manager who nearly bankrupted the company.
Supposedly, the business only took off after the New Orelian merchants bailed him out, transforming United Harvest into a corporate giant.
Hmph. The Senate certainly works hard when it comes to revising history.
Samuel founded United Harvest with a single vision: affordable, quality bread for every person in Nova.
He poured his profits straight back into the land—expanding fields, building greenhouses, and improving seeds and irrigation.
But Firenze isn't entirely wrong. Five years in, unprecedented storms hit Philae. That year went down as one of the worst harvests in history.
The company's finances tanked. To save the farms and his workers, Samuel sold his shares to the New Orelian merchants and moved the headquarters there.
Flush with new cash, United Harvest spread its farms and storefronts to every city. Better yet, their food was cheap and top-tier.
Eventually, people stopped buying from anyone else. A natural market shift, I suppose.
Are we talking about the same company? That doesn't sound like the United Harvest we know at all.
Yeah. That business model sounds a lot like ... well, the ideal version of the company Firenze has been fighting for.
Undercut the market using deep pockets and endless supply. Sure, the customers win at first.
But once they're the only option left on the shelf...
Fast forward thirty years. United Harvest had become the largest grain and food supplier in all of Nova.
The Senate decided it was time to reap the harvest. Only they weren't after wheat—they wanted Dorra.
United Harvest gutted their product lines. Low-margin goods were axed, while top sellers saw their production costs slashed and retail prices hiked.
But wouldn't that ruin the flavor? They'd lose their customer base... Wait, no. They still have bustling shops in every city. Unless...
Wait, what? Am I the only one lost here? Boss, do you know what they are talking about?
The food industry demands massive, long-term investment for thin margins.
By the time United Harvest started hiking prices, they had a thirty-year head start. No ordinary farm could ever compete with roots that deep.
Once they secured a monopoly, they could inflate prices unsupervised. People had no choice but to buy from them.
Spot on. That is the reality of their monopoly.
People have to eat. As long as the bread isn't entirely inedible ... they'll keep buying it. Eventually, they'd even get used to the taste.
Tell me, my brilliant Boss... What do you make of United Harvest's success story?
Blinded by greed. They'll rot from the inside out eventually.
Nobody meant any harm, yet everyone will end up losing.
Boring. Spare me the corporate whitewashing.
Without a single competitor breathing down their neck, quality and fair pricing go out the window. They're free to strong-arm the market.
But people aren't fools. Whether it's the drop in quality or the soaring prices, public patience will run dry.
Keep this up, and it's only a matter of time before some new force—internal or external—tears them down.
Samuel had a noble vision, but he ignored the risks. As a result, the company became completely dependent on outside money.
Profit drives the economy. No matter who funded them, they were always destined for this outcome.
Customers naturally want the best products at the lowest prices. There's nothing wrong with that.
Samuel's dream matched those demands perfectly, creating a fragile cycle.
Nobody realized this setup would ultimately benefit no one.
But look at the outcome... The Senate is rolling in cash. Isn't that a happy ending? Sounds like a total win!
True. Though even the Senate must know they're bleeding the system dry.
Otherwise, nobody would resort to assassinations over the Philae branch's director seat.
United Harvest is clearly tearing itself apart.
Grand Inspector, you left out one crucial detail:==W== the Seal of Grace.
Sure, United Harvest expanded through massive production and deep pockets.
But you're likely the only agricultural firm in Nova holding a Seal of Grace.
A Seal of Grace lets you raise an army—but not every company chooses to do so.
Why would United Harvest, a food company, command a formidable private legion? Surely it isn't just for show. No. It must be because...
There are external forces standing in opposition to the company. Probably more than just a couple.
Meanwhile, your internal issues are boiling over. That assassination attempt at the banquet proves it.
You hit the mark. Without Samuel's guidance, United Harvest has been morphing into a monster over the decades, a greedy monster whose only concern is the Dorra in its own pockets.
The Senate fractured into warring factions. Nobody cares about the company's future anymore. Anyone who did was devoured by the rest long ago.
They don't even bother checking if the soldiers' wages are paid on time. They have no idea they're sitting on a massive powder keg.
So that's the mess you're dealing with.==W== Honestly, I'm even more certain now that there is not much I can do to help a giant like United Harvest.
My guild's a company, and so is United Harvest. Under the Seal of Grace's authority, we stand on equal footing. No one outranks anyone here.
The only real difference is that we're Trekkers.
But I don't see how our time in the field can be much help when it comes to running a corporate empire.
People rarely see their own worth. It seems like you haven't realized the true nature of the power you hold.
This may sound odd, but as proof... Gibel Corregio, the senator who orchestrated your assassination attempt, is already in custody.
You caught him?! But you just arrived in Philae. How'd you even pull that off so fast?
We have Boss to thank for that.
Good day, Grand Inspector Matilda. I've been expecting you.
Cosson? Thought you and your people were supposed to be retreating to Port Goldfinch.
That was the plan. But en route, I received a transmission from the Senate. They've given me a temporary mandate to represent the company at the Monolith bidding here in Philae.
Sounds like they really trust you.==W== Give it a few years, and you might be the talk of the Senate.
You flatter me. But clinging to power after a defeat is hardly "elegant." Once I return, I intend to resign my seat and focus on rebuilding the legion.
Rebuilding the legion? Are you sure? You've always obsessed over elegance, and life in the barracks is anything but.
If our military were truly "elegant," we wouldn't have suffered such a humiliating defeat over unpaid wages. The whole thing was a total farce.
Fair point. Let me make you a promise, then. To help you regain that "elegance," the Compliance Department will give you our full support.
I appreciate it.==W== But the main reason I waited was to hand this individual over to you.
You traitor! You're handing me over to Compliance? My friends in New Orelian will have your head for this, Cosson!
"Friends" in New Orelian, huh? Good to know. We'll just round them up right along with you.
Matilda?! What are you doing here?!
One more thing. Please tell the Boss and Lady Firenze that with you away from New Orelian, the Senate is moving fast. They're tabling an emergency motion today—
What are they thinking? If that branch closes, food supply will drop by ten percent. That's not just a shortage. It's a continental crisis.
They can't skim off the top in Philae, so they lose nothing killing it. Plus, they'll make a fortune hoarding the rest.==W== Typical inelegant behavior, wouldn't you say, Grand Inspector?
But the Senate backed Gibel. He was handpicked by them to run the Philae branch next.
Gibel, you orchestrated an assassination while under the Senate's wing. This is a slap in their face.==W== Are you planning to cross the New Orelian merchants?
That isn't the point, Grand Inspector. This is about what's elegant. Dragging everyone down for his own petty ambition... It's pathetic.
Besides, our main force only survived that massacre because the Boss commanded those Intelligent Plants with such ... undeniable elegance.
It's only right. When the Boss shows such consideration, we must respond with equal elegance.
Understood. You're putting a lot of faith in the Boss.==W== I'll make sure ==SEX== knows.
Just look at the people you've won over. Cosson who fought you, the Goodwind assassin who targeted you...
Firenze and Nyx who trust absolutely no one... Even Darcia holds you in high regard.
Boss, you possess something United Harvest lost long ago: the power to earn people's trust.
Please, help us. Let's save the Philae branch and keep Samuel's dream alive.

Our first priority now is figuring out how to halt the Senate's resolution... Do you have any strategy?
Honestly, I'm stuck. If I were in New Orelian, I could stop them... But they knew that and waited for me to leave before striking.
I'm in Philae now, and even with a witch's help, I can't get back to New Orelian in time. The Senate has me in checkmate. That's why I'm turning to you...
It's not checkmate yet. If you can make it to that meeting, you can turn the tide—correct?
Don't worry. I have a very reliable friend over in New Orelian.

strings.text: The United Harvest Senate votes to dissolve its Philae branch. You contact Nazuka's team and halt the resolution at the right moment. Matilda needs you to win the Monolith bid and save the branch for good.
Philae is a worthless plot of dirt.
Six years ago, the Philae branch botched a wish. The Grace==RT==Imperium has barred them from the city's Monolith ever since.
Four years ago, Giotto de Feltro's embezzlement bled headquarters dry.
And last month, Darcia staged a coup! It failed, yes—
—but it cost us three legions and shattered public trust in United Harvest!
All of that in a mere six years! That's outrageous! And the Philae branch has been in the red for six straight years too! They're dead weight.
Why? Why is everything out of Philae a complete disaster?
The answer is obvious. The soil itself is poisoned! And that rot has infected the minds of everyone living there.
There is absolutely no reason to keep the branch. Fire the staff. Sell off the land and the Artifacts. Cut them loose, and we'll turn a profit this year.
Gentlemen, it is time to act. I formally move to shut down the Philae branch. With immediate effect!
All in favor, step to the right!
United Harvest saw us coming. The Senate is packed with soldiers. They even bought off Imperial Guards for backup.
Who cares about numbers? We got that Monolith blessing yesterday. These guys are toast!
Pew! Blew their shields clean off.
Nazuna, save your arrows. We need to breach the Senate and stop that vote.
While you were busy making eyes at Boss, I've already radioed Fuyuka.
I-I was not doing that! I was briefing Boss on critical...
Captain! We've got a breach at the rear!
Hold the line! Keep your eyes on these two Trekkers. Our orders are to keep the rats out of the Senate.
How are two Trekkers pinning down my entire squad...? What is going on?
I-I'm sorry! It was an accident!
We're fine. Since you and Nazuna kept them busy, we slipped right past those knights without a hitch.
Those idiots were so fixated on us that they left their backs wide open. Amateurs like that wouldn't last a day in the Wilds.
The Senate doors are locked...==W== Hey! Is anyone there? We're the representatives from the Philae branch! Open up!
Looks like the Senate is dead set on stalling.==W== Fuyuka, give that door a proper greeting. Don't hold back.
You mean ... my full strength? Are you sure about this?
Mina has every right to be in that room.==W== Besides, I've got a special guest who needs to make an entrance.
Heh, we've got the two-thirds majority. By the end of the day, the Philae branch will be history.
And our straw buyers for the buyout? Are they ready?
Yes. We've secured a few reliable merchants to act as fronts. They'll snap up Philae's land and Artifacts for a pittance.
Still... Word is some outsider Trekkers have escorted the Philae representative all the way here.
Don't sweat it. The CEO is on our side. She'd love to see the Philae faction uprooted. Bet she won't lift a finger to stop us.
Technically, the only one with the rank and the nerve to oppose this is Grand Inspector Matilda.
Too bad for her. We've sent her on a fool's errand to Port Goldfinch. There's no way she makes it back in time.
I've even had all inter-city comms blacked out. Remoting into the meeting is out of the question.
Besides, a few measly Trekkers aren't getting past the Imperial Guard.
The majority is clear. It's time to make the motion official, don't you think?
With over two-thirds of the Senate in favor,==W== I hereby declare the Philae branch—
Cough cough... What was that?! Explosion?!
The... The door is smashed open.
But that's impossible. Not even a giant monster could breach those doors.
Forget the doors! Speaker, declare the motion passed!
Hold it! I am exercising my veto power on this resolution!
G-Grand Inspector Matilda? How? Shouldn't she be out of New Orelian by now?!
Nazuka walks to the center of the Senate chamber holding up a phone.
I will repeat myself.==W== I am vetoing this resolution.
Don't panic. The voice is coming from the Trekker's phone. It might be a recording.
Who is whispering? Do you think this is pre-recorded? Is that you, Obart?
Ahem! Grand Inspector, surely you didn't crash the Senate in this fashion solely to use your veto?
My veto power is explicitly written in the company charter. Do you have a problem with that?
I checked my device. Inter-city comms in New Orelian are still blocked. Which means...
She's already back within the New Orelian Monolith's coverage? How did she return from Port Goldfinch...
Wait. What if she never left New Orelian? What if this was a trap to lure us out?
Then her real goal is...==W== Yes, that's it! She plans to raid our offices while we are stuck in this meeting!
Damn it... Forget the motion! We need to head back now!
The Senate is an absolute mess right now.
They severed the inter-city lines to New Orelian to keep me out of the meeting. Phones under different Monoliths can't connect without an operator bridging the signal.
None of them realized I was actually dialing in from Philae.
Ultimately, the paranoia ate them alive...
"Matilda's going to raid our offices while we're stuck here." They handed me the perfect alibi for my absence on a silver platter.
Having them abandon that room worked in my favor.
Which proves ...==W== coming to you for help was the right call.
I admire your competence. On that note... Could I ask for one more favor?
Matilda takes a file from Nyx and solemnly hands it over.
This represents a forty-one percent stake in the Philae branch.
Forty-one percent? Don't tell me you expect me to buy this off you.
I do. That was the plan all along.
Samuel held these shares forty-five years ago. He sold his stake in United Harvest, but kept a piece of the Philae branch.
Those of us left over from the old guard inherited this forty-one percent directly from him.
Headquarters holds forty-nine percent, leaving the final ten percent to the Senate representative of the Philae branch.
If that representative aligns with our faction, we secure a fifty-one percent majority and take control of the branch.
But if they side with headquarters, HQ commands fifty-nine percent, and the branch becomes their puppet.
The shares Samuel kept versus those allocated to the Senators... It's too deliberate.
Almost like he saw this coming. Like he wanted to forge this city into a crucible, forcing both sides to clash and challenge each other.
Sharp as ever, Boss. You hit the mark perfectly.
Even so, the New Orelian faction has held the Senate majority for forty-five years. The Speaker's role always goes to a headquarters appointee.
It's kept our faction backed into a corner... But we can't afford a clean break. If food production crashes, the people will starve.
We had to swallow our pride and accept the status quo.==W== But your arrival changes the game.
I wouldn't say that... The one turning the tides here is Mina, your branch representative.
I don't know about her politics, but I do know that she wants the company to produce better food, and I back that.
Her raw conviction is just like Samuel when he founded United Harvest.
Setting that aside, even if we wanted to buy those shares, the capital is a massive hurdle...
I hate admitting this, but I rarely carry more cash than the allowance Iris gives me. Speaking of... Iris, what's our current bank balance?
Um... Fifty-one thousand and one Dorra.
As you see, Boss Accord isn't exactly flush with cash.==W== Matilda, what's the actual market value of those shares?
At current rates? Roughly fifty billion Dorra.
F-Fifty billion Dorra?! Fifty billion! Do you know how many zeros that is?!
Yeah, fifty billion is astronomical. We can't afford that. Honestly, I can't even process a number that high.
You don't need to worry about the upfront cost.==W== Boss, have you heard the Grace Imperium opened bidding for the Monolith?
Yeah. The auction to decide who gets operating rights to the Philae Monolith for the next decade?
Correct. But we are only a branch office. Without authorization from a parent company holding a Seal of Grace, we can't even enter the bid.
And given the New Orelian faction's recent stunts, they'd never sign off on our request.
If we lose access to the Philae Monolith, whoever wins the bid will use the Artifacts it produces to crush us.
What do you need from me?
I'll discount these shares down to thirty billion Dorra. A ninety-nine-year payment plan, with a one-Dorra down payment.
There's one condition.==W== To get us into that auction, I need you to use your Seal of Grace and sponsor us. We need your backing.
Even then, that's roughly three hundred million Dorra a year.
Don't you think that's a bit steep for a company with exactly fifty-one thousand and one Dorra in the bank?
I get that your branch needs an official endorsement, but I need a better reason to take on that kind of financial risk...
Boss Accord isn't a one-person show. I have my crew to think about.
I understand... I was hoping to avoid playing the sympathy card.
His absurd, impossible dream...==W== It's mine, too.

I don't know about her politics, but I do know that she wants the company to produce better food, and I back that.
Her raw conviction is just like Samuel when he founded United Harvest.
Setting that aside, even if we wanted to buy those shares, the capital is a massive hurdle...
I hate admitting this, but I rarely carry more cash than the allowance Iris gives me. Speaking of... Iris, what's our current bank balance?
Um... Fifty-one thousand and one Dorra.
As you see, Boss Accord isn't exactly flush with cash.==W== Matilda, what's the actual market value of those shares?
At current rates? Roughly fifty billion Dorra.
F-Fifty billion Dorra?! Fifty billion! Do you know how many zeros that is?!
Yeah, fifty billion is astronomical. We can't afford that. Honestly, I can't even process a number that high.
You don't need to worry about the upfront cost.==W== Boss, have you heard the Grace Imperium opened bidding for the Monolith?
Yeah. The auction to decide who gets operating rights to the Philae Monolith for the next decade?
Correct. But we are only a branch office. Without authorization from a parent company holding a Seal of Grace, we can't even enter the bid.
And given the New Orelian faction's recent stunts, they'd never sign off on our request.
If we lose access to the Philae Monolith, whoever wins the bid will use the Artifacts it produces to crush us.
What do you need from me?
I'll discount these shares down to thirty billion Dorra. A ninety-nine-year payment plan, with a one-Dorra down payment.
There's one condition.==W== To get us into that auction, I need you to use your Seal of Grace and sponsor us. We need your backing.
Even then, that's roughly three hundred million Dorra a year.
Don't you think that's a bit steep for a company with exactly fifty-one thousand and one Dorra in the bank?
I get that your branch needs an official endorsement, but I need a better reason to take on that kind of financial risk...
Boss Accord isn't a one-person show. I have my crew to think about.
I understand... I was hoping to avoid playing the sympathy card.
His absurd, impossible dream...==W== It's mine, too.

strings.text: The guests from the recent banquet reemerge as your rival bidders. While you and Firenze try to untangle the ulterior motives behind these coincidences, Vita issues a bold new objective: Acquire a Monolith.
Boss, here's the equity transfer contract for the United Harvest Philae branch.
Forty-one percent of the greenhouses,==W== buildings,==W== and fields out there now belong to Boss Accord.
Should I start calling you the big boss now, Boss?
Call me whatever you want.==W== Sounds the same to me anyway.
Alright, if Boss wants to keep the status quo... What do we do about the "Philae branch" title?==W== Technically, we're a joint venture now.
Any thoughts on a new name, Boss?
A new name...==W== Let's drop "branch" and go with "United Harvest Philae."==W==
Huh?==W== No Boss Accord in the title?
Normally,==W== a merger like this goes by "United Harvest & Boss Accord Philae Joint Venture,"==W== or a compound name like "Boss Harvest."
That's not necessary. Boss Accord better keep a low profile for now.==W== Besides, a major rebrand might disrupt operations,==W== and updating signage just costs way too much.
Heh, always watching the bottom line.==W== Speaks like a true boss.
It's not purely about saving money.==W== Back then...
Join me. Let's change United Harvest, together.
You wished for us to "change United Harvest together."
Anyway,==W== here in Nova, every Seal of Grace comes with a franchise patent.
I assume United Harvest's patent has something to do with food?
Correct. United Harvest holds a black "Castle" piece, and the patent covers food—==W==specifically, bulk grain trading.
They are not concerned with family farms and independent bakeries.==W== But if anyone tries to run a large-scale agricultural operation, the company steps in.
To fix United Harvest, we have to do it from the inside.
With HQ still holding forty-nine percent of United Harvest Philae, total independence isn't happening...
But with Boss Accord backing you, they can't just do whatever they want anymore.
Once your model proves profitable while also helping the customers, the other branches—maybe even HQ—will rethink their approach.
Trust me. Keep your eyes on the goal==W== and give it everything you've got.
I appreciate the vote of confidence, but ...==W== what's your angle?
You took on thirty billion in debt for those shares, and now you're bidding. Sure, it's a joint venture,==W== but doesn't Boss Accord shoulder all the risk?
If we pull this off, we earn the trust of both you and the Grand Inspector.==W== For Boss Accord's future,==W== that kind of leverage is priceless.
Well, you're on the hook for all our Tawny Nightingales==W== and travel rations.==W== Plus==W==...==W==
The sooner I grant your wish,==W== the sooner I get to officially collect that soul of yours.
Heh. You're something else, Boss.==W== Hate to admit it,==W== but I'm starting to see why Darcia is so obsessed with you.
The first Monolith bidding session kicks off at 2:00 PM. I'll double-check our paperwork and pick you up in an hour.==W== Get some rest.
Phew. Can't "fight" on an empty stomach.==W== I should go track down Noya and the others for a bite.
If Iris sees this stock transfer contract==W== and realizes we've put thirty billion Dorra of debt on the books,==W== she's going to pass out==W==...==W==
Apologies for the interruption, Tyrant.==W== I have important news.
The Well of Worlds Tyrant Development System has issued a new objective.==W== Your second mission is to acquire a Monolith.
How thoughtful of this system. Its missions always seem to align perfectly with my current plans.
The objectives and their release timings are predetermined. As for the uncanny coincidence,==W== I suspect the mission designer possessed a gift for prophecy.
I don't care about the coincidence. I want to confirm something else:==W== completing this mission grants me new powers and higher authority in the system, right?
Tyrant, I am detecting a shift in your attitude toward the system and its missions.
My system indicates you are experiencing confusion.
Heh. For someone who doesn't understand human feelings,==W== you're surprisingly sensitive to my moods.
I hold my phone up. The chess piece on the lanyard catches the sunlight.
It's hard not to change==W== after everything we've been through lately.
Even though I cannot stand by your side, please remember:==W== every other company in this world is your enemy.
Holding this Seal grants immense power.==W== But wielding it when I can barely protect myself...==W==
It is like painting a massive target on my back.
I've only survived this long==W== on pure luck.

From Darcia's twisted loyalty,==W== running into a highly unusual assassin like Otoha at the banquet,==W== the White Room, to my friends backing me up...==W== we've scraped by one crisis after another.==W==
That can't continue.==W== If I want to protect myself and my crew,==W== I need actual power and resources.
Vita,==W== this is what the system wants me to realize, isn't it?
That is correct, Tyrant.==W== But please remember, the system is meant to safeguard your journey,==W== not control your fate.
Its ultimate purpose doesn't matter. I decide where this journey takes me.
You are one step closer to becoming the true Tyrant.==W== I shall take my leave.==W== One day, you will reclaim your rightful throne.
Boss, you made it!==W== Your cute little clerk Bastelina has been waiting ages for you.
Oh, hey Bastelina. It's been a while...==W== Wait,==W== when did you get to Philae?
The bigwigs at the Grace Imperium are completely swamped with the Monolith bidding. They sent me over as backup! I was actually at the banquet earlier, too!
Oh, right! There's someone I want you to meet.==W== This is my senior from the Purchasing Department,==W== Laru.==W==
Hey there. I'm Laru.==W== I'm vetting the bidding qualifications for all the companies this time around.
So if you're the Boss, that makes you the rep for Boss Accord.==W== And United Harvest Philae is using your Seal of Grace for this bid, right?
Yep. As a shareholder, Boss Accord is fully backing United Harvest Philae's bid.
Oh? A joint venture jumping into the bidding war? You guys must have a lot of free time.==W== Anyway,==W== good luck with that.
Straight down to business. She's a serious one.
Right this way, Boss,==W== Lady Firenze.==W== I'll show you to the lounge.
Whoa,==W== it's packed here.==W== I'm seeing a lot of familiar faces from the banquet.
Looks like the Grace Imperium called this Monolith bid on short notice,==W== taking advantage of all the company reps already being in Philae to snoop on the Darcia incident.
Otherwise, rounding all these people up would've taken a month at least.
If that's true...==W== There might be an ulterior motive behind this whole bid.
Wouldn't be the first time the Grace Imperium pulled a stunt like this.==W== Sit tight and rest up. I'm gonna track down some contacts from the other companies and see what I can dig up.
Oh, free drinks and snacks. Nice touch.==W== Munch, munch...==W== These fries aren't bad.
Hold on,==W== why is every single snack bowl filled with fries?!
Oh, hey Laru. Yeah, they're authentic. Taste identical to the ones wished for from the Monolith.
See, Bastelina?==W== Even the Boss appreciates my fries!
That doesn't excuse filling every single bowl with the same snack.
What do you mean "the same"?==W== Look—==W==sea salt, BBQ, cheese!==W== Back me up, Boss.

I knew it!==W== You get me,==W== and you get fries!==W== Here, try this batch.==W== Spirit of Brutality flavor! Eating them feels like getting punched in the face by a fry.==W== The kick is unbelievable!
Weren't you acting completely normal a minute ago?!==W== What's with the sudden fries fanaticism?!
Laru, I have important business to discuss with Boss.==W== Could you take your fries and wait for us over there?
You got it!==W== And for the record, Bastelina explicitly told me to "eat fries while I wait." This isn't slacking off.==W== Catch ya later,==W== Boss!
Thanks for the save, Bastelina.==W== I was about to get force-fed the entire range of fries.
Ahaha, she means well.==W== She's just incredibly passionate about fries. Seeing you enjoy her spread probably made her day.
Can't say I entirely get it, but the fries obsession is loud and clear.==W== Anyway, what was this "important business"?
Oh, that's just a little white lie to rescue a VIP client.==W== Let her keep going, and she'd talk right through the Monolith bidding.
Of course! You emptied your security safe, but I still manage it. That makes you a VIP to your favorite clerk.
And as a client perk,==W== allow me to offer you some ... <color=#bd3059>special services</color>.
Hehe. Won't take up much of your time. Step over here with me please?

strings.text: Before the bid, Bastelina briefs you on your main rivals: Deepsea Finance, the Imperial Guard, and Omnisky Aegis. You secure the bid, but it also leaves your company staring down a massive funding gap...
I follow Bastelina up the stairs into an empty hallway.
Bastelina? Am I even supposed to be here? I saw a "Staff Only" sign.
No worries! Boss is adorable Bastelina's VIP. Calling you authorized personnel isn't a stretch at all! ♪
Really? Authorized? That's more than a stretch...
This hallway overlooks the lounge. Following Bastelina's gaze through a hidden window, I have a clear view of those representatives in the lounge.
Since the Desert Scorpions crashed the banquet, you never got to chat with the company reps.
As the Loongs say: Knowing your enemy is half the fight.
Before the bidding starts, let me walk you through their quirks. Hope it helps.
Oh! That'd be incredibly helpful! Thanks, Bastelina!
Alright... Let's start with the most important one over there—
Ugh, nobody here appreciates the beauty of fries. Tragic.
Oh, I know! I'll put the reheated ones in the conference room!==W== Everyone will want a snack when the bidding gets tense. Aren't I thoughtful <size=50>♪</size>
Weird, why the sudden chill? Is the AC turned up?
Albedo...?! Uh, heh... Hehe. U-um... I haven't done anything to make you mad today... Right?
Sigh... Honestly, why do you always assume I'm here to scold you?==W== Never mind. I need to run final checks. Come with me to the conference room.
Ah, perfect timing! I was actually about to bring some fries in there for a snack break <size=52>♪</size>
In case you didn't know, the Grace Imperium has four parts. Our Soul Shop falls under the Sky Institute.
That was Lady Albedo, Chief Bookkeeper of the Sky Institute, who dragged Laru off. Strictly by the book, she's Laru's superior, and her worst nightmare.
She's overseeing this Monolith bidding. You can count on total fairness.
That armored lady over there is Lady Greyhorn, Knight Commander of the Imperial Guard.
She fights on the front lines, hunting Neo Grace dealers. Her tracking magic always corners her targets—they call her the "Neo Grace Hound."
She values the Guard's image over profit, normally avoiding messy financial events like this.
She's only representing the Imperial Guard at this bidding because she was the closest Knight Commander to Philae. A last-minute fill-in.
Aren't the Imperial Guard a security company? Why would they need a Monolith?
They need steel, and a lot of the steel for their armor only comes from Monolith wishes.
That's the official story, anyway. The truth...==W== Well, I'm crossing a line here. You'll have to dig into that yourself, Boss.
Appreciate it. I'll look into it when the mood strikes.
By the way, Bastelina, one can only participate if they hold a Seal of Grace, meaning everyone here represents a company, right?
Boss Accord meets that bar. But this is a bidding war... What kind of numbers are we talking about?
Setting United Harvest Philae's funds aside, even thinking about Boss Accord's side feels like taking on a century of debt...
This bidding grants ten years of exclusive Monolith access. Going by past averages, a decade's rent easily hits the tens of billions.
Tens of billions...==W== I can already picture the look on Iris's face.
Hehe.==W== I smell it... Oh, I smell it.
Oh? The fries? They do smell appetizing. Let me go grab a plate for you too!
Don't be silly.==W== Not the fries. It's the sweet scent of Dorra.==W== Look at these reps—you can see the greed gleaming in their eyes.
The winning bid will be astronomical. That's when we swoop in and pitch financing to all the poor little ducks desperate for cash.
But what if they play it safe? If the rent stops at around ten billion, they won't really need a loan from us.
If they won't drive up the price, we buy the Monolith ourselves and sublease it. We make a killing either way.
Hehehe, with enough Dorra, you can do whatever you want.
They are Erinis and Meikyo from Deepsea Finance, the top-performing loan officers in the Credit Department last year.
Deepsea Finance is Nova's largest bank, known for fast approvals and fair rates. Boss, if we run short on funds, they might be worth a chat.
The auction will begin shortly. Before it does, take a look at==RT==the woman in the corner of the lounge.
That's Mercurio, sole representative for Omnisky Aegis.
They're a massive insurance firm covering all of Nova, and==RT==word is that they're sitting on a mountain of cash.
Hmph... Quite the crowd at today's auction.
Number Twenty. Go wrangle a few attendees and pitch our new insurance packages.
They're a newer player with only one Monolith under their belt, but don't underestimate them, Boss. They'll be tough to beat.
Exactly. That's the firm Hazana from the Desert Scorpions was impersonating at the banquet.
They've already put out a statement claiming they were totally in the dark—just another victim of the scam.
The Imperial Guard, Deepsea Finance, and now Omnisky Aegis... This is a crowded field of heavy hitters.
Bastelina, what's the deal with that group over there?
That elegant lady in the kimono? That's Shuo,==W== the manager for Goodwind's Philae branch. She's the real deal.
Goodwind doesn't usually bid on Monoliths though. They're likely just here to maintain their presence and network for new clients.
See those two the Scarlet Sights witch is cornering?
They're Xuan Shi from the territory of Loongs. This event is==RT==invite-only, so they must be using "Fenghuang Diner" as a cover.
Hi there! Ophir from Scarlet Sights Media! Got a sec?
Tell us, what's the strategy behind Fenghuang Diner's bid for the Philae Monolith?!
Oh, um, that's a lot... Senior, help! How do I answer this? We're just here for the ride!

Fenghuang Diner is committed to fostering pragmatic cooperation with all representatives through mutual respect. We aim to play a constructive role in Philae's market, driving local growth for the benefit of the community.
We'll share more regarding our bidding strategy and objectives at the appropriate time. No further comments for now.
Uh... Huh? Ah, right...==W== I see. Well, thanks for the insight!
Wow, classic Loong corporate-speak. Total word salad. Did you catch any of that, Boss?
Basically: "We're just tourists with zero interest in the bid, but we can't admit that on the record."
Spot on. Loongs rarely meddle in core affairs outside Cangwu. They're likely just scouting the local market, so they aren't a threat to you.
That's the lineup for today. Bidding's about to start, so let's head into the conference room, Boss.
Right. Still... Something about this feels off.
I know I'm a client, but I'm only renting one safe in your vault. Calling me a "VIP" is a big leap. Why go to all this trouble for me?
Hey, I'm a professional Soul Shop clerk! Helping clients is what I do. Don't worry about it.
Once your company takes off, you'll be renting dozens of safes from us anyway. Consider this an investment in a future big spender!
The room is dead quiet, save for the steady rustle of paper as corporate reps pore over the tender documents.
This Monolith bid will wrap up in one or two rounds. Round one is a public auction to set the lease for the next ten years.
The cap is 40 billion, but everyone's looking to slash costs and snag the rights for cheap. Well, mostly everyone. But...
The "auction" is just a label. The final price is likely a given. That's probably why they've got a second round lined up...
Time to make this system work for me.
HQ won't bridge the funds for tomorrow. Can United Harvest Philae handle this alone?
I've checked the data across Nova from the last five years. Winning bids usually fall between 10 and 18 billion.
We've scraped together 20 billion in liquid assets. Based on the trends, we're in the clear.
If we can stay in the game and hit that 18-billion-Dorra mark, we'll force a technical review.
Time's up. We'll open the floor at 4 billion Dorra.
6.6 billion! It's got a nice ring to it.
You're all moving too slowly.==W== 12 billion.
Whoa... 10 billion already? What do you think?
Bastelina was right. Loongs and Goodwind never wanted the bid. They just threw out token numbers before folding.
Deepsea Finance is just driving up the price. This is down to Firenze and the Imperial Guard.
Hmm, no profit margin left at this point. Deepsea Finance is out.==W== Best of luck, you two. Our doors are open if you need a loan.
United Harvest Philae and the Imperial Guard are tied at 18 billion. Any other offers? Hearing none, these two will proceed to the technical review—
Omnisky Aegis?! I thought they were spectating. Why are they jumping in...?
Insane... There's zero profit left. Why is Omnisky Aegis obsessed with this Monolith?
Besides, anything over twenty billion wipes out our liquid assets. What's the plan, Firenze...?
Before I can finish, Firenze squeezes my hand under the table. A silent message: Don't panic. I have this handled.
40 billion? Are you out of your mind?
Heh... Now things are getting interesting.
40 billion.==W== United Harvest Philae, Imperial Guard—your move?
Boss, hehe...==W== Sorry for going rogue here, but...==W== Care to join me in hell? <size=54>♪</size>
Sorry for the scare back there, Boss.
After the auction, Firenze and I head back to her office.
No need. If the Monolith is essential to United Harvest Philae, it's a necessary expense. Omnisky Aegis and the Imperial Guard were the true wildcards here.
But reality check—how do we cover this 20-billion gap?
We've got three days, right? Has to be in their account by sunset on the 15th?
Yeah. I'll handle it. I made the bid, so I'll find the cash one way or another.
Someone from Grace Imperium mentioned Deepsea Finance. Think we could get a loan there?
Excuse me. Lady Firenze, Boss, an invitation just arrived from Omnisky Aegis.
Their rep, Mercurio, is hosting dinner tonight to discuss the auction. They say they aren't looking to monopolize the Monolith.
"Not looking to monopolize"? What's Mercurio's angle here...
Put my faith in my partner.
Seek a loan from Deepsea Finance
A 20-billion debt would turn Deepsea Finance into an ally.
Take the free meal and see what she's offering.
How do we bridge this 20-billion gap?
If we take a loan from Deepsea Finance or settle with Omnisky Aegis, United Harvest Philae is going to lose its independence.
And if that happens... Firenze, I won't be able to make your wish come true.
You can't get something for nothing. That's just how the world works, right?
Since you said you'd find a way, I'll leave the funding to you.
Grace Imperium's assessment of our wishing ability starts tomorrow—I'll handle that part.
Through thick and thin huh?==W== No problem. I'll scrape up those 20 billion Dorra even if it kills me.
Let's try for a loan from Deepsea Finance.
20 billion... We'll have to give up something big.==W== What are you planning to use as collateral?
How about Boss Accord's Seal of Grace? That should be worth enough to cover it.
But, Boss... That belongs to you.
It belongs to all of us.==W== Besides, this is our best shot at winning the bid and securing United Harvest Philae's future.
If Deepsea Finance lends us that much, they'll be stuck with us whether they like it or not.
Let's take Mercurio up on that dinner and see what she wants.
I'm curious why Omnisky Aegis would pay such a crazy price just for the Monolith's usage rights.
True. What could possibly be worth 20 billion past the break-even point? I'd love to hear her explain that in person.
Yeah. Feels like ... she's after something else.

param: Before the bid, Bastelina briefs you on your main rivals: Deepsea Finance, the Imperial Guard, and Omnisky Aegis. You secure the bid, but it also leaves your company staring down a massive funding gap...
I follow Bastelina up the stairs into an empty hallway.
Bastelina? Am I even supposed to be here? I saw a "Staff Only" sign.
No worries! Boss is adorable Bastelina's VIP. Calling you authorized personnel isn't a stretch at all! ♪
Really? Authorized? That's more than a stretch...
This hallway overlooks the lounge. Following Bastelina's gaze through a hidden window, I have a clear view of those representatives in the lounge.
Since the Desert Scorpions crashed the banquet, you never got to chat with the company reps.
As the Loongs say: Knowing your enemy is half the fight.
Before the bidding starts, let me walk you through their quirks. Hope it helps.
Oh! That'd be incredibly helpful! Thanks, Bastelina!
Alright... Let's start with the most important one over there—
Ugh, nobody here appreciates the beauty of fries. Tragic.
Oh, I know! I'll put the reheated ones in the conference room!==W== Everyone will want a snack when the bidding gets tense. Aren't I thoughtful <size=50>♪</size>
Weird, why the sudden chill? Is the AC turned up?
Albedo...?! Uh, heh... Hehe. U-um... I haven't done anything to make you mad today... Right?
Sigh... Honestly, why do you always assume I'm here to scold you?==W== Never mind. I need to run final checks. Come with me to the conference room.
Ah, perfect timing! I was actually about to bring some fries in there for a snack break <size=52>♪</size>
In case you didn't know, the Grace Imperium has four parts. Our Soul Shop falls under the Sky Institute.
That was Lady Albedo, Chief Bookkeeper of the Sky Institute, who dragged Laru off. Strictly by the book, she's Laru's superior, and her worst nightmare.
She's overseeing this Monolith bidding. You can count on total fairness.
That armored lady over there is Lady Greyhorn, Knight Commander of the Imperial Guard.
She fights on the front lines, hunting Neo Grace dealers. Her tracking magic always corners her targets—they call her the "Neo Grace Hound."
She values the Guard's image over profit, normally avoiding messy financial events like this.
She's only representing the Imperial Guard at this bidding because she was the closest Knight Commander to Philae. A last-minute fill-in.
Aren't the Imperial Guard a security company? Why would they need a Monolith?
They need steel, and a lot of the steel for their armor only comes from Monolith wishes.
That's the official story, anyway. The truth...==W== Well, I'm crossing a line here. You'll have to dig into that yourself, Boss.
Appreciate it. I'll look into it when the mood strikes.
By the way, Bastelina, one can only participate if they hold a Seal of Grace, meaning everyone here represents a company, right?
Boss Accord meets that bar. But this is a bidding war... What kind of numbers are we talking about?
Setting United Harvest Philae's funds aside, even thinking about Boss Accord's side feels like taking on a century of debt...
This bidding grants ten years of exclusive Monolith access. Going by past averages, a decade's rent easily hits the tens of billions.
Tens of billions...==W== I can already picture the look on Iris's face.
Hehe.==W== I smell it... Oh, I smell it.
Oh? The fries? They do smell appetizing. Let me go grab a plate for you too!
Don't be silly.==W== Not the fries. It's the sweet scent of Dorra.==W== Look at these reps—you can see the greed gleaming in their eyes.
The winning bid will be astronomical. That's when we swoop in and pitch financing to all the poor little ducks desperate for cash.
But what if they play it safe? If the rent stops at around ten billion, they won't really need a loan from us.
If they won't drive up the price, we buy the Monolith ourselves and sublease it. We make a killing either way.
Hehehe, with enough Dorra, you can do whatever you want.
They are Erinis and Meikyo from Deepsea Finance, the top-performing loan officers in the Credit Department last year.
Deepsea Finance is Nova's largest bank, known for fast approvals and fair rates. Boss, if we run short on funds, they might be worth a chat.
The auction will begin shortly. Before it does, take a look at==RT==the woman in the corner of the lounge.
That's Mercurio, sole representative for Omnisky Aegis.
They're a massive insurance firm covering all of Nova, and==RT==word is that they're sitting on a mountain of cash.
Hmph... Quite the crowd at today's auction.
Number Twenty. Go wrangle a few attendees and pitch our new insurance packages.
They're a newer player with only one Monolith under their belt, but don't underestimate them, Boss. They'll be tough to beat.
Exactly. That's the firm Hazana from the Desert Scorpions was impersonating at the banquet.
They've already put out a statement claiming they were totally in the dark—just another victim of the scam.
The Imperial Guard, Deepsea Finance, and now Omnisky Aegis... This is a crowded field of heavy hitters.
Bastelina, what's the deal with that group over there?
That elegant lady in the kimono? That's Shuo,==W== the manager for Goodwind's Philae branch. She's the real deal.
Goodwind doesn't usually bid on Monoliths though. They're likely just here to maintain their presence and network for new clients.
See those two the Scarlet Sights witch is cornering?
They're Xuan Shi from the territory of Loongs. This event is==RT==invite-only, so they must be using "Fenghuang Diner" as a cover.
Hi there! Ophir from Scarlet Sights Media! Got a sec?
Tell us, what's the strategy behind Fenghuang Diner's bid for the Philae Monolith?!
Oh, um, that's a lot... Senior, help! How do I answer this? We're just here for the ride!

Fenghuang Diner is committed to fostering pragmatic cooperation with all representatives through mutual respect. We aim to play a constructive role in Philae's market, driving local growth for the benefit of the community.
We'll share more regarding our bidding strategy and objectives at the appropriate time. No further comments for now.
Uh... Huh? Ah, right...==W== I see. Well, thanks for the insight!
Wow, classic Loong corporate-speak. Total word salad. Did you catch any of that, Boss?
Basically: "We're just tourists with zero interest in the bid, but we can't admit that on the record."
Spot on. Loongs rarely meddle in core affairs outside Cangwu. They're likely just scouting the local market, so they aren't a threat to you.
That's the lineup for today. Bidding's about to start, so let's head into the conference room, Boss.
Right. Still... Something about this feels off.
I know I'm a client, but I'm only renting one safe in your vault. Calling me a "VIP" is a big leap. Why go to all this trouble for me?
Hey, I'm a professional Soul Shop clerk! Helping clients is what I do. Don't worry about it.
Once your company takes off, you'll be renting dozens of safes from us anyway. Consider this an investment in a future big spender!
The room is dead quiet, save for the steady rustle of paper as corporate reps pore over the tender documents.
This Monolith bid will wrap up in one or two rounds. Round one is a public auction to set the lease for the next ten years.
The cap is 40 billion, but everyone's looking to slash costs and snag the rights for cheap. Well, mostly everyone. But...
The "auction" is just a label. The final price is likely a given. That's probably why they've got a second round lined up...
Time to make this system work for me.
HQ won't bridge the funds for tomorrow. Can United Harvest Philae handle this alone?
I've checked the data across Nova from the last five years. Winning bids usually fall between 10 and 18 billion.
We've scraped together 20 billion in liquid assets. Based on the trends, we're in the clear.
If we can stay in the game and hit that 18-billion-Dorra mark, we'll force a technical review.
Time's up. We'll open the floor at 4 billion Dorra.
6.6 billion! It's got a nice ring to it.
You're all moving too slowly.==W== 12 billion.
Whoa... 10 billion already? What do you think?
Bastelina was right. Loongs and Goodwind never wanted the bid. They just threw out token numbers before folding.
Deepsea Finance is just driving up the price. This is down to Firenze and the Imperial Guard.
Hmm, no profit margin left at this point. Deepsea Finance is out.==W== Best of luck, you two. Our doors are open if you need a loan.
United Harvest Philae and the Imperial Guard are tied at 18 billion. Any other offers? Hearing none, these two will proceed to the technical review—
Omnisky Aegis?! I thought they were spectating. Why are they jumping in...?
Insane... There's zero profit left. Why is Omnisky Aegis obsessed with this Monolith?
Besides, anything over twenty billion wipes out our liquid assets. What's the plan, Firenze...?
Before I can finish, Firenze squeezes my hand under the table. A silent message: Don't panic. I have this handled.
40 billion? Are you out of your mind?
Heh... Now things are getting interesting.
40 billion.==W== United Harvest Philae, Imperial Guard—your move?
Boss, hehe...==W== Sorry for going rogue here, but...==W== Care to join me in hell? <size=54>♪</size>
Sorry for the scare back there, Boss.
After the auction, Firenze and I head back to her office.
No need. If the Monolith is essential to United Harvest Philae, it's a necessary expense. Omnisky Aegis and the Imperial Guard were the true wildcards here.
But reality check—how do we cover this 20-billion gap?
We've got three days, right? Has to be in their account by sunset on the 15th?
Yeah. I'll handle it. I made the bid, so I'll find the cash one way or another.
Deepsea Finance is Nova's largest bank, known for fast approvals and fair rates. Boss, if we run short on funds, they might be worth a chat.
Someone from Grace Imperium mentioned Deepsea Finance. Think we could get a loan there?
Excuse me. Lady Firenze, Boss, an invitation just arrived from Omnisky Aegis.
Their rep, Mercurio, is hosting dinner tonight to discuss the auction. They say they aren't looking to monopolize the Monolith.
"Not looking to monopolize"? What's Mercurio's angle here...
Put my faith in my partner.
Seek a loan from Deepsea Finance
A 20-billion debt would turn Deepsea Finance into an ally.
Take the free meal and see what she's offering.
How do we bridge this 20-billion gap?
If we take a loan from Deepsea Finance or settle with Omnisky Aegis, United Harvest Philae is going to lose its independence.
And if that happens... Firenze, I won't be able to make your wish come true.
You can't get something for nothing. That's just how the world works, right?
Since you said you'd find a way, I'll leave the funding to you.
Grace Imperium's assessment of our wishing ability starts tomorrow—I'll handle that part.
Through thick and thin huh?==W== No problem. I'll scrape up those 20 billion Dorra even if it kills me.
Let's try for a loan from Deepsea Finance.
20 billion... We'll have to give up something big.==W== What are you planning to use as collateral?
How about Boss Accord's Seal of Grace? That should be worth enough to cover it.
But, Boss... That belongs to you.
It belongs to all of us.==W== Besides, this is our best shot at winning the bid and securing United Harvest Philae's future.
If Deepsea Finance lends us that much, they'll be stuck with us whether they like it or not.
Let's take Mercurio up on that dinner and see what she wants.
I'm curious why Omnisky Aegis would pay such a crazy price just for the Monolith's usage rights.
True. What could possibly be worth 20 billion past the break-even point? I'd love to hear her explain that in person.
Yeah. Feels like ... she's after something else.

strings.text: You and Firenze put your heads together to find a way out. Inside an old safe, you uncover a letter from Darcia. Even now, her fierce loyalty and resolve reach across time, striking right at your heart.
Through thick and thin huh? I'm in. I'll scrape up those 20 billion Dorra even if it kills me.
Don't jinx it.==W== I'm still banking on those free Tawny Nightingales on the company's dime.
If you're gone,==W== who's gonna feed us?
Oh?==W== So my life is worth less than a free Tawny Nightingale?
Ah, hey,==W== that's not what I meant...!
I'm kidding, Boss. I appreciate you trying to lighten the mood.==W== But don't worry, a little pressure won't break me.
Though honestly, raising 20 billion Dorra in two days borders on the impossible.
But with all the corporate reps gathered here in Philae—and a few already dropping out—==W==20 billion isn't a pipe dream.==W== Expect good news.
As for your end, Omnisky Aegis knows they can't beat you and the New Star Guild at making wishes.
You mean ...==W== like at the banquet? Hiring assassins and mercenaries to ambush us?
They might avoid direct violence.==W== There are plenty of ways to sabotage your wishing without firing a shot.
Let's face it, Boss, you're practically a celebrity now.==W== With a target that big on your back, tracking the Boss Accord is almost too easy for Omnisky Aegis.
You need a wildcard in the shadows—someone off the other companies' radar.==W== Oh, what about that maid?==W== Can you still reach her?
If you mean Otoha,==W== I've tried messaging her a few times since the banquet.==W== Total silence.
Hmm. I'll figure something out.==W== Get some rest, Boss. You have a Monolith to climb tomorrow.
... Ruby?==W== Excuse me a second, Boss.
Lady Firenze, good news!==W== We finally cracked that safe!
The safe? Heh, excellent work.==W== I'm heading over now.
Sorry about this, Boss, but could you stick around a bit longer?==W== There's something you need to see.
We've cleared out the Intelligent Plants since Darcia's passing,==W== and in that process, Ruby found a safe hidden inside one of the incubators.
It's a four-digit code, so I just started guessing from 9999. Finally cracked it at 0606.==W== Ugh, I'd have saved so much time==W== if I'd started from 0000 instead.
I told her to start from 0000, but she insisted 9999 would be faster.==W== Took us three days of messing around to get it open.
Whatever,==W== it's open now!==W== Let's see what secrets Darcia was keeping in here!
A bearer check from Deepsea Finance?==W==<size=58> Wait, for ... 2 billion?!</size>==W==
There's a letter, too. It's addressed to ...==W== ==SEX12== Tyrant.
A letter for me ... from Darcia?
By the time you read this, I'll likely be nothing more than a withered branch, burned to ash or buried in the dirt.
It means you've chosen a future with your companions, and in doing so, you've rejected one with me.
Truthfully, reaching this end leaves a bitter taste. But if this is the path you've chosen, I'll accept it and take my leave.
There's something I never told you. While I spent every day longing for your arrival, I feared it just as much.

Even if granted an audience, was I ever worthy of your salvation? Could I ever earn your approval? It's embarrassing to admit, but despite my bravado, I have no real talent. I know I lack the capability to stand by your side.
Even after all my research, I knew deep down that these soulless plants—no matter how strong they seemed—weren't the power you sought.
Perhaps this sounds like an excuse, the bitter rambling of a loser. But in the end, I simply wasn't worth saving. That's all there is to it.
If, on the day you reclaim your throne, you remember that a soul once offered you everything—that my devotion never wavered despite my fate—then my life was not in vain.
To wither away holding that belief... There is no happier end for me.
The Dorra in this safe came from selling my family's estate. It's clean money, and my way of cutting ties with a past I'd rather forget. Please, use it freely.
It may seem like a pittance when the world eventually turns against you, but being able to help, even in this small way, is my greatest honor.
I wish I could hear back from you, though I know that's wishful thinking.
35 days ago.==RT==The day Firenze finalized plans with Petal Bloom and the New Star Guild to launch the assassination.
Lady Darcia. Field recon is complete. I have the report here...
Stop right there, Firenze. You shouldn't be reporting to me.==W== ==SEX12== Tyrant must be the first to hear any intelligence.
My apologies. I'll keep that in mind.
Good. ==SEX12== Tyrant recently retired to bed. Go wake ==SEX2== Majesty and bring ==SEX4== down to the lab. I need to make preparations.
Your Majesty, your light is still on. Did you leave it on for her?
It's time I put that letter away.
I'll set the passcode to the day I first read your story. The day you saved me.
I only hope my feelings reach you, Your Majesty...
And now...==W== I must face my end.==W==
Um... Lady Firenze? Boss?==W== What does the letter say?
... Alright, time for us to head back, Ruby. We still have paperwork to finish.==W== Boss, Lady Firenze,==W== we'll take our leave.
Darcia... I will never forgive you as Firenze de Feltro.==W== But ... your feelings have certainly reached Boss.
You don't need to worry anymore.==W== Rest easy.
I should get back to work.==W== We'll all be busy starting tomorrow—
Wait, Firenze. Take this check.==W== That makes a tenth of the 20 billion we need.
Her letter reads like she knew this would happen.==W== If this is what Darcia wanted, we should accept it and put the money to good use.
Understood. We'll do it your way.==W== See you tomorrow, Boss.
I slide down against the open safe door and close my eyes.==RT==Memories of our time together in this room wash over me.
I'm sorry.==W== If I were stronger...==W== Maybe I could have saved you, too...==W==
If I had reached you==W== before you made that choice...==W== Would things be different now?
May you...==W== May you...==W== Find peace at last.
