strings.text: You and Firenze secure a massive loan from Deepsea Finance. Refusing to give up your shares, you put two Seals of Grace on the line as collateral instead.
Thank you for visiting Deepsea Finance today. I'm Erinis, Credit Department Manager.==W== We've been expecting you. It's an honor that United Harvest Philae trusts us with this.
Let me guess—==W==you're here about the bidding deposit,==W== right?
How much capital==W== are you looking for?
Wait,<size=52> 40 billion?==W== That's the entire bid!</size>
Exactly.==W== But you look surprised.==W== Is the number too high for the manager who was expecting us?
Hmm, no profit margin left at this point.==W== Deepsea Finance is out. Best of luck, you two. Our doors are open if you need a loan.
W-==W==well,==W== of course not!==W== The phrase "too high" doesn't exist in our dictionary.
It's just...==W== As the Credit Manager, I have to be careful with a transaction of this scale.
Frankly, it's a terrible deal.==W== 40 billion shatters every record for Monolith rent.==W== Meikyo—==W==
On it!==W== Nice to meet you both, I'm Meikyo from Credit.==W== I'll be assisting Erinis.
I ran the numbers. Between this rent, hiring Trekkers to climb the tower, facility maintenance, and Artifact taxes to the Grace Imperium...==W== You'll never break even on a ten-year lease.
Economically,==W== you're much better off hiring Trekkers for the Monoliths out in the Wilds.
Flawless analysis.==W== But you both know==W== owning a City Monolith was never just about math.
Understood.==W== We really do.==W== And with a sum this large, Deepsea Finance certainly won't turn you away.
However...==W== Lending this much capital==W== means we take on immense risk.
So,==W== to offset that risk,==W== we typically hike up the interest rate.
Expected. So,==W== let's hear the number.
... The rumors about your efficiency were true. Alright.==W== Last month,==W== a company took out a ten-billion emergency loan at a 15 percent annual rate.
15 percent...==W== That's 6 billion Dorra a year in interest. That's not a heavy burden—that's crippling...
But after your speech at the banquet,==W== Boss, I imagine a lot of companies felt inspired.
Factor in United Harvest Philae's track record,==W== and I'd personally give you top marks for credit.
Taking all that into account...==W== We're prepared to offer a 5 percent annual rate.
Strange as this sounds coming from me, nothing comes that cheap.==W== A loan this massive at five percent means there's a catch. What else do you want?
Hehe, dealing with smart people does make things easy.==W== Deepsea Finance wants a grain purchase agreement with United Harvest Philae.
Until the loan is paid off, we get the first right of refusal on your grain and food products.==W== The price will be locked at the ten-year market average.
Given our situation, we accept.==W== But==W== is Deepsea Finance looking to break into the grain market?
Oh, no.==W== We don't hold the franchise patents for that.==W== It's strictly a hedge—part of our standard risk management.
40 billion negotiated that easily?==W== Deepsea Finance is definitely hiding their real angle.
Well then! Since we agree on the amount, the rate, and the terms, that leaves one thing—collateral.==W== A 40-billion loan requires 60 billion in assets to back it up.
Producing 60 billion in collateral is no small feat.==W== What are you bringing to the table?
From what I hear, the Senate holds 49 percent of United Harvest Philae.==W== Are you mortgaging your remaining shares?
They want the shares? Combine that with the purchase agreement,==W== and I guess their real goal is to corner a stable bulk grain supply. But why?==W== Grain market profit margins aren't high.
I absolutely can't use the shares.==W== Matilda entrusted those to me. They belong to everyone.
We're using this Seal of Grace as collateral.
Oh my, a surprise. Handing over a precious Seal of Grace, franchise patents and all?==W== Still... It's a solid offer.
I sincerely apologize, Boss.==W== This Seal of Grace falls short of the required value.
This is the seal you acquired during the company war in Emor—Creta Trading's Seal of Grace, is it not?
It is. Is there a problem?
Its franchise patents are strictly for mining.
Mining is lucrative. Shouldn't this be worth 60 billion?
20 years ago, it would have fetched a hundred billion easily.==W== But there hasn't been an active mine in Nova for two decades now.

Grand Inspector Matilda... No, it's CEO Matilda now. She won.

We're walking a tightrope. One slip and we're done for.
But doing nothing means a slow death. This market drags us down anyway.

strings.text: You and Firenze take Mercurio's tempting wager. But a year later, she leaves the company, and Omnisky Aegis springs their trap. Blindsided and ambushed, you fall into a desperate situation, with your fates unknown...
Thank you for coming. It's a pleasure to finally be able to talk face-to-face.
Apologies for the modest venue. I arranged this to clear the air:==W== Omnisky Aegis has no desire to make enemies of United Harvest Philae or Boss Accord.
I like Loong food, but ...==W== isn't it a bit loud in here?
The noise prevents eavesdropping. Besides, this is a Loong establishment. You don't have to worry about me pulling tricks—==W==like hiding assassins out in the hall.
I'm curious. Why is Omnisky Aegis fighting so hard for the Monolith? 40 billion is a terrible deal.
You're right. In fact, we aren't attached to leasing it at all. Say the word, and my company will drop our bid.
So...==W== You only bid to drive up the price and meddle with us?
Oh, we aren't that petty. We had our reasons. It all goes back to that banquet...
So...==W== You needed a distraction. You used the auction to make headlines.
Precisely. Omnisky Aegis could use a new Monolith, but we aren't desperate enough to blow 40 billion Dorra on one.
Hmph. You have it all figured out. You walk away, and we're stuck with a 40-billion lease.
True. And we feel awful about that. That's why I'm proposing a win-win solution.
You must be wondering how you'll scrape that money together. To show our good faith, Omnisky Aegis will cover half the lease. 20 billion Dorra.
United Harvest Philae keeps full usage rights. We ask for 30 percent of the climbing rights—for every ten climbs, our Trekkers take three.
You're putting up 20 billion, but you don't want usage rights or even half the climbs. Only 30 percent.
Lady Mercurio, those terms are too generous.
Naturally, there are strings attached.==W== Omnisky Aegis would like to propose a wager.
If you two still work for United Harvest Philae at the next Monolith bid in ten years, Omnisky Aegis won't contest the rights—we'll help you win.
But if you no longer work for United Harvest Philae by then, we expect the company to withdraw and do everything possible to help us win.
A wager on where we'll be in ten years... Fair enough.==W== But why stake this on Boss and me?
Omnisky Aegis considers you two far more valuable—and better allies—than the company itself.
We're offering these terms purely because you're at the helm. We're happy to spend extra Dorra to clear the air.
If you stay in charge, we stand as your allies. But if you step away, we expect your help in taking over Philae ourselves.
Then it looks like we're allies. Firenze and I will never consider abandoning this company.
That works for us. Omnisky Aegis lacks grand ambitions. We only want reliable partners in this chaotic world of Nova.
Her terms sound sincere, but I can't tell how true they are. I'll need to read every clause of that magic contract carefully.
Mercurio, we need to discuss this privately. Barring any surprises, we'll accept the wager.
Heh. Then, to our working together. Cheers.
Hold on. Now that business is settled, we have a personal question. Can you tell us about your new life insurance policies?
Oh? You're looking for insurance? Welcome. We offer several types: medical, life, and comprehensive. Which one interests you?
Life insurance? Hmm. People ask about it, but no one ever follows through.
After all, the policy is simple: if the insured passes away under the contract's terms, the beneficiary gets a payout.
Most people see it as betting your own life against Omnisky Aegis for a payout.
But we aren't selling a death payout. We're selling proof of your value. You two are exceptional. If the worst happens, this protects your families.
Honestly, I pushed for this policy myself, so no other child ends up like me.
Picture me as a kid. My family gets into a terrible crash.
My parents shield my sister and me. They take the hit and end==RT==up in the hospital, kept breathing only by a Monolith Artifact.
We sell everything. We drown in debt. And we still lose them.
As they die, their worst agony isn't physical.==RT==It's knowing they leave us with nothing.
They beg us to stop wasting Dorra on them.
But how do we pull the plug?==RT==We lose them anyway, and go bankrupt.
Someday I'll be a mother. I push this policy so I never experience that regret again.
I have no idea there's such heartbreak behind this.==W== It says death insurance, but it's a beautiful way to protect people.
Understood. Put us down for a thousand policies each.
Firenze, I know that her story is heartbreaking, but isn't that amount overkill?
100 thousand Dorra per policy. A thousand each means 200 million a year. We can't afford that!
Boss, what if I tell you her parents are alive and perfectly healthy?
Well, that's great news...==W== Wait, what? Alive? Didn't she say they died in a car crash?
That's her pitch. From what I hear, her parents have died a dozen different ways by now.
That's ... messed up. She really commits to the con. So why are you still buying the policies?
She plays the respectful host at dinner. It seems Omnisky Aegis wants to avoid a war.
But we can't ignore the wager they propose. It's a trap.
You mean ...==W== they plan to kill us to win the bet?
Exactly. The wager is tied to United Harvest Philae. Even if we drop dead, it's legally binding.
That's why I bought the policies. At our age, dying within 20 years triggers a 100-million payout per policy.
A thousand policies are 100 billion. 200 billion total for both of us...
Precisely. Now, they not only get nothing from killing us—it bankrupts them entirely.
I see. 200 million a year is a low price to keep them off our backs.
By the way, Boss. Who's your beneficiary?
Lucky them. If Omnisky Aegis murders us anyway, they walk away with 200 billion.
Because my beneficiary is you, Boss.
Mercurio wasn't bluffing. The next day, Omnisky Aegis drops out and sends 20 billion Dorra to United Harvest.
The Imperial Guard follows suit.==W== The Philae Monolith bidding ends before the second technical review even begins.==W== As the sole candidate, United Harvest Philae wins.
After that, we enjoy a peaceful stretch.==W== I stay in Philae to help Firenze build the company. The New Star Guild and Petal Bloom keep trekking,==W== bouncing from Monolith to Monolith.
The company's finally on stable footing. Time to hit the road with Noya and the others to hunt for the orphanage.
Huh? Mercurio? Calling me? That's new.
Morning. Here for next year's premium? Firenze already sent the payment.
Ah, thanks for the business. But that's not why I'm calling. I just quit Omnisky Aegis. I want to say goodbye.
Quit? Aren't you doing great? I hear you basically run half the company.
Heh, you're not wrong. But it just hit me...==W== This job is meaningless. Absolutely meaningless.
I may not look it, but I'm one of the few decent people there. Once I'm gone, watch your back.
Hey, is Omnisky Aegis secretly a mob front?
... Hah, maybe it is. Goodbye, Boss.
Mercurio's quitting...==W== Something feels off. I should call Firenze.
Urgh—Something's strangling me...==W== I-I can't breathe—
==SEX1== went without oxygen for too long. The brain damage is irreversible.==W== ==SEX1=='s alive, but ... there's no telling if ==SEX== will ever wake up.
Boss, it's me, Iris. Can you hear me? Listen. I'm singing the song that woke you up.
Master... You'll pull through this, right? You have to.==RT==You still have so much to teach me.
Boss, your assailant has been riddled with my bullets.==RT==Hurry up and wake up. We have claw machines to play!
The sun is warm today. Look, I bring you flowers from the base==RT==of the Monolith. Everyone in Petal Bloom is waiting for you.
You idiot! You broke your promise! You massive idiot!
Thanks to you, the Ashwind kids thrive.==RT==I read to you every day... Can you hear me?
Come on, Boss, this makes for a terrible headline.
Tell you what—you wake up, and I'll make an exception.==RT==I take you flying for as long as you want.
You and Firenze, both stuck in bed... And here I am, awake,==RT==when I'm the one who actually likes sleeping.
Forgive me, my ==SEX11==. I arrived too late. From now on,==RT==I'm staying by your side. I'll never leave you again.
If you never wake... Then I'll follow you into the next world.
What... What is happening to me?
Someone strangled you on the street. At that exact moment, mercenaries ambushed Firenze.
Their method was precise. They didn't kill you, just choked you out long enough to cause irreversible damage.
The human brain is fragile. A few minutes without oxygen guarantees irreversible damage.
You and Firenze are neither living nor dead. You appear alive, but unplug the medical Artifacts, and you die instantly.
Your companions refuse to give up. They nurse you for over a decade. But eventually, your organs fail, and you die.
A cruel strategy. Your friends tear that company apart to avenge you, but neither you nor Firenze can ever speak to them again.
What a sick scheme—stealing Philae while dodging the life insurance payout.
Hehe... They'll do absolutely anything for Dorra.
I was too naive. I thought contracts and insurance would keep them honest.
Vita, open the door. I'm taking these memories back with me.
Someday,==W== I'll wipe Omnisky Aegis off the map.
"Not looking to monopolize"? What's Mercurio's angle here...
And to think Mercurio really passes for decent at Omnisky Aegis.
There's no way we're working with this company.

param: You and Firenze take Mercurio's tempting wager. But a year later, she leaves the company, and Omnisky Aegis springs their trap. Blindsided and ambushed, you fall into a desperate situation, with your fates unknown...
Thank you for coming. It's a pleasure to finally be able to talk face-to-face.
Apologies for the modest venue. I arranged this to clear the air:==W== Omnisky Aegis has no desire to make enemies of United Harvest Philae or Boss Accord.
I like Loong food, but ...==W== isn't it a bit loud in here?
The noise prevents eavesdropping. Besides, this is a Loong establishment. You don't have to worry about me pulling tricks—==W==like hiding assassins out in the hall.
I'm curious. Why is Omnisky Aegis fighting so hard for the Monolith? 40 billion is a terrible deal.
You're right. In fact, we aren't attached to leasing it at all. Say the word, and my company will drop our bid.
So...==W== You only bid to drive up the price and meddle with us?
Oh, we aren't that petty. We had our reasons. It all goes back to that banquet...
So...==W== You needed a distraction. You used the auction to make headlines.
Precisely. Omnisky Aegis could use a new Monolith, but we aren't desperate enough to blow 40 billion Dorra on one.
Hmph. You have it all figured out. You walk away, and we're stuck with a 40-billion lease.
True. And we feel awful about that. That's why I'm proposing a win-win solution.
You must be wondering how you'll scrape that money together. To show our good faith, Omnisky Aegis will cover half the lease. 20 billion Dorra.
United Harvest Philae keeps full usage rights. We ask for 30 percent of the climbing rights—for every ten climbs, our Trekkers take three.
You're putting up 20 billion, but you don't want usage rights or even half the climbs. Only 30 percent.
Lady Mercurio, those terms are too generous.
Naturally, there are strings attached.==W== Omnisky Aegis would like to propose a wager.
If you two still work for United Harvest Philae at the next Monolith bid in ten years, Omnisky Aegis won't contest the rights—we'll help you win.
But if you no longer work for United Harvest Philae by then, we expect the company to withdraw and do everything possible to help us win.
A wager on where we'll be in ten years... Fair enough.==W== But why stake this on Boss and me?
Omnisky Aegis considers you two far more valuable—and better allies—than the company itself.
We're offering these terms purely because you're at the helm. We're happy to spend extra Dorra to clear the air.
If you stay in charge, we stand as your allies. But if you step away, we expect your help in taking over Philae ourselves.
Then it looks like we're allies. Firenze and I will never consider abandoning this company.
That works for us. Omnisky Aegis lacks grand ambitions. We only want reliable partners in this chaotic world of Nova.
Her terms sound sincere, but I can't tell how true they are. I'll need to read every clause of that magic contract carefully.
Mercurio, we need to discuss this privately. Barring any surprises, we'll accept the wager.
Heh. Then, to our working together. Cheers.
Hold on. Now that business is settled, we have a personal question. Can you tell us about your new life insurance policies?
Oh? You're looking for insurance? Welcome. We offer several types: medical, life, and comprehensive. Which one interests you?
Life insurance? Hmm. People ask about it, but no one ever follows through.
After all, the policy is simple: if the insured passes away under the contract's terms, the beneficiary gets a payout.
Most people see it as betting your own life against Omnisky Aegis for a payout.
But we aren't selling a death payout. We're selling proof of your value. You two are exceptional. If the worst happens, this protects your families.
Honestly, I pushed for this policy myself, so no other child ends up like me.
Picture me as a kid. My family gets into a terrible crash.
My parents shield my sister and me. They take the hit and end==RT==up in the hospital, kept breathing only by a Monolith Artifact.
We sell everything. We drown in debt. And we still lose them.
As they die, their worst agony isn't physical.==RT==It's knowing they leave us with nothing.
They beg us to stop wasting Dorra on them.
But how do we pull the plug?==RT==We lose them anyway, and go bankrupt.
Someday I'll be a mother. I push this policy so I never experience that regret again.
I have no idea there's such heartbreak behind this.==W== It says death insurance, but it's a beautiful way to protect people.
Understood. Put us down for a thousand policies each.
Firenze, I know that her story is heartbreaking, but isn't that amount overkill?
100 thousand Dorra per policy. A thousand each means 200 million a year. We can't afford that!
Boss, what if I tell you her parents are alive and perfectly healthy?
Well, that's great news...==W== Wait, what? Alive? Didn't she say they died in a car crash?
That's her pitch. From what I hear, her parents have died a dozen different ways by now.
That's ... messed up. She really commits to the con. So why are you still buying the policies?
She plays the respectful host at dinner. It seems Omnisky Aegis wants to avoid a war.
But we can't ignore the wager they propose. It's a trap.
You mean ...==W== they plan to kill us to win the bet?
Exactly. The wager is tied to United Harvest Philae. Even if we drop dead, it's legally binding.
That's why I bought the policies. At our age, dying within 20 years triggers a 100-million payout per policy.
A thousand policies are 100 billion. 200 billion total for both of us...
Precisely. Now, they not only get nothing from killing us—it bankrupts them entirely.
I see. 200 million a year is a low price to keep them off our backs.
By the way, Boss. Who's your beneficiary?
Lucky them. If Omnisky Aegis murders us anyway, they walk away with 200 billion.
Because my beneficiary is you, Boss.
Mercurio wasn't bluffing. The next day, Omnisky Aegis drops out and sends 20 billion Dorra to United Harvest.
The Imperial Guard follows suit.==W== The Philae Monolith bidding ends before the second technical review even begins.==W== As the sole candidate, United Harvest Philae wins.
After that, we enjoy a peaceful stretch.==W== I stay in Philae to help Firenze build the company. The New Star Guild and Petal Bloom keep trekking,==W== bouncing from Monolith to Monolith.
The company's finally on stable footing. Time to hit the road with Noya and the others to hunt for the orphanage.
Huh? Mercurio? Calling me? That's new.
Morning. Here for next year's premium? Firenze already sent the payment.
Ah, thanks for the business. But that's not why I'm calling. I just quit Omnisky Aegis. I want to say goodbye.
Quit? Aren't you doing great? I hear you basically run half the company.
Heh, you're not wrong. But it just hit me...==W== This job is meaningless. Absolutely meaningless.
I may not look it, but I'm one of the few decent people there. Once I'm gone, watch your back.
Hey, is Omnisky Aegis secretly a mob front?
... Hah, maybe it is. Goodbye, Boss.
Mercurio's quitting...==W== Something feels off. I should call Firenze.
Urgh—Something's strangling me...==W== I-I can't breathe—
==SEX1== went without oxygen for too long. The brain damage is irreversible.==W== ==SEX1=='s alive, but ... there's no telling if ==SEX== will ever wake up.
Boss, it's me, Iris. Can you hear me? Listen. I'm singing the song that woke you up.
Master... You'll pull through this, right? You have to.==RT==You still have so much to teach me.
Boss, your assailant has been riddled with my bullets.==RT==Hurry up and wake up. We have claw machines to play!
The sun is warm today. Look, I bring you flowers from the base==RT==of the Monolith. Everyone in Petal Bloom is waiting for you.
You idiot! You broke your promise! You massive idiot!
Thanks to you, the Ashwind kids thrive.==RT==I read to you every day... Can you hear me?
Come on, Boss, this makes for a terrible headline.
Tell you what—you wake up, and I'll make an exception.==RT==I take you flying for as long as you want.
You and Firenze, both stuck in bed... And here I am, awake,==RT==when I'm the one who actually likes sleeping.
Forgive me, my ==SEX11==. I arrived too late. From now on,==RT==I'm staying by your side. I'll never leave you again.
If you never wake... Then I'll follow you into the next world.
What... What is happening to me?
Someone strangled you on the street. At that exact moment, mercenaries ambushed Firenze.
Their method was precise. They didn't kill you, just choked you out long enough to cause irreversible damage.
The human brain is fragile. A few minutes without oxygen guarantees irreversible damage.
You and Firenze are neither living nor dead. You appear alive, but unplug the medical Artifacts, and you die instantly.
Your companions refuse to give up. They nurse you for over a decade. But eventually, your organs fail, and you die.
A cruel strategy. Your friends tear that company apart to avenge you, but neither you nor Firenze can ever speak to them again.
What a sick scheme—stealing Philae while dodging the life insurance payout.
Hehe... They'll do absolutely anything for Dorra.
I was too naive. I thought contracts and insurance would keep them honest.
Vita, open the door. I'm taking these memories back with me.
Someday,==W== I'll wipe Omnisky Aegis off the map.
"Not looking to monopolize"? What's Mercurio's angle here...
And to think Mercurio really passes for decent at Omnisky Aegis.
There's no way we're working with this company.

strings.text: The bidding is far from over. Round two: wish for the Scepter of Death. Meanwhile, intel hints at something lurking inside the lake Monolith. Out on the streets of Philae, you see someone familiar, quietly praying…
Morning, Mercurio!==W== It's beautiful here in Geminia today. How's the weather in Philae?
Madame CEO. The weather doesn't affect our premiums. Please get to the point.
Oh, Merky. All business, zero fun.==W== I was just trying to catch up!
And drop the "Madame CEO" routine. It's so cold. I'm your big sister, right?
That was an exception. I use titles on the clock. It's my policy.
Stuffy as ever.==W== Fine, to business. You killed it at the Monolith auction.
Every paper in town is running the same headline: Omnisky Aegis Drops a Bizarre 40 Billion on Philae Monolith. The Desert Scorpion scandal is ancient history.
The whole city is talking about our bid. They see us as an absolute financial juggernaut now, and their willingness to purchase has increased.
Your stock has never been higher.==W== The numbers speak for themselves—they can't deny it.
So, once this wraps up, you're transferring back to HQ. I'm handing you the entire Marketing Department.
I must decline. Philae is exactly where I need to be.
What?==W== Why?==W== Do you hate working with me that much?
First, diversification of risk. If we're both in Geminia, it's too easy for the Senate to wipe us out in one fell swoop.
Wipe us out? It shouldn't go that far.==W== Usually, when a CEO and a Senator clash, someone loses a debate and steps down.
Should I remind you of the banquet? A United Harvest Senator hired assassins to kill Firenze over the Philae branch authority.
Second, you fought hard to get me this authority. If I go back to Geminia, I have to give it up.
Well, you have the point there.==W== You were never meant to keep that authority anyway. The PR fire is put out, so you have to hand it back.
Play keep-away with it, and even I won't be able to cover for you.
The PR fire. Right...==W== Let's talk money.==W== Do we have the 40 billion Dorra ready?
Of course. I transferred liquid assets from several branches.==W== We take a narrow loss in the wishing test, then wire the funds back in a few days. That's the plan.
Mercurio. Why are you quiet? Don't tell me you actually want the Philae Monolith.==W== 40 billion is just the rent! It's a complete money pit.
It's the only way we keep our power.
Merky, be reasonable.==W== Omnisky Aegis doesn't have 40 billion Dorra to set on fire.
40 billion...==W== Spending that much capital drains our cash flow.==W== What good is authority if the company goes under?
Relax.==W== A client from Geminia is dropping a massive contract in our laps today.==W== Insuring their entire workforce.
I'll route them to your office. Consider it a gift—our esteemed CEO takes home top sales rep this year.
Uh... My secretary just flagged a VIP walk-in.
Wait, how on earth is it this company?!
I tried inviting Firenze and that Boss to dinner last night to hash out a win-win.==W== They were unexpectedly cautious and shot me down.
When I was struggling to find a way out, this company's rep came knocking.
Their only condition for this multi-billion-Dorra deal is that==W== we go all-in on the bid. No backing down.==W== I signed on the spot. It's an offer we couldn't refuse.
Unbelievable. Why would they do this?
Who cares?==W== That's none of our business.==W== And frankly, we're better off not knowing.
Alright. This is wildly out of left field, but I'll run interference with the Senate.==W== Tell me, Mercurio, are you confident you can win the second round?
Hah, that's my sister. I knew you'd—wait.==W== Hold on. What did you say? Not in the slightest?
Grace Imperium sent over the prompt of "wishing ability assessment" right before we spoke. Read it yourself. It's totally incomprehensible...
But rest assured, Madame CEO. Even though playing by the book won't win us this fight, finding a way out is exactly what I'm here for.
I'll squeeze every drop out of this authority you fought so hard to give me ...==W== and make sure Omnisky Aegis takes that Monolith.
Is this ... the wishing prompt from the Grace Imperium?
Knows no caste, judges no cause. Needs no training, demands no magic.
Forged of adamant, locking thunder in cold iron.
Throw the bolt, and instant death descends.
It's named the Scepter of Death. And that is your prompt for the wishing test.
At 12:00 PM today, the lake island Monolith—the one up for auction—opens its doors.

Omnisky Aegis,==W== the Imperial Guard,==W== and United Harvest Philae==W== will send Trekkers inside to make a wish. You have until sunset on the 15th to submit your Artifact at the Soul Shop conference room.
One Artifact per company. Whoever matches the prompt best wins a ten-year lease for the Philae Monolith.
And those are the rules for round two. Thank you for listening!
Thanks for dropping this off, Bastelina.==W== But ... is this really a prompt? It reads like an ancient prophecy.
Good eye, Boss. It's a verse from the ancient Book of Grace Prophecies, describing the legendary Scepter of Death.
But honestly? Your cute little Bastelina thinks wishing up a legendary treasure like that is impossible. The best you can do is get as close to the description as you can.
So it all boils down to who can pull out an Artifact that comes closest to the Scepter of Death!
I get that we need the Scepter of Death... But how are we supposed to wish for it? Ugh, my head hurts.
You aren't the only one with a headache, Noya.
I doubt anyone here can even picture this Scepter of Death.
Judging by the prophecy, it's a devastating Artifact that fires something like lightning to kill its target instantly.
Plus, this Artifact knows no caste and judges no cause... Maybe something anyone can use, even without magic?
Taken literally, it sounds a lot like the magic firearms Amber and I use.
Except our bullets run on magic. That breaks the "demands no magic" rule.
It fails the "needs no training" condition, too.==W== Mastering a magic firearm takes years of practice with shooting arrays. An amateur can't just pick one up.
A gun that requires zero magic, and takes zero effort to use...
The shape of a specific weapon flashes in my mind. Aside from the overly dramatic "Scepter of Death" moniker, it perfectly fits the Grace Imperium's prompt.
But ... why is no one else seeing this?
Have any of you ever seen a weapon that...
I describe the weapon to the group.
A weapon that requires no magic and fires metal bullets using black powder in a casing... I apologize, but I simply cannot picture it.
Black powder? You mean the stuff for fireworks?
Probably. But that is only good for fireworks. Packed into something the size of a bullet, there's no way it can unleash the punch you're describing, Boss.
It gives us a direction, at least. This "firearm" Boss is imagining sounds plausible. It certainly fits the prophecy.
Strange. They truly have no concept of the "gun" I know, and I haven't seen one either since waking up in the Monolith.
Yet even though Amber's firearms work differently, the design is almost identical. Is it just a coincidence?
Whatever. Now isn't the time for that. I need to focus on the Monolith climb and making the wish.
Remember our talk about finding someone to watch your back?
Yeah. You said you'd look around on your end.
I have. Sadly, I haven't found anyone suitable.
But we're heading into the Philae Monolith next. It's incredibly dangerous, for real. I'd rather gather a full team and prep everything before we make a move.
Huh? Is it that dangerous? We used it as a hideout before.
You didn't go deep enough to feel it. If you had gone further in, you'd understand why they sealed that tower.
Yeah. This was six years ago. I was still a student, so I only heard bits and pieces from my father.
During the last ten-year cycle, the Philae Monolith belonged to United Harvest.
But one day, a Trekker squad from the Philae branch wished for an Artifact that never should have existed. It was a massive violation of the Grace Imperium.
After that, they locked down the lake island Monolith and shut off the cable cars.
United Harvest had to start relying on Trekkers bringing Artifacts from the Wilds. That's actually how the Trekker Camp boomed...
I see. So that's the danger. Six years without a single wish is definitely a problem. In a Monolith dormant for that long, anything could happen.
What kind of Artifact breaks the rules like that?
No idea. HQ locked it down as top secret. There isn't a record of it in the Philae archives.
Bastelina, do you know anything about this?
Eh? Even cute little Bastelina doesn't have the answer to that! I only joined the Grace Imperium this year, and my seniors have never brought it up. It's probably a taboo.
But speaking of bodyguards, why don't you just ask her, Boss?
Yeah! When I got here this morning, I saw her standing by the river over there. Looked like she was praying for something.
I follow Bastelina down an alley just outside United Harvest Philae.
O Guardian of Goodwind, hear my prayer. Wash away all misfortune, sin, and impurity. With deepest reverence, I ask of you:
Please keep my ==SEX11== safe and grant ==SEX4== good health.==RT==May ==SEX3== journey be smooth and grant ==SEX4== lasting blessings.
Should misfortune find my ==SEX11==, let it strike me instead.
Should enemies stand in ==SEX3== way, let me be the blade that strikes them down.
I beg of you... Mend our severed fate, and bind me to my ==SEX11== once more. I humbly pray.
Phew. I've lost count of how many prayers I've offered since coming here. Yet my ==SEX11== and I remain apart.
... No, I know why.==W== I try to clear my mind to pray, but my head is just filled with thoughts of my ==SEX11==. I'm drowning in worldly attachments.
The Guardian of Goodwind must be exasperated with me.
Then again, I am a blade. Isn't it perfectly natural that I can't think of anything else until I'm back in the hands of my wielder?
Wait! That means these aren't worldly attachments at all! It's pure, undeniable loyalty! Oh, Guardian of Goodwind, please forgive my foolishness!
What a strong, soothing breeze... Is this a sign from the Guardian of Goodwind?
Cleaved in two, the rock no longer parts the current. Fallen wisteria petals simply drift through the gap, floating downstream together.
I see. My ==SEX11== and I are just like those petals. We may be separated for now, but we are destined to reunite.
O Guardian of Goodwind, thank you for showing me the way.
Still... I should be satisfied just having my prayers answered. But part of me selfishly hopes that tomorrow is the day we meet. Am I asking for too much?

Should misfortune find my ==SEX11==, let it strike me instead.
Should enemies stand in ==SEX3== way, let me be the blade that strikes them down.
I beg of you... Mend our severed fate, and bind me to my ==SEX11== once more. I humbly pray.
Phew. I've lost count of how many prayers I've offered since coming here. Yet my ==SEX11== and I remain apart.
... No, I know why.==W== I try to clear my mind to pray, but my head is just filled with thoughts of my ==SEX11==. I'm drowning in worldly attachments.
The Guardian of Goodwind must be exasperated with me.
Then again, I am a blade. Isn't it perfectly natural that I can't think of anything else until I'm back in the hands of my wielder?
Wait! That means these aren't worldly attachments at all! It's pure, undeniable loyalty! Oh, Guardian of Goodwind, please forgive my foolishness!
What a strong, soothing breeze... Is this a sign from the Guardian of Goodwind?
Cleaved in two, the rock no longer parts the current. Fallen wisteria petals simply drift through the gap, floating downstream together.
I see. My ==SEX11== and I are just like those petals. We may be separated for now, but we are destined to reunite.
O Guardian of Goodwind, thank you for showing me the way.
Still... I should be satisfied just having my prayers answered. But part of me selfishly hopes that tomorrow is the day we meet. Am I asking for too much?

strings.text: You choose to partner with Matilda, dealing a direct blow to the Senate's power in New Orelian. Matilda achieves a total victory. However, the resentful remnants ambush you with a huge Artifact car...
Monolith Calendar Year 998, Messis Month, Philae
Boss, thank you for stepping up.==W== The new United Harvest owes you.
You're too kind, Lady Matilda. Without your backing, United Harvest Philae wouldn't have survived.
Now we return the favor.==W== My team agrees—your shares go back to you.
United Harvest Philae stands with you. Let's rebuild Nova's food supply together.
Why? You don't want us on your side?
Never. I truly admire what you and Firenze have accomplished here.
The two of you carry Samuel's vision.==W== And that's why I refuse to drag United Harvest Philae into this internal war.
You steer the future. Don't waste it on this ugly blood feud.
Blood feud?==W== What do you mean? You hold the Seal of Grace—United Harvest's absolute authority.
I do. I also built the new United Harvest, but too many have sacrificed in the process. I lack the strength to crush the rogue branches and those New Orelian elites now.
The old branches are rebelling,==W== and two New Orelian legions sit tight, ready to strike south anytime.
Delay any longer, and we ruin the spring sow. That means Nova starves.
I won't let my grandfather's legacy become this continent's curse.
So I'll march our remaining troops north. We end them before winter break.
Let me stain my hands, win or lose.==W== Come spring, you finish Samuel's dream.
I understand.==W== But how many march with you?
You stand no chance.==W== A full legion runs eleven thousand. Those odds are basically suicide.
Our morale beats theirs cold. Even in defeat, we bleed them enough to buy you time.
I see no other move.==W== Otherwise, they strike south next year.==W== As far as I know, United Harvest Philae fields no army, right?
That's true...==W== I feel ashamed that we offer nothing on the battlefield.
Wait. Two thousand against twenty thousand.==W== That's not a sure loss.
Not if ...==W== each of them forges a soul pact with me.
One month later, near New Orelian
Boss!==W== Our soldiers are making their way into the neighboring Monoliths, nice and orderly!
I still have no idea how you convinced our Director. Mass-farming Monolith blessings for soldiers? I can't believe she approved it!
Maybe your Director is ...==W== a nice person?
I've never even met the Grace Imperium's Sky Institute Director, so there's no way I "convinced" her.==W== She's probably just worried about Nova's food supply next year, so she's extending a hand.
The Trekkers are gathered. They're escorting the remaining troops to the Monoliths in the Wilds for their blessings.
Everyone reports back by 6 a.m. tomorrow. Then, we march on New Orelian.

Completing Vita's mission of collecting ten souls two years ago gives me a new authority:==W== anyone who signs a soul pact with me keeps their Monolith Blessing for a full day after leaving the Monolith.
The Monolith gives this special blessing to climbers. It multiplies their combat strength several times over—sometimes even tenfold.
That strict one-day limit makes it hard to use day to day. But when it counts, it can completely turn the tide.
Gah!==W== What crazy strength are we dealing with?!
They take hits and don't even flinch!==W== No—our magic bullets aren't even piercing their armor!
This Monolith blessing is insane!==W== I feel like I can take on ten guys!
Pace yourself. Your twenty-four hours are almost up. Fall back and rest. I'll take over.
I still have thirty minutes! That's plenty of time to fight our way to the Senate and plant our flag on their roof!
The explosions...==W== They're getting closer. That Matilda woman is coming back to New Orelian!
Keep your composure. We outnumber them ten to one. This is clearly a tactic by our commanders. Lure them in and surround them, so Matilda can't escape.
Funny. I'm not the one who needs to escape.
First time here, but it feels so familiar...==W== Didn't Nazuka and Fuyuka blast a door open like this two years ago?
Matilda! In the name of the Senate, I strip you of your rank at United Harvest and sentence you to ninety-nine years in prison!
Oh?==W== Does a Senate without its Seal of Grace still hold any power?
Hmph. You must have the Seal on you.==W== Guards! Seize her and her accomplices!
Stealing the Seal, betraying the company, undermining the Senate...==W== Your crimes are endless!
If treason is my crime, what about everyone here? What's the penalty for engineering a famine and hoarding supplies to gouge prices, all for the company's "interests"?
Such a grand Senate, yet the silence is deafening.
Not a whisper on the right,==W== not a whisper on the left.
Good. Prick up your ears and listen to the uproar outside. I'm not the one judging you.==W== It's the people you've condemned to starve!
Boss. Lady Matilda. All 153 Senators are in custody. City combat has ceased.
We routed their defending legions with minimal losses. Casualty reports are coming in now.
I'm fine. Exhausted. The second I let my guard down, my body gave out.
You know, Boss... You finally dropped the formalities with me.
Same to you.==W== We've fought side-by-side for a long time. Formalities don't matter anymore.
Heh... Does that mean==W== I'm officially your comrade now?
Ah, I already made a soul pact with you. Why am I overthinking this...==W== Sorry, Boss, for dragging you into this mess.
What do you mean?==W== You didn't want us getting our hands dirty in this war?
I knew you'd see right through me. Whoever leads the new United Harvest can't bear the weight of this hatred.
My plan is simple. Win or lose, I step down and hand the company to you. The hatred ends with me.
Firenze can play CEO.==W== I have a promise to keep—I'm climbing the Monolith with a certain someone.
Oh...==W== Well, the Monolith can wait. Whenever you have free time.
Besides, I'm the Boss. Nobody mentions it anymore, but two years ago, plenty of people were convinced I was the Tyrant.
Since when does a Tyrant let a little blood get in ==SEX3== way?
You have a strange way of comforting people, Boss.
This costs you more than your reputation.==W== We won, but we upended the entire New Orelian elite.==W== We'll have targets on our backs from now on.
Let them come. I doubt they're any scarier than the Big Three or a massive Stellaroid.
Boss, the doctor says Grand Inspector Matilda will be fine. It's extreme exhaustion and anemia. She needs rest.
Phew...==W== It's finally over. We can look forward to some peace and quiet now.
Come on, Nazuka. If you aren't too tired, let's go explore the Monoliths in New Orelian.
I'm not tired at all!==W== Let me change first. These work heels are too thin—they always get caug==W==—ah!
Caught your heel in the cobblestones?==W== Hold on, let me help.
Matilda ... and that Boss...==W== You ruined our lives! Now you pay! Let's see how you handle my Artifact truck!
Look, there they are! The one with the ==SEX14== is the Boss. I'm sure of it.
Then the woman next to ==SEX4== must be Matilda! Hit the gas!
Out of the corner of my eye, a massive Artifact truck==RT==is barreling straight at Nazuka and me.
Next thing I know, I'm flying through the air…
Did I ...==W== just get hit by a truck?
Yep! A massive Artifact truck. We saved a recording right before impact. Take a look!
Oh my. That looks way nastier than the Spirit of Brutality.
Probably tougher than that giant Stellaroid at the Waterway, too. That thing shattered the second the Lucky Oasis rammed it, but this truck is huge.
You faced an unprecedented enemy this time, Tyrant.==W== Losing to that monster is completely fair.
You know, I read somewhere that getting hit by an Artifact truck is actually a ritual for entering another world.
Tons of people travel to other worlds this way and end up becoming heroes.
Huh? Then why did Tyrant end up here with us?==W== Is this room supposed to be the "other world"?
Or maybe Tyrant still has too many ties here, so the other world couldn't pull you in.
Enough joking around, you two. How's Nazuka?==W== Is she hurt?
She's completely fine. You shoved her out of the way right in time.
She's been crying over your body for a while. Honestly...==W== If you hadn't pushed her, she probably could've blasted that truck to pieces with her magic.
Yeah, that's entirely possible...==W== Guess I just did something completely pointless.
But in the heat of the moment, anyone's first instinct is to protect their friends!
Oh, I wouldn't be so sure. If it were me, I'd instantly use Virigia as a human shield.
Then I'd cling on to you so tight you couldn't get away either!
... New Orelian really is a snake pit.==W== Just like Matilda warned: even if we win the war, we can't dodge all the backstabbing and schemes from those elites.
When I go back, I need a completely different angle for the New Orelian problem.
Make sure to look both ways next time you cross the street, Tyrant!
Or just train your body until it's tougher than a truck.
I will go back...==W== This time, I must go back to the<color=#bd3059> even more distant past.
"Not looking to monopolize"? What's Mercurio's angle here...
Perhaps taking out a loan from Deepsea Finance is the first step into the box. I should look for another way.
But doing nothing means a slow death. This market drags us down anyway.
This time, we cannot attack New Orelian head-on.

strings.text: You lead the army to victory, and United Harvest thrives. In a rare lull, Nazuka invites you to the Monolith again. But the Monolith crumbles, the earth gives way, and your dream of a normal life is buried with it...
A year and a half later
Welcome to the United Harvest's grand opening in Emor! Come on in for fresh bread!
Grand opening: 20% off storewide! Plus a free gift for 10,000 Dorra spent!
Wait,==W== United Harvest already has a shop here. Why the grand opening?
You're out of the loop. Grand Inspector Matilda rebuilt this from the ground up. The company's reborn, so the shops are, too.
Grand Inspector Matilda... Rings a bell.
She's the executive all over the news lately. A beautiful young blonde with a real motherly vibe.
Young with motherly? Do those even go together?
Just go see for yourself. They've got her picture right inside.
Business is booming, Boss. A line out the door on day one. Looks like people are embracing the new United Harvest.
All thanks to Matilda, Firenze, Nyx ...==W== and everyone at United Harvest Philae.

==RT====RT====A-1==A year and a half ago, the internal war decimated Grand Inspector Matilda's forces.==RT==She claimed the Seal of Grace, but barely two thousand soldiers remained.==P====RT====RT====A-1==Opposing her are the New Orelian remnants. They command two full legions—ten times her strength.==RT====RT==Meanwhile, the other branches are completely splintered.

==RT====RT====RT====A-1==The New Orelian faction plans to march south in the spring.==RT==Their goal is to sabotage the planting season, worsening the Nova food crisis, and==RT==cashing in on their hoarded grain.==P====RT====RT====A-1==To save Nova from famine, Matilda intends to personally march north and defeat—or at least stall—those two legions.
After Firenze and I settle on a strategy to play it safe and bide==RT==our time, I sit down with Grand Inspector Matilda for a long talk.
Lady Matilda, I can't support this plan.
Maybe you think a suicide mission is heroic. That it'll wash away your guilt over your grandfather...==W== Over Samuel.
But from where I'm standing, throwing your life away on a reckless gamble isn't the answer.
Right now, I'm out of options.
Two thousand soldiers can't hold off two entire legions. A preemptive strike is the only way to save the spring harvest and keep our people from starving.
If you want to help, lend me your troops. Use my attack as a distraction to convince the other branches to resume farming. We need that grain.
No, you have a choice. Let Firenze and me command those soldiers.
Swapping commanders won't fix this. No strategy survives a numbers gap that wide.
Mine can. If the soldiers make a soul pact with me, my authority will let them carry the Monolith's blessings outside the Monolith.
You know what those blessings can do. I can only make them sustain outside the Monolith for a single day. But if we anchor our defenses around the city's Monoliths...
We can rotate troops between climbing the Monolith and holding the line. That's how we protect the harvest.
You possess an authority like that? Boss... You're full of surprises.
Plus, we won't protect everyone. We'll prioritize the branches still loyal to Samuel's ideals. As for the fence-sitters... Let's give them time to make a choice.
Five branches are leaning our way right now. If we hold the line for them, Philae, the Lushwood Jungle, and those five can scrape together enough grain to spare Nova from a famine.
Grand Inspector, please. Neither of us wants you to take this risk.
I don't mean to be grim, but if anything happens to you out there, the newborn United Harvest loses its symbol. The entire company will collapse.
...==W== Alright. You win. But I have a condition.
I leave the troops to you, Boss. But you need to find me a new role. I refuse to sit around in the rear.
Firenze and I already planned for that. We want to make you the true face of the new United Harvest.
Got it. You need me to tour the branches? Visit the staff? Or attend banquets to bring in outside support?
Those are important, but they aren't the priority.
The civil war traumatized our employees and customers with terrible memories. We need a gentle figurehead—someone to heal those wounds.
Makes sense. I can start looking for candidates right away...==W== Wait. Why are you staring at me?
Firenze and I both agree that you are the perfect person for the job.
A-Are you kidding?! Do you know how many people I have sentenced? How many exile orders I have signed?!
Don't worry, Grand Inspector Matilda. That stern look of yours only makes people appreciate your warmth more.
A certain someone also doesn't need to pass off all the credit.
Those wildly popular goods with Grand Inspector Matilda's face on them were that someone's idea, weren't they?
But hey, that someone's idea worked. We never lifted a finger against New Orelian, but I hear they are already tearing themselves apart.
Besides, I returned my shares to Matilda and stepped down from every role. I leave the rest to them.
Stepping down while you are ahead is fine, but...==W== Boss, total victory is right there. Are you walking away from the applause?
The applause is nice, sure. But I'd rather answer ...==W== a certain someone's old invitation.
Nazuka, want to climb the Monolith with me?
Hey, come on...==W== That invitation was ages ago. Don't you think it's a bit cheap to take me up on it now?
Here you go, Boss. Your Soul Shop application's been approved.
You're building a camp by that desolate Monolith and adding a Soul Shop? That's gonna cost a fortune.
Yeah. That Monolith's deep in a primeval forest. A camp gives Trekkers a base and makes climbing those Monoliths easier.
A Soul Shop for recharging...==W== Even with that, a camp out there will take years.
It's fine. I promised someone. When no one else is around, we'll explore those Monoliths together.
Not many people climb them, so we hardly know anything about them. We'll put together detailed guides so others can come make wishes.
You're too kind, Boss. Almost makes me want to transfer and run that Soul Shop myself.
Haha, you're welcome anytime.==W== I'd better get going... Hey, what's that?
On Bastelina's desk sits a familiar transparent box.
Oh, this?==W== It's the Artifact you wished for when you bid on the Philae Monolith.
Our Director's obsessed. She's always staring at it, muttering "the world is safe" and "the Boss isn't the Tyrant." She even made a little doll of you to put inside.
But her health's been slipping since last year...==W== She stares at the box with a guilty look, like she did something wrong. We've asked, but she won't say a word.
To keep her from getting worse, we took the box away. I'm holding it for now.
The Boss isn't the Tyrant...==W== Wait... A transparent box...
Well... I hope the Director gets better soon.==W== Take care, Bastelina.
That's a long flight. Thanks for the lift, Nazuka. How far are we from Philae?
About five hundred kilometers as the crow flies. Double that if you take the winding forest path.
We're out in the middle of nowhere. It's going to be a nightmare for other Trekkers to reach us.
You're the one who wants this spot, Boss. If it feels too remote, we can always find a closer Monolith.
No, no, I'm not complaining. The isolation is the point—no interruptions. Plus, I get to climb the Monolith with you every day.
Don't be ridiculous! We can't just climb the Monolith and call it a day. To build a camp from scratch... Even with Petal Bloom pitching in, we're looking at years of work.
My bad. I was just pulling your leg.
But honestly... I like the idea of us quietly building a Trekker camp out here, miles from the city.
Back in town, even while helping Firenze and Matilda rebuild United Harvest...==W== I feel suffocated when the night falls quiet, like I'm trapped.
Not entirely. I couldn't put it into words until I saw that Artifact at Bastelina's—==W==the transparent box we wished for during the bidding. That was when it clicked.
Taking that loan from Deepsea Finance locks me in a cage of invisible rules.
Sure, we secured the Dorra, saved United Harvest and Philae, and stopped a famine. But as long as the Seals of Grace exist—as long as these companies hold absolute power...
It's only a matter of time before it happens again. We can't guarantee every CEO turns out like Matilda or Firenze.
And the thing creating that box is the Monolith itself.==W== Whoever controls the wishes, controls the city.
That explains the camp in the middle of nowhere. You want to give everyone a chance to reach the Monoliths.
Yeah. And we need to study them. If we figure out how the Monoliths and Artifacts work, maybe one day we will finally shatter that transparent box for good.
A storm fills the valley, a fish the river.
Never mind. I feel happy all of a sudden. Reminds me of a poem from a Monolith.
Point is, I understand your goal, Boss. You turned my dreams into reality, so it's my turn to do the same for you.
Should we start climbing? Judging by this elevator, no Trekker has set foot here in forever.
Hold on, aren't you exhausted from the flight? And shouldn't you change? That outfit doesn't scream climbing gear.
I'm fine! Pulling all-nighters as your secretary was standard routine. A quick flight like this is nothing.
As for the clothes... I feel like the second I take them off, I go back to being a regular Trekker. Let me savor this for one last day—the feeling of having you all to myself as your secretary.
"All to myself"? That's a bit dramatic...
No, it's not an earthquake.==W==<color=#bd3059> The Monolith is sinking!</color>
Boss, it's pulling us down with it...==W== I'm sorry. We might not make it back.
Virigia, Bernina, Vita... What's going on?
The Monolith sank? How is that even possible? Nazuka can fly. How'd she get dragged down too?
I'm sorry... Tyrant. The Monoliths aren't eternal.
It's not just the Monolith sinking. The land around it goes down with it too.
Tyrant, a sinking Monolith creates violent mana turbulence. Even if Lady Nazuka withstood the disruption, escaping that downdraft would be nearly impossible.
Then why do they sink in the first place?
Tyrant, my clearance isn't high enough to run a proper analysis.
I'm sorry, but as Monolith staff, we aren't allowed to disclose anything.
Can you at least tell me if the other Monoliths have sunk too?
No. The Philae Monolith is fine, at least.
Your friends from Petal Bloom spend their free time by the window, waiting for you to come back.
I will go back... This time, I must go back to the<color=#bd3059> even more distant past</color>.
Vita, open the door. I'm going back.
Tyrant...==W== The Monoliths might be more complex than you think.
Enough, Bernina. We can't divulge more.
"Not looking to monopolize"? What's Mercurio's angle here...
Perhaps taking out a loan from Deepsea Finance is the first step into the transparent box. I should look for another way.
But doing nothing means a slow death. This market drags us down anyway.
So the Monoliths will sink... I need to resolve this United Harvest crisis faster.

param: You lead the army to victory, and United Harvest thrives. In a rare lull, Nazuka invites you to the Monolith again. But the Monolith crumbles, the earth gives way, and your dream of a normal life is buried with it...
A year and a half later
Welcome to the United Harvest's grand opening in Emor! Come on in for fresh bread!
Grand opening: 20% off storewide! Plus a free gift for 10,000 Dorra spent!
Wait,==W== United Harvest already has a shop here. Why the grand opening?
You're out of the loop. Grand Inspector Matilda rebuilt this from the ground up. The company's reborn, so the shops are, too.
Grand Inspector Matilda... Rings a bell.
She's the executive all over the news lately. A beautiful young blonde with a real motherly vibe.
Young with motherly? Do those even go together?
Just go see for yourself. They've got her picture right inside.
Business is booming, Boss. A line out the door on day one. Looks like people are embracing the new United Harvest.
All thanks to Matilda, Firenze, Nyx ...==W== and everyone at United Harvest Philae.

==RT====RT====A-1==A year and a half ago, the internal war decimated Grand Inspector Matilda's forces.==RT==She claimed the Seal of Grace, but barely two thousand soldiers remained.==P====RT====RT====A-1==Opposing her are the New Orelian remnants. They command two full legions—ten times her strength.==RT====RT==Meanwhile, the other branches are completely splintered.

==RT====RT====RT====A-1==The New Orelian faction plans to march south in the spring.==RT==Their goal is to sabotage the planting season, worsening the Nova food crisis, and==RT==cashing in on their hoarded grain.==P====RT====RT====A-1==To save Nova from famine, Matilda intends to personally march north and defeat—or at least stall—those two legions.
After Firenze and I settle on a strategy to play it safe and bide==RT==our time, I sit down with Grand Inspector Matilda for a long talk.
Lady Matilda, I can't support this plan.
Maybe you think a suicide mission is heroic. That it'll wash away your guilt over your grandfather...==W== Over Samuel.
But from where I'm standing, throwing your life away on a reckless gamble isn't the answer.
Right now, I'm out of options.
Two thousand soldiers can't hold off two entire legions. A preemptive strike is the only way to save the spring harvest and keep our people from starving.
If you want to help, lend me your troops. Use my attack as a distraction to convince the other branches to resume farming. We need that grain.
No, you have a choice. Let Firenze and me command those soldiers.
Swapping commanders won't fix this. No strategy survives a numbers gap that wide.
Mine can. If the soldiers make a soul pact with me, my authority will let them carry the Monolith's blessings outside the Monolith.
You know what those blessings can do. I can only make them sustain outside the Monolith for a single day. But if we anchor our defenses around the city's Monoliths...
We can rotate troops between climbing the Monolith and holding the line. That's how we protect the harvest.
You possess an authority like that? Boss... You're full of surprises.
Plus, we won't protect everyone. We'll prioritize the branches still loyal to Samuel's ideals. As for the fence-sitters... Let's give them time to make a choice.
Five branches are leaning our way right now. If we hold the line for them, Philae, the Lushwood Jungle, and those five can scrape together enough grain to spare Nova from a famine.
Grand Inspector, please. Neither of us wants you to take this risk.
I don't mean to be grim, but if anything happens to you out there, the newborn United Harvest loses its symbol. The entire company will collapse.
...==W== Alright. You win. But I have a condition.
I leave the troops to you, Boss. But you need to find me a new role. I refuse to sit around in the rear.
Firenze and I already planned for that. We want to make you the true face of the new United Harvest.
Got it. You need me to tour the branches? Visit the staff? Or attend banquets to bring in outside support?
Those are important, but they aren't the priority.
The civil war traumatized our employees and customers with terrible memories. We need a gentle figurehead—someone to heal those wounds.
Makes sense. I can start looking for candidates right away...==W== Wait. Why are you staring at me?
Firenze and I both agree that you are the perfect person for the job.
A-Are you kidding?! Do you know how many people I have sentenced? How many exile orders I have signed?!
Don't worry, Grand Inspector Matilda. That stern look of yours only makes people appreciate your warmth more.
A certain someone also doesn't need to pass off all the credit.
Those wildly popular goods with Grand Inspector Matilda's face on them were that someone's idea, weren't they?
But hey, that someone's idea worked. We never lifted a finger against New Orelian, but I hear they are already tearing themselves apart.
Besides, I returned my shares to Matilda and stepped down from every role. I leave the rest to them.
Stepping down while you are ahead is fine, but...==W== Boss, total victory is right there. Are you walking away from the applause?
The applause is nice, sure. But I'd rather answer ...==W== a certain someone's old invitation.
Nazuka, want to climb the Monolith with me?
Hey, come on...==W== That invitation was ages ago. Don't you think it's a bit cheap to take me up on it now?
Here you go, Boss. Your Soul Shop application's been approved.
You're building a camp by that desolate Monolith and adding a Soul Shop? That's gonna cost a fortune.
Yeah. That Monolith's deep in a primeval forest. A camp gives Trekkers a base and makes climbing those Monoliths easier.
A Soul Shop for recharging...==W== Even with that, a camp out there will take years.
It's fine. I promised someone. When no one else is around, we'll explore those Monoliths together.
Not many people climb them, so we hardly know anything about them. We'll put together detailed guides so others can come make wishes.
You're too kind, Boss. Almost makes me want to transfer and run that Soul Shop myself.
Haha, you're welcome anytime.==W== I'd better get going... Hey, what's that?
On Bastelina's desk sits a familiar transparent box.
Oh, this?==W== It's the Artifact you wished for when you bid on the Philae Monolith.
Our Director's obsessed. She's always staring at it, muttering "the world is safe" and "the Boss isn't the Tyrant." She even made a little doll of you to put inside.
But her health's been slipping since last year...==W== She stares at the box with a guilty look, like she did something wrong. We've asked, but she won't say a word.
To keep her from getting worse, we took the box away. I'm holding it for now.
The Boss isn't the Tyrant...==W== Wait... A transparent box...
Well... I hope the Director gets better soon.==W== Take care, Bastelina.
That's a long flight. Thanks for the lift, Nazuka. How far are we from Philae?
About five hundred kilometers as the crow flies. Double that if you take the winding forest path.
We're out in the middle of nowhere. It's going to be a nightmare for other Trekkers to reach us.
You're the one who wants this spot, Boss. If it feels too remote, we can always find a closer Monolith.
No, no, I'm not complaining. The isolation is the point—no interruptions. Plus, I get to climb the Monolith with you every day.
Don't be ridiculous! We can't just climb the Monolith and call it a day. To build a camp from scratch... Even with Petal Bloom pitching in, we're looking at years of work.
My bad. I was just pulling your leg.
But honestly... I like the idea of us quietly building a Trekker camp out here, miles from the city.
Back in town, even while helping Firenze and Matilda rebuild United Harvest...==W== I feel suffocated when the night falls quiet, like I'm trapped.
Not entirely. I couldn't put it into words until I saw that Artifact at Bastelina's—==W==the transparent box we wished for during the bidding. That was when it clicked.
Taking that loan from Deepsea Finance locks me in a cage of invisible rules.
Sure, we secured the Dorra, saved United Harvest and Philae, and stopped a famine. But as long as the Seals of Grace exist—as long as these companies hold absolute power...
It's only a matter of time before it happens again. We can't guarantee every CEO turns out like Matilda or Firenze.
And the thing creating that box is the Monolith itself.==W== Whoever controls the wishes, controls the city.
That explains the camp in the middle of nowhere. You want to give everyone a chance to reach the Monoliths.
Yeah. And we need to study them. If we figure out how the Monoliths and Artifacts work, maybe one day we will finally shatter that transparent box for good.
A storm fills the valley, a fish the river.
Never mind. I feel happy all of a sudden. Reminds me of a poem from a Monolith.
Point is, I understand your goal, Boss. You turned my dreams into reality, so it's my turn to do the same for you.
Should we start climbing? Judging by this elevator, no Trekker has set foot here in forever.
Hold on, aren't you exhausted from the flight? And shouldn't you change? That outfit doesn't scream climbing gear.
I'm fine! Pulling all-nighters as your secretary was standard routine. A quick flight like this is nothing.
As for the clothes... I feel like the second I take them off, I go back to being a regular Trekker. Let me savor this for one last day—the feeling of having you all to myself as your secretary.
"All to myself"? That's a bit dramatic...
No, it's not an earthquake.==W==<color=#bd3059> The Monolith is sinking!</color>
Boss, it's pulling us down with it...==W== I'm sorry. We might not make it back.
Virigia, Bernina, Vita... What's going on?
The Monolith sank? How is that even possible? Nazuka can fly. How'd she get dragged down too?
I'm sorry... Tyrant. The Monoliths aren't eternal.
It's not just the Monolith sinking. The land around it goes down with it too.
Tyrant, a sinking Monolith creates violent mana turbulence. Even if Lady Nazuka withstood the disruption, escaping that downdraft would be nearly impossible.

I'm sorry, but as Monolith staff, we aren't allowed to disclose anything.
Can you at least tell me if the other Monoliths have sunk too?
No. The Philae Monolith is fine, at least.
Your friends from Petal Bloom spend their free time by the window, waiting for you to come back.
I will go back... This time, I must go back to the<color=#bd3059> even more distant past</color>.
Vita, open the door. I'm going back.
Tyrant...==W== The Monoliths might be more complex than you think.
Enough, Bernina. We can't divulge more.
"Not looking to monopolize"? What's Mercurio's angle here...
Perhaps taking out a loan from Deepsea Finance is the first step into the transparent box. I should look for another way.
But doing nothing means a slow death. This market drags us down anyway.
So the Monoliths will sink... I need to resolve this United Harvest crisis faster.

strings.text: You take out another loan to rein in United Harvest's warring factions. But Matilda dies suddenly, throwing the company into chaos. Later, an employee's mistake gets you jailed. You try to escape, only to drown in the storm...
Not a chance.==W== Even with collateral, Deepsea Finance isn't lending you another Dorra.
From what I hear, United Harvest Philae's margins are terrible.==W== You move plenty of product, but you barely scrape together a single Dorra.
Your payment is due any day now. You need to worry about clearing that debt, not scheming for another loan.
Wh-What are you doing?!==W== I'm warning you, bank robbery is a major crime!==W== One press of this button and the Imperial Guards are on their way!
Relax. We need privacy for what we are about to discuss.
Manager Erinis... If memory serves, that 40-billion loan to United Harvest Philae from two years ago is still the biggest contract you've landed, isn't it?
Y-Yeah, so what if it is? Right now, my performance metrics depend entirely on your post-loan management...
Meaning... If we miss this month's payment, your superiors come down on you hard, right?
T-That still doesn't mean I can approve another loan!==W== Even with more money, you still can't pay it back!
No, no, no. Manager Erinis,==W== you need to look at the bigger picture.
Grain is in massive demand right now, yet United Harvest Philae's profit margins sit at rock bottom.==W== But profits never vanish. They merely migrate from one pocket to another.
So,==W== where do United Harvest Philae's profits go?==W== Straight to Deepsea Finance.==W== You buy our grain at the contract rate and flip it for a massive markup, don't you?
Y-Yes... But I don't run that division! I get zero credit for it. The profit they bleed out of you has nothing to do with me!
Easy now. I'm not here to point fingers. I want fairness, that's all.
Think about it. You do the heavy lifting to negotiate a brilliant deal, only for another department to steal the glory. You must find that unfair.
... That is company policy. N-Nothing unfair about it.
Your face says otherwise, Manager Erinis. Here is my proposal—
Go on.==W== I can take it.
40 billion clears our old loan and interest.==W== The rest goes to scooping up the fractured branches of the old United Harvest.
Deepsea Finance strictly forbids financing debt with debt,==W== Boss. Even I can't get this approved.
Exactly. That's why the loan isn't under United Harvest Philae. It falls under the Boss Accord.
For collateral: Artifacts in our warehouse, and my Seal of Grace.==W== An exclusive patent on soul trading easily covers the cost.
B-But Boss Accord and United Harvest Philae are still co-managed. A joint liability check kills the deal immediately.
Not anymore. Boss Accord has surrendered all its shares to Grand Inspector Matilda's new United Harvest.
As of right now, Boss Accord has zero ties to United Harvest Philae.
Technically... That bypasses the rules. But getting 80 billion approved... I don't know...
Manager Erinis, this loan offers massive benefits to you—and your department.
We hold a magical contract with the new United Harvest. We guarantee the purchase of half their grain output.
We can also add a rider to the loan: we sell all that grain to Deepsea Finance at our old, discounted rate.
Just don't let another department steal the credit this time.
If they absorb those fractured branches...==W== Their grain output skyrockets. Even half of that means exponential profits.==W== That alone could convince the Senate.
And the credit for all of it goes straight to you,==W== Manager Erinis.
Boss...==W== Can Boss Accord actually pay back 80 billion Dorra?
Relax.==W== I've got everything under control.
Pay our back wages,==W== and the Port Goldfinch branch immediately rejoins the new United Harvest!
Sigh... Grand Inspector Matilda's up north fighting the New Orelian elites, leaving the forest clearing totally abandoned.==W== If we don't clear it now, spring planting is ruined.
Supply us with the clearing equipment, and we gladly take your orders.
To think the new United Harvest actually remembers our little branch.==W== The wheat is rotting in the warehouse—please, just haul it away!
Over two months, Nazuka's magic has carried us to every==RT==United Harvest branch and office outside New Orelian.
The 30 billion Dorra we borrowed from Deepsea Finance==RT==pulled them back from the financial brink.
Our promises for the future and Grand Inspector Matilda's==RT==pristine reputation gave them something to believe in.
Like an inflating balloon, the new United Harvest rapidly==RT==reclaims its former territory, except for New Orelian.
Great news, everyone. Boss's trip is a success. Every regional office is ready to rally under the Grand Inspector's banner.
We now control half of Nova's grain output. If we manage the planting right, we avert the food crisis.
Amazing work, you two. You're the heroes keeping United Harvest up and running.
We can only negotiate with confidence because you're here holding the fort, Firenze. You keep this place running.
Still... This adds a hundred thousand names to our payroll. Can we really handle this load?
We know our people in Philae, but the other branches... We barely have any contact with them.
Grand Inspector Matilda knows the ins and outs of every branch. Too bad she isn't here.
I hear she's leading troops north to wipe out the New Orelian remnants. Any updates from the front?
Radio silence. Communications are completely cut.
Pitting two thousand troops against 20 thousand is a suicide mission. Nyx and I urged her not to rush north, but she told us—
The New Orelian faction won't sit back and watch us consolidate. Even if it's only to buy you time, I have to go.
She made the right call... We never would have secured those branches without her holding the line.
Nyx?! When did you get here? Aren't you deployed with the Grand Inspector?
Seeing branch after branch siding with us shattered their morale.
With the Grand Inspector leading the charge, we overcame their numbers and captured most of the Senate alive.
We won... But the Grand Inspector took a direct hit.==W== She's gone.
Matilda's death triggers a fallout far worse==RT==than we ever imagined.
Lacking the people or the know-how to run so many new==RT==branches, overexpansion catches up with us fast.
Report. The Lushwood Jungle wheat failed the inspection. A large batch of it is moldy.
What went wrong with the quality check?
Inspectors claimed it was clean when they checked it.
Then the issue is storage. Who's the manager for this batch?
Um, the manager had an accident unloading at Port Goldfinch. The cargo straps gave way, and he was crushed. He's still in a coma.
I see... We'll sort out the screw-up later. Make sure his family gets compensated first.
New Orelian just contacted. Their warehouse burned down.
A fire breaks out in the middle of our audit? Nyx, you'll have to go down there yourself.
Sure, but I've already got a backlog of embezzlement cases waiting...
Boss, you're running on empty. Let me take over.
It's fine. We're all stretched thin right now. We just have to keep pushing.
But some mistakes can't be fixed by hard work alone.
We lack the ability to screen employees across all branches,==RT==so we have to keep all of them on board for now.
Greed, laziness, sheer incompetence—==RT==the toxins of the old United Harvest seep straight through==RT==the corporate structure and infect Philae.
What are you doing? Why am I under arrest?==W== Erinis,==W== we're in this together! What do you gain from throwing me in prison?
Throwing you in prison?==W== Oh, please! I'm going down right alongside you!
Deepsea Finance audited us! Most of the Artifacts you put up as collateral are fake—empty shells!==W== We're both up for loan fraud. You've completely ruined me!
Fake...? How is that even possible?!
Nazuka... Is the fraud mess cleared up? I swear I'm innocent.
Boss, our investigation confirmed that a few greedy employees embezzled company assets. That's how the collateral got compromised.
But they've already blown through the money. The scandal is tanking the new United Harvest's business. And the worst part is...
By law, Deepsea Finance can refuse to release you until Boss Accord repays the full 80-billion loan. As CEO, you're on the hook.
Well, Firenze and I crunched the numbers. We're supposed to be able to pay it off in 15 years... 20 at most.
Dammit, I can't make Nazuka wait that long. I need a plan...==W== Wait,==W== I saw this in a Stella Drama once!
<size=50>Guard! I want a book!==W== And bring me the newest Magical Girl poster!</size>
It's been almost two years ...==W== since they locked me in here.
I keep a stolen cafeteria spoon hidden in a book.==W== Every day at yard time, I dump the dirt I dig out with it.
There's a massive storm tonight==W==—perfect cover for an escape.
Hold on, Nazuka.==W== I'm coming back!
Alright... Squeeze through this hole,==W== dig through the last bit of dirt blocking the sewer,==W== and I'm free...
Huh?==W== What's that noise?==W== Where's all this water coming from?!==W==
Gurgle...==W== <size=52>This is not how it goes in the Stella Drama!</size>==W==
Gasp... Cough...==W== How...==W== How did I drown?!
That storm is Philae's worst in a century.==W== Your escape route turns into a deadly underground river.
Not much of a swimmer, are you, Tyrant?
... Never should have trusted the Stella Dramas!
Take a look at your cell. Missing the prison life already?
Actually,==W== you're getting great sleep, regular exercise, and balanced meals in there.
You're healthier than before you went in.
Plus,==W== a cute girl who really cares visits you every week.==W== With a setup like that, I'd never leave.
Vita, open the door.==W== I'm going back.
Goodbye, Tyrant.==W== Without the right team, managing that many people is just a burden.
A company is far deadlier and trickier than a Monolith.
I will go back...==W== This time, I must go back to the<color=#bd3059> even more distant past.
"Not looking to monopolize"? What's Mercurio's angle here...
Perhaps taking out a loan from Deepsea Finance is the first step into the box. I should look for another way.
But doing nothing means a slow death. This market drags us down anyway.
Grand Inspector Matilda is vital. Without her, we can't run the entirety of United Harvest.
This time, I can't let her die.
