strings.text: Advance payments bring you closer to your goal. Negotiations with Goodwind Homecare and the Imperial Guard succeed. Yet upon hearing the news, Mercurio just smiles. She clearly has a card left to play…
Is everything alright, Lady Mistique? We appreciate Scarlet Sights Media buying our grain...==W== But I didn't expect you to drop by at 4 a.m. to sign the contract.
I-It's a disaster!==W== I'm a witch who feasts on the truth, yet I'm missing scoop after scoop.==W== Bwaahh... The God of Grace hates me...
Mistique,==W== aren't you in New Orelian with Petal Bloom?
Sigh... Long story.==W== I followed Mina's group==W== and managed to interview Boss's blade. I got great material—==W==but that was where my luck ended.
Another witch from Flavio intercepted me. She babbled about how tight I was with Boss and dragged me back to Philae as Scarlet Sights' acting rep for some banquet.
Because of that, I missed the big scoop: Petal Bloom blowing the doors off the United Harvest Senate!
Then my broom acted up on the way back. I missed the banquet, missed the Monolith bidding, and didn't even get to see Boss climb the tower. I have the worst luck.
That sounds rough. But for United Harvest Philae, having you sign this contract as the Scarlet Sights rep helps immensely.
You always look out for us.==W== On behalf of the company, thank you.
I'm glad I can help,==W== but...==W== I'm a witch. My life's purpose is the news.
So Ophir...==W== Get this feature story ...==W== to print...==W== Zzz...
Miss Mistique? Asleep already?==W== She must be exhausted. I need to get her to bed.==W== Please excuse us.
Lady Firenze, everything unfolds as you predict.==W== Companies are reaching out to sign grain contracts, paying substantial Dorra upfront.

Counting the Scarlet Sights order and the Fenghuang Diner deal, we hold 10 billion Dorra in advance payments. Combined with our reserves and Darcia's funds,==W== our liquid capital sits at 33 billion Dorra. We remain seven billion short of our 40-billion goal.
It all unfolds according to your plan, Lady Firenze.

I can't take all the credit. This only works thanks to Nyx's intel, your data analysis, and everyone's hard work here at United Harvest Philae. Not to mention the support from Boss and the New Star Guild.
Deepsea Finance is the real concern. We are scheduled to sign the grain contract today, but they called at midnight to say they needed more time to think.
It seems Omnisky Aegis is making their move.==W== Still, as long as they aren't openly opposing us right now, we can afford to ignore them.
U-um... Is this the time to be this relaxed? We're still 7 billion short, and the Dorra are due before sunset! Are we going to make it?!
Fair point. But we still have two more companies to pitch to. We aren't out of options yet.

Take Goodwind Homecare. They have a massive demand for flowers. Our joint greenhouse project is still on the table, though the Darcia incident put it on hold. Now is the perfect time to reopen those talks.
A stalled project like that... Can we finalize a deal in half a day?
Easily. But I need the New Star Guild's help. It's simple—you three need to exaggerate what happens at the banquet.
Yes. Spin the wildest tale you can imagine. But whatever you say, make sure it ties back to "flowers."
Sapphire, Ruby, prep a cart full of flowers for me. I need a suitable gift for Goodwind Homecare.
The grain quality is exceptional now that you're leading United Harvest Philae, Lady Firenze. Our maids absolutely swear by your rice.
However... I must apologize. Our maids don't eat much, so we have no plan to place bulk grain orders. We won't be able to support your Monolith bid this time.
As for reviving the joint greenhouse project, we will reach out the moment we reach a decision. Is that acceptable?
(United Harvest Philae's greenhouse can cultivate all sorts of rare flowers, which would be a massive help to Goodwind Homecare... But catching Otoha comes first.)
(Though it's a shame... A polite refusal is best.)
Not a problem.==W== On another note—please accept these flowers as a small thank-you for hosting us the other night.
During that banquet,==W== a Goodwind maid protected Boss==W== and saved the entire evening.
Uh, ah... Yes...==W== But why flowers?
Because that particular maid seemed fond of these varieties. Heh. She picked a large batch from our greenhouse.
(That woman tied me up and threw me in a cell!==W== Yet here I am, smiling and accepting their gratitude on her behalf. This is infuriating!)
(Wait. Our mai<r=ninjas></r>ds use flowers to craft tools, sure, but why would Otoha raid their greenhouse?)
I... I apologize.==W== To think she harvested flowers from her employer's greenhouse.
Oh, we actually asked her to! She's brilliant at flower arrangement. We hired her to decorate the venue, and her work was a huge hit.
(Flower arrangement?==W== Otoha is skilled at it, but she's not fond of it. Why go out of her way to help?==W== I need to keep them talking.==W== It might expose her endgame.)
We are honored by your praise.==W== In that case, allow me a quick quality check.==W== Lady Firenze, esteemed guests of the Boss Accord, were you satisfied with her bodyguard services?
Beyond satisfied!==W== The whole unit of Desert Scorpions dropped the second a flurry of petals blew past.
Exactly. She twisted the enemies' gun barrels into flowers.

When she finally landed in the courtyard with Boss, she looked like an elegant night heron.==W== She drifted down from the sky, carrying the scent of fragrance.==W== Had she not been missing wings, I would've thought she could actually fly.

(A night heron? Aren't those birds completely dopey? How is that elegant?==W== They're blowing this way out of proportion. Otoha is strong, but she couldn't take down that many Desert Scorpions alone.)
(Wait. They all mentioned flowers...==W== Did Otoha find some new plant in their greenhouse and weaponize it into a brand-new ninja tool?)
(So that's how she knocked me out so fast! It wasn't because I'm weaker than her—she had a secret weapon!==W== There's about that sleep magic in her gun.)

(That's why she took the job guarding the Boss. It gave her free rein to harvest the flowers she needed from United Harvest Philae!==W== Using the banquet as cover, she could have stockpiled years' worth of materials.==W== She never could have pulled that off by sneaking in...)
Well then, we have other pressing matters to attend to. We will take our leave for today.
Heh. Is there something else, Miss Shuo?

I gave it some more thought. A massive project like the joint greenhouse does require headquarters' approval. But as head of the Philae branch, I can certainly start some preliminary work with you ...==W== strictly within my authority, of course. Would you be interested, Lady Firenze?
T-That's amazing!==W== We barely mentioned Otoha and some flowers, and the same Miss Shuo who shot us down is suddenly pitching a partnership! She even fronted a 2 billion Dorra advance!
I don't get it. Was she that obsessed with our greenhouse?==W== She signed the paperwork, mentioned an inspection, and bolted.
She's not inspecting the greenhouse.==W== She's hunting for Otoha.

Even the most rational, complex business deals are driven by people.==W== Miss Shuo is a formidable manager and an exceptional maid. Rumor has it she's the leading candidate to take over Goodwind Homecare.
Normally, she would see right through our little exaggerations. But ...==W== her rivalry with a certain someone is simply too blinding.
Well, that still leaves us 5 billion short.==W== Firenze, who's next on the list?
The Imperial Guard will be our bet for the final 5 billion. However, I must handle this negotiation alone.
Aren't they our competition?==W== ==PLAYER_NAME== said their rep, Greyhorn, went really hard in the bidding, didn't even blink when bidding up.
Correct. But when you throw around billions of Dorra without a second thought, it means one of two things. Either the Imperial Guard is determined to win at all costs,==W== or—==W==
What exactly are you implying, Lady Firenze? Of course the Imperial Guard intends to win this Monolith bid.
Oh, don't mind me. I'm not questioning the Imperial Guard; it was merely a passing thought. After all, getting on your bad side right now wouldn't do me any favor.
... I see. If you say so, then no harm done. By the way, I was just heading out for lunch. Care to join me?
I grew up in Philae, yet I had no idea a restaurant was hiding out here.
No?==W== Then,==W== are you here for a picnic?
Not exactly. I wanted a little pre-meal workout.==W== I was hoping for a sparring partner, and what do you know? We just "happen" to cross paths.
... I see. Your defense is tight, Lady Firenze.==W== Flawless footwork.==W== You live up to your reputation.
And you, Lady Greyhorn.==W== That glancing strike is hard to parry.
So...==W== What do you consider the essence of the rapier?
I favor the rapier because ...==W== the most vital skill in this discipline is calculation.
Calculation... True. I can feel that precision in your technique.
But I have a different answer.==W== The key to the rapier is efficiency—==W==no wasted movement!
The tip of Greyhorn's blade comes to rest lightly against Firenze's shoulder.
A calculated style isn't bad,==W== but thinking slows you down.
And yet,==W== you're so caught up in your own lecture==W== that you've neglected your surroundings.
Black smoke billows, and the cane sword vanishes from Firenze's hand. When Greyhorn==RT==looks down, she finds the real blade against her stomach—held by Firenze's shadow.
Heh.==W== I've never had a rapier duel this exciting.
The pleasure is mine. But it's a pity I missed out on seeing the Hound's true skills.
I wasn't holding back. I showed you the<r=·> true</r><r=·> power</r><r=·> of </r><color=#6690de><r=·>Greyhorn</r></color>.==W== Now, care for a bite?==W==
Oh?==W== Heh. So it is a picnic.
I despise wasted effort. I wouldn't travel all this way to test you.
So you had no intention of winning the Monolith bid, did you?
My sources tell me that==W== the Imperial Guard team on the lake island==W== hasn't even set foot inside the Monolith.
The bidding records show the Imperial Guard joins every time,==W== but only to match the highest offers. You never win the rights to the Monolith.
Could it be ... your organization is a shill planted to drive up the price?
I'm not supposed to answer that...==W== But with your network, you'll find out the truth soon enough anyway.
... You have the gist. But it works both ways. If the other companies fail to secure the bid, the Imperial Guard steps in to take over.
The public remains unaware, however. To everyone else, we're a weak faction doomed to lose every bid.
This reputation gives me endless headaches.
United Harvest Philae and Omnisky Aegis are determined to win this bid.==W== Our participation means nothing.
And yet, you still deploy a team to the island.
I'm an employee at the end of the day. The Imperial Guard's orders trump my personal preferences.
You know this, Lady Firenze. That is why you came alone and so patiently accompanied me all the way out here.
Hehehe. Guilty.==W== Then, building on our conversation,==W== United Harvest Philae wants to hire the Imperial Guard for all corporate and city security.
Oh? United Harvest forces currently handle your security. You feel safe bringing in outsiders? You are handing your entire defense over to the Imperial Guard—
That's the point. We need to cut ties with the old regime.
Besides, we lack the manpower. From now on, our internal guards focus solely on logistics, like escorting long-haul freight.
For daily patrols and street management, we prefer to leave the job to professionals like the Imperial Guard.
You don't beat around the bush.
If the Imperial Guard accepts our massive contract,==W== your endless bidding losses suddenly look like a marketing stunt.==W== People would assume you were using the bids to advertise your services.
We'll also publicly mention your deep pockets and praise your ironclad reliability.==W== That reputation problem of yours improves overnight.
You play a beautiful game, Lady Firenze. Since you're solving my biggest headache, it's only right that I return the favor.
I'll leave this year's Mirage delivery contract to you. Your former parent company is a total mess. They are in no shape to handle it.
Per Imperial Guard tradition, we pay the six billion Dorra advance in crystal diamonds.
If the terms suit you, we'll head back to the outpost and sign the contract right now.
A pleasure doing business with you.
Manager, Firenze is seen leaving the Imperial Guard. She's on her way here.
Looks like she has locked in a massive deal with them. They must have the full 40 billion.
She is the woman who overthrew Darcia and the Senate to claim United Harvest Philae. I expect nothing less.
But Firenze... You know nothing of the Dorra's true power.
Hahaha... You have no chance in this bid!

strings.text: Mercurio maliciously tanks the market, putting your fundraising effort on the brink of failure. As word spreads, Philaens who support United Harvest come forward, and their contributions cover the final gap.
I'd like to exchange these crystal diamonds for Dorra, please.
R-Right away. This is a massive deposit, so counting them will take a moment. Please bear with me.
Whoa, there's gotta be over a thousand in here! Why does the Imperial Guard pay with these? Wouldn't a Deepsea Finance check be easier?
These gems are uniform in size and fuel major spells.==W== That's why crystal diamonds have been the standard for massive transactions since ancient times.
Dorra might be the standard now, turning these gems into a strategic resource, but the Imperial Guard clings to the old ways—like using them to pay for huge contracts.
Stockpiling for combat. A strategic reserve.
Exactly. For a faction that fights as often as the Imperial Guard, paying in crystal diamonds instead of Dorra kills two birds with one stone.
Well, well. If it isn't Firenze ...==W== and the Boss Accord crew. What a surprise running into you here.
Hiring thugs to ambush Boss, sabotaging the cable car...==W== You have some nerve showing your face here, Mercurio.
Oh, how terrifying! <size=60>♪</size> If I actually did something to upset you, I suppose I could apologize...
But we've operated strictly within the rules of the technical review.==W== Is there a problem with that?
And let's be honest: if you can't afford the deposit, any little victories you score during the review are meaningless. Right?
Sorry to burst your bubble, but we've got the deposit! With the money sorted, there's no way United Harvest Philae loses this!
Hahahaha, so confident. Let's see what you're really capable of, then <size=60>♪</size>
Thank you for waiting, Lady Firenze.==W== The count is complete. You brought 1,200 crystal diamonds. At today's rate of 5.05 million Dorra each, that totals 6.06 billion Dorra.
6 billion...! Perfect. After the deposit, we'll still have a billion Dorra left over...==W== That secures the company's daily operating costs, too.
Process the exchange immediately, please, and deposit the funds into our Monolith bidding account.

I-I'm so sorry, Lady Firenze ... and everyone from the New Star Guild! We just received an emergency alert from headquarters. The crystal diamond market is experiencing massive volatility. We need a moment to recalculate the exchange rate.
Wait, huh? What do you mean? Didn't we have over 6 billion Dorra?
Don't panic. It's just a technical correction. Stay calm.
A price drop is perfectly normal if someone else is selling off their stock.
But ... Nova doesn't have any active crystal diamond mines left. Even if someone is selling, the supply is limited. It shouldn't impact the market price that much—
The new rate from headquarters is ...==W==<color=#bd3059> 4.1 million Dorra</color> each.
How is that possible...?!==W== A 20 percent drop in a single day?! Can the market even do that?!
I'm sorry, but we have only just received the news, too.
Around noon, someone dumped a massive stockpile of crystal diamonds at Port Goldfinch. There's also rumor that a mage discovered a substitute casting material. The market is crashing.
Those factors caused the crash. Right now...==W== These diamonds are only worth 4.92 billion Dorra.
The sell-off aside, that rumor is absolute nonsense. We expect prices to bounce back by tomorrow.
That's too late. At 4.92 billion, we are still 80 million short of the deposit.
Mercurio... How desperate is Omnisky Aegis for the Philae Monolith? Crashing the crystal diamond market like this must have cost tens of billions of Dorra.
She took out a 40-billion Dorra loan from Deepsea Finance yesterday at 30 percent interest. I'd say it's safe to assume she bet the house.
Oh? And who might you be? I don't know what you're plotting, but spreading rumors is terribly rude.
Oh, no, no. An information broker values her reputation above life itself. I don't deal in rumors.
A cloaked woman strides into the lobby, holding up a cassette tape—the exact kind wished out of a Monolith.
Omnisky Aegis has two choices. Option one—buy this tape from me.==W== Option two—I play it right here, and everything on it goes public.
And looking at these Trekkers, I'm sure someone would be more than happy to lend me an Artifact to play it on.
It's been a while, my friends from the New Star Guild.
A playback Artifact? We have one in the car! I'll go grab it!
Be my guest. Let's hear what you've got.
I must admit, your bluntness actually improves my opinion of you.
Tell your manager Omnisky Aegis requires a loan of 40 billion Dorra!
I want it tonight. Ready for withdrawal at Port Goldfinch.
Y-You're joking, right? A sum that massive won't be ready==RT==until tomorrow morning at the earliest...
5 percent. Clear the funds tonight, and I'll personally==RT==guarantee a 5 percent kickback.
Are you out of your mind? Deepsea Finance has strict protocols.
We can't just approve a massive uncollateralized loan like that—
I'll put up my sister as collateral. Plus a 10 percent kickback.==RT==Do we have a deal?
H-Hey, don't look at me like that! I never took the kickback!
Her collateral was perfectly valid! And at 30 percent interest, Deepsea Finance had no reason to deny the loan.==W== It's not our job to monitor how clients spend their money...
I don't need to explain myself. I knew Firenze was scrambling for deals, so I struck first and crushed their little operation.
I simply played a brilliant move within the rules. You can't honestly say I did anything wrong.
If anything, blame your own pathetic risk management.==W== Given the circumstances, United Harvest Philae only had two real options.
Option one: win over the deep-pocketed Imperial Guard.
Option two: beg Deepsea Finance for a loan to cover the gap.
So that's why cap—==W==manager drained Deepsea Finance! And crashed the crystal diamond market!
I'll admit, I didn't expect them to raise that much cash. Still, crashing the market was definitely the right insurance <size=60>♪</size>
Which begs the question. How do you plan to fill an 80-million-Dorra hole before time's up?
B-Bull! We can absolutely find 80 million!==W== A collector offered top dollar for Loxy once... We... We'll sell Loxy if we have to!
Be my guest. I certainly won't stop you...==W== Hahaha. Two hours until sunset. Think you can make it?
Just throw in the towel. Why sell your crystal diamonds at a massive loss today? Wait for a rebound, and you might actually afford severance pay for your staff.
Umm...==W== Lady Firenze? Do we still proceed with the exchange?
Of course. We still have two hours until sunset, don't we?
... If I give up now,==W== I wouldn't be able to look Boss and Chitose in the eye. Not while they're fighting for their lives in the Monolith.
Ruby, Sapphire, come with me. We are finding that 80 million right now.
New Star Guild, stay here. Make sure the Dorra actually hits our account.
How pathetic. Who else could you possibly beg at this point?
Ruby, what is Lady Firenze planning? I hate to admit it, but that woman is right—we're completely out of companies to negotiate with...
Lady Firenze has already sold off all her personal assets just to keep the company afloat.
I have no idea what her plan is...==W== But should we start selling our own stuff, too?
Sell what?==W== Do you actually own anything valuable, Ruby?
Nope. Sigh... I guess we just have to trust Lady Firenze.
Hm? Are you talking to me? What's up?
You're the lady who always sings at the United Harvest bakery...==W== Right?
Singing? That sounds like me. But ...==W== sorry, honey. I'm completely swamped right now. I can't give you a show.
No, I'm not here for the song. I have all my Dorra here to buy a whole month's worth of bread!
Mom and Dad say if United Harvest loses that auction thing, you have to leave Philae.
But if that happens... I can never eat your yummy bread or hear you sing again...
So I figure if I use my allowance to buy lots of bread, maybe it'd help you stay.
Hehe... Thank you, sweetheart. But don't worry. The bakery stays right here—and so does she.
Ugh... More of Omnisky Aegis's hired goons? Give it a rest...
<size=50>Who are you calling Omnisky goons? We don't work for those scumbags!
We know all about the Monolith bidding war. We're here to pitch in and back up Boss Accord.

Damn right. Siding with Omnisky Aegis? Not a chance. I held a policy with them. They promised to cover injuries, but the second I got hurt and filed a claim, they gave me the runaround and dodged the payout!
Plus, Scarlet Sights Media reports they're hiking the deposit to 40 billion. You know they plan to squeeze every Dorra back from the Philaen people.
Many Trekkers here are Omnisky victims, but plenty of us are here to support the Boss.
You teamed up with Petal Bloom for the Grand Commissions. You stopped the Intelligent Plants. You saved Philae.
Boss Accord or Omnisky Aegis? It's a no-brainer. Here, take this—
Our guild's heading to the Lushwood Jungle next. We need supplies, so we're buying from the Boss's partners to show support.
And me! Put me down for 20 boxes of Tawny Nightingale. We're off to find a legendary Monolith in the desert, and that bread is perfect.
To buy or pre-order, please line up here!
Leave your address, and we'll deliver ASAP.
Everyone...==W== What are you doing here?
We're part of United Harvest Philae too. Helping protect our company is only natural.
We don't have much, but we all chipped in our savings. The money's with Miss Nyx. Please, accept it.
But you have your own lives to worry about.
Don't say that. If the company goes under, everything goes with it.
Besides, without you, Lady Firenze, we'd have lost our jobs to those Intelligent Plants already.
We want to repay your kindness, even a little. That's why we're here.
A massive line forms outside Deepsea Finance—people rushing over as word spreads.==RT====W==Hundreds, thousands, tens of thousands of Dorra... Old notes and crisp bills pile into a mountain of cash.
Number 20, get out there and stop them. Now!==W== If you can't drive them off, cause a panic and break the line. Stall them until sundown, and we win.
L-Lady Albedo?!==W== What are you doing here? And what do you mean, "stand down"? We haven't broken any rules—
Maybe. But the rules just changed.
The Director of the Sky Institute issued an absolute directive. From this moment on, all sabotage in the bidding war is strictly forbidden.
Impossible...! Why drop this on us now, of all times?!
Save your breath. If you have a problem, take it up with the Director herself.
Laru. Keep an eye on them.
You got it. It will just be like going on a fishing trip—eyes glued to the float until they bite.
Manager, what's our move? That line stretches for miles. At this rate, they'll hit the 80 million Dorra target in no time.
It doesn't matter. Even if they make the deposit, the Boss will never touch that required Artifact.
I planned for this. Our teams inside the Monolith have already secured every large Wishing Box.
Hi, here's your receipt. Thanks for your purchase <size=60>♪</size> We'll deliver everything to your address right away.
Bastelina? Why are you playing vendor for United Harvest Philae?
The Director's new orders! She said this isn't a Monolith bidding war anymore—it's a bid for the hearts of Philae's people.
She told us to do whatever we want...==W== And I hate sitting still! So I'm pitching in. Plus, United Harvest Philae really does sell the best fruit.
Hehe. With a little push from a brilliant witch like me, of course the people give their hearts to Boss!
Wait, did you rally all these people for us, Mistique?
Nope! The citizens and Trekkers see everything you do. They know who actually cares. I just made sure they heard you needed a hand, that's all.
Rallying this much support...==W== You truly are like the legendary Tyrant who guides the masses.
I wonder ... if you'll pick up on my hints and step into that room...
Will you summon <color=#bd3059>the Artifact</color> from the prophecy…==RT==The one that absolutely shouldn't exist in this world?

param: Mercurio maliciously tanks the market, putting your fundraising effort on the brink of failure. As word spreads, Philaens who support United Harvest come forward, and their contributions cover the final gap.
I'd like to exchange these crystal diamonds for Dorra, please.
R-Right away. This is a massive deposit, so counting them will take a moment. Please bear with me.
Whoa, there's gotta be over a thousand in here! Why does the Imperial Guard pay with these? Wouldn't a Deepsea Finance check be easier?
These gems are uniform in size and fuel major spells.==W== That's why crystal diamonds have been the standard for massive transactions since ancient times.
Dorra might be the standard now, turning these gems into a strategic resource, but the Imperial Guard clings to the old ways—like using them to pay for huge contracts.
Stockpiling for combat. A strategic reserve.
Exactly. For a faction that fights as often as the Imperial Guard, paying in crystal diamonds instead of Dorra kills two birds with one stone.
Well, well. If it isn't Firenze ...==W== and the Boss Accord crew. What a surprise running into you here.
Hiring thugs to ambush Boss, sabotaging the cable car...==W== You have some nerve showing your face here, Mercurio.
Oh, how terrifying! <size=60>♪</size> If I actually did something to upset you, I suppose I could apologize...
But we've operated strictly within the rules of the technical review.==W== Is there a problem with that?
And let's be honest: if you can't afford the deposit, any little victories you score during the review are meaningless. Right?
Sorry to burst your bubble, but we've got the deposit! With the money sorted, there's no way United Harvest Philae loses this!
Hahahaha, so confident. Let's see what you're really capable of, then <size=60>♪</size>
Thank you for waiting, Lady Firenze.==W== The count is complete. You brought 1,200 crystal diamonds. At today's rate of 5.05 million Dorra each, that totals 6.06 billion Dorra.
6 billion...! Perfect. After the deposit, we'll still have a billion Dorra left over...==W== That secures the company's daily operating costs, too.
Process the exchange immediately, please, and deposit the funds into our Monolith bidding account.

I-I'm so sorry, Lady Firenze ... and everyone from the New Star Guild! We just received an emergency alert from headquarters. The crystal diamond market is experiencing massive volatility. We need a moment to recalculate the exchange rate.
Wait, huh? What do you mean? Didn't we have over 6 billion Dorra?
Don't panic. It's just a technical correction. Stay calm.
A price drop is perfectly normal if someone else is selling off their stock.
But ... Nova doesn't have any active crystal diamond mines left. Even if someone is selling, the supply is limited. It shouldn't impact the market price that much—
The new rate from headquarters is ...==W==<color=#bd3059> 4.1 million Dorra</color> each.
How is that possible...?!==W== A 20 percent drop in a single day?! Can the market even do that?!
I'm sorry, but we have only just received the news, too.
Around noon, someone dumped a massive stockpile of crystal diamonds at Port Goldfinch. There's also rumor that a mage discovered a substitute casting material. The market is crashing.
Those factors caused the crash. Right now...==W== These diamonds are only worth 4.92 billion Dorra.
The sell-off aside, that rumor is absolute nonsense. We expect prices to bounce back by tomorrow.
That's too late. At 4.92 billion, we are still 80 million short of the deposit.
Mercurio... How desperate is Omnisky Aegis for the Philae Monolith? Crashing the crystal diamond market like this must have cost tens of billions of Dorra.
She took out a 40-billion Dorra loan from Deepsea Finance yesterday at 30 percent interest. I'd say it's safe to assume she bet the house.
Oh? And who might you be? I don't know what you're plotting, but spreading rumors is terribly rude.
Oh, no, no. An information broker values her reputation above life itself. I don't deal in rumors.
A cloaked woman strides into the lobby, holding up a cassette tape—the exact kind wished out of a Monolith.
Omnisky Aegis has two choices. Option one—buy this tape from me.==W== Option two—I play it right here, and everything on it goes public.
And looking at these Trekkers, I'm sure someone would be more than happy to lend me an Artifact to play it on.
It's been a while, my friends from the New Star Guild.
A playback Artifact? We have one in the car! I'll go grab it!
Be my guest. Let's hear what you've got.
I must admit, your bluntness actually improves my opinion of you.
Tell your manager Omnisky Aegis requires a loan of 40 billion Dorra!
I want it tonight. Ready for withdrawal at Port Goldfinch.
Y-You're joking, right? A sum that massive won't be ready==RT==until tomorrow morning at the earliest...
5 percent. Clear the funds tonight, and I'll personally==RT==guarantee a 5 percent kickback.
Are you out of your mind? Deepsea Finance has strict protocols.
We can't just approve a massive uncollateralized loan like that—
I'll put up my sister as collateral. Plus a 10 percent kickback.==RT==Do we have a deal?
H-Hey, don't look at me like that! I never took the kickback!
Her collateral was perfectly valid! And at 30 percent interest, Deepsea Finance had no reason to deny the loan.==W== It's not our job to monitor how clients spend their money...
I don't need to explain myself. I knew Firenze was scrambling for deals, so I struck first and crushed their little operation.
I simply played a brilliant move within the rules. You can't honestly say I did anything wrong.
If anything, blame your own pathetic risk management.==W== Given the circumstances, United Harvest Philae only had two real options.
Option one: win over the deep-pocketed Imperial Guard.
Option two: beg Deepsea Finance for a loan to cover the gap.
So that's why cap—==W==manager drained Deepsea Finance! And crashed the crystal diamond market!
I'll admit, I didn't expect them to raise that much cash. Still, crashing the market was definitely the right insurance <size=60>♪</size>

strings.text: Acting on Portia's hint, you and Chitose recreate the trial of the Armless Saint, finally unlocking Floor 51. Waiting for you in the shadows is a terrifying evil deity, the very one that cursed Philae with endless rain...
This floor's clear of Stellaroids, my ==SEX11==. Please watch your step.
Thanks, that's a big help.==W== But there's no Wishing Box big enough on this floor either... How many Trekkers did Omnisky Aegis send to sweep this Monolith?
That means our only option is the hidden 51st floor from the files.
My ==SEX11==, I checked the walls for hidden passages and found nothing. I also stepped on every pressure plate. They were merely traps—none opened a path to the 51st floor.
How do we get up there...?
Shall I cut a hole in the ceiling?
No, no... Brute force isn't always the answer.
Wait, there might be one other way... Noya mentioned something once. Back when the New Star Guild found the Wishing Box I was sleeping in—
O God of Grace, please…==RT==Please let us find an absurdly huge Wishing Box!
Apparently, Iris made that exact wish right before stepping into the elevator.==W== I don't know if her prayer was actually answered...
But either way, they ended up on the floor with that Wishing Box. The one I was inside.
I see. If we make a wish before entering the elevator...
O God of Grace, please... Please let us find an absurdly huge Wishing Box!
O God of Grace, please let us find a Wishing Box bigger than my hand.
H-How...?! Hmm... Let me try this instead—
O God of Grace, please... Please let us find an absurdly huge Stellaroid!
... Sigh... Nothing, huh. Guess wishing alone won't get us to the hidden 51st floor.
Makes sense, actually. If saying your wish out loud was enough, way more Trekkers would be there by now.
Our only other option... Ugh, I hate to admit it... Is the convenience store. We might find a lead there.
Welcome. What can I get for you today?
Hey Portia, afternoon. Got a question for you.
... Huh? Portia, no time for games.==W== Please, listen to me.
Um... My ==SEX11==? What are you doing? As far as I can tell, she is acting the same as always...
The same? No way! The whole New Star Guild has heard her talk normally!
Every time I see her, she only repeats a few phrases.==W== I always assume she is a magic doll.
N-No, that's not it at all...==W== Come on, Portia.
Do a former coworker a favor. Tell me how to reach the hidden room in this Monolith, or the 51st floor.
No comment. I like customers, but not when they block the counter without buying.
That is a first. You are right, my ==SEX11==, she does speak off-script.
Even so, she looks annoyed.==W== Ugh... Guess I have to use that trick.
Tell you what. You tell me how to reach the hidden room, and I'll think about picking up shifts here again.
Really? We have the pork cutlet bento in stock—your favorite, right? Here, on the house.
No thanks, I'm not hungry... I'll pass.
If I eat that bento and lose my mind like last time, we're in trouble.
Hmph, suit yourself. Buy a Potential Drink then. It's good.
Portia pulls a Potential Drink from behind the counter and slides it over.
... Yeah. This should be safe to drink.
Thank you. Hope to see you soon.
My ==SEX11==, she clearly knows the way to the hidden room. Do we really walk away without finding out?
Monolith staff are restricted by their own rules. They can't just speak freely. But—she already gave us the answer.
I flip over Chitose's empty bottle. Scrawled on the bottom is:
<size=38>==RT====RT====RT==<align="right">Next to it is a tiny footnote: Danger. Be careful.==RT==And if you don't take a job here, I lose my excuse to slack off.
Repeat history... Where have I heard that before?
According to records from centuries ago, the Saint and attendant==RT==started from where that exact cable station is located.
They ziplined through the dangerous lake...
Scaled the Monolith, and faced down the evil deity...
Come to think of it, I'm looking at Philae's newest hero and an attendant with an injured hand right now. You walked that exact same path to the Monolith to end this pointless bidding war.
It's almost like that legendary scene. Quite a sight... Too bad someone's trying to ruin the moment.
Am I? You know what they say about history repeating itself.
Wait... Was Serena tipping me off back then?==W== No, that's impossible. She couldn't have predicted I'd end up in this exact situation. I'm overthinking it.
Chitose, I have a plan.==W== We're going to play the role of the Armless Saint.
My ==SEX11==, please hold onto my family.
You want to play the Armless Saint. Therefore, an arm must be severed.
But I refuse to watch you mutilate yourself. If an arm must go, take mine...
Whoa, wait! I said play the Armless Saint. I never said anything about actually chopping an arm off.
If repeating history is the key to that hidden room, the New Star Guild must have done something similar by accident when they found me.
They didn't plan for it, so there's no way they pulled off a perfect reenactment. A few key elements must have lined up by chance.
Following that logic, it doesn't need to be exact. If we recreate the right conditions, the path should open.
I see. So an amputation is unnecessary?
Right. No amputations. But to fake an unusable arm...
Chitose, I need you to dislocate my shoulder.
No. Even if we make it inside, we still have a massive Stellaroid to fight.
Besides, I'm no help in combat anyway. Let me pull my weight here.
Chitose, this is an order from your ==SEX11==.==W== Dislocate my left shoulder.
... Understood. My ==SEX11==,==W== please bite down on this cloth.
It happens in a flash. A sickening crunch, and my left arm goes completely limp.
Ugh... I braced myself, but damn, that hurts... Still, that covers the "armless" requirement.
God of Grace above, grant us passage to vanquish the evil deity... The one drowning Philae in endless rain.
How did Serena even know about this trick...?
No time to overthink it. Let's keep moving.
I will count to three, and set your shoulder on "three."
千都世接上主角的关节
Ngh...?! That hurts... Well, at least the arm moves again.==W== And you reset it on "two"!
My apologies.==W== If you brace yourself, your muscles tense up, making it much harder to reset the joint.==W== Also, your shoulder remains injured. Please avoid using this arm for now.
Thanks for the heads-up.==W== But considering the Stellaroid we face next... You bear the real burden, Chitose.
I feel bad leaving the tough parts to you.
No apology needed. I am your blade, my ==SEX11==. Carving a path for you remains my sole duty, no matter the danger.
Going by Noya's experience, the Stellaroids in these hidden rooms are massive and impossible to beat. They only manage to grab the Wishing Box and run.
We have no reason to force a fight. Making our wish is all that matters.
Understood. However...==W== After you make your wish, I have a favor to ask, my ==SEX11==.
No need to be so formal. What's on your mind?
Are you willing to make a <color=#3faeae>"soul pact"</color> with me? I am a blade. A blade supposedly has no soul.
But ... to my shame, this body is an incomplete weapon. Since I retain human parts, perhaps a soul lingers inside me too. That is what I think, anyway.
Besides... Everyone else by your side already shares a <color=#3faeae>soul pact</color> with you. I am the only one left out. It feels ... unfair.
A <color=#3faeae>soul pact</color>... It seems safe enough. And looking ahead, the benefits definitely outweigh the drawbacks.
Alright. If you want a pact, Chitose,==W== start thinking of a wish.
My ==SEX11==, there is a Wishing Box over there.
Finally! A Wishing Box bigger than my hand!
Wait... This place looks like the other floors. Are we sure this is a hidden room?
It appears identical, yes. But unlike the floors below... The air carries a faint scent of the tide.
... The tide? Well, as long as there's no giant Stellaroid guarding the box, I'll take it.
Let's make our wish and get out of here.
Chitose clears out the smaller Stellaroids. I rush to the box and make my wish.
O God of Grace,==W== please grant me a compact, short-barreled gun I can fire one-handed—
A flash of steel cuts across my vision.==W== Then, something in front of me is silently cleaved in two.
How bizarre... These books are moving as if they have a mind of their own.
Identical picture books sprout from the floor. Before I know it, Chitose and I are surrounded by a floating swarm.
...==W== Are these books==W== the Stellaroids guarding the box?
And these books look just like the ones from Darcia's memories...
Please hurry, my ==SEX11==. I'm sensing a vile aura.
I turn to the Wishing Box to recite the prayer.==RT==But the severed page flutters down and lands on it.
The ink pulses with a strange power. I open my mouth,==RT==and the words read themselves.

<color=#bd3059>The Devil Emperor wakes within the pupil,==RT==dividing the power of death among all living things.==RT====RT==The Emperor withdraws their grace.==RT==Sweet dew becomes bitter wormwood.==RT====RT==The earth shatters. The anointed wicked rise==RT==from the bottomless pit.</color>
<color=#bd3059>This place shall be stripped of its name.==RT==Left barren and lifeless...
My ==SEX11==, please make your wish with peace of mind;==W== no matter what demons may appear, I shall hold them back for you.
I was once mere iron, caked in dirt.
<color=#bd3059><size=78>Its roar scrapes through my mind like iron filings.</color></size>
The stench of the deep sea floods the room.
But then I met you, my ==SEX11==.
I am the blade you wield.
This corruption cannot dull my edge.

Um... My ==SEX11==? What are you doing? As far as I can tell, she is acting the same as always...
The same? No way! The whole New Star Guild has heard her talk normally!
Every time I see her, she only repeats a few phrases.==W== I always assume she is a magic doll.
N-No, that's not it at all...==W== Come on, Portia.
Do a former coworker a favor. Tell me how to reach the hidden room in this Monolith, or the 51st floor.
No comment. I like customers, but not when they block the counter without buying.
That is a first. You are right, my ==SEX11==, she does speak off-script.
Even so, she looks annoyed.==W== Ugh... Guess I have to use that trick.
Tell you what. You tell me how to reach the hidden room, and I'll think about picking up shifts here again.
Really? We have the pork cutlet bento in stock—your favorite, right? Here, on the house.
No thanks, I'm not hungry... I'll pass.
If I eat that bento and lose my mind like last time, we're in trouble.
Hmph, suit yourself. Buy a Potential Drink then. It's good.
Portia pulls a Potential Drink from behind the counter and slides it over.
... Yeah. This should be safe to drink.
Thank you. Hope to see you soon.
My ==SEX11==, she clearly knows the way to the hidden room. Do we really walk away without finding out?
Monolith staff are restricted by their own rules. They can't just speak freely. But—she already gave us the answer.
I flip over Chitose's empty bottle. Scrawled on the bottom is:
<size=38>==RT====RT====RT==<align="right">Next to it is a tiny footnote: Danger. Be careful.==RT==And if you don't take a job here, I lose my excuse to slack off.
Repeat history... Where have I heard that before?
According to records from centuries ago, the Saint and attendant==RT==started from where that exact cable station is located.
They ziplined through the dangerous lake...
Scaled the Monolith, and faced down the evil deity...
Come to think of it, I'm looking at Philae's newest hero and an attendant with an injured hand right now. You walked that exact same path to the Monolith to end this pointless bidding war.
It's almost like that legendary scene. Quite a sight... Too bad someone's trying to ruin the moment.
Am I? You know what they say about history repeating itself.
Wait... Was Serena tipping me off back then?==W== No, that's impossible. She couldn't have predicted I'd end up in this exact situation. I'm overthinking it.
Chitose, I have a plan.==W== We're going to play the role of the Armless Saint.
My ==SEX11==, please hold onto my family.
You want to play the Armless Saint. Therefore, an arm must be severed.
But I refuse to watch you mutilate yourself. If an arm must go, take mine...
Whoa, wait! I said play the Armless Saint. I never said anything about actually chopping an arm off.
If repeating history is the key to that hidden room, the New Star Guild must have done something similar by accident when they found me.
They didn't plan for it, so there's no way they pulled off a perfect reenactment. A few key elements must have lined up by chance.
Following that logic, it doesn't need to be exact. If we recreate the right conditions, the path should open.
I see. So an amputation is unnecessary?
Right. No amputations. But to fake an unusable arm...
Chitose, I need you to dislocate my shoulder.
No. Even if we make it inside, we still have a massive Stellaroid to fight.
Besides, I'm no help in combat anyway. Let me pull my weight here.
Chitose, this is an order from your ==SEX11==.==W== Dislocate my left shoulder.
... Understood. My ==SEX11==,==W== please bite down on this cloth.
It happens in a flash. A sickening crunch, and my left arm goes completely limp.
Ugh... I braced myself, but damn, that hurts... Still, that covers the "armless" requirement.
God of Grace above, grant us passage to vanquish the evil deity... The one drowning Philae in endless rain.
How did Serena even know about this trick...?
No time to overthink it. Let's keep moving.
I will count to three, and set your shoulder on "three."
千都世接上主角的关节
Ngh...?! That hurts... Well, at least the arm moves again.==W== And you reset it on "two"!
My apologies.==W== If you brace yourself, your muscles tense up, making it much harder to reset the joint.==W== Also, your shoulder remains injured. Please avoid using this arm for now.
Thanks for the heads-up.==W== But considering the Stellaroid we face next... You bear the real burden, Chitose.
I feel bad leaving the tough parts to you.
No apology needed. I am your blade, my ==SEX11==. Carving a path for you remains my sole duty, no matter the danger.
Going by Noya's experience, the Stellaroids in these hidden rooms are massive and impossible to beat. They only manage to grab the Wishing Box and run.
We have no reason to force a fight. Making our wish is all that matters.
Understood. However...==W== After you make your wish, I have a favor to ask, my ==SEX11==.
No need to be so formal. What's on your mind?
Are you willing to make a <color=#3faeae>"soul pact"</color> with me? I am a blade. A blade supposedly has no soul.
But ... to my shame, this body is an incomplete weapon. Since I retain human parts, perhaps a soul lingers inside me too. That is what I think, anyway.
Besides... Everyone else by your side already shares a <color=#3faeae>soul pact</color> with you. I am the only one left out. It feels ... unfair.
A <color=#3faeae>soul pact</color>... It seems safe enough. And looking ahead, the benefits definitely outweigh the drawbacks.
Alright. If you want a pact, Chitose,==W== start thinking of a wish.
My ==SEX11==, there is a Wishing Box over there.
Finally! A Wishing Box bigger than my hand!
Wait... This place looks like the other floors. Are we sure this is a hidden room?
It appears identical, yes. But unlike the floors below... The air carries a faint scent of the tide.
... The tide? Well, as long as there's no giant Stellaroid guarding the box, I'll take it.
Let's make our wish and get out of here.
Chitose clears out the smaller Stellaroids. I rush to the box and make my wish.
O God of Grace,==W== please grant me a compact, short-barreled gun I can fire one-handed—
A flash of steel cuts across my vision.==W== Then, something in front of me is silently cleaved in two.
How bizarre... These books are moving as if they have a mind of their own.
Identical picture books sprout from the floor. Before I know it, Chitose and I are surrounded by a floating swarm.
...==W== Are these books==W== the Stellaroids guarding the box?
And these books look just like the ones from Darcia's memories...
Please hurry, my ==SEX11==. I'm sensing a vile aura.
I turn to the Wishing Box to recite the prayer.==RT==But the severed page flutters down and lands on it.
The ink pulses with a strange power. I open my mouth,==RT==and the words read themselves.

<color=#bd3059>The Devil Emperor wakes within the pupil,==RT==dividing the power of death among all living things.==RT====RT==The Emperor withdraws their grace.==RT==Sweet dew becomes bitter wormwood.==RT====RT==The earth shatters. The anointed wicked rise==RT==from the bottomless pit.</color>
<color=#bd3059>This place shall be stripped of its name.==RT==Left barren and lifeless...
My ==SEX11==, please make your wish with peace of mind;==W== no matter what demons may appear, I shall hold them back for you.
I was once mere iron, caked in dirt.
<color=#bd3059><size=78>Its roar scrapes through my mind like iron filings.</color></size>
The stench of the deep sea floods the room.
But then I met you, my ==SEX11==.
I am the blade you wield.
This corruption cannot dull my edge.

strings.text: Using fragmented knowledge, you wish the Scepter of Death into existence and win the bid. Mercurio leads Omnisky Aegis out of Philae. Meanwhile, a friend you thought you knew reveals who she really is.
... I need this weapon to fire lead-core, brass-cased rounds.==W==
Rounds are packed with smokeless powder and a sensitive primer.
That's my wish. Please grant it.
I grab the dark Artifact. Cold metal and plastic... It feels familiar.
My ==SEX11==, its arm is severed! Your status?
The wish worked.==W== We're done here—let's move, Chitose!
Trekkers...==W== Why do you not fear—
My ==SEX11==, its arm is regenerating! Fast! It's about to strike!
Get to the elevator. I will cover you.
Chitose slides in, and I hammer the close button.
Chitose uses her Swordless Style, blocking the giant hand coming toward us.
Phew, that was close.==W== Good move, Chitose.
You flatter me.==W== As your blade, it's my duty.
Still...==W== Is this the Scepter of Death?
Yeah...==W== Looks like Amber's gun,==W== but this one uses gunpowder.==W== Pull the trigger, no magic required.
Powder... Like that in fireworks? It can do this?
Not exactly. It's a different kind. I don't remember the details,==W== but it's buried in my head.
Anyway, we won. Omnisky Aegis could never wish for an Artifact like this.
A weapon requiring no magic... Hmm—
My ==SEX11==, I am also a weapon that requires no magic—and I can talk to you!==W== You clearly don't need this Scepter of Death...!!
What? Where did that come from? It's going to the Grace Imperium. I won't be using it.
But you looked too happy when you were describing it.
Chitose is getting competitive. Time to change the subject...
Right, we got what we came for. Let's make our soul pact while we have the chance.
Ah, right. The soul pact. As you command.==W== Boss, here is my wish—
U-Um...==W== Apologies, my ==SEX11==. I realized I don't have a wish.==W== Or rather, all my wishes have come true.==W== I can't think of anything to ask of you...
How can that be? There must be something you want to do.
The wish to be with you again==W== is already fulfilled.
The wish to see the world through your eyes, as your blade...==W== That has come true, too.
I do want to protect you and never leave your side.==W== But that's my duty as your blade—something I have to earn myself. Wishing for it ...==W== doesn't feel right.
So... Can we complete the soul pact without a wish?
Can't do that. If I take your soul without giving anything back, it's no longer a trade.
The best I can do is <r=·>owe</r> <r=·>you</r> <r=·>a</r> <r=·>wish</r> <r=·>for</r> <r=·>later</r>, but even then, you still need an actual wish in mind.
A wish... A wish...==W== Ah...==W== Well, there is one thing I might wish for...
O-Okay...==W== Then...==W== Boss, here is my wish...
My ==SEX11==, would you... Would you forge a new blade with me?
And when that wish comes true... My soul is yours.
Yeah. I've got your back. Forging a blade sounds like fun. I'm looking forward to it.
Chitose reaches out==W== and holds on to the hem of my shirt.
Is everything ok?==W== You're blushing. Are you feeling alright?
It-It's nothing! I must be flustered by the intense battle just now...
Um... I look forward to the day we forge that blade together, my ==SEX11==...
Ah, we're here. Let's head back together, Chitose.
Stepping outside the Monolith, we hand the Artifact to Mistique,==RT==who is waiting outside, yawning.
We manage to deliver it right before sunset.
The next day, Grace Imperium announces the final bidding results—
For the Philae Monolith leasing project spanning 996 to 1005, the winning bidder is:==W== United Harvest Philae.

The official award notice will be sent to your company shortly. You have 30 days upon receipt to assume control of the Philae Monolith per the contract.==W== Dated: Monolith Calendar Year 996, Venatio Month 16th.
We pulled off an impossible comeback at the end. A miracle.
Oh, come on. We couldn't have done it without everyone pitching in!==W== Right, Chitose?
Mm...==W== Yeah...==W== This means I have time to forge a blade with my ==SEX11==.
Phew... Now that I can relax, I'm exhausted.==W== We'll leave the rest to you, Firenze.
We thank the Grace Imperium, Lady Albedo.
No need.==W== We chose the company that prioritizes the freedom and happiness of the people of Philae.
Well, I have other business to attend to, so I'll take my leave.
Photos,==W== photos,==W== more photos!==W== Look here, Boss! You're tomorrow's front page.==W== Smile! ★
Hey, camera off me. Aim it at Firenze.
At least Philae is finally at peace.
We lost, and burned 10 billion crashing the crystal diamond market...==W== Will we be fired?
The Senate will definitely axe me.==W== As for you? Hard to say.
Then again... If we'd blocked that 80 million, we would've won...==W== What is the Sky Institute Director playing at?
A call from Geminia?==W== They definitely want my head.
I'm sorry, Madam CEO. I promised a win and failed.==W== I officially resign from all positions.
Nonsense. You're staying, with full authority.==W==
The Senate threw a fit, but I handled it.==W== The bid, the market crash... They were all my calls.==W== I've already submitted my resignation.
Heehee, it takes me resigning for you to call me "sis" at work huh? Relax, they rejected it,==W== so no one takes the blame. <size=53>♪</size>
They did? But ... how?==W== No one needs to take the fall?
A big shot came straight to me for a lifetime policy.==W== Once the Senate saw who it was, they were too terrified to even squeak.==W== Hilarious.
... I see.==W== Even so, Omnisky Aegis should just pull out of Philae.
Worried about Firenze and the Boss retaliating? Relax. The big shot promised to smooth things over.
No, it's not Firenze.==W== I think I made a fatal mistake.
I thought riding the coattails would buy us more power at Omnisky Aegis...==W== But I was wrong.==W== We—and this entire company—are nothing but pawns in this little game.
Omnisky Aegis quietly pulls out of Philae the very same night==RT==United Harvest Philae wins the bid.
Right now, Noya and the crew are prepping the Lucky Oasis.==RT==They plan to set sail tomorrow to track down leads on the orphanage.
Phew... Time to leave Philae. It's only been a few months, but honestly, it feels like a lifetime.
Such beautiful petals. They remind me of home.
Your home...==W== It must be an incredibly peaceful place. I'd love to see it for myself someday.
Wait for me here, Chitose. I have a private meeting with Serena.==W== Once I wrap this up, we can hit the road.
So this is Serena's room...==W== Right. I should probably ask her about the Armless Saint while I'm at it.==W== And those weird texts about the Tyrant I found in the Monolith.
I've been waiting. Please, come in.
Excuse me—==W==huh?==W== Oh, sorry, I think I have the wrong room.
You don't.==W== I'm just not wearing my cloak today.==W== Don't you recognize me, Boss?
The cloak...==W== Wait, so you really are Serena?==W== Since I'd never actually seen your face, I was dead sure I had the wrong person.
Guilty as charged.==W== Since it's just the two of us, hiding under a hood felt rather rude.==W== I figured it was time we met face-to-face.
Still...==W== It's crazy how just ditching a cloak completely changes a person's entire aura.
Anyway... You mentioned there was something you wanted to discuss?
Truth be told, selling information is just a side gig. My real passion is the history of the Tyrant.
You unfroze the legendary Boss Accord. You possess multiple Seals of Grace, including one that's never even been documented.
So, I was hoping we could talk. I figured you might be able to shed some light on my Tyrant research.
Makes sense. You've done a lot for us, so it's only right that I tell you what I know. No secrets.
Unfortunately...==W== By the time the New Star Guild pulled me out of the Monolith, I'd already lost my memories.
I can't mention <color=#3faeae>Vita</color>, <color=#3faeae>the White Room</color>, or <color=#3faeae>the king piece's power</color>... But the rest should be fine.
I know about your amnesia. That's why I'd rather ask about a few things that seem ... off.

For instance,==W== you waged a company war for the New Star Guild and the Ashwind Clan.==W== Actually, once you have the Seal of Grace, you should be able to get Creta Trading to treat your companions with proper respect just by going through a few well-connected intermediaries.==W== That would've been the smarter play.
Back then, I barely knew which way was up. I wasn't thinking that far ahead.
But even if I had, I still would've chosen the company war.
Sure, those of us with a Seal of Grace could negotiate peace. But what about the kids on the street who don't have one?
Haha, you are a gentle soul.==W== I imagine you would've stepped in to help Fuyuka even if I hadn't offered information in exchange.
Probably.==W== Just like the New Star Guild saved me at my lowest. We're all Trekkers. Helping each other out is what we do.
A spirit of mutual aid...==W== What about later, then? When Darcia hailed you as the Tyrant, why did you turn her down?
H-How do you know about that?
Heh, I'm an information broker. I have my sources.==W== With her unwavering loyalty, you could've used her power to get things done a lot faster.
It was a strong power, sure.==W== But if you rely on brute force to make people do what you want...==W== Even with good intentions, it always ends badly.
It's like trekking.==W== If I only want to follow the paved path, I'll only ever take the same route as every other==W== and never see anything new.
If I want real change, then I can't just pick the path that "looks easy."
Your mindset surprises me.==W== It's nothing like that of a CEO.
Someone told me the same thing recently.==W== So, how does a proper CEO think?
It varies. But at the end of the day, most people who climb that high aren't saints.
And someone like you, willing to sacrifice yourself for others? That's rare...==W== You could say it's practically nonexistent.
I think you're exaggerating...==W== But either way, someone like me clearly has nothing to do with the legendary evil Tyrant.
True.==W== Even if you were the real Tyrant... I'm sure you'd be a kind one.
Then, let's try a different angle...==W== During your time in Philae, what has been your impression of the place?
Phew. That's all I can tell you.
Thank you for your time. This information is invaluable—it's a massive step forward for my Tyrant research.
Wait here a moment. I have a gift for you, to thank you for today.
You don't have to do that.==W== Oh, and Serena? Since you've been studying the Tyrant, have you heard of this before?
The Devil Emperor wakes within the pupil...
Dividing the power of death among all living things.
The legendary Tyrant is immortal. Kill ==SEX4== with ordinary weapons, and ==SEX== resurrects time and again.==W== And with every rebirth, ==SEX== returns stronger.
The Tyrant overturns the rules of society, empowers ordinary people to slaughter powerful mages, and destroys the world.
The Emperor withdraws their grace.==RT==Sweet dew becomes bitter wormwood.
The earth shatters. The anointed wicked==RT==rise from the bottomless pit.
This place shall be stripped of its name.==RT==Left barren and lifeless for eternity.
So...==W== This prophecy foretells==W== the end of the world?
Yes.==W== Every century, the Tyrant is reborn in Nova. And the only way to stop the world from ending ...==W== is to <color=#bd3059>kill ==SEX4==</color>.
Right... Kill the Tyrant.==W== Haha...==W== A legendary figure like that couldn't actually exist, right?
Hehe. I forgot to mention... The Tyrant in the Book of Grace Prophecies is someone who does the good deeds no one else will.
Oh. So they're a good person.==W== But why are you telling me this? It sounds like you're implying that … I'm...
I've watched you for a long time. Every action, every word—they perfectly align with the prophecy.
And who else but the Tyrant could wish for a weapon that doesn't even belong in this world?
W-Wait a minute! What are you talking about?! This is all your speculation!
Speculation... Yes. But the prophecy is never wrong, and you are a ninety-nine percent match.
But what if I'm not the Tyrant?!==W== You'd be killing the wrong person!
You're right.==W== But if sacrificing your one life could save the world...==W== I am willing to take that gamble.
If my judgment is wrong, I will find a way to atone.
What good is atonement after I'm dead?!==W== This is insane...!
You are a good person, and I hold no personal grudge against you.==W== So, I am deeply sorry, but for the sake of this world... I must ask you to die. You have my gratitude.
Please, accept this bullet—one that grants equal death to all.
I hope this time, you find eternal rest.==W== Farewell...==W== Tyrant.

You unfroze the legendary Boss Accord. You possess multiple Seals of Grace, including one that's never even been documented.
So, I was hoping we could talk. I figured you might be able to shed some light on my Tyrant research.
Makes sense. You've done a lot for us, so it's only right that I tell you what I know. No secrets.
Unfortunately...==W== By the time the New Star Guild pulled me out of the Monolith, I'd already lost my memories.
I can't mention <color=#3faeae>Vita</color>, <color=#3faeae>the White Room</color>, or <color=#3faeae>the king piece's power</color>... But the rest should be fine.
I know about your amnesia. That's why I'd rather ask about a few things that seem ... off.

For instance,==W== you waged a company war for the New Star Guild and the Ashwind Clan.==W== Actually, once you have the Seal of Grace, you should be able to get Creta Trading to treat your companions with proper respect just by going through a few well-connected intermediaries.==W== That would've been the smarter play.
Back then, I barely knew which way was up. I wasn't thinking that far ahead.
But even if I had, I still would've chosen the company war.
Sure, those of us with a Seal of Grace could negotiate peace. But what about the kids on the street who don't have one?
Haha, you are a gentle soul.==W== I imagine you would've stepped in to help Fuyuka even if I hadn't offered information in exchange.
Probably.==W== Just like the New Star Guild saved me at my lowest. We're all Trekkers. Helping each other out is what we do.
A spirit of mutual aid...==W== What about later, then? When Darcia hailed you as the Tyrant, why did you turn her down?
H-How do you know about that?
Heh, I'm an information broker. I have my sources.==W== With her unwavering loyalty, you could've used her power to get things done a lot faster.
It was a strong power, sure.==W== But if you rely on brute force to make people do what you want...==W== Even with good intentions, it always ends badly.
It's like trekking.==W== If I only want to follow the paved path, I'll only ever take the same route as every other==W== and never see anything new.
If I want real change, then I can't just pick the path that "looks easy."
Your mindset surprises me.==W== It's nothing like that of a CEO.
Someone told me the same thing recently.==W== So, how does a proper CEO think?
It varies. But at the end of the day, most people who climb that high aren't saints.
And someone like you, willing to sacrifice yourself for others? That's rare...==W== You could say it's practically nonexistent.
I think you're exaggerating...==W== But either way, someone like me clearly has nothing to do with the legendary evil Tyrant.
True.==W== Even if you were the real Tyrant... I'm sure you'd be a kind one.
Then, let's try a different angle...==W== During your time in Philae, what has been your impression of the place?
Phew. That's all I can tell you.
Thank you for your time. This information is invaluable—it's a massive step forward for my Tyrant research.
Wait here a moment. I have a gift for you, to thank you for today.
You don't have to do that.==W== Oh, and Serena? Since you've been studying the Tyrant, have you heard of this before?
The Devil Emperor wakes within the pupil...
Dividing the power of death among all living things.
The legendary Tyrant is immortal. Kill ==SEX4== with ordinary weapons, and ==SEX== resurrects time and again.==W== And with every rebirth, ==SEX== returns stronger.
The Tyrant overturns the rules of society, empowers ordinary people to slaughter powerful mages, and destroys the world.
The Emperor withdraws their grace.==RT==Sweet dew becomes bitter wormwood.
The earth shatters. The anointed wicked==RT==rise from the bottomless pit.
This place shall be stripped of its name.==RT==Left barren and lifeless for eternity.
So...==W== This prophecy foretells==W== the end of the world?
Yes.==W== Every century, the Tyrant is reborn in Nova. And the only way to stop the world from ending ...==W== is to <color=#bd3059>kill ==SEX4==</color>.
Right... Kill the Tyrant.==W== Haha...==W== A legendary figure like that couldn't actually exist, right?
Hehe. I forgot to mention... The Tyrant in the Book of Grace Prophecies is someone who does the good deeds no one else will.
Oh. So they're a good person.==W== But why are you telling me this? It sounds like you're implying that … I'm...
I've watched you for a long time. Every action, every word—they perfectly align with the prophecy.
And who else but the Tyrant could wish for a weapon that doesn't even belong in this world?
W-Wait a minute! What are you talking about?! This is all your speculation!
Speculation... Yes. But the prophecy is never wrong, and you are a ninety-nine percent match.
But what if I'm not the Tyrant?!==W== You'd be killing the wrong person!
You're right.==W== But if sacrificing your one life could save the world...==W== I am willing to take that gamble.
If my judgment is wrong, I will find a way to atone.
What good is atonement after I'm dead?!==W== This is insane...!
You are a good person, and I hold no personal grudge against you.==W== So, I am deeply sorry, but for the sake of this world... I must ask you to die. You have my gratitude.
Please, accept this bullet—one that grants equal death to all.
I hope this time, you find eternal rest.==W== Farewell...==W== Tyrant.

strings.text: Otoha and Chitose arrive in time to pull you out of Serena's sights. The rest of Grace Imperium doesn't seem to support her. Desperate to shake your pursuers, you and Chitose dash for the hotel's only way out.
But what if I'm not the Tyrant?!==W== You'd be killing the wrong person!
You're right.==W== But if sacrificing your one life could save the world...==W== I am willing to take that gamble.
If my judgment is wrong, I will find a way to atone.
What good is atonement after I'm dead?!==W== This is insane...!
You are a good person, and I hold no personal grudge against you.==W== So, I am deeply sorry, but for the sake of this world... I must ask you to die. You have my gratitude.
Please, accept this bullet—one that grants equal death to all.
I hope this time, you find eternal rest.==W== Farewell... Tyrant.
The moment Serena pulls the trigger—a crack of violet lightning blasts through the window and rips the Scepter of Death from her hand.
That magic energy signature…==RT==So you stationed a sniper on the roof across the street.
(That violet shot... I think I've seen it before.)
Huh, a miscalculation on my part.==RT==I didn't expect you to have a backup plan, Tyrant.
But this confirms it. I am now one hundred percent sure==RT==that you are the legendary Tyrant.
Most CEOs don't need a sniper watching over them at a meet-up.
That means you're terrified of the "Hero"==RT==in the prophecy taking you out. Am I right, Tyrant?
We are way off the track...?!==W== What Tyrant? What Hero? Where is she getting all this gibberish from?!
Otoha, I thought it was you. How did you—
My field of fire is narrow. I can barely pin that crazy woman down.
I'll cover you. Backup's outside. Now go!
Still, with the Scepter of Death only five meters away from Serena, even if I bolt for the door, there is no guarantee that I can make it out...
Great aim... Your sniper really wants to keep you alive, don't they, Tyrant?
Serena, just listen. I'm not who you think I am, and I know nothing about the world ending! This has to be some kind of mistake. So please, just stay calm and let's talk this through.
Serena... That name... Heh, I might as well tell you. It's a name I've cast aside, from back when I was still human.
I cherish the time we've spent together under that name. But now, please call me Angie. That is who I am today—the one who has sworn to save the world.
Your friends are desperate to keep you breathing. I can feel it.
But I'm a lot more resolved to make sure you don't!
What the hell?! She'd rather take a shot than let me live!
My ==SEX11==, this woman reeks of corruption, and she wishes you harm... I should have ended her when I had the chance.
But now she's pointed her gun at you. This time, I will show no mercy.
Chitose, no need to take her head-on.==W== Let's get out of here.
Cough... They slipped away. That girl blocked the bullet of the Scepter of Death with a blade! Tyrant, the people you keep close ... are tough to deal with.
"A woman reeks of corruption..."==W== Huh, she's not wrong. I really am hopeless. But as long as I can protect Nova...
Tyrant, the Nova you know is just a bubble. You and your companions have no idea what kind of horrors are out there.
My ==SEX11==, fall back behind me. I'll clear the way.
Where the blade strikes, all falls silent. Ha—
The intel is true—warriors by the Tyrant's side all have a knack for something.
You blocked my Swordless Style. Now, who are you, and why are you coming after my ==SEX11==?
You want our names...? Why bother? You will die here today anyway.
The Tyrant seeks to end the world. Any Novian has the right to put ==SEX4== down.
You've got skill, I give you that. Why don't you drop that blade and surrender? We'll put in a good word with the Chairperson. Get you enrolled into the Salvation Committee.
I reject the offer. My life belongs to my ==SEX11== entirely.
Chitose, stop wasting time on them. Stay close to me.
Damn it! There's a sniper outside!
You took your eyes off me in the fight. That's why you lost.
Otoha, nice save! Right on time.
Heh. Chitose distracted them, and they left their backs wide open. Easy shot.
Thanks for your aid, but you flatter me. I was just following my ==SEX11=='s command.
May I ask... Was it you who directed me to my ==SEX11== with those petals outside the hotel?
(My ==SEX11== has been inside for a while now. Can that information broker really be trusted?)
(A puff of wind stirs the petals... Is this a sign from the Gods again? Wait... Their movement looks ... unnatural.)
(The petals randomly drift toward a room window. The woman==RT==who stands by the window looks like that information broker.)
Good guess. But don't thank me yet. Your ==SEX11== owes me a favor, one I plan to collect later,==W== so I won't let anything bad happen to ==SEX4==. You could say I did this for myself.
... Alright, Boss, time to head to the higher floor. I've arranged an escape route for you—Heh heh, you already know my methods, don't you?
What's all that clattering? Are they refurnishing rooms or something?
Stay focused, Laru. We have to find the Director. Fast.
I say the chance is slim. Being all elusive and secret, we'll never find her if she doesn't want to be found.
Oh, I've got an idea! Let's grab some fries. I know her favorite kind. She'll come out the second she smells them. What do you say?
...==W== Can't you get serious, sometimes perhaps?
I am being serious! I racked my brain for this "fishing her out" plan, you know!
Lady Albedo, we've got a situation. The hotel is swarming with Sentinels of Dawn and Imperial Guards. Outside are Dusk Arbiters.
Wait, those three are teaming up? That's new.
No, none of them are calling the shots here. The Salvation Committee does.
Salvation ... Committee? Sounds like some kind of charity group.

No, it's a secret faction inside Grace Imperium. Officially called "The Special Committee for the Salvation of the Nova Continent and Neutralization of the Tyrant." Their mission is to kill the legendary Tyrant and stop the apocalypse the prophecy foretells.
Alright, they are after the legendary Tyrant, not the Boss from Boss Accord. But how are we supposed to kill a legend?
Lady Albedo, why did you just go silent?
Our Director also runs the Salvation Committee. So if the Committee is getting involved, that means ... she has concluded that ==PLAYER_NAME== is the Tyrant.
Why would she even think that? How could the good old Boss be the one to end the world? That just doesn't make sense...

I don't know what the Director has decided. But she has already made her call. Normally, a resolution from Tetrad Aspects is required to motion all three factions. But this time, I haven't received any notification at all.
So, she went this far without the Tetrad Aspects' approval. Which means...<r=·> She</r><r=·> is</r><r=·> probably</r><r=·> acting</r><r=·> on</r><r=·> her</r><r=·> own</r><r=·> authority</r>.
Ugh... What is she even thinking?
The Director is ... acting on her own authority? So Boss didn't do anything wrong, right?
Then let's beat her to it. Protect the Boss before the Director can get ==SEX4==, and keep things from spiraling further. What do you say?
Good point! Finding Boss is way easier. I got this!
Good, the Sky Institute's here to help. Hahaha! Tyrant, you've got nowhere to run!
Damn it, the Grace Imperium is also in the way.
That's ... Bastelina, Laru, and Albedo—all in Grace Imperium uniforms. Which side are they on?
Otoha, is there another way out?
No. The only exit's behind them, Boss. Lure them to the window, and I'll handle the rest.
Boss, come over here to us lovely ladies!
Lady Albedo, the Chairperson has ordered us to capture the Tyrant. Your assistance is appreciated.
Sorry, but Lady Albedo isn't a member of the Salvation Committee, and she's under no obligation to follow those orders.
And you, as Sentinel of Dawns, how dare you attack the CEO of Boss Accord without the Tetrad Aspects' approval?
We will deal with the procedure later. If we waited for the Tetrad Aspects to authorize every action, Nova would already be in ruins.
We're here to save the world, save the future of Nova. So set aside whatever connection you have to the Tyrant and work with us.
I'm afraid I can't. Even if your cause is just, you still can't bypass Grace Imperium's authorization process.
Hah... What a load of bureaucratic crap. Since you won't budge, don't blame me for what happens next...
Hey, wait, wait! Cooperating is enough, right? I'll join you!
Miss Laru! What are you doing...!
Well, the Director is our boss to begin with. Since she also runs the Committee, we have to follow those orders too. Loyal employees do what the boss says, right?
Besides, I don't really care if the world ends. But if it does, that means no more fries. And I can't have that!
Bring it on, Boss! I mean business! You there, Sentinels, let's go get them!
Hmph. At least someone's smart enough.
Chitose, charge toward Laru, but use the back of your blade.
Take the full swing of mine!!
Oops, my bad, my bad. Chill out, will ya? I haven't touched this spear in ages, feeling kinda rusty.
Ouch... Whose side are you on?!!!
Uh-oh, sorry... That's weird. Guess my spear's a little out of control today.
Boss, jump out of that window! Now!
And just like that, Chitose and I made our exit as Bastelina and Albedo looked on.
