A pleasure to meet you. I am Chitose, my ==SEX11=='s guarding blade.
Boss's blade...==W== I see.==W== I'm Nazuka.==W== Thank you for looking after ==SEX4====W== while we were away.
No need to thank me. As my ==SEX11=='s blade, protecting ==SEX4== is simply my duty.
A dutiful guard...==W== Well,==W== now that I'm back, I'll take over from here.==W== You can step away.
I decline.==W== A blade must stay within ==SEX3== reach at all times.==W== Even while ==SEX== sleeps,==W== I remain at ==SEX3== side.
S...<size=52> SSSSSSSSLEEP at ==SEX3== side?!!!</size>==W== Boss,==W== what exactly is going on?!
D-Does...==W== Does she really get to sleep with you every single night...?!?!==W== That's so nic—==W==uh I mean,==W== shameless!! Totally shameless!!!!
Whoa, that's a strong word?! Wait, wait, wait, none of that ever happened!==W== Chitose, please clear this up!
My ==SEX11==, is this Lady Nazuka, the one you've mentioned so often?==W== She seems quite worked up.==W== I've heard she's a woman with wisdom,==W== but...
She doesn't seem to understand a word I'm saying.==W== Are you sure someone like her==W== is capable of protecting you?
Ahhh!==W== You're both getting the wrong idea!==W== Please,==W== just hear me out...
<size=52><color=#6fb1d2>Who do you want to watch your back?!</color>==RT==<color=#a87dc0>Whom do you wish to protect you?</color></size>==W==
Heh, so this is what they call "grown-up dilemma."==W== Amber, let's not turn out like them.
Leave them be, check out my new plushie! It's so soft and adorable.
Cute. Want to catch one in the machine.
Hey, hey! Kaede worked hard on this.==W== There's no way I'm tossing it into a claw machine.
...==W== Whoa,==W== you could cut the tension here with a knife.==W== What happened?
D-Don't worry about that,==W== Firenze. We just got here too.==W== Now,==W== what exactly are you planning by having Petal Bloom sneak into the city?
Well...==W== Before I dive into my plan,==W== let me introduce a very special guest.==W==
Hellooo, Boss! Long time no see~!==W== It's me, Itoha~!==W== The highly sought-after makeup artist across Nova for various activities and events!
I heard you were in serious trouble. How could I just stand by?==W== So I came straight over to help!
"Came to help"?==W== My ==SEX11==, do you even know this woman?
Makeup artist?==W== I don't know anyone like that...
And judging from Firenze's cautious look...==W== Is she trying to verify Itoha's story with me?
And if anything is out of place...==W== She would have her taken care of right on the spot?
Oh my, Boss...==W== Don't tell me you've already forgotten==W== that magical night we spent together on the rooftop,==W== just you and me...
(Who is she? What is she talking about?!==W== A...==W== A night on the rooftop?)
(Wait a second...==W== Could it be...==W== N-no way...==W== But...)
Everyone, calm down. Itoha and I...==W== Well, we met at the banquet.==W== All I did was ask her to do my makeup, and that was it.
Boss, you sure took your sweet time remembering me~!==W== Anyway, I'll do my best this time.==W== Can't wait to work with everyone~♪
Hmmm... There's a lot I could comment on...==W== But let's leave it at that.==W== Boss, I assume you want to hear the next part of the plan?
We'll have someone act as your double to submit the videos.==W== And Itoha is here to help.

I took training as a makeup artist at Goodwind Homecare and learned transformation magic from the Loong people.==W== Putting on a disguise is like a walk in the park for me ♪==W== In just a minute, I can turn anyone into a completely different person.
So,==W== could the four of you come with me please?
Wait... You want one of us ...==W== to play the double?
Because we can't ask people living in Philae to play the double. People start asking questions if someone they see every day suddenly disappears.
But we aren't supposed to be here in the first place.==W== So no one will be skeptical if we don't show up.
But it is a breach of our agreement with Albedo, right?==W== If she finds out...==W==
Well,==W== it depends on how you interpret the terms.

Thank you for your cooperation.==W== One more thing. Before you depart for Emor, you must submit a short video each day, documenting your activities in Philae.==W== Scarlet Sights will then broadcast it across Nova.
Every day, I have to film a short video and submit it to Scarlet Sights Media==W== to show the world that I'm staying put in Philae.
Heh. I guess you are too literal-minded for business negotiations.==W== Albedo's reputation for dotting every 'i' and crossing every 't' is well known across all the major companies.

In her usual practice, she never misses a tiny mistake, not even a misplaced comma in the agreement.==W== So if she'd really wanted to confine you in the city, she would've made that crystal clear. The terms would sound like this...==W==

First, you must remain within the legal boundaries of Philae at all times.==W== Second, every day you must record a video of yourself and submit it to Scarlet Sights to prove you're still here,==W== and also check in at the Soul Shop with a staff member I designate.
And she didn't.==W== In other words, the agreement was worded that way to <r=·>leave </r><r=·>room </r>for us to work with.
W-Wait, that's actually a valid interpretation?
Of course. In business negotiations, any ambiguity in wording will inevitably become an opportunity to exploit.

As the assigned representative of Grace Imperium and the person in charge of this investigation, Albedo can't put up some irresponsible remark like, "I trust you, Boss. Just show up in Emor a month from now and do whatever you like until then."

And yet, despite being caught in a web of complications, she still managed to carve out a little breathing room for you.==W== Because if you can clear your name, it helps her achieve her own goal too.
This is so complicated...==W== All the second-guessing and mind games are too difficult to keep up with.==W== And you people are caught up on this every day... Just the thought of it tires me out.
Now I get what Albedo really meant, but I still fear the idea of using the double is too risky.==W== The Salvation Committee is out for my blood...==W== What if we get caught?
Hey, Iris, quick question:==W== how much Dorra do we have left?
(Wh-==W==who is that?!==W== Why does ==SEX== look exactly like me?!)
Oh,==W== uh...==W== Around 200,000 Dorra.==W== And there are some pending commission fees from my side hustles,==W== so,==W== altogether it should be enough for the desert trip...==W==
Um, Iris,==W== I'm the real one.
That's a lie! I'm the real Boss!==W== I have proof:==W== there's a little cute bird==W== on Iris's cup!
Ugh...==W== I surrender, I really can't tell one from another!
Nazuka, how about you?==W== Which one do you think is the real Bo—==W==
Whoa,==W== Nazuka senpai saw right through her!
How...==W== How is that possible?!==W== The disguise was supposed to be flawless!
Words can't explain it.==W== It's more of a feeling...==W== A deep bond of the heart.==W== Heh,==W== with the real Boss around,==W== I feel a lot safer...==W==
Ugh...==W== Too much lovey-dovey.==W== I'm gonna be sick.
Hehe, don't worry.==W== I chose you, so you should have a little more confidence in yourself ♪
Itoha is right. I'm an exception.==W== Other people wouldn't be able to tell who the real Boss is. I actually wanted to volunteer, but I'm clearly not cut out for it...==W==
The key to acting as a double lies in a deep understanding of the person you're going to imitate.==W== Out-of-character behavior would easily give my flawless disguise away.

Body shape is another important factor. The double needs to have a roughly matching build, because transformation magic won't hold up forever, and gait patterns can give you away.==W== With that in mind, out of all the candidates...==W==
Nazuna's the closest match to the Boss's figure—flat as a board.==W== How wonderful! (As for the difference in height, heel lifts can fix that.)
<size=52>Flat as a board?!==W== What are you even talking about?! And what's so wonderful about that!</size>
Well then, my ==SEX11==, I'm ready. When do we head out to the desert?
Hmm...==W== Miss Itoha's makeup skills are truly impressive, but...==W==
Oh dear Boss, don't "but" me. I know you've got your concerns, but your friends have theirs too.==W==
Don't worry, Boss. Just go and do what you need to do. Once I get serious, I won't mess it up. And if anything bad happens, I'll give them a good beating!
We'll give Nazuna special training so she can perfectly step into your role. And Fuyuka, from now on, you'll need to treat her as your "Master."
Nazuna senpai is my Master...==W== Nazuna senpai is my Master...==W== I-I'll try my best to brainwash myself!
Boss, go ahead. We'll keep Nazuna safe.==W== But do let us know you're okay, so...==W== Be sure to reach out to me ...==W== regularly.
Alright...==W== Nazuna, I'll leave everything in your hands...==W== No, I should call you Boss now.==W== I hereby appoint you CEO of Boss Accord for the duration of my absence.
Hehe, you can count on me!==W== Oh, by the way, can I use company funds to buy some plush toys?
Unfortunately, no. We need every Dorra for the desert trip.
And Chitose, I'm sorry, but you'll have to stay in Philae, keeping watch by Nazuna's side.
But why? As your blade, I want to follow you wherever you go...==W==
From now on, Nazuna is your ==SEX11==. You were spotted fighting by my side in the Monolith, remember?
If you don't show your face, it'll raise suspicions about Nazuna's identity.==W== And this speculation,==W== in itself, proves that the world already recognizes you as my blade.
They do...?!==W== Then I'll stay by your double's side as you wish. Safe travels, my ==SEX11==.
Rest easy, ==PLAYER_NAME== is in safe hands with us.
Right now.==W== Boss and I will give you a public send-off as you board the Lucky Oasis.
Alright,==W== everyone,==W== get ready!==W== Our mission against the Salvation Committee starts now!==W==

strings.text: After a grueling trek, you and the New Star Guild reach the distant Sunset Desert, only to find no trace of the Monolith or the old signpost. With supplies running low, the group heads for Mirage, a rumored desert settlement.
Thanks to Firenze, I slip out of Philae stashed in the trunk of Lucky Oasis.
Nazuna's decoy act works like a charm.
Before we even hit the desert, I catch a glimpse of a shop window's Projector==RT==showing footage of "me" all dressed up for a United Harvest Philae event.
But that's where our luck ends. The moment we step into the desert, the Wilds bare their fangs.
Phew, it's roasting out here. Iris, how's our water looking?
We've been rationing, but we're down to three days' worth. It's getting dangerous. If we don't find the Monolith today, we'll have to head back for supplies.
Supplies, yeah... Still, this makes zero sense. According to Amber's photo, the Monolith should be right next to that signpost.

And that compass we got from Firenze, the one from under the orphanage, used to point at the desert. I thought it was connected to the Monolith, but the second we hit the dunes it started spinning in circles. How peculiar.
This is where I ran into enemies. I climbed the dune and saw the Monolith.
So why can't we find it?
Could there be multiple signposts like this? Maybe we're looking at the wrong one.
No way. I cross-checked the photo with that signpost over and over, and the erosion marks match perfectly. This is the one.
Then there's only one explanation. I read that sand dunes shift constantly. In strong winds, they can travel far in a single night.
This signpost probably got carried away from its original spot by the shifting sand. That's why the Monolith isn't actually nearby.
That explains it! We've walked this far and haven't even seen the Wishing Box ==PLAYER_NAME== was in. I knew something was off!
We've been searching this area for days. No Monolith, no Wishing Box. The signpost moving is the only logical conclusion.
Makes sense... ==PLAYER_NAME==, what do you think?
Huh? Sorry, I'm fine, just spaced out. What was the question?
I was asking if you think we can't find the Monolith because the signpost in Amber's photo shifted with the dunes.
Yeah... Probably. It's not like the Monolith could up and move.
Hey, are you okay, ==PLAYER_NAME==? You look awful. Please don't tell me it's heatstroke.
琥珀贴了主角额头一下
Here, let me feel your skin.
No fever, face not flushed, palms not sweaty... Boss, any headache or dizziness?
Then it's pure exhaustion. We've been pushing for ten days straight.
Everyone, with the signpost gone, we need to widen our search. But that means our supplies won't last. I say we find a town to restock and get some proper rest.
Time enough to reach a town outside the desert?
No amount of time would be enough. But I remember hearing about a town in this desert that's not charted in the Trekker's Handbook.
Found it. I took these notes from Willow back when we first became Trekkers. She mentioned this place. Let me see... It should only take half a day from here.
A town not charted in the Trekker's Handbook? I hate to be a downer, but what if it's already a pile of ruins?
No, Willow called it "the edge of the world," but she said people still live there, so we should be able to stock up there.
Sounds romantic. As long as there are people I guess. It saves us three days, and we might even get directions to the Monolith.
Come on, hop in. Let's go.
I wonder how everyone in Philae is holding up...
Zzz... Noya, don't buy that bread. Too expensive. Get the Tawny...
Mmph... Tawny Nightingale... I'm sick of it... Zzz...
Ten hours later, the Lucky Oasis is still crawling through endless dunes.
Headlights dance across shifting sand, but Mirage, the edge of the world from Iris's notes, remains nowhere in sight.
I don't know how to explain it. My gut says we're almost there. I can't put my finger on it, but driving through here feels familiar, like I've done it before.
Really? You've never been to Mirage. How can it feel familiar?
It's just a feeling. Listen to the tires. They sound different now. Hear that rumble? They're gripping the road. Can you hear it?
Sounds the same to me.==W== But look, you've been driving for ten hours straight. You must be exhausted.
Iris and Amber are already out. Let's stop and get some rest. Driving tired is dangerous.
No way! If I stop, my intuition will be interrupted.==W== We're almost there! ==PLAYER_NAME==, hold on tight!
Lucky Oasis surges up a towering dune.
Below, faint lights flicker across a sleeping settlement.
Welcome to Mirage, ==PLAYER_NAME==.==W== Welcome to the city at the edge of the world.
Uh, you're a guest here too, remember?
Anyway, the air feels amazing.==W== Nothing like the desert. Every breath burned like fire the past few days.
I spotted a lake on our way down the dune. Looks like this place is a true oasis.
Too bad most of the lights are off. I can't tell if everyone is asleep or if the place is abandoned. It feels a bit eerie. Plus, we shouldn't go knocking on doors this late...
We can look for supplies again in the morning.
Yeah. You must be exhausted from the drive. Go get some sleep. I'll take watch.
Really? Alright, I'll leave it to you! I'm going to run back to the car and get changed. I'll be right back, wait here!
Thanks for waiting...==W== Yawn... Changing into these pajamas makes me sleepy. It's like magic. Are you sure you're okay keeping watch alone,==W== ==PLAYER_NAME==? You're exhausted too, aren't you?
I'll be fine. I slept plenty during the day, so I'm not tired yet.
Noya presses her warm fingers to my lips. She leans in close.
Our noses are nearly touching, and gazes meet.
I get it that you have a lot on your mind, but...==W== ==PLAYER_NAME==, you aren't sleeping at night either, are you? You looked terrible earlier. That's proof enough.
I know what's bothering you. It's not the New Star Guild. You're worried about everyone back in Philae. You wonder if you've been a burden to them...
You always put everyone else first. You forced yourself to stay awake tonight to keep me company while I drive. You're going to burn yourself out like this.
You're giving me too much credit. You're guessing based on intuition, aren't you?
Not even close. Have you looked in a mirror lately, ==PLAYER_NAME==? I don't need intuition to see those dark circles under your eyes. Anyone could see them.
I pull out my phone and take a picture.
She is right. I look like a panda.
I didn't realize I looked that bad. Sorry to worry you guys.
I am really worried. About everyone in Philae, and about you guys too.
We set up a decoy Boss with makeup, and Albedo has been helping us. When I checked the projector the other day, she was actively covering for Nazuna's disguise.
But what if we fail to find proof in a month?
Or if Angie and the Salvation Committee launch another assassination attempt on the decoy Boss...
Then Nazuna and everyone protecting her would be in danger, danger meant for you.
If they got hurt or killed, it would be because they took your place. Meanwhile, the rest of us here would be stuck on the run, looking over our shoulders for the rest of our lives.
We knew from the start. That makeup artist was Otoha from the banquet.
I guessed by instinct, Amber caught a floral scent, and Iris tracked your schedule. You never had a chance to sneak out at night and meet someone we didn't know.
Then why didn't anyone stop her?
Because everyone else knew too. Nazuna, Nazuka, Fuyuka, Kaede, Firenze, Chitose. They all understood this would paint a target on Philae. On themselves.
As for Otoha, she saw through Firenze's plan and volunteered.
Everyone believes you can find the proof. But even if you fail, they hoped this would buy you a way out, a chance for you to survive.
So everyone knew... This whole time...
Boss, I had a feeling this was bothering you... I just didn't expect it to be weighing on you this heavily.
Wait... I thought you were asleep.
We got tossed around pretty hard coming down that dune... We've been awake since we hit Mirage. We kept quiet because Noya clearly wanted a moment with you...
Anyway, Boss.==W== I heard one of Angie's main reasons for calling you the Tyrant is that you're always helping people, always doing good deeds.
If you're the Tyrant... We're fine with that.
Exactly! The world could use a few more Tyrants like you.
I've been an idiot. I was so focused on keeping all of you safe, I forgot you wanted to keep me safe too.
Keep your head up! Don't underestimate us. Everyone in Philae has been to hell and back with you.
We're way tougher than you, Boss.
Right! By the time we find your proof, they'll probably call to say they've already wiped the floor with Angie and her committee. You won't even need to go to the conference, Boss!
Alright, let's not get ahead of ourselves.
I'm an optimist, what can I say? Anyway, sweating the small stuff won't help right now. Let's head back to the vehicle and sleep. We have an early start tomorrow.
I've slept enough. I'll keep watch.
Honestly, after that pep talk, I'm wide awake.
Then please lie down and close your eyes. Even resting is better than staying awake.
Tyrant, let me help you fall asleep.
Huh? Why are you here? I've completed another mission?
Unfortunately, Mission: "Acquire a Monolith" remains incomplete. Your shares in United Harvest Philae only grant partial access to the Philae Monolith, not full ownership.
But seeing the bond between you and your companions made me want to help out too.
So please accept a trial run of this mission's reward: the Monolith Melody.
Basically, I'll play soothing music to help everyone relax and fall asleep.
That sounds fun! Like a lullaby? I'm in. Let's try it out. I'm actually getting sleepy.
So it's basically a music player...?==W== Alright, if it helps us sleep, go ahead, Vita. Thanks.
Tyrant, may tonight's starlight and sweet dreams wash away the exhaustion for you and your companions.==W==

Unfortunately, Mission: "Acquire a Monolith" remains incomplete. Your shares in United Harvest Philae only grant partial access to the Philae Monolith, not full ownership.
But seeing the bond between you and your companions made me want to help out too.
So please accept a trial run of this mission's reward: the Monolith Melody.
Basically, I'll play soothing music to help everyone relax and fall asleep.
That sounds fun! Like a lullaby? I'm in. Let's try it out. I'm actually getting sleepy.
So it's basically a music player...?==W== Alright, if it helps us sleep, go ahead, Vita. Thanks.
Tyrant, may tonight's starlight and sweet dreams wash away the exhaustion for you and your companions.==W==

strings.text: In your sleep, you saw Iris's memories. Iris grew up in the orphanage with Noya and Amber, and she was the most studious of the three. After leaving the orphanage, they set off together toward an unknown future…
... was a kid without any talents.
I never knew my parents. For as long as I can remember,==RT==I lived with Aunt Allie at the orphanage under the Waterway.
It didn't have an official name, but since it's the only one in the Ash District,==RT==everyone called it the Ash Orphanage.
I didn't have a name either. Aunt Allie called me Iris after the flowers==RT==growing along the orphanage wall.
There were Aunt Allie, Noya, Amber...
Aunt Allie ran the entire place on her own.
As the older sisters, the three of us helped out with whatever chores we could.
Hehe, you always catch the biggest fish, Amber! Everyone gets a feast tonight!
Iris, the fire's too hot! Pull some firewood out!
Ah, sorry, I wasn't paying attention! On it!
Amber had a gift for foraging.
Noya could cook a meal out of anything.
But all I could manage were basic chores.
Aunt Allie looked after us during the day. Once we were asleep,==RT==she'd sneak out to work night shifts.
She thought she hid it well, but we figured it out a long time ago.==RT==Worse, we knew it was dangerous work.
More than once, we saw her quietly bandaging her injuries.
Then the next morning, she'd act as if nothing happened==RT==and go back to taking care of us.
Feeding that many kids had to cost a fortune. We wanted to make things easier==RT==on her. We figured if we could go out and earn some money too...
Let's become Trekkers! I heard if you score an Artifact from a Wishing Box, you make tons of Dorra!
I asked about that at the Trekker Association, but the lady there said we were far too young to be trainees. We'd have to be at least seven or eight years older.
Chimney sweeps... I think they hire kids.
Yeah, I heard about that too...
The employers want to squeeze in more jobs, so they'd force kids down the chimneys the second the fires go out.
Plus, the adult running the crew takes almost all the pay. As kids, we'd barely earn a single Dorra.
You always know everything, Iris!==W== But if we can't do this, and we can't do that, what are we supposed to do?
Our talks always ended the same way. We were kids with no real answers. So, I decided to go ask Aunt Allie...
Aunt Allie... What do you think I should do when I grow up?
Aunt Allie went unusually quiet. She scratched her head, thought for a long time,==RT==and then handed me a key without saying a word.
I had no idea what it meant. I used it to unlock the orphanage basement,==RT==and inside were more books than stars in the sky.
Looking at them all, it hit me. I must be completely ordinary.
Aunt Allie couldn't spot a single talent in me, let alone give me advice.==RT==She was leaving it to me to find my own answers in those books.
I broke down crying. But the moment I realized my tears might ruin==RT==those precious pages, I forced myself to stop.
Sniffling, I grabbed the nearest book like a lifeline and cracked it open.
I wanted it to give me an answer.
I was a kid terrified of taking risks.
Huff, huff... Finally made it. This Waterway is high and dangerous. Why do Noya and Amber always hang out up here?
No way... Noya and Amber are actually reading books!
Frowning and thinking hard... They must be working on those magic problems I lent them yesterday.
That's more like it! You know that blue-haired girl Aunt Allie talks about? She got a scholarship to Platinum Academy and moved to a better district for school.==W== Well, I am not losing to her!
For an ordinary kid like me, studying is the only way up. Imagine if we all got into Platinum Academy. No, Grace Light Academy!

Plus, Aunt Allie hasn't taken dangerous jobs lately. The Artifacts she pulls from the Wishing Box sell for a lot of Dorra!==W== Things at the orphanage are looking up. We even get dessert once a week now!
You're studying so hard. Come on, dessert time!
Iris, perfect timing! Amber and I are stuck on a part in this book.
Wait. This is a fairy tale book! Didn't you promise to finish the magic problems I gave you?
Ahaha. About those problems... I am positive they are cursed.
Knocked me out in five seconds flat.
You need to check that book again, Iris. It has to be rigged with some terrifying sleep magic!
Read fairy tales to stay awake.
Exactly! We needed a quick brain break, that's all.
Ugh, fine. But you still need to practice reading, or you'll get tricked when you're older. Let me see...==W== The Tale of the Tyrant? That's a classic.
Hey Iris, do you think the Tyrant is ... like, super evil?
Of course! ==SEX1== sends demons crawling out of the pitch-black abyss to snatch up kids who skip homework and stay up late.
But in this book, the Tyrant's not like that at all!
==SEX1== farms the land with everyone, builds tools, puts up houses. Those are good things, right?
That's bait! The Tyrant never shows ==SEX3== fangs right away. ==SEX1== plays nice and sets traps with sweet talk. Then, the second you let your guard down... Chomp! You're dinner.
Aunt Allie says there's no free lunch in Nova; the Tyrant can't be good forever. If ==SEX== is doing good deeds, there's a hidden catch.
So it's all fake? But c'mon, if ==SEX== acts good forever, what's the difference? That makes ==SEX4== good!
You're only on volume one. There's a second book. And in that one, the Tyrant wants to conquer every single Monolith in Nova!
Wahaha! Conquer every Monolith? That's amazing! You'd have to be the strongest Trekker ever to pull that off. Right, Amber?
==SEX1== should move the Monolith. Just a little.
And the orphanage gets some sun. We'll be warm.
Hey, if they can conquer Monoliths, they can definitely move one out of the way!
Okay. I'm on team Tyrant. Let ==SEX4== move the Monolith.
Ha! Two to one, Iris! Amber and I say the Tyrant's a good person!
Wait, how did it come to this... Listen up! The Tyrant isn't just conquering the Monoliths, ==SEX=='s going to destroy them! Then we won't have any Artifacts!
Of course it's bad! See that big box in the hall that blows freezing air? That's an Artifact!
And that phone you've always wanted? That's an Artifact too.
Amber wants a phone. I'm out. No more Tyrant.
Ha! Now the Tyrant-is-evil side has two people. How the tables have turned! <size=54>♪</size>
Huh? Noya? Where'd she run off to?
Haha! I know the Tyrant's good, that's enough for me! Don't need to read the rest!
And I'm telling you that the Tyrant isn't a good person...==W== Whatever, suit yourself.
Amber, dessert's almost here! How about I race you back to the orphanage! First one to the table gets first pick!
Hey, what are you doing?==W== Don't jump from there! Aaaaaaah!
Noya and Amber jumped off that towering Waterway without even blinking. Terrified, I covered my eyes. When I looked again, they had already stormed into the orphanage.
I still don't know how they made it down. I was too scared, so I took the stairs.
By the time I got back, dessert was nearly over.
But even though they said the first one back picks first, they both left my favorite cookies for me. I've never forgotten that.
I was a kid who was good at reading.
Iris, there's a kitten on the courtyard wall. Wanna come see?
No thanks, I'm practicing my magic circles.
Iris, I think these two Artifacts Aunt Allie brought back might fit together! Wanna help me try?
Hmm, maybe later. I need to finish memorizing this incantation.
Once I got the key to the basement, I finally found what I was good at. Reading.
I wasn't like Noya, who taught herself swordsmanship and made friends==RT==with half the Trekkers in the Trekker Association.
And I wasn't as fast as Amber, who could chase cats across==RT==every rooftop and alleyway in Emor.
But thanks to my books, I could understand Noya's sword techniques==RT==without ever swinging a blade.
And I knew every shop in Emor without ever leaving Ash District.
My future was in those books. I truly believed that back then.
Iris, we found these weird Artifact parts in the basement. Any idea what they are?
Oh, that's a steering wheel. It's part of a rare Artifact. I know I read about it somewhere... Let me look it up. I'll bring it to you once I find it.
Iris. How do I use this gun?
These magic guns run on Neo Solution and activate with a magic circle. I can teach you the circle, but go easy on the Neo Solution.
It's hard to get. Plus... The Grace Imperium cracks down on it.
Winter gave way to spring, and the days kept slipping by.==RT==Before we knew it, we were old enough to leave the orphanage.
As the first batch to leave, we were fired up to take on the world==RT==and set an example for the younger kids.
Iris. Amber. How much Dorra do you two have on you?
Wait, wasn't this your idea, Noya? We agreed we wouldn't burden Aunt Allie, so we secretly returned the Dorra she gave us. I shoved all of mine under her pillow!
Then what do we do now?! We're completely broke!
Unbelievable. You acted on impulse again, didn't you? This is what happens when you refuse to plan ahead.
B-But come on! We had to show Aunt Allie we could make it on our own so she wouldn't worry, right?
I guess ... you have a point there. That's the only reason I went along with it.
No Dorra, we find our own food. I can fish. There are mushrooms this time of year.
Whoa, that's our Amber! Exactly! Living off the land is what a real adventure is all about!
... You sure know how to let yourself off the hook.
Anyway, I refuse to play wilderness survival on day one.
I had a feeling this would happen, so I stashed a little Dorra away...
Are you serious?!==W== Iris, you are an absolute lifesaver!

strings.text: While balancing work and exam prep, Iris was supported by Amber and Noya—even knowing her dream may take them on separate paths. But just before the test, a wish made her forget something important…
I'd like to use this coupon, this voucher, and this discount slip. They're supposed to stack.
Let me double-check that...==W== Hmm. You're right. They stack. Your total comes to ... one thousand Dorra.
A thousand Dorra for all this? That barely buys a loaf of bread out there.
This shop's coupons are popular because they stack.==W== I used to get paid in these instead of cash for odd jobs. I never thought we'd actually use them.
You never know what'll happen. I need to make my savings last. The hundred thousand Dorra from my odd jobs has to stretch.
And a genius! I still can't believe you stash Dorra in your boots.==W== Why not use a wallet?
Well... I read that the Wilds and the cities are both dangerous. It's smarter to spread your cash around. If you get robbed, you don't lose everything at once.
Makes sense!==W== But what if the bad guys read the same book and search every single spot?
Beat the bad guys. You keep your money, and you turn them in for a bounty.
I-I guess that works if you can pull it off?==W== Anyway, changing the subject. What are your plans?
I want to ... see other cities. Nova is big.
I'm gonna be a Trekker! Climb every Monolith just like the Tyrant. All the way to the very top.
But first, I need to build this.
Is this ... the Artifact you asked me about?

Yeah! The book you lent me called it a steering wheel. It drives a super-fast vehicle.==W== Nova is a large stretch of land with tons of Monoliths. Walking would take forever. Wouldn't driving be more convenient?
It would... But Artifact cars are rare. Can you actually build one?
Hehehe. Feast your eyes on this.
It's huge. And heavy. What is it?
Heh. It was sitting in the orphanage basement this whole time, covered in dust. I asked Aunt Allie if I could take it when I left.
She didn't know what it was either. But my gut says ... it's the heart of an Artifact car!
Yeah! Anyway, my gut says if I piece this hunk of metal together right and hook it up to the steering wheel, it'll zoom like crazy.
Hehe, we've shared our plans. Your turn, Iris!
M-Me? Well, before leaving the orphanage, I passed the preliminary exam for Grace Light Academy. The entrance exam is next week.==W== I ...==W== want to go to college.
College? Is that to learn powerful magic?
I don't have grand dreams like that. I want a job at a big company like Grace Imperium or United Harvest ... somewhere with steady pay and vacation time.
That way I can stay in Emor. On my days off, I can help out at the orphanage and take some weight off Aunt Allie's shoulders.
But it all depends on next week's exam. Before then, I need to find a temp job to scrape together the material fees. I have to pay them on the exam day.
Yeah. Grace Light Academy tests you on six subjects.
Math, Rhetoric, Magic Principles, Magic Application, Grace Energy Studies, and Grace Spells.
The exam takes three days, and every subject is at a different location.
The magic and Monolith subjects require special materials and destructible arenas.
Altogether, the fees come out to two hundred thousand Dorra.
You only had a hundred thousand, and you shared it with us. Didn't save any extra for the fees?
No.==W== But it's fine! If I work twenty hours a day between now and then, I can probably scrounge up the rest.
Whoa, hey now! Do that, and you'll have no time left to study or sleep!==W== I know how we can earn that Dorra and still get you some shut-eye. Wanna give it a shot?
W-Wahhh! I-Is that a real Stellaroid?!
Yep! You've read about them, right? This guy is an Ignis monster. Your Aqua magic makes a perfect match!
I'll cover you, Iris. Don't worry, go for it.
I did it! Did you see that?! I can fight now, like you two! I didn't hold you back... Oh, thank goodness.
Why would you say that? You've always been the best out of the three of us!
The best...?==W== No, no, no, what are you talking about, Noya? I'm terrible at fighting, and I'm a coward.
But you read a lot. You know things we don't.
Forget all that. Let's go make a wish! There's a big Wishing Box up ahead.
To make a wish... I heard you just touch it and say what you want.
Please give me a phone. Please give me a phone. Please give me a phone.
No, Amber, that's not how it works.==W== You have to pray sincerely to the God of Grace and describe your Artifact in detail.
A phone... How would you describe that? A machine that talks to people far away?
Let me do it. I looked this up beforehand. I know the prayer.
Wait, hold on. I'm no bookworm, but I know how exams work.
Making a wish costs memories. If you forget what you studied, you'll bomb your exam!
Give me the prayer. I'll make the wish.
It took us days to get here, and it'll take days to go back. We can't afford any mistakes. We need to get this right the first time.
Besides, I had fun climbing with you. They say wishes work better when you're happy. I appreciate you looking out for me,==W== but I'm making this wish.
If you say so...==W== Alright, it's all yours.
Leave it to me. Here I go...==W== O mighty God of Grace, please hear our prayer... Please grant me...
We made it back to Emor by Monday morning. We rushed to the Soul Shop, traded the phone for Dorra, set a time to meet up, and went our separate ways.
And just like that, I scraped together the material fees and finally took my entrance exam for Grace Light Academy.
Thanks to you both, I think I did well on all five subjects. The wish didn't seem to erase any of my book knowledge. Guess I got lucky this time.
Is this ... a phone?! Where did you get it?

After you left for the exam, Amber and I went back up the Monolith.==W== We copied your prayer and made some wishes. Failed a bunch of times, but three of them worked.==W== Now all three of us have phones.
Can... Can I really keep this? You two made the wishes. Shouldn't we sell it for Dorra instead?
No. Noya and I are leaving Emor. With phones, we can reach each other when we end up in the same city. Makes meeting up easier.
Yeah, a guild offered me an internship. I leave today.
Joined a treasure-hunting team. They're leaving tomorrow.
When you come back to Emor, I'll be a Grace Light Academy student, and I'll treat you both.==W== I'll have enough saved up from odd jobs by then.
Ah, sorry, it's time for my shift. I have to go. You two take care of yourselves, okay?
You take care too, Iris! We'll be back before you know it!
Let's head out, Amber. I'm finishing that Artifact car no matter what.
Earlier... Iris said the exam had six subjects.

But it all depends on next week's exam. Before then, I need to find a temp job to scrape together the material fees. I have to pay them on the exam day.
Yeah. Grace Light Academy tests you on six subjects.
Math, Rhetoric, Magic Principles, Magic Application, Grace Energy Studies, and Grace Spells.
The exam takes three days, and every subject is at a different location.
The magic and Monolith subjects require special materials and destructible arenas.
Altogether, the fees come out to two hundred thousand Dorra.
You only had a hundred thousand, and you shared it with us. Didn't save any extra for the fees?
No.==W== But it's fine! If I work twenty hours a day between now and then, I can probably scrounge up the rest.
Whoa, hey now! Do that, and you'll have no time left to study or sleep!==W== I know how we can earn that Dorra and still get you some shut-eye. Wanna give it a shot?
W-Wahhh! I-Is that a real Stellaroid?!
Yep! You've read about them, right? This guy is an Ignis monster. Your Aqua magic makes a perfect match!
I'll cover you, Iris. Don't worry, go for it.
I did it! Did you see that?! I can fight now, like you two! I didn't hold you back... Oh, thank goodness.
Why would you say that? You've always been the best out of the three of us!
The best...?==W== No, no, no, what are you talking about, Noya? I'm terrible at fighting, and I'm a coward.
But you read a lot. You know things we don't.
Forget all that. Let's go make a wish! There's a big Wishing Box up ahead.
To make a wish... I heard you just touch it and say what you want.
Please give me a phone. Please give me a phone. Please give me a phone.
No, Amber, that's not how it works.==W== You have to pray sincerely to the God of Grace and describe your Artifact in detail.
A phone... How would you describe that? A machine that talks to people far away?
Let me do it. I looked this up beforehand. I know the prayer.
Wait, hold on. I'm no bookworm, but I know how exams work.
Making a wish costs memories. If you forget what you studied, you'll bomb your exam!
Give me the prayer. I'll make the wish.
It took us days to get here, and it'll take days to go back. We can't afford any mistakes. We need to get this right the first time.
Besides, I had fun climbing with you. They say wishes work better when you're happy. I appreciate you looking out for me,==W== but I'm making this wish.
If you say so...==W== Alright, it's all yours.
Leave it to me. Here I go...==W== O mighty God of Grace, please hear our prayer... Please grant me...
We made it back to Emor by Monday morning. We rushed to the Soul Shop, traded the phone for Dorra, set a time to meet up, and went our separate ways.
And just like that, I scraped together the material fees and finally took my entrance exam for Grace Light Academy.
Thanks to you both, I think I did well on all five subjects. The wish didn't seem to erase any of my book knowledge. Guess I got lucky this time.
Is this ... a phone?! Where did you get it?

After you left for the exam, Amber and I went back up the Monolith.==W== We copied your prayer and made some wishes. Failed a bunch of times, but three of them worked.==W== Now all three of us have phones.
Can... Can I really keep this? You two made the wishes. Shouldn't we sell it for Dorra instead?
No. Noya and I are leaving Emor. With phones, we can reach each other when we end up in the same city. Makes meeting up easier.
Yeah, a guild offered me an internship. I leave today.
Joined a treasure-hunting team. They're leaving tomorrow.
When you come back to Emor, I'll be a Grace Light Academy student, and I'll treat you both.==W== I'll have enough saved up from odd jobs by then.
Ah, sorry, it's time for my shift. I have to go. You two take care of yourselves, okay?
You take care too, Iris! We'll be back before you know it!
Let's head out, Amber. I'm finishing that Artifact car no matter what.
Earlier... Iris said the exam had six subjects.

strings.text: After failing her exam, Iris drifted through dead-end jobs. Though finally offered a place at a prestigious institute, she turned it down and chose to become a Trekker with her friends after reuniting with them...
One point below the cutoff...==W== I-I failed? How?==B====W== Excuse me, I need a score review.
Of course.==W== It is a pity, though. You nearly made the cutoff with only five subjects.==W== If you'd taken the last one, you might have passed.
<size=40>Wait,==W== the...==W== The last exam?==W== What do you mean?==W== I took all five!</size>
You must be mistaken.==W== The entrance exam always has <color=#3faeae>six subjects</color>.==W== That hasn't changed once in the academy's history.
You missed the last one: Grace Spells.==W== Shame.==W== That exam is pure memorization.==W== Judging by your other scores, you would have aced it.
(No... I couldn't have forgotten a subject.==W== Wait. Back then...)
It took us days to get here, and it'll take days to go back. We can't afford any mistakes. We need to get this right the first time.
Besides, I had fun climbing with you. They say wishes work better when you're happy. I appreciate you looking out for me,==W== but I'm making this wish.
Thanks to you both, I think I did well on all five subjects. The wish didn't seem to erase any of my book knowledge. Guess I got lucky this time.
(The memory I lost wasn't the exam material. It was the list of subjects...)
I didn't remember leaving Grace Light Academy.==RT==I didn't remember taking that business trip for my part-time job, either.
Next thing I knew, I was working in Port Bellin.
(If only I hadn't made that wish.)
I still think that sometimes. But dwelling on it now won't change a thing.
(I was overjoyed back then. Too full of myself. I actually thought I was good at something...)
(This must be fate... Punishment from the God of Grace.)
(... No. Noya and Amber only came to help me.==RT==It wouldn't be fair for them to lose their memories too.)
(So this isn't even... Yeah. This doesn't even count as a punishment.)
That part-time job ended fast.==RT==I started looking for work in other cities and never went back to Emor.
I was too ashamed to face everyone at the orphanage.==RT==I had no money to send back. But...
Looking at your resume... You have no formal education.
Born in the Ash District... Sorry, I don't think we're a good fit...
No recommendation letters? Okay. Let's stop here for today.==RT==If we decide to move forward, we'll send a notice to your address via a Trekker.
Most applications were tossed before my resume even reached a desk.==RT==The few times that I got to interviews, they barely looked at me.
All those certificates I paid Dorra for, all those late nights studying…==RT==Completely useless.
In the end, the Grace Imperium took me in.
A Soul Shop from Emor needed someone to run a mobile station in a nearby city,==RT==recharging Soul Stones with Grace.
So I became a glorious Soul Shop—
Brr, freezing. Snow's coming down hard. It's Snowish Festival Eve, isn't it...==W== Wonder how Noya and Amber are doing.==W== Hope they're bundled up tonight, or they'll catch a cold.
Dead again tonight.==W== Everyone's switching to the cheaper Neo Solution instead of Grace. Tough making a living at a Soul Shop these days.
(Funny thing is, I'm officially a clerk for Soul Shop #305 in the Emor region, but I've never stepped inside. Never even been back to Emor.)
(Never even got a uniform. I set up a little folding table in nearby cities and take whatever comes. Scraping by, day after day.)
(But I've been Employee of the Month three times.==W== One more, and maybe I'll finally get a permanent spot.)
Oh, hello! Need a Grace refill?
Good evening. You must be Iris.==W== I'm from Grace Imperium HR.==W== There's something important that I need to inform you.
Yes, I'm Iris, clerk at Soul Shop #305. How can I help you?

I'll be direct.==W== To navigate current market challenges and maintain our competitive edge, the Sky Institute is restructuring. We are pivoting to a core-focus, cost-reduction strategy. Unfortunately, this involves large-scale layoffs and downsizing.
Consequently, your branch, Soul Shop #305 in Emor, has been permanently shut down.
W-Wait, what?==W== Shut down?==W== Then where do I go?
We all recognize and appreciate your hard work out here.==W== But unfortunately, since you aren't a full-time employee of Sky Institute, we cannot offer you an internal transfer.
Per company policy, we will provide you with the same severance package as our regular staff.==W== We hope you understand.
B-But...!==W== ... Okay. I understand. Thank you.
Whenever I got overwhelmed, I pulled out an old entrance exam for Grace Light Academy.
Tests always have a right answer. Study hard, learn the patterns, and you can solve even the toughest problems eventually.
But my life doesn't seem to have one.
Apply, fail. Apply, fail. Apply, fail. Apply, succeed... Become an outsourced worker.
A different-colored badge makes you invisible. And the snacks in the breakroom aren't meant for invisible people.
Even so, I still gravitated toward companies with Emor in the name,==W== or agencies without a Seal of Grace that tried to look like real corporations.
That name made me feel like they might take me back.
What about this job in Philae? It is United Harvest. Huge corporation.
A job that enticing... Would they even take someone like me?==W== I've heard that ...==W== a lot of these Philae jobs are covers to send you to the Lushwood Jungle.
Oh, you know your stuff, kid.==W== But the Lushwood Jungle is a solid option. Room, board, and travel are all covered. Work is easy, no degree required. If you can use a phone, you're hired.
They'll train you when you get there. You'll be making Dorra before you know it.
Oh. I see...==W== I'll pass on that. Do you have anything else?
Hmph. Picky, are we?==W== By the look of you, you got fired and haven't landed a thing since.
No, I wasn't fired. The agency shut down.==W== And I'm not being picky, I'm just...
Tons of agencies are doing fine. So why is yours the only one that goes under?==W== Are you a jinx?==W== Everywhere you go, it falls apart.
Jobs are everywhere.==W== Take a good look at yourself.==W== Have you improved yourself? Have you put in the effort?
Good. Now you know you're unwanted.==W== So what about that Philae job? Sign here and you're set.
A familiar hand pressed down on mine, stopping the pen.
Seriously! We've been looking for you for two months. I can't believe you almost fell for this scammer.
What are you talking about? You out-of-town Trekkers have zero respect.
I was helping this lazy girl find a job that suits her.
Don't act like you know her. Iris is the hardest worker I've ever met!
Back at the orphanage, she studied late every single night. Always the last one to sleep and the first one up.
She memorized obscure travel facts most Trekkers don't even know. When I decided to hit the road, she walked me through everything!
You sit here tricking people into dangerous jobs.==W== <size=50>What gives you the right to call her lazy?!</size>
Keep your voice down... Her being unemployed speaks for itself, doesn't it?
What is this...==W== Wait, an interview invite? With the official Eye of Grace seal?!
See? She is in high demand!==W== Hmph! Talk trash about her again and I'll bite you.==B====W== Come on, Iris, let's ditch this scammer.

Hey, hold on! If she has an Eye of Grace invite, why is she looking for work here?==W== Wait...==W== If those crazy professors find out I tried to ship their candidate off to the Lushwood Jungle...==W== I better pack my bags and run!
Noya, Amber, what are you doing here?==W== What do you mean you spent two months looking for me?==W== And what is the deal with that invitation?
One question at a time! I promise I'll explain everything,==W== but first...==W== Check this out!
Is that ... an Artifact car?!==W== Noya, did you actually build it?!
No. Only the shell. Inside's empty.
Hey, don't ruin the magic! Let her be amazed for a second.

Alright, alright.==W== Over these past few months, I wished for Artifact parts at the Monolith, and Amber dug up some ancient treasure. We barely managed to piece it together.==W== Now we fill up the inside, and it's good to go.
Oh, by the way. While we were putting it together, we ran into someone from the Eye of Grace.
Yeah! We mentioned we were your friends,==W== and she handed over this invite.
This expiration date makes me a little nervous... Let's see what it says...

Please excuse this abrupt letter.==RT==Your performance on the Grace Light Academy entrance exam left a profound==RT==impression on us. We were disappointed to learn that you were not admitted,==RT==which is why we are reaching out now.==P====RT====RT==If you are currently seeking employment, we may be able to offer a suitable==RT==position. We warmly invite you for an interview to discuss future possibilities.==P====RT====RT==<align=right>Sincerely, The Society for the Study of Life</margin>
Sounds like they operate under the Eye of Grace. We only chatted for a bit,==W== so I don't know the exact details, but the lady was incredibly polite. I think they are legit.
Study notes... Do you still have them? She said they wanted to discuss the exam questions.
I do, I do.==W== I carry them with me everywhere...
This was everything I'd ever wanted. Right in front of me.==RT==With this invitation, they wouldn't care about my degree==RT==or where I come from.
I'd done so many Grace Light Academy's past papers==RT==that I can basically recite them in my sleep.==RT==I can definitely answer all of their questions.
Why did I do all this? All those practice questions…==RT==What was the point?
If it was all to get one answer correct==RT==on a test someone else wrote for me…==RT==Is that what I want?
<size=30>... I don't know. How do I find the answer I'm after? The answer to my own life?</size>
By the way, Iris.==W== Let me clear something up so you don't get the wrong idea.
We didn't spend two months tracking you down to hand-deliver a letter.
Huh? You didn't?==W== Then... What for?
What do you mean "what for"? Are you serious?==W== Didn't you hear me back there?==W== "She is in high demand!"==W==
...==W== Wait!==W== You seriously don't get it?!
Err? Um... Sorry. I'm not following.
No, no, no!==W== Right here!==W== In front of you!==W== Two people who need you!
Took you long enough... But you got there.
When putting together that car, Noya kept talking about you. ==W==She's been looking for you to join the guild.
If you hadn't told me that thing was a steering wheel, none of this would've happened.==W== On my own, I'd never have found those blueprints in the basement.
So when I decided to start my own guild...==W== I knew right then I wanted you with me!
But hey, I've got my dreams, and if you've got yours, no pressure!

Anyway, that's the deal. Go to your interview, I won't stop you.==W== But if you end up hating it at that Society or whatever,==W== I'd be thrilled if you kept us in mind as a backup plan<size=54>♪</size>
If you aren't happy there, we'll steal you away.
Ooh, I love that!==W== So cool! Done deal!!
... Thank you both!==W== I...==W== I've made up my mind!
Uh...==W== You tossed your study materials? ==W==You're not doing exams?
I love exam papers. They're my favorite thing. They make me feel safe.
I wanted to get into a big corporation. I wanted to stay in Emor. I wanted to see the orphanage every single day.
But what I want most ...==W== is just ...==W== <size=50>to be with my two favorite people, Noya and Amber, forever.</size>
Even if we go a whole day without talking, knowing you're nearby... That feeling is enough.
Noya, Amber, I've decided. I want to be a Trekker.
I'm done solving problems with standard answers.==W== The answer to my life is something I need to find myself.
Nope, the answer to OUR lives.==W== If you become a Trekker, the rest of our lives is one big exam for the three of us...
And—==W==we get to decide the answers.
Yeah!==W== Then, Noya, Amber...==W==<size=50> I'm counting on you from here on out!</size>

strings.text: You share these forgotten memories with Iris, Noya, and Amber. Truth uncovered, your bond runs deeper than ever. Meanwhile, chaos engulfs Mirage as the Desert Scorpions close in on you.
Mmm... Where am I...?==W== Oh, right. We fell asleep once we made it to Mirage last night.
Good morning, Tyrant. Did you sleep well? Any dreams?
Morning, Vita. I had a dream. A really long one.
Tyrant, may tonight's starlight and sweet dreams wash away the exhaustion for you and your companions.
Wait. You weren't behind that dream, were you?
I did no such thing, Tyrant. You and your companions agreed to try the Monolith Melody.
I did,==W== but you told me it was regular sleep music.
That melody was composed from records inside the Monolith.==W== If the listener resonates with those records, the music can awaken things they have forgotten.
Forgotten? But I didn't dream about my own past. I dreamt about Iris, Noya, and Amber...==W==
... Hold on. Are you saying...==W== I saw their memories? The ones they lost?
Perhaps yes, perhaps no. The Monolith does hold memories offered by wish-makers, but those records contain more than that.
Also, my apologies, but this melody was only a trial. You and your companions will forget the dream shortly after waking.

If you are interested in the Monolith's records, please focus on the system mission "Acquire a Monolith."==W== Once it is accomplished, I will pass on these melodies in a format that allows for repeated resonance.
So that was the real goal all along. Pushing me to finish the mission.
Fine. Don't worry about it.==W== As long as it gives me the power to protect everyone, I will get the task done.
Your command is my will.==W== I will take my leave now. Safe travels, Tyrant.
("Tyrant," huh... If everything Vita just said is true, then I...)==W==
Been up for a while. Saw you talking to Vita, so I didn't interrupt. Just messing with my phone.
Boss, can I ask you something? What was in your dream?
I dreamt about you, Iris, and Noya as kids. Things like wanting to get jobs, reading on the Waterway bridge...
And later on. Iris looking for jobs, Noya building Loxy, you going treasure hunting...
Whoa, hey!==W== Amber, that's too close!
Boss. Can you tell us the whole dream?==W== In detail.
Noya, can you try to stay still in your sleep? Your leg was crushing me.
Hey, blame Amber. She had me in a bear hug from behind.
Well she hugs me too, and you don't see me crushing anyone.
Everyone feels different.==W== I grab whoever my mood finds fitting.
Noya is warm.==W== Iris is squishy.==W==
S-Squishy?!==W== Did I put on weight?!==W== Okay, listen up.==W== From now on, no one touches me in their sleep without my explicit permission.
See? You need to eat more, ==PLAYER_NAME==.
Hold on, we're getting derailed.==W== Amber, weren't you asking about my dream?
We all need to know.==W== That's why I woke everyone up.==W== Do you remember your dreams last night?
Dreams? I know I dreamt about something,==W== but it slipped my mind the second I woke up.
... W-Why the sudden subject change?==W== I don't remember the details either...==W== But I woke up feeling pretty good. Must have been a nice one.
Let me ask you something else. How much do you actually remember about the orphanage? Or what you did right after leaving, before you built Loxy?
The orphanage is a blur. I only remember Aunt Allie's face.
I've got bits and pieces of what happened after we left. Like scavenging parts for Loxy.
But we were all doing our own thing back then. I draw a complete blank on how we actually teamed up to form the New Star Guild.
The Monolith probably took those memories as payment for our wishes. The books say they feed on intense emotions...==W== And looking back, that was a nerve-wracking period of our lives.
Rumor has it that if your prayer is even slightly vague, the Monolith takes extra memories as a toll.==W== I guess that's the price we had to pay for being rookies.
Thank goodness we have Iris.==W== If it were up to me, I'd have botched every single wish and wiped my own brain by now.
So none of you remember your childhood.==W== Which means...==W== That dream I had... Those were your memories?
Vita said I'd forget the dream as soon as I woke up, but my magic-immunity must have blocked the memory wipe.
As for what I dreamt about...==W==
No way! That explains why I missed the mark by one point. The Monolith took my memory of the last exam when I made my wish.
We should have made the wish instead.
Then you could've gone to Grace Light Academy.
What are you talking about?==W== If I went off to college, I wouldn't be here traveling with you!
Besides, failing that exam is how I ended up at Boss Accord. My dream of becoming a corporate employee came true anyway!==W== Missing that test must have been a sign from the God of Grace.
You... You're all taking this surprisingly well. I thought ... you'd be way more upset or freaked out after hearing what you lost.
Hehe, I guess it is a little scary when you think about it.==W== But whether we laugh or cry, we're facing the same reality.==W== We might as well laugh and cheer up.
The second we chose to be Trekkers, we accepted the risk of losing our memories. Honestly, as long as the Monolith doesn't make me forget where I stashed my Dorra, I'm fine.
It already did. You found Dorra in your boot once and thought you hit the jackpot. You were thrilled.
Hey, drop it! Anyway, we have a soul pact with you now. Our wishes don't cost us memories anymore, so we have nothing to worry about.
Oh, right.==W== ==PLAYER_NAME==, give me your hand.
Because from here on out, life isn't an exam for three anymore.==W== It's an exam for all four of us.
I know we've said something similar before, but we mean it.==W== We're glad to have you with us, Boss.
Yeah. Together, we'll write our own answers.
Exactly! Everyone's awake, so let's get moving. Mirage, here we come!
It was too dark to see much when we got here... This is Mirage? Looks like a typical desert city. Why call it the Edge of the World?
Most cities in Nova are built around Monoliths.==W== Mirage doesn't have one. There aren't any in the entire region.
That's why it's known as the land beyond Monoliths—==W==the Edge of the World.
But why build a city==W== where there's no Monolith?
There has to be a reason. I asked some veteran Trekkers about it, but they either didn't know or clammed up.
Makes sense. The people here must be desperate for a Monolith. Finding one out in the desert would be huge news.
But with no Monolith, no industry, and no trade... How do people survive?
Hey! Are you Trekkers from outside the desert?
Whoa!==W== We haven't seen outsiders besides the Imperial Guard in ages!==W== What brings you to Mirage?==W== I can show you around if you want!
Do you know anywhere more crowded? I'd like to ask around.
==PLAYER_NAME==, you go ahead. I'll follow in Loxy. Amber, hit me up once you get there.==W==
Our city looks pretty barren, but we have our ways to keep food on the table.
Like desert plants? Or rare goods?
You're smart! Spot on. We have the sweetest dates in all Nova, and we have crystal diamond ore.
But the dates never make it out of the desert, and the mines shut down ages ago.
So, as kids, we make our living off that.
Wait... Are those the Desert Scorpions who tried to kill me at the banquet?!
Looks like a street stall. Are they selling ... Artifacts?==W== Is that how you keep food on the table?
Look,==W== a knight's buying one now.
Hey, Desert Scorpion.==W== What's the price on these?
Two hundred thousand Dorra a pound.
By the pound?==W== Never heard of selling Artifacts by weight.==W== Are the casings made of crystal diamond, or are they stuffed with them?
You think that's steep? Tell me about it.
Look around. No Monolith in Mirage means no Artifacts. We hauled these across the desert in bags. Course we charge by weight.
Fine. Pick me out a Projector.==W== Being stuck in this dump is boring me to tears.
Everyone in Mirage knows the Desert Scorpions. You think I'd sell you a fake?
I asked you, is it real or not?
You looking for trouble?==W== Buy it or move on.
If it's real and works, I'll buy it.
If it's broken, I'll eat it on the spot.==W== Satisfied?
No way that's fifteen pounds. Your scale is rigged!
Look! There's a gravity magic seal under it!
You said if it's broken, you'd eat it.==W== Let me carve it up for you!
Fight! Fight! The Imperial Guard and the Desert Scorpions are going at it! Come quick!
Kid, stop yelling. We need to leave. It's not safe here.
What are you talking about? A fight means we can finally make some deals!
Hey, Mister Scorpion! Miss Guard! Look this way!==W== There are White Cats over here!
White Cats? What? No, we're not—==W==
What? No! We only got here yesterday!==W== We don't know anything about any White Cats!

strings.text: Amber defeats a Desert Scorpion, forcing the mercs to retreat. Myrsha then reveals that Mirage's factions are deliberately keeping the enemy alive. Following the lead, you arrive at the old theater—straight into a trap...
Ugh. Those White Cat magic guns are ridiculous. They shoot faster and hit harder than ours. It's the only reason I'm in the dirt right now.
Huh? Then what else could it be?!
See?==W== It's not the weapon.==W== Your draw is slow, and your trigger pull is weak.
Can we talk now?==W== Why do you keep calling us White Cats?==W== And what are they?
You wear White Cat clothes, carry White Cat weapons, and fight like White Cats. What else would you be?
You mean Amber's outfit and weapons?==W== So she looks like someone from the White Cat Troupe?==W== We found all this in our basement a long time ago.
Yeah. Never heard of White Cats.
A basement... Not a basement here in Mirage, right?
Our home is in Emor... Or it used to be.==W== This is our first time in Mirage. We arrived last night.
Emor...==W== So you scavenged a dead Cat's gear.==W== Whatever. It doesn't matter now.
We mistook you for White Cats and lost an embarrassing fight.==W== By desert law, we owe you a favor.==W== Name your request.
A request...==W== Boss, do you need them to do anything?
A request... Let me think.==W== How about we agree not to be enemies? You stay out of our way, and we stay out of yours.
That's it? What's your angle?==W== Winners usually demand a massive ransom or even take the losers as slaves.
Usually? I don't know those rules.==W== We're in Mirage for supplies and to find the Monolith out in the desert. If you can help us with that, we're even.
Generous. You definitely aren't White Cats.==W== Consider the supplies an apology for starting this mess. I'll ask the vice-captain if we can get you restocked.
The Desert Scorpion's deputy captain...==W== Wait. The people who ambushed me at the banquet were the Desert Scorpion captain and deputy.==W== Can I actually trust them right now?
Boss! What brings you all the way out to Mirage? Did something happen?==W== Wait, are you here to join the Desert Scorpions? Hah! I'd welcome you with open arms!
Scorpion. Let go. Or I shoot.
Wait, she's not a threat right now!==W== But Myrsha, let go. Personal space, please. This is terrifying.
Huh?==W== We only talked once, and you remembered my name?==W== That makes me so happy!
Talked?==W== I tend to remember the name of the assassin who tried to kill me.
An assassin?!==W== It was her? ==PLAYER_NAME==, she was the one who attacked you at the banquet?
Hey now, easy with the sword. That was then, this is now.
The contract is off, and the client is locked up. Why would we keep coming after you?
Besides, my guys lost fair and square, and you let them off easy. I don't repay kindness with a knife.
Consider your request granted. From now on, we are officially not enemies.
Still don't trust me? Look, sis.==W== I've got my neck pressed right against your blade. Good enough for you?
==PLAYER_NAME==, what's the call? She's even more forward than I am.
Stand down, Noya.==W== They were just hired knives back then, and she's not hostile now.==W== We're new here. No point picking a fight with the locals.
Heh. Knew you were smart, Boss! So we're friends now, right?
Alright, Scorpions, scatter!==W== Go prep those supplies and top up the Boss's ride with Grace.==W== I'm taking them on a food tour of Mirage. I'll see you when you're done.
Appreciate it.==W== And that works out perfectly. We needed a local to answer a few questions anyway.
I never saw food like this back in Emor, but every dish is incredible! <size=53>♪</size>==W== I'm stuffed. And our supplies are fully sorted out!
Got the recipe down! As soon as I find the ingredients, I'm cooking this for you.
See? We're out in the middle of nowhere, but Mirage still has charm, right?
Like they say. Home is where you feel at peace.
Though you were fighting the Imperial Guard pretty hard earlier. Is there bad blood between the Imperial Guard and the locals too?
Nah, not at all. We get along with the Imperial Guard fine.
How should I put it...==W== Let's call it a business partnership.==W== We're also teammates when it comes to fighting the White Cat Troupe.
The White Cat Troupe...==W== I keep hearing that name. Who are they?
They used to be the old Nova Empress's personal guard. Over a decade ago they betrayed and took the Empress's life. Total villains.
Grace Imperium hired the Imperial Guard to hunt them down. The White Cats fought a running battle all the way here. Mirage is their last stand.
Word is Mirage used to be loaded back then. But years of fighting turned it into this. Now most of the city is empty ruins.
E-Even the Empress?!==W== They're that ruthless?==W== Oh no.==W== We're already in their territory!==W== What if they're hiding behind a wall right now waiting to jump us?!
Relax. That all happened when I was a kid.==W== Nowadays Mirage is technically at war, but there are no battles left to fight.

We Desert Scorpions hold the abandoned crystal diamond mine up northeast.==W== The Imperial Guard has the central oasis out west. The White Cat leftovers took the second oasis down south.==W== Everyone has their turf, and we've kept out of each other's way for years.
Besides, there are barely any White Cats left. We could wipe them out with sheer numbers anytime we wanted.
If they're that dangerous, why not take them out?
And lose our business?==W== Wipe out the White Cats, and we have nothing to do.
Business... The kids this morning said something similar.
What are you talking about? A fight means we can finally make some deals!
You're keeping the enemy alive on purpose.
Sharp as always, Boss.==W== Mirage today is a city that runs entirely on war.
We Desert Scorpions are rough mercenaries. Even if we partner with the Imperial Guard, a little friction is part of the deal.
So we stage a fight every now and then. We leave behind some junk weapons as spoils for the Guard, and they use it to claim victories up the chain.
And the Guard? War always costs something, right?==W== They dump some expensive gear, snap evidence with a Photo Capturer,==W== and bill Grace Imperium for battlefield losses.
But those gears aren't broken. They submit a report for new armor and spears,==W== and the money gets cleared.

Then they pay the kids a twentieth of the price to drag that gear back. As for the money marked for new equipment,==W== thirty percent to us, seventy to them. Round and round, and the Dorras keep rolling in.
Talk about a shameless racket...==W== But I guess the kids earn a bit of honest coin from it.==W== I don't know what to think.
Come on, don't overthink it <size=53>♪</size> Nobody loses out here. Win-win, right?

And~==W== Guess what?==W== Today we put on a real show with the "White Cats."==W== The Guard's gonna file a report on a grueling battle, claim they repelled the entire White Cat army, and demand a massive payout.
Hehe. From that angle, we oughta thank you!
So ... you turned war into a business.
Ahaha!==W== Mirage has no goods worth hauling out of the desert. Without war, nobody here would survive.
If only there were a Monolith here. Everyone could live off Artifacts.==W== Hey, Myrsha, have you ever found one out in the desert?
A desert Monolith?==W== Never seen one.==W== People here spot things in the sands all the time, but when they go check, there's nothing there. Probably a castle in the air.
I exchange looks with the New Star Guild.==W== Forget my amnesia, those three had been inside that Monolith. It was no mirage.
But ... ==W==I heard that before my time, Mirage had a Monolith.
Wait, there used to be a Monolith here?==W== What happened to it?
What it sounds like. One day it just vanished. No warning.
Our captain seems to know something, but clams up whenever the topic comes up.
A Monolith vanishing... Could it be like what I went through...
No, it's not an earthquake.==W==<color=#bd3059> The Monolith is sinking!</color>
Boss, it's pulling us down with it...==W== I'm sorry. We might not make it back.
No, no... That's a memory of something that didn't happen.
Besides, if a Monolith sank into the ground, the impact would be huge. The people of Mirage would've noticed.
Spreading that speculation would cause panic. I'll keep quiet and play dumb for now.
A Monolith vanishing... It sounds crazy, but if it's true... It might be connected to the desert Monolith we're after.
Myrsha, besides your captain, does anyone else know about the vanishing Monolith?
The White Cat captain might know...==W== But I've never had contact with them.==W== And I don't think the townsfolk know about it. Not many old-timers left in Mirage anyway.
But, I know one place where we might find some answers about what happened.
Um...==W== Are we actually sneaking in here?==W== It looks creepy.
Myrsha said this was the old White Cat theater, before they betrayed the Empress.
The White Cats were here the longest. There might be clues inside about the city's past.
But Myrsha also said the terrifying==W== Dark-Footed Devil Cat took over this place!
Boss is more powerful than a devil. Don't be afraid.
Uh, I don't think that's how it works...==W== But we're out of options.==W== Let's go. We're here for clues. No fighting.
Boss? Where are you?==W== Is that you, Boss?
A-Amber?!==W== Hey, don't just grab things in the dark!
Huh... Can't see a thing, but this place feels strangely familiar...
W-We should get out! It's pitch-black! What if the Dark-Footed Devil Cat attacks us—
A low voice comes from behind us.==RT==Something smooth and metallic presses against our heads.
