param: The Scepters of Death flood the cities, sparking a massive turf war between oppressed citizens, angry companies, and the Salvation Committee. Blaming herself, Angie puts herself behind bars...
I'm fine. The enchanted breastplate stopped the bullet, and the padding cushioned the blow. But ... the force still felt like a battering ram to the chest.
Impact aside, it stopped the bullet. That is a success. Can we mass-produce this for the Committee?
The Tyrant and the Desert Scorpions are bleeding our people dry with their hit-and-run tactics.

The energy cost is massive, and the effect is brief. Enchanting a full suit only buys you thirty minutes. Five casts will drain a Soul Stone completely. The cost-to-duration ratio makes it unviable for the field.
Plus, armor has gaps. One lucky shot in between the plates and you are dead. Trying to ward those weak points would burn an entire Soul Stone per cast.
An entire Soul Stone for thirty minutes? I'm no soldier, but blocking a standard magic gunshot shouldn't be that taxing.
It shouldn't. But magic guns and the Scepters of Death operate entirely differently.==W== A magic gun simply shapes magic energy into a projectile.
Experienced fighters sense that mana spike,==W== cast a quick ward,==W== and neutralize the hit.
Enchanted arrows work the same way.==W== You dispel the magic aura first,==W== then parry the wooden shaft.
Which brings us to the problem. The Scepter does not fire mana. It fires solid metal slugs.
There is no mana signature to track before impact,==W== and it outpaces any arrow in both speed and power.
Since we can't see the attacks coming,==W== we have to keep our shields on maximum mana output==W== constantly.
And we lack the time to refine the magic, or the logistics to forge better armor...
Heh. The Tyrant has us checkmated.
I owe you an apology, Lady Angie.==W== I didn't believe ==PLAYER_NAME== was the legendary Tyrant. I thought you were jumping to conclusions.
Up until now, I was only obeying the Grand Captain. I was going through the motions of helping you, nothing more.
So these recent battles changed your mind? You believe ==PLAYER_NAME== is the Tyrant now?
Casualties are expected in war. That is not what convinced me.
Flooding the cities with the Scepters of Death,==W== planting seeds of chaos across the continent...==W== Who else would orchestrate that but the Tyrant?
Is that how you see it? Then you've misjudged me, you've misjudged ==PLAYER_NAME==, and you completely misunderstand how this world would end.
The Tyrant brought chaos, yes. But ==SEX3== actions stray entirely from the prophecy.
Looking back, ==SEX== was never the world-ending Tyrant we thought.
The one responsible for shaping ==SEX4== into this ... is no one else but...
Meanwhile,==RT==at the Omnisky Aegis Business Department in Geminia.
That policyholder from earlier is back. His sister was rushed to an Eye of Grace hospital for heart palpitations and fainting. She needs surgery, and he expects us to cover the bills.
The Eye of Grace? Does he have any idea what they charge? We are not approving that. Deny the claim.
B-But we don't have a valid reason. Can we deny him outright?
Do I have to teach you everything? Did he submit a pre-approval request before letting them admit her? Is the surgery considered excessive treatment? Pick one and reject him.
He says she collapsed on the street and a passerby rushed her to the ER. He has all the diagnostic reports from the Eye of Grace. Everything checks out. If we deny the claim...
No means no. We hit our payout cap for the month. If we authorize a payout this massive, the Senate will breathe down our necks again...==W== Hand me her file.
... Perfect. There is our out. Reject his claim for breach of disclosure. Tell him he failed to report a pre-existing condition when he signed up.
Pre-existing condition? Sorry, but I don't think his sister has any medical history of...
You idiot, look right here. Does this or does this not say she once had a cavity?
I am sorry, sir. Because of an irregularity when you opened the policy, we cannot approve your claim.
Is that so... I am sorry to bother you. I will figure out another way to pay for the surgery.
Wait. Even though we can't approve the claim, please take this...==W== It's a little something from my own pocket. I hope your sister recovers soon.
I... Thank you! I can't believe there is someone this kind at Omnisky Aegis. I am glad I ran into you today. I will never forget this as long as I live!
Haha... Kind, yeah right. I'm a spineless coward doing my supervisor's dirty work.
Look at you, dipping into your own savings again.==W== You know privately assisting a canceled policyholder is a strict violation of company policy, right?
No, wait, it's a misunderstanding! Let me explain!
Relax, I'm messing with you. I already quit, remember? You don't have to worry about me snitching.

Oh, it's you. Don't scare me like that.==W== Ever since you quit, that garbage boss has been dumping all your unfinished work on me.==W== These clients clearly meet the payout conditions, but he forces me to deny their claims and cancel their policies every single day.
It kills me watching them walk away with nothing.==W== Anyway, why did you quit? You never told me.
Same exact crap you're dealing with now. He kept denying every claim, saying they did high-risk activities without prior approval.
But my entire client list was Trekkers. Was I supposed to make them file an application and sit around waiting for days every time they climbed a Monolith?
Eventually I realized it was total bullshit. I got pissed, marched up to protest, got the crap kicked out of me ... and was fired on the spot.
This whole company is rotten to the core...
Damn right. That bastard's a parasite.==W== He took the safety net meant for everyone and turned it into his personal piggy bank.
Footsteps... It's him! Quick, hide! He's been traveling with a whole squad of armed guards lately. If he catches you, you're dead meat!
Hide? I've been waiting for him. I came here today to settle the score once and for all.
Well, well. If it isn't the trash I fired the other day.==W== What's this? You even brought a little weapon. Here for revenge?
Hah! Revenge? Don't be silly. You took such great care of me. I'm just here to return the favor.
Is that right? Let's see you try. You think you can take on my entire escort by yourself?==W== Get her! Throw this loudmouth in the river to feed the fish!
C-Calm down! Don't do this, you're no match for the Imperial Knights!
Oh, I'm perfectly calm. But this is about to get messy. You'd better stand back.
What the—! Is that ... Scepter of Death?!==W== Oh crap, fall back! Retreat!
Guh... No way... I specifically prepared ...==W== a top-tier protection scroll... How did you...
A few days later.==RT==In the Trekker Association outside the Emor City.
Hey, miss! Wait up! You come here a lot?
Uh... Yeah. I only started coming around lately.
I'm Myrsha, from the desert. What's your name?
Sorry to pry, but I noticed you staring at the board forever. Can't find a good commission?
Yeah. Nobody wants a partner. Clients take one look at an average Trekker like me and pass.
I hear you. Standard leather armor, basic sword, fresh to the adventurer life. People size you up fast.
But hey, that's how it works everywhere in Nova.
That's why I've got the perfect weapon for you. Check this out! With this in your hands, clients will be lining up to hire you.
Is that ... a magic gun? I've never seen one shaped like that. But honestly, I suck at magic...
Oh, don't worry about that! This is no magic gun.==W== You ever hear of the Scepter of Death?
The Scepter of Death? That artifact they keep talking about on the news? I heard it's rare... The metal feels unlike anything I've ever touched.
Hehe, that's right! This is the newest Desert Scorpion product. The Scepter of Death 47.==W== Easy to use, easy to maintain. Even a kid like me can easily aim.
Only 99,999 Dorra. This Scepter came out of a Monolith yesterday. Brand new and all yours.
That price seems way too low for a rare Artifact.==W== Is this a scam?
Take it and try it out. If you like it, come back in a week and pay. If not, bring it back within seven days. No questions asked.
A Scepter of Death...! Hehe, the news calls you villains, but you Desert Scorpions are actually pretty sweet.
Alright, I'll borrow it then. Thanks!
Nah, it's not me! Thank Boss. ==SEX1== pulled all kinds of Scepters from the Wishing Box. We're cashing in big time ♪
But honestly, I expected more. I thought the Scepter of Death had some legendary power. Turns out it's just a handy tool.
That works in our favor. Once it's widespread, people will see it's not the apocalyptic weapon from the prophecies.
And once that happens, all those rumors about the Tyrant destroying the world will fall apart on their own.
Sell the weapon cheap or give it away, then make a profit on the ammo. Haha, Boss is a damn business genius.
Thanks to you, we Desert Scorpions can walk through Emor with our heads held high under the Boss Accord banner. I mean it. Thank you.
We look out for each other. We never would have escaped Angie's assault without your help.
Besides, the Scorpions have taken their fair share of hits lately too.
We aren't afraid of a few casualties to get what we want.
Here's the weird part, though. I heard the big companies are hunting Angie even harder now that the Scepters of Death are everywhere.
If these Scepters are what's pushing the workers to rebel, you'd think the Senate would be gunning for us instead of her.
Ha! They would love to get rid of us. But we're the only ones who know how to wish up more Scepters, so they can't afford to touch us.
Trace it all back and this whole mess is Angie's fault anyway. Coming after us would be a waste of time.
A few major companies have actually approached me in secret. They want to partner up and sell the Scepters of Death together.
I turned them down. Told them Boss Accord is too busy dodging the Salvation Committee to think about partnerships right now.
I'm sure they got the hint—deal with the Committee first, and then we talk business.
You're even getting outside companies to do your work. That's some terrifying strategy, Boss.
But ... are you sure about this? Flooding the market with these Scepters... I have a bad feeling. Word is a top executive at Omnisky Aegis has been murdered.
You worry too much. Those corporate suits had it coming. Besides, we're putting power in the hands of people who never had a way to fight back.
If you ask me, this is way healthier than the old days, when your worth was measured by your magic and your wallet.
I see where Myrsha's coming from, but Iris isn't wrong to worry.
Once we're done with the Salvation Committee, I need to rethink our distribution strategy for the Scepters of Death.

<size=52>It's Claire!</size>==W== Ugh... Forget it.==W== What are you doing here?

==PLAYER_NAME==? You mean the Boss. Small world.
This whole block is full of people ==SEX== took down.
The babbling mess next door is Feagin. Total scumbag who ran a child labor ring.
She couldn't stomach losing the company war. Got mixed up with Nocturn Eterna, made a Monolith wish beyond her control, and now she's ... this.
And those are Joseph and Lady Gray next to me. Joseph's whatever, but Lady Gray's scrap metal after Darcia squeezed every last bit of value out of her.
Tch... Shut your mouth, Claire.==W== When I get out of this hole, I'll collect—with interest.

... I see. So this is where my journey ends.

strings.text: Taffett juggled odd jobs to support the children, but with assassins closing in, she considered leaving them to keep them safe. Narida proposed using the Monolith to erase memories of the White Cat Troupe...
Here you go—white bread and veggie soup.==W== Careful,==W== it's hot.
There's enough for everyone.==W== Stop pushing.
I haven't had a hot meal in forever...==W== Sniffle...
Gulp, gulp—==W==ahh... I'm okay. Sorry, I ate too fast.==W== It's just... I haven't eaten in three days.
Th-Three days...?==W== Then just sip the soup for now. You've been starving too long. Eating all that bread will just make you sick.
Iris, there are way more kids out here now.==W== We've got at least ...==W== a dozen more coming for food than last week.
A bunch of orphanages shut down lately. A few lucky kids got foster homes, but the rest have nowhere to go. They're stuck on the streets.
It's those soldiers in white. The grown-ups say they're hunting the White Cat Troupe, so they're going after any orphanage connected to them.
Good thing we're just kids Mom took in, not an actual orphanage. They won't come after us... Right?
Shh! Don't call her "Mom." You have to say—==W==
Oh, right. Kids at the White Cat orphanages always say "Mom." We must not raise suspicion...==W== So stick to "Auntie."
Do you think Auntie could help these kids?==W== She took Amber and me in,==W== after all.
No.==W== I feel awful for them, but I secretly did the math...==W==
Auntie already exhausts herself with her tailoring jobs every day,==W== yet the Dorra she makes==W== is barely enough to feed us.
Didn't we already talk about this?==W== Kids our age can't find proper jobs.

When I asked Auntie about it, she just handed me the basement key and told us to focus on our studies. That tells me no matter how hard we try, we're just kids. We can't earn the kind of Dorra we need.
You're right. Even if we try watching shops ... or running errands...
The three of us worked a whole week,==W== and the food we earned barely covered one meal for everyone here.
Sigh... Getting a full meal is hard.
Sigh... Being a grown-up is hard.
They're still kids themselves, but are already trying to help out.==W== Taffett, your kids have really good hearts.==W== How'd you do it? Got any secrets you mind sharing?
I have a little sister, Benito, sweet as can be. But we're so far apart in age, I honestly don't really know how to talk to her.
Secrets? Well...==W== After teaching them basic self-defense, I completely stopped showing them how to fight.
In the end, it's up to them to decide who they want to become. So I gave Iris the key to the basement. That's where Her Majesty's books and treasures are kept.
Huh. Just let them figure it out on their own?==W== Then I guess I'll go home and see what it is Benito actually wants to do.
Yeah, I was surprised too.==W== They're way more mature than I thought.==W== They actually do almost all the housework now, so I can rest a bit when I get home.
No, no.==W== That's just because the more you try to clean, the messier the place gets. They probably just couldn't stand it anymore...==W==
Ahem... Let's drop that.==W== Narida, know any ways to make a lot of Dorra fast?==W== My tailoring job barely covers the bills.
Barely? You spend your days sewing clothes and your nights stitching wounds. You're keeping a family of four afloat—that's actually pretty good money for Ash District.
Even while I'm currently on the run, I've heard of the famous "Dark-Footed Cat."
Yeah.==W== Word on the street is that when the sun goes down,==W== a lady in fancy black leather shoes slinks through the alleys like a ghost. Like a cat.
Mending clothes, patching up wounds,==W== and casually taking out the street gangs.==W== Walking around at night is way safer now than it's ever been.
Her style reminds people of those dark-footed cats out in the desert—==W==small, but fierce.==W== So the name stuck.
What a weird nickname...==W== Wait, you're changing the subject again.==W== My income is decent, but it's really only enough to support the three kids...
Well, I do know one way to make big Dorra—let's go knock over Deepsea Finance!
Stop joking. That would put us right on the Grace Imperium's radar.
Oh, so you're worried about being exposed, are you?

The old you would never take a job this flashy. And got yourself a "Dark-Footed Cat"? That practically screams "White Cat." Are you begging the Sentinels of Dawn and the Imperial Guard to come knocking?
And sure, you always pitied the street kids, but you never actually stepped in. You knew you couldn't. You were a soldier on a mission—you couldn't save everyone.
But now you're actually trying to figure out how to make more Dorra for someone else's sake. You really have changed, Taffett.
That's not...==W== No, you're right.==W== You're out there fighting with the White Cats, and I'm hiding here, playing mother. Maybe I don't deserve to call myself a soldier anymore.
Hey, maybe that's not a bad thing. For the kids, it's—==W==shh. Hear that? Footsteps.==W== The Imperial Guard is heading right for us.
The Guard... Narida, take the kids and run. I'll hold them off.
Let me handle it. It's probably just a routine sweep, so don't start a war. I'll just step out, flash the prime bait, and they'll go after me instead.
You owe me for this one. And hey...==W== I actually like this new you.
Get the kids inside and lock up.==W== You're running out of time, Taffett.==W== If you want to keep them safe, you need to have a plan by the time I return.
The moment Taffett pulls the street kids inside,==RT==heavy gunfire erupts from the next block over.
What am I ...==W== supposed to do?
That night, after the kids finally fell asleep, I lay awake for hours,==RT==going over everything in my head.
I am a White Cat. Even if I'd spent those last few years playing house,==RT==that doesn't change who I am.
I was careful. I didn't leave traces. But the memories are still stored in my head,==RT==never scrubbed away.
The Troupe uses interrogation magic to extract memories. Since the Dusk Arbiter==RT==has captured enough of us, they've definitely learned the trick by now.
If I stay, they'd find me eventually,==RT==and I'd be dragging the kids down with me for nothing.
Then... I think I know what I should do—
I would leave this place, or I would leave this world entirely.
And while I'm at it, I need to draw their eyes away from Ash District for good.
Mom, it's getting dark.==W== Are you really going out?
Listen to me, Noya.==W== I have important work to take care of tonight. You three stay inside,==W== and don't open that door for anyone. Understand?
But Mom...==W== You said you'd stay home tonight with us. You promised.
It's important. Don't make this difficult.==W== And what did I tell you? Stop calling me that.
I'll be late. Set up the traps and go to bed.==W== Don't stay up.
B-But...==W== The last time you and Narida had "work," you were gone for days.==W== We didn't know if you were coming back.
And what's that fire in the kitchen?==W== Are you feeding the Ash District kids again?
You know those soldiers in white are grabbing people off the streets. Stop drawing attention to yourselves. Noya, put that fire out. Now.
But ... we were making that for you, Mom...==W==
Noya,==W== stop calling me Mom!==W== How many times do I have to say it?!
Waaah!==W== Mo—==W==Auntie doesn't want us anymore!
No,==W== I-I'm sorry...==W== That came out wrong. I... I didn't mean it.
You just don't want to be our mom. You say it's "work," but the bag you carry is huge. You're not coming back tonight, are you?
Like all the other parents in Ash District. When things get hard, they just leave. They don't come back.
Fine! Then you're not our mom anymore! From now on, you're just Auntie. Auntie, Auntie, Auntie, Auntie!
That's not what I meant...==W== Okay. I promise. No matter how late it gets, I'll be back before sunrise!==W== Just this once...==W== Please believe me.
The Imperial Guard's prisoner convoy is coming tonight. We'll ambush them here.
Narida, I need to be sure. All the captured White Cats in Emor are being brought here together?
Right. Once we pull them out, the White Cats are withdrawing from Emor and the other cities. We'll regroup in Mirage and keep fighting the new Empress.
Why Mirage? It's remote, but supplies are scarce, and the desert cuts us off.==W== If we're surrounded, our guerrilla tactics will be rendered useless.
Because... Her Majesty ordered every White Cat except you to seal off the Monolith in Mirage.==W== No one's allowed in.
But that Monolith doesn't have an entrance. It's impossible to get inside.
True, but the Grace Imperium sent a lot of people to Mirage. They've been studying it. They might have found a hidden entrance.
The remaining White Cats held meetings. Everyone insists on carrying out Her Majesty's final order. We have no choice but to make our stand.
But what about you? Are you okay? That fight with the kids was a first for you, wasn't it?
I'm fine. Ever since you told me I had to make a choice, I've been thinking. And my choice is...==W==
After tonight, I'm leaving Emor with the White Cats. That way the kids don't get dragged into this, and I draw the searchers away.
Can you really leave those kids behind?
They can take care of themselves. The Dusk Arbiter has the Imperial Guard doing a dragnet search of Ash District. They could show up any day.
Me leaving Emor is what's best for them. At least...==W== That's what I thought until tonight.
Narida, once we rescue everyone and grab the intel, take the White Cats and fall back. I'm going to the cathedral, where the Dusk Arbiter is.
If I take out every arbiter who knows the memory extraction spell, I can safely stay in Emor.
Taffett, do you know how tight security is at that cathedral? You might be able to kill all the arbiters, but you'll also die doing it.
The dead can't talk...==W== As long as it protects those kids, I'm fine with it.
But no matter what, I don't... I don't want to leave them. And I'm not stupid enough to throw my life away for nothing.
The White Cat who earned the codename Taffett for being the strongest is willing to risk it all to take care of some kids?==W== Still, I get why you feel that way.
When I found out you were going to be a mom, I was jealous for ages. I thought, why the battle-crazed Taffett? I'd be way better at it!
That's because I'm good at hiding it.
Logically, it would've made more sense for me to watch the kids while you led the White Cats to guard the Monolith in Mirage. That would've played to our strengths.
But watching you with those kids, I finally got it. Back when we were little, you weren't obsessed with fighting because you enjoyed it...==W==
... It was your way of protecting the people you cared about.
If they needed you to, you'd even alter your own mind for them.
You're giving me too much credit. I didn't think that far ahead. I just ...==W== did what needed to be done. Back at the orphanage, nobody else wanted to fight, so I stepped up.
Your Majesty... I finally understand your plan.==W== This is the only way to rewrite destiny for me, Taffett,==W== and the White Cats.
Huh? What are you talking about, Narida? You lost me.
Oh, nothing. Sigh... You're hopeless. Letting you die in some pointless brawl with the Dusk Arbiter would defeat the whole purpose of Her Majesty's plan.
I know a way to beat their memory extraction spell, but it comes at a steep price.
I don't care. As long as I can stay with those kids,==W== I'll do anything.
Glad to hear it. Look, if the Dusk Arbiter gets suspicious, they'll use that spell on you.==W== But if you wipe every trace of the White Cats from your memory beforehand, you'll come up clean.
So ... as long as I completely forget the White Cat Troupe? Is it even possible to cherry-pick which memories you lose?
If it is, I don't know how. Besides, normal amnesia just buries things deep in the brain. Magic can still dig them back out.
For a complete wipe, there's only one option. The Monolith.
Make a wish ... and offer my memories as payment...==W== But I thought you can't choose what it takes from you.
You can't. But I picked up a neat trick from the Trekkers.
First, write down everything you want to keep in a notebook. Then go on a massive wishing spree. Review your notes after every single wish.
That way, the memories you want get reinforced, and the ones you don't eventually get scrubbed. Supposedly, some Trekkers completely rewrote their personalities doing this.
Makes sense.==W== Got it. I'll start climbing tomorrow.
Decisive as always. Let's adjust our plan then.

Rewriting your memory like this will take a while.==W== We need to cause a massive scene and drag every Dusk Arbiter and Imperial Guard out of Emor after me.==W== Make them think the White Cats pulled one last heist and skipped town for good.
Forget the ambush. Let's hit the streets and make some noise!
We're Her Majesty's personal guards! What gives you the right to arrest us?!
Regicidal bastards! Still got the nerve to talk back?!
Stand down! We're knights, not executioners!
Hmph. Consider yourselves lucky for now. The cells are right ahead. You crazy cats can sit tight and wait for the chopping block.==W== No one's coming to save you.
Don't be so sure. The cavalry's right here!
Bring it on, tin cans! Eat some White Cat lead!
Form ranks! Hold the line!==W== Reinforcements are coming. The Sentinels of Dawn will be here any second!
Captain, stay back! It's a trap!==W== They're parading us around to draw you out!
So you set a net.==W== But==W== do you actually believe that you can hold a White Cat when she's fighting for real?
Move, move, move! Firefight at the port! The White Cats are staging a rescue. Box them in and take them all down!
Ugh! I'm hit! Where did that come from?
No sound of gunshots?==W== Defensive formation! Locate that sniper!
We can't see them!==W== They're moving too fast!
Dammit.==W== Someone send a distress signal!==W==
First wave of reinforcements at the port is down.==W== Moving to the next street.
Don't bother waiting. I took out your backup before I even got here.
You did this alone? Th-That's impossible.
I am Narida, Captain of the First Squad and acting troupe leader. Remember the name.==W== Now hand over the keys, and I'll let you live.
That's a win! ♪ Alright everyone, get those shackles off. Your gear is in these crates.==W== Suit up and catch a boat out of Emor. Move!
No, you go ahead. I'll cover you.==W== Tonight, not a single Knight or Sentinel in Emor gets to sleep.
White Cat! This is as far as you go!
Gah?!==W== Where did that come from?!
Nice, Taffett. You still have your edge.==W== Keep it up. I'll draw their fire out in the open, and you keep striking from the shadows. Don't let anyone see your face.
I squeezed a knight for intel. The Sentinels' temporary command post is a hotel in Gold District. Security is light. All our files and rosters are there.
We caused enough chaos in the Ash District to pull their forces here. Let's slip through the waterway and catch them completely off guard.
Burn those files, and you disappear from their records, Taffett. Let's move!
Commander. We were ambushed during transport, and the White Cats escaped. The attacker identified herself as Narida, claiming to be the First Squad Captain and acting troupe leader.
And? Ash District is a complete disaster right now. How many White Cats are we dealing with?
One... As far as we could tell, it was only one person.
Come up with a better lie.==W== We have over a hundred Knights and Sentinels down, and you expect me to believe it was a single enemy?
They're fast asleep. You two should surrender. And by the way, our fighting style gave you the wrong idea. You actually thought White Cats were pushovers.==W==
This is our true strength. Remember it well.==W== You asked for a war, so now you're getting one.
She triggered a blast circle in the office. Wanted to take you down with her.
I... I'm okay. But why did you save me?==W== I'm your enemy.
Heh. The Imperial Guard just takes orders from the Grace Imperium. You didn't ask for this fight. Besides, you protected my people during the escort.
This place is going to burn. Go get some help and carry your friends out of here.
They were all in the command center. They burned up along with the commander.
Taffett, what's wrong? That's so much blood. Did you take the blast protecting me?!
Narida, I'm okay.==W== Now...==W== I can finally ...==W==<size=30> be with ... the kids...</size>==W==

param: Taffett juggled odd jobs to support the children, but with assassins closing in, she considered leaving them to keep them safe. Narida proposed using the Monolith to erase memories of the White Cat Troupe...
Here you go—white bread and veggie soup.==W== Careful,==W== it's hot.
There's enough for everyone.==W== Stop pushing.
I haven't had a hot meal in forever...==W== Sniffle...
Gulp, gulp—==W==ahh... I'm okay. Sorry, I ate too fast.==W== It's just... I haven't eaten in three days.
Th-Three days...?==W== Then just sip the soup for now. You've been starving too long. Eating all that bread will just make you sick.
Iris, there are way more kids out here now.==W== We've got at least ...==W== a dozen more coming for food than last week.
A bunch of orphanages shut down lately. A few lucky kids got foster homes, but the rest have nowhere to go. They're stuck on the streets.
It's those soldiers in white. The grown-ups say they're hunting the White Cat Troupe, so they're going after any orphanage connected to them.
Good thing we're just kids Mom took in, not an actual orphanage. They won't come after us... Right?
Shh! Don't call her "Mom." You have to say—==W==
Oh, right. Kids at the White Cat orphanages always say "Mom." We must not raise suspicion...==W== So stick to "Auntie."
Do you think Auntie could help these kids?==W== She took Amber and me in,==W== after all.
No.==W== I feel awful for them, but I secretly did the math...==W==
Auntie already exhausts herself with her tailoring jobs every day,==W== yet the Dorra she makes==W== is barely enough to feed us.
Didn't we already talk about this?==W== Kids our age can't find proper jobs.

When I asked Auntie about it, she just handed me the basement key and told us to focus on our studies. That tells me no matter how hard we try, we're just kids. We can't earn the kind of Dorra we need.
You're right. Even if we try watching shops ... or running errands...
The three of us worked a whole week,==W== and the food we earned barely covered one meal for everyone here.
Sigh... Getting a full meal is hard.
Sigh... Being a grown-up is hard.
They're still kids themselves, but are already trying to help out.==W== Taffett, your kids have really good hearts.==W== How'd you do it? Got any secrets you mind sharing?
I have a little sister, Benito, sweet as can be. But we're so far apart in age, I honestly don't really know how to talk to her.
Secrets? Well...==W== After teaching them basic self-defense, I completely stopped showing them how to fight.
In the end, it's up to them to decide who they want to become. So I gave Iris the key to the basement. That's where Her Majesty's books and treasures are kept.
Huh. Just let them figure it out on their own?==W== Then I guess I'll go home and see what it is Benito actually wants to do.
Yeah, I was surprised too.==W== They're way more mature than I thought.==W== They actually do almost all the housework now, so I can rest a bit when I get home.
No, no.==W== That's just because the more you try to clean, the messier the place gets. They probably just couldn't stand it anymore...==W==
Ahem... Let's drop that.==W== Narida, know any ways to make a lot of Dorra fast?==W== My tailoring job barely covers the bills.
Barely? You spend your days sewing clothes and your nights stitching wounds. You're keeping a family of four afloat—that's actually pretty good money for Ash District.
Even while I'm currently on the run, I've heard of the famous "Dark-Footed Cat."
Yeah.==W== Word on the street is that when the sun goes down,==W== a lady in fancy black leather shoes slinks through the alleys like a ghost. Like a cat.
Mending clothes, patching up wounds,==W== and casually taking out the street gangs.==W== Walking around at night is way safer now than it's ever been.
Her style reminds people of those dark-footed cats out in the desert—==W==small, but fierce.==W== So the name stuck.
What a weird nickname...==W== Wait, you're changing the subject again.==W== My income is decent, but it's really only enough to support the three kids...
Well, I do know one way to make big Dorra—let's go knock over Deepsea Finance!
Stop joking. That would put us right on the Grace Imperium's radar.
Oh, so you're worried about being exposed, are you?

The old you would never take a job this flashy. And got yourself a "Dark-Footed Cat"? That practically screams "White Cat." Are you begging the Sentinels of Dawn and the Imperial Guard to come knocking?
And sure, you always pitied the street kids, but you never actually stepped in. You knew you couldn't. You were a soldier on a mission—you couldn't save everyone.
But now you're actually trying to figure out how to make more Dorra for someone else's sake. You really have changed, Taffett.
That's not...==W== No, you're right.==W== You're out there fighting with the White Cats, and I'm hiding here, playing mother. Maybe I don't deserve to call myself a soldier anymore.
Hey, maybe that's not a bad thing. For the kids, it's—==W==shh. Hear that? Footsteps.==W== The Imperial Guard is heading right for us.
The Guard... Narida, take the kids and run. I'll hold them off.
Let me handle it. It's probably just a routine sweep, so don't start a war. I'll just step out, flash the prime bait, and they'll go after me instead.
You owe me for this one. And hey...==W== I actually like this new you.
Get the kids inside and lock up.==W== You're running out of time, Taffett.==W== If you want to keep them safe, you need to have a plan by the time I return.
The moment Taffett pulls the street kids inside,==RT==heavy gunfire erupts from the next block over.
What am I ...==W== supposed to do?
That night, after the kids finally fell asleep, I lay awake for hours,==RT==going over everything in my head.
I am a White Cat. Even if I'd spent those last few years playing house,==RT==that doesn't change who I am.
I was careful. I didn't leave traces. But the memories are still stored in my head,==RT==never scrubbed away.
The Troupe uses interrogation magic to extract memories. Since the Dusk Arbiter==RT==has captured enough of us, they've definitely learned the trick by now.
If I stay, they'd find me eventually,==RT==and I'd be dragging the kids down with me for nothing.
Then... I think I know what I should do—
I would leave this place, or I would leave this world entirely.
And while I'm at it, I need to draw their eyes away from Ash District for good.
Mom, it's getting dark.==W== Are you really going out?
Listen to me, Noya.==W== I have important work to take care of tonight. You three stay inside,==W== and don't open that door for anyone. Understand?
But Mom...==W== You said you'd stay home tonight with us. You promised.
It's important. Don't make this difficult.==W== And what did I tell you? Stop calling me that.
I'll be late. Set up the traps and go to bed.==W== Don't stay up.
B-But...==W== The last time you and Narida had "work," you were gone for days.==W== We didn't know if you were coming back.
And what's that fire in the kitchen?==W== Are you feeding the Ash District kids again?
You know those soldiers in white are grabbing people off the streets. Stop drawing attention to yourselves. Noya, put that fire out. Now.
But ... we were making that for you, Mom...==W==
Noya,==W== stop calling me Mom!==W== How many times do I have to say it?!
Waaah!==W== Mo—==W==Auntie doesn't want us anymore!
No,==W== I-I'm sorry...==W== That came out wrong. I... I didn't mean it.
You just don't want to be our mom. You say it's "work," but the bag you carry is huge. You're not coming back tonight, are you?
Like all the other parents in Ash District. When things get hard, they just leave. They don't come back.
Fine! Then you're not our mom anymore! From now on, you're just Auntie. Auntie, Auntie, Auntie, Auntie!
That's not what I meant...==W== Okay. I promise. No matter how late it gets, I'll be back before sunrise!==W== Just this once...==W== Please believe me.
The Imperial Guard's prisoner convoy is coming tonight. We'll ambush them here.
Narida, I need to be sure. All the captured White Cats in Emor are being brought here together?
Right. Once we pull them out, the White Cats are withdrawing from Emor and the other cities. We'll regroup in Mirage and keep fighting the new Empress.
Why Mirage? It's remote, but supplies are scarce, and the desert cuts us off.==W== If we're surrounded, our guerrilla tactics will be rendered useless.
Because... Her Majesty ordered every White Cat except you to seal off the Monolith in Mirage.==W== No one's allowed in.
But that Monolith doesn't have an entrance. It's impossible to get inside.
True, but the Grace Imperium sent a lot of people to Mirage. They've been studying it. They might have found a hidden entrance.
The remaining White Cats held meetings. Everyone insists on carrying out Her Majesty's final order. We have no choice but to make our stand.
But what about you? Are you okay? That fight with the kids was a first for you, wasn't it?
I'm fine. Ever since you told me I had to make a choice, I've been thinking. And my choice is...==W==
After tonight, I'm leaving Emor with the White Cats. That way the kids don't get dragged into this, and I draw the searchers away.
Can you really leave those kids behind?
They can take care of themselves. The Dusk Arbiter has the Imperial Guard doing a dragnet search of Ash District. They could show up any day.
Me leaving Emor is what's best for them. At least...==W== That's what I thought until tonight.
Narida, once we rescue everyone and grab the intel, take the White Cats and fall back. I'm going to the cathedral, where the Dusk Arbiter is.
If I take out every arbiter who knows the memory extraction spell, I can safely stay in Emor.
Taffett, do you know how tight security is at that cathedral? You might be able to kill all the arbiters, but you'll also die doing it.
The dead can't talk...==W== As long as it protects those kids, I'm fine with it.
But no matter what, I don't... I don't want to leave them. And I'm not stupid enough to throw my life away for nothing.
The White Cat who earned the codename Taffett for being the strongest is willing to risk it all to take care of some kids?==W== Still, I get why you feel that way.
When I found out you were going to be a mom, I was jealous for ages. I thought, why the battle-crazed Taffett? I'd be way better at it!
That's because I'm good at hiding it.
Logically, it would've made more sense for me to watch the kids while you led the White Cats to guard the Monolith in Mirage. That would've played to our strengths.
But watching you with those kids, I finally got it. Back when we were little, you weren't obsessed with fighting because you enjoyed it...==W==
... It was your way of protecting the people you cared about.
If they needed you to, you'd even alter your own mind for them.
You're giving me too much credit. I didn't think that far ahead. I just ...==W== did what needed to be done. Back at the orphanage, nobody else wanted to fight, so I stepped up.
Your Majesty... I finally understand your plan.==W== This is the only way to rewrite destiny for me, Taffett,==W== and the White Cats.
Huh? What are you talking about, Narida? You lost me.
Oh, nothing. Sigh... You're hopeless. Letting you die in some pointless brawl with the Dusk Arbiter would defeat the whole purpose of Her Majesty's plan.
I know a way to beat their memory extraction spell, but it comes at a steep price.
I don't care. As long as I can stay with those kids,==W== I'll do anything.
Glad to hear it. Look, if the Dusk Arbiter gets suspicious, they'll use that spell on you.==W== But if you wipe every trace of the White Cats from your memory beforehand, you'll come up clean.
So ... as long as I completely forget the White Cat Troupe? Is it even possible to cherry-pick which memories you lose?
If it is, I don't know how. Besides, normal amnesia just buries things deep in the brain. Magic can still dig them back out.
For a complete wipe, there's only one option. The Monolith.
Make a wish ... and offer my memories as payment...==W== But I thought you can't choose what it takes from you.
You can't. But I picked up a neat trick from the Trekkers.
First, write down everything you want to keep in a notebook. Then go on a massive wishing spree. Review your notes after every single wish.
That way, the memories you want get reinforced, and the ones you don't eventually get scrubbed. Supposedly, some Trekkers completely rewrote their personalities doing this.
Makes sense.==W== Got it. I'll start climbing tomorrow.
Decisive as always. Let's adjust our plan then.

Rewriting your memory like this will take a while.==W== We need to cause a massive scene and drag every Dusk Arbiter and Imperial Guard out of Emor after me.==W== Make them think the White Cats pulled one last heist and skipped town for good.
Forget the ambush. Let's hit the streets and make some noise!
We're Her Majesty's personal guards! What gives you the right to arrest us?!
Regicidal bastards! Still got the nerve to talk back?!
Stand down! We're knights, not executioners!
Hmph. Consider yourselves lucky for now. The cells are right ahead. You crazy cats can sit tight and wait for the chopping block.==W== No one's coming to save you.
Don't be so sure. The cavalry's right here!
Bring it on, tin cans! Eat some White Cat lead!
Form ranks! Hold the line!==W== Reinforcements are coming. The Sentinels of Dawn will be here any second!
Captain, stay back! It's a trap!==W== They're parading us around to draw you out!
So you set a net.==W== But==W== do you actually believe that you can hold a White Cat when she's fighting for real?
Move, move, move! Firefight at the port! The White Cats are staging a rescue. Box them in and take them all down!
Ugh! I'm hit! Where did that come from?
No sound of gunshots?==W== Defensive formation! Locate that sniper!
We can't see them!==W== They're moving too fast!
Dammit.==W== Someone send a distress signal!==W==
First wave of reinforcements at the port is down.==W== Moving to the next street.
Don't bother waiting. I took out your backup before I even got here.
You did this alone? Th-That's impossible.
I am Narida, Captain of the First Squad and acting troupe leader. Remember the name.==W== Now hand over the keys, and I'll let you live.
That's a win! ♪ Alright everyone, get those shackles off. Your gear is in these crates.==W== Suit up and catch a boat out of Emor. Move!
No, you go ahead. I'll cover you.==W== Tonight, not a single Knight or Sentinel in Emor gets to sleep.
White Cat! This is as far as you go!
Gah?!==W== Where did that come from?!
Nice, Taffett. You still have your edge.==W== Keep it up. I'll draw their fire out in the open, and you keep striking from the shadows. Don't let anyone see your face.
I squeezed a knight for intel. The Sentinels' temporary command post is a hotel in Gold District. Security is light. All our files and rosters are there.
We caused enough chaos in the Ash District to pull their forces here. Let's slip through the waterway and catch them completely off guard.
Burn those files, and you disappear from their records, Taffett. Let's move!

One... As far as we could tell, it was only one person.
Come up with a better lie.==W== We have over a hundred Knights and Sentinels down, and you expect me to believe it was a single enemy?
They're fast asleep. You two should surrender. And by the way, our fighting style gave you the wrong idea. You actually thought White Cats were pushovers.==W==
This is our true strength. Remember it well.==W== You asked for a war, so now you're getting one.

I... I'm okay. But why did you save me?==W== I'm your enemy.

This place is going to burn. Go get some help and carry your friends out of here.
They were all in the command center. They burned up along with the commander.
Taffett, what's wrong? That's so much blood. Did you take the blast protecting me?!
Narida, I'm okay.==W== Now...==W== I can finally ...==W==<size=30> be with ... the kids...</size>==W==

strings.text: You stop wishing, and Hazana agrees to go home. Peace seems close—until fake Scepters of Death appear and the Senate retaliates. To end the chaos for good, you lead the New Star Guild into enemy territory...
==Off==Monolith Calendar Year 997, Trekker Association, Outside Emor
Thanks for your business. How's it treating you?
It's amazing!==B====W== Yesterday I stepped out of a Monolith and ran straight into a pack of bandits...
Normally I'd be helpless, at their mercy.==W== But the second I pulled out the Scepter of Death, they scattered before I could blink.==W==
If I had one complaint, it's the noise...==W== And you have to watch your ammo.==W== By the way, do you sell bullets separately?
We do! A box of fifty is fifty thousand Dorra.
Wait, seriously?==W== The Scepter was only a hundred thousand Dorra. Fifty bullets cost that much?
You've got it backwards, friend. The Scepter's real value is in the bullets.==W== Without ammo, it's nothing but an expensive club.
Fair point...==W== I'll take one hundred rounds.
One hundred rounds,==W== coming up!==W== Thanks for your business <size=53>♪</size>
Yahaha! Five million Dorra today alone.==W== We cleared over a hundred million this week alone. We're on a roll!
Haha! Never thought we'd get this rich hunting the Salvation Committee.==W== Teaming up with the Boss was a good call.
Hazana, Myrsha.==W== We need to talk.
You saw the news. Angie's locked away for life, without parole. Heresy and attempted murder.
Now that Angie and the Salvation Committee are done, we should stop wishing for the Scepters.==W== They're too dangerous and unpredictable. For world peace. For Nova's safety.
I knew you'd bring this up the moment I heard Angie got busted.
But don't get me wrong. The Desert Scorpions couldn't care less about world peace or Nova's safety.
Sure, the Artifact is dangerous.==W== But is an attack from a Scepter of Death any different than an attack from magic?
If there's demand, we supply. We aren't forcing anyone to buy them, let alone use them on each other.
But we respect our friends.==W== You cranked out thousands of these things for us. You said your constitution was unique...
But it's clearly wearing you down...==W== Even if you get to keep your memories, you're physically drained.==W== We Scorpions don't put our friends through that.
That takes a huge weight off my shoulders.==W== Thanks. I appreciate it.
Don't get soft on me, Boss.==W== We know a good thing when we see it. Reliable, brilliant partners with actual miracle powers don't grow on trees.
I am selling off the rest of our stock, though.==W== No objections?
Right. Sitting on a stockpile like that paints a massive target on our backs. Best to clear it out.
And ... that means every Scepter we sell is one we can't replace. Perfect excuse to jack up the prices!==W== Hehe, wonder how much we'll rake in by the end! <size=53>♪</size>
I'm heading back to Philae soon. What's next for you two?
The rest of the Desert Scorpions are still in Mirage. It's been a while, hasn't it?
Yeah. Time we headed back with our earnings.
With Boss Accord backing us, we're legit corporate folks! No more getting lowballed by the big guys.==W== Heading back to help build up our hometown sounds pretty good! <size=53>♪</size>
Life without a Monolith is tough. Why not move to Philae? Or anywhere else?
Haha. Appreciate the offer, Boss,==W== but we're staying put. Doesn't matter how nice a place is. There's nowhere like home.
I think, I made the right call this time.
I never found the desert Monolith, and my true identity is still a mystery.
But after all I've been through, I picked up quite a few titles:

I doubt there's anyone left on Nova who actually believes I'm the legendary Tyrant.

And if I keep going,==W== there's Chitose's ==SEX11==,==W== Fuyuka's Master,==W== Nazuka's absolute most important person (her exact words),==W== Otoha's partner in crime, and more.==B====W== No wonder Noya jokes every time I hop in Loxy:
This ride can't fit that many people!
Time passes.==W== The Desert Scorpions and the White Cat Troupe bury the hatchet==W== and start mining a new crystal diamond vein together.
United Harvest Philae helps the people of Mirage grow valuable desert crops and buys the harvest.==W== With everyone working together, the former Edge of the World is thriving.
Allie moves the Daisy Orphanage back to Mirage.==W== She says the kids from White Cat and the Scorpions prefer the open desert over the skyscrapers of Philae.
With Mirage's population booming, busy parents keep asking Allie to watch their kids.==W== The Daisy Orphanage has basically turned into a daycare.
As for me,==W== I'm buried under company paperwork. I had to rope Mistique into being my personal chauffeur, flying me back and forth between Emor, Philae, and Mirage.
It's been a while==W== since I traveled with the New Star Guild.
Hehe, welcome to the reality of running a business<size=53>♪</size>==W== Not that I've ever been a boss myself★==W== But hey, once you retire, you'll have all the free time in the world.
Stop zoning out and hold tight!==W== We're flying straight to Mirage! ★
Wait!==W== You can't just floor it from the start!==W==<size=50> Waaaaaah—!</size>
==Off==I thought this peaceful routine would go on forever.
==Off==But what I had done finally brought a storm.
W-What?==W== A Trekker from outside the desert shot up the Eureka Bar with a Scepter of Death? And Benito was hit?
Yeah... She got a scratch. Nothing serious.==W== We have the Trekker detained,==W== but we have no idea where that Scepter came from.
Wasn't it one of the ones we sold?
That's the weird part.==W== First of all, it looks completely different. It's weaker than ours, and it has this strange attachment on the barrel. Barely makes a sound when fired.
Boss, I just heard from Albedo. She wants us in Emor. Says it's urgent.
Leaving already, Boss?==W== Stay for dinner with the kids. They've been looking forward to it.
I'm sorry, Allie. Something urgent came up. I have to skip dinner.
If you can't stay, at least take some bread for the road.==W== You have to eat properly no matter how busy you are, you hear me?
I hear you.==W== Do me a favor and tell everyone at the New Star Guild I'll be back soon. Tell them not to worry.
But after hearing the truth from Albedo... I finally understood==RT==the gravity of the situation. It went far deeper than I imagined.
Yes. After you flooded the market with the Scepters of Death, the corporate Senators felt threatened. They immediately formed teams to crack the wishing prayers.
But the success rate of their reverse-engineered prayers was too low, and the toll on the wishers was too high. It never went anywhere.
Then, two months ago, the prison holding Angie was attacked. She escaped in the mass breakout. Since then, a mysterious group has appeared, flooding the black market with new Scepters.
You're saying...==W== Angie rebuilt the Salvation Committee, perfected the prayer, and made the wishes work?
There is more.==W== Willow, take it from here.

Dozens of guilds have gone dark recently. I suspect they were abducted and forced to make wishes. That only covers the ones we know about. We don't track guilds missing for under a month, so the actual number could be much bigger.
Even if you're looking our way, you won't find a thing. We don't touch jobs with zero payoff.
Yeah, this is on you for not watching your prisoners.
Hazana, Myrsha, drop it.==W== I'm the one who started the Scepter mess.==W== This one is on me.
We are not blaming anyone. On the contrary...==W== We invite Boss here today to entrust you with the investigation.
Naturally, Grace Imperium will back you fully.==W== Greyhorn?
She will lead her team in support, with all expenses covered by us.==W== If you need anything else, every resource Grace Imperium has is yours to command.
Greyhorn, are they at it again outside?
Yeah.==W== Two gangs are tearing up the streets with Scepters of Death. No one dares to step outside after dark anymore.
We need to hold out for three more days.==W== We've identified the corporate Senators funding the smuggling ring.==W== They're holding a gathering on Snowish Eve. We'll take them all down at once.
We also found a familiar name on the guest list.==W== Angie. We've been tracking her for a year, and she's going to be there.
Good work, Greyhorn.==W== Where are Hazana and Myrsha?
We fell for a decoy earlier. The Scorpions are split up between Port Goldfinch and Geminia.
Backup from the Dusk Arbiter and Sentinel of Dawn just left Emor. Neither squad will make it in time.
We're short-handed.==W== Can you call in the local Imperial Guard?
I'm sorry.==W== Our casualties this past year have been too severe... The Grand Captain ordered a full withdrawal from the operation.
The Imperial Guard is a company that puts Dorra first.==W== But there are things our knights care about more than money.
You've been crossing the continent to keep the peace.==W== Until every last criminal is brought to justice, I am personally at your command.
It's what the Guard was founded to do. And I need to atone for my mistakes.
Mistakes?==W== I didn't think a by-the-book knight like you ever messed up.
I did.==W== I followed the Grand Captain's orders and helped Angie hunt you down.
Watching you peddle Scepters of Death back then,==RT==I even suspected that you were really the legendary Tyrant. But...
Angie set me straight. She said I didn't understand you, or how this world would end.
At the time, her words made no sense to me.==W== But after working alongside you, I think I finally get it.
You and Angie are the same.==W== Both of you would risk everything for this world, for other people...
... and do things everyone else finds insane. Thankless. Even heretical.
The same, huh.==W== Maybe you're right. I'm doing exactly what she did. The only difference is that we swapped sides.
I know it's too late. But I still wish I'd found another way to stop her, instead of spreading those Scepters...
I kept my friends safe. Mirage even prospered from it. But that came at a price, and everyone else paid it.==W== I'm no different from you, Greyhorn. We're both trying to fix our mistakes.
... Sorry, let's focus.==W== We're completely understaffed right now. Got any tactical ideas?
I wouldn't worry about that. As luck would have it, your friends are already here.
Come on, ==PLAYER_NAME==, don't leave us hanging! You're going to settle this with Angie without us? How could you?
Noya?!==W== Iris and Amber are here too?==W== How did you find this place...?
Easy.==W== We pinpointed the city with the heaviest Scepter trafficking. Noya's gut feeling narrowed the search grid.==W== Amber scouted the rest.
You are the best...==W== But it's not just Angie today.==W== We're up against an entire mob packing Scepters of Death.
We figured.==W== We've been perfecting heavy-duty defensive spells for this exact moment. Even Scepter bullets won't get through.
It'll hurt. But we won't die.
Oh! I almost forgot!==W== We need a tiny favor from you.
You have to keep it a secret from Aunt Allie...==W== I mean, Mom... That we're fighting alongside you today. She cannot find out.
Hey, Allie?==W== I met up with Noya and the others. Don't worry, they're sticking to rear logistics.==W== They're perfectly safe out of harm's way.
Huh? Wait... What was that noise?==W== It sounded like a Scepter of Death firing...
Ah, no, definitely not!==W== We're in Cangwu. The new year is around the corner, those are Loong firecrackers!
Thank goodness...==W== Boss, could I ask you for a favor?
Of course. If it's something I can do, name it.
Thank you.==W== Please ...==W== bring those kids back to me safe and sound.
Boss,==W== they converted the inside of that house up ahead into a massive warehouse.==W== The Senators and Angie are holding their meeting inside.
Got it.==W== Here's the plan. Greyhorn, take your team and hit the front doors to draw their fire.==W== The New Star Guild and I will use the rooftops to flank them.==W==
Is everyone ready?==W==<size=50> Let's move out!</size>
Whoa, ==PLAYER_NAME==, you're way faster on your feet now!
My swordplay leveled up too. I practice that technique you taught me every single day. I'm up to a thousand swings a day now.
This trip was well worth the trouble. To think we'd finally gaze upon Lady Angie in the flesh.
I know, I was an absolute nervous wreck coming here. I thought that dreadful Boss or the Imperial Guard might track us down...==W== But attending this gathering was definitely the right move.
Besides, even if things go south, with Lady Angie running the show, what is there to worry about?
Watch your tongue, madam.==W== The Imperial Guard has recalled its forces. Commander Greyhorn is acting entirely on her own.==W==
Oh? Does the Imperial Guard want a cut of the Scepter trade too?
Hmph. We have zero interest in selling them.==W== We simply want one sample from every new batch to field test our bulletproof armor.
Do we have a deal, Lady Angie?==W== Agree to this, and the Imperial Guard will gladly make things convenient for everyone in this room...
Heh. Let's save the side deals for later. I called you all here to map out our direction for the coming year.
Ahem. First order of business.==W== To set up a proper front company for Scepter sales, we first need a Seal of Grace.
Heh! Now you're talking! I love a guy who gets straight to the point!
Going corporate means moving serious volume. Mr. Colston, can your people keep up with the Trekker supply?
Relax. I can drag in as many Trekkers as you need. Once the wishing wipes their memories, we'll dump them in the labor camps.
Hmph. With a monopoly on Scepters and the Guard's new armor, those peasants won't stand a chance. No more dirty sneak attacks from the rabble.
Once that happens, United Harvest HQ can raise a new army and take back control of United Harvest Philae.
I want to see Matilda on her knees, begging for my forgiveness!
Lady Angie, how are you allocating next quarter's supply?==W== The New Orelian faction can move ten thousand, no, twenty thousand units!
Unbelievable... Who is interrupting us at a time like this? Didn't I order to have this place locked down?
Sorry for the wait! Black Cat Pizza delivery here<size=53>♪</size>!==W== Your ten jumbo pineapple and sausage pizzas have arrived! Better eat up before they get cold!
Pizza? Heh! Hot pizza in this freezing weather? You guys sure know how to host a meeting!
Pineapple and sausage on a pizza?! Ugh, what kind of blasphemous abomination is this?!
<size=50>Imperial Guard!</size>==W== Hands on your heads and get on the ground! Nobody move!
You rely too much on those Scepters! Your backs are wide open!
Damn it, I can't pull it!
Boss, suspects secured.==W== But Angie seems off.
Angie hasn't said a word since the meeting started.
She's not Angie. She's just dressed up like her... And she's completely out of it?!
Heh...==W== Bwahahahaha!==W== You actually thought Angie was calling the shots? That she was the one running our Scepter trade?
You idiots. Brainless trash.==W== I figured out the Scepter's prayer myself! I've finally proven it!==W==<size=50> My research is as good as anyone's!</size>

As for the Angie you were waiting for, we did ask her to join.==W== But she insisted on investigating the Monoliths alone and vanished the day she broke out.==W== Heh. She's probably dead in some Monolith by now. So don't blame us for using her name.
You despicable scum...==W== Do human lives mean nothing to you?
Hehehe... Can you really afford to worry about others right now?
Boss. On the table. A phone. It's on a call.
<color=#3faeae>Lady Gray</color>. Does that name ring a bell, Boss?
You played well in Philae. I admit that.==W== But I only lost because Darcia let blind devotion cloud her judgment.
If she hadn't interfered, there wouldn't be enough of you left to bury.
The Scepter trade.==W== You've been running it this whole time?
Hah. Got it in one.==W== The New Orelian crew broke Angie out hoping she'd take the business. She turned her nose up at it.==W== So I stepped up.
Take a look around you, Boss.
Boss, these crates are packed with dark gray powder. It's the explosive from the Scepter rounds!
They rigged the main gates with explosive arrays. Every exit is completely sealed...==W== We walked right into a trap.
Lady Gray, your investors are still in here! Are you leaving them to die?
You can't spring a trap without bait.
Lady Gray! What is the meaning of this?! You played us too?!
Oh, poor Joseph... Please understand.==W== I wouldn't do this if I had a choice.==W== But rest easy. I will take excellent care of your family.
Boss, we found an emergency hatch! This way, move!
They might have an ambush waiting outside. Watch your backs!
Let me take point. My armor is bulletproof.==W== Even if I catch a few rounds—
Wait. Are... Are these shields? Why are they stacked up here?

param: You stop wishing, and Hazana agrees to go home. Peace seems close—until fake Scepters of Death appear and the Senate retaliates. To end the chaos for good, you lead the New Star Guild into enemy territory...
==Off==Monolith Calendar Year 997, Trekker Association, Outside Emor
Thanks for your business. How's it treating you?
It's amazing!==B====W== Yesterday I stepped out of a Monolith and ran straight into a pack of bandits...
Normally I'd be helpless, at their mercy.==W== But the second I pulled out the Scepter of Death, they scattered before I could blink.==W==
If I had one complaint, it's the noise...==W== And you have to watch your ammo.==W== By the way, do you sell bullets separately?
We do! A box of fifty is fifty thousand Dorra.
Wait, seriously?==W== The Scepter was only a hundred thousand Dorra. Fifty bullets cost that much?
You've got it backwards, friend. The Scepter's real value is in the bullets.==W== Without ammo, it's nothing but an expensive club.
Fair point...==W== I'll take one hundred rounds.
One hundred rounds,==W== coming up!==W== Thanks for your business <size=53>♪</size>
Yahaha! Five million Dorra today alone.==W== We cleared over a hundred million this week alone. We're on a roll!
Haha! Never thought we'd get this rich hunting the Salvation Committee.==W== Teaming up with the Boss was a good call.
Hazana, Myrsha.==W== We need to talk.
You saw the news. Angie's locked away for life, without parole. Heresy and attempted murder.
Now that Angie and the Salvation Committee are done, we should stop wishing for the Scepters.==W== They're too dangerous and unpredictable. For world peace. For Nova's safety.
I knew you'd bring this up the moment I heard Angie got busted.
But don't get me wrong. The Desert Scorpions couldn't care less about world peace or Nova's safety.
Sure, the Artifact is dangerous.==W== But is an attack from a Scepter of Death any different than an attack from magic?
If there's demand, we supply. We aren't forcing anyone to buy them, let alone use them on each other.
But we respect our friends.==W== You cranked out thousands of these things for us. You said your constitution was unique...
But it's clearly wearing you down...==W== Even if you get to keep your memories, you're physically drained.==W== We Scorpions don't put our friends through that.
That takes a huge weight off my shoulders.==W== Thanks. I appreciate it.
Don't get soft on me, Boss.==W== We know a good thing when we see it. Reliable, brilliant partners with actual miracle powers don't grow on trees.
I am selling off the rest of our stock, though.==W== No objections?
Right. Sitting on a stockpile like that paints a massive target on our backs. Best to clear it out.
And ... that means every Scepter we sell is one we can't replace. Perfect excuse to jack up the prices!==W== Hehe, wonder how much we'll rake in by the end! <size=53>♪</size>
I'm heading back to Philae soon. What's next for you two?
The rest of the Desert Scorpions are still in Mirage. It's been a while, hasn't it?
Yeah. Time we headed back with our earnings.
With Boss Accord backing us, we're legit corporate folks! No more getting lowballed by the big guys.==W== Heading back to help build up our hometown sounds pretty good! <size=53>♪</size>
Life without a Monolith is tough. Why not move to Philae? Or anywhere else?
Haha. Appreciate the offer, Boss,==W== but we're staying put. Doesn't matter how nice a place is. There's nowhere like home.
I think, I made the right call this time.
I never found the desert Monolith, and my true identity is still a mystery.
But after all I've been through, I picked up quite a few titles:
