strings.text: You set up defenses throughout the Monolith as the battle grows intense. Though the Committee is powerful, they struggle to ascend. Holding the 45th floor alone, Chitose halts No. 160 while enduring deadly poison.
Weird. Isn't this Monolith supposed to be abandoned? It looks exactly like the ones back in the city.
Monoliths react to people. If one sits empty long enough, it goes barren and strips down to bare rock, like what we saw just now.
But the second people step inside, it wakes up and shifts back into the form we're used to.
I had no idea. You Sentinels of Dawn really know your stuff.
Heh, it's nothing. If you fight Nocturn Eterna in dormant Monoliths far from the Cities every day, you pick things up too.
But Trekkers are the real experts. The Tyrant's forces are full of them, and we're fighting on their turf. Stay sharp.
Understood. I've cast my strongest defensive magic on everyone. We can take four or five hits from any weapon. Even the Tyrant's lackeys can't jump us.
Is this ... fog? Since when does it get foggy in a Monolith?
How ironic…==RT==I died in this Monolith before I ever found an Artifact.==RT==Left to rot... Forgotten...
The air... It just turned ice cold. Is that ...==W== a dead Trekker's ghost?
I gave my life to protect them…==RT==But they had already moved on to someone else...
Whatever, whatever…==RT==This lightless place makes a fine tomb…==RT==No one in this world cares about me anyway...
Are you kidding me?! Ghosts aren't real!==RT==It must be one of the Tyrant's lackeys playing tricks!
B-But look! What are all those twisted shadows behind it?!
One, two, three...==W== About twenty of them? Heh. I get it. Cheap illusion.
The Tyrant doesn't even have that many fighters! They're just stalling. Blow the fog away!
Hehe! You're the ones who attacked first!
Look! Those shadows are ... Stellaroids! And they're charging right at us!
Great job, Kaede! You dragged over quite the swarm.
It's Petal Bloom's signature move. Group the Stellaroids together, then let Nazuka wipe them out.
Except today, our targets aren't the Stellaroids. It's these self-righteous Salvation Committee jerks.
Honestly, what a bunch of idiots. Do they really not know Stellaroids aggro onto whoever casts magic first?
True. But you also burned through all your defensive magic.
You dared to hurt the person most important to me.==W== Biting winter winds, bury them in this Monolith!
A penguin? Is that a new breed of Stellaroid?
No, I think it's a mascot for a Monolith convenience store. Trying to drum up business.
A convenience store? In a place crawling with Stellaroids?
Yeah, they act as safe zones. You can buy magic-boosting drinks here while climbing.
Let's check it out. The Tyrant and ==SEX3== lackeys got here way before us. They have a massive head start on gathering power, so we need this store to close the gap.
Welcome. What can I get for you today?
Pool the Monolith Coins we found. We should have enough for one magic-boosting drink each.
Well, that went well. Drink up, everyone. Get your boost and let's keep climbing.
Three hundred of us entered this Monolith. If even one squad catches up to the Tyrant, we win.
Tastes a bit off. Were these drinks always this thick?
Hey, snap out of it! Dammit, my eyes are heavy too... The drinks are spiked...
I have to warn the others. The elevator... Fall back to the ground floor...
That's a wrap. Third squad down. Your plan works like a charm, Otoha. They see a clerk and just drop their guard.
Only because you make such a convincing Sherlock. A cute little penguin puts everyone at ease. Lugging this suit all the way from Philae paid off.
Plus, we still need your bat for anyone who fights off the sleeping potion.
My bat never fails. One swing knocks them out cold. No way are we letting these guys catch up to Boss.
Ah, here comes another batch. Back into character~
Descend,==W== World-Ending Light!==W== The great Chaton will pin them in the elevator!
Hold still and be baptized by the dark power!
Dammit, their firepower is too heavy! We can't even clear the doors! Are these magic bullets buffed by a Monolith blessing?!
Hold the line! Her magic isn't infinite. We push the second she swaps her Neo Solution canister!
This punch is for my Master!
Whoa, that giant gauntlet shot out like a rocket! So cool! You look all soft and delicate, but your dark power is off the charts!
N-No, it's not dark power! It's the Monolith blessing I picked based on Iris's notes... I never knew it could hit so hard!
We hold here. As long as we keep the high ground, our crossfire locks down the elevator. No matter how many Committee members they send, they're just target practice.
One slipped through the net. Did your squad shield you?
Captain Gunhild... This is the last of ... my magic!
Cough, cough... Heavy close-range blast. Are you two alright?
I-I'm fine. Just a few scrapes.
The great Chaton only suffered a singed lock of hair! Flawlessly dodged the rest! Shame, though... I almost had a full combo.
You're quick, I'll give you that. But I already won. Once Piercer tags you, you can never escape its lock-on.
Let's see.==W== The White Cat Captain with the shotgun is behind the cabinet.==W== The sniper is behind the potted plant.
Hey, hey! She's cheating! She has wallhacks!
It's not cheating, you ignorant alley cats. This is a relic bestowed upon me by Lady Angie.
The omniscient God of Grace blesses me. Finding your little hiding spots is child's play!
You pinned my squad long enough. Now it's my turn.
Chaton, Boss was right. Gunhild's cannon really does have this absurd ability.==W== I didn't believe it at first, but I have to admit... ==SEX1== really can see the future.
Then let's use Boss's strategy and take down this cheater!
Keep running! Even if you flee to another floor, my Piercer locks on right through the floorboards.
Huh? Only two White Cats in my sights? Where did that white-haired Trekker go? Piercer should be tracking her.
If she isn't hiding around here, the only place left is ...==W== the ceiling!
Surrender! You're out of options. The Tyrant is not worth your loyalty!
You're the one out of options.
Fuyuka! Use the formation your Master taught you!
Going for close combat? Piercer packs a heavy punch. And even at this range, my lock-on works!
Yes. But you can't aim that barrel in every direction at once.
Despicable... Attacking from three angles at once.
Lady Angie... ==W==This is as far ... as I go.
(What the hell is going on with this Monolith? I hit the Tyrant's lackeys every few floors. It's exactly like...)
(... that legendary Monolith of the Tyrant the heroes had to climb.)
(I've abused my time stop to get this far. Just five more floors until I catch the Tyrant.)
(I have to pave the way for Lady Angie. At any cost.)
You must be the arbiter who stops time by harming herself.
I am Chitose. So long as I stand here, your filthy gaze shall never cross my blade, let alone touch the hem of my ==SEX11=='s garments.
(Another one?==W== The Trekker with the blade. She already knows how my magic works.==W== Heh, the Committee definitely has a mole.)
(Doesn't matter. I've been slashing myself this entire climb. I've stockpiled plenty of fear.)
Oh God of Grace, if you truly exist... Please stop the clock! Make it stop!
Now then, elegant Trekker. You're infected with my Scar. Let's see how long you last.
The botanical venom on my dagger plunges its victims into the deepest, darkest terror imaginable.==W== No escape. They just drown in their own fear.
Hahaha... It's working!==W== Let me see that delicate, pretty face of yours twist and break in pure terror! I want to see how beautiful you look when you snap!
How noisy. I have no desire to listen to such foul drivel.
H-How is this possible?! You're poisoned!
I am the blade of my ==SEX11==. As long as my ==SEX11== resides in my heart, I fear absolutely nothing!
You thought a mundane poison could corrode my spirit? Utterly foolish.

<size=45>My ==SEX11==...==P==</size>==RT==<size=45>By now, you must have reached that room. My heart is at peace.==P==</size>==RT==<size=45>Please, allow me to offer this final prayer for your journey ahead...

strings.text: You and Angie agree to negotiate in two hours, buying time for both sides to regroup and prepare for battle. Firenze sends word: reinforcements will arrive within three days, so you only need to hold out for two.
I beg your forgiveness, my ==SEX11==. A wall of knights held me back, and I failed to stop the arbiter who struck at you. I bear the blame entirely.
Don't blame yourselves. The Committee had us severely outmanned. You both did everything you could.

Heh! The great Chaton returns in triumph! Those Committee goons kept scurrying around like rats,==W== but they didn't stand a chance against my surging dark power and flawless beats.==W== Not a single one crossed my line!
Reel it in, Chaton. Arrogance leads to downfall!
Boss, the Committee's warding magic is thick. We fought them off, but hardly left a scratch. The second they reform their ranks, they're coming right for us again.
Sitting here makes us easy targets. We need to move. Chaton, get back out there and scout the mineshafts.
Understood! The great Chaton is on her way!
Hold on. There's no rush. The Committee isn't attacking anytime soon.
Angie and I just agreed to negotiate in two hours. We have a ceasefire until then.
Negotiate? Boss, don't do it.==W== You can't trust Angie or her Committee for a second.
I must agree. She lured you to her quarters once before, my ==SEX11==, only to spring a lethal trap. This is the exact same ploy. Do not fall for it.
We've got the desert and the old mineshafts right outside! We can find a way to slip away. There's zero reason to parley with her.
I hear you. But the only reason she even offered a truce is that you all fought her to a standstill.
Before you arrived, Minova checked in. She, Otoha, and Kaede slipped into the dunes in disguise and hit the Committee's artillery camp.
Mistique also used a fake interview to feed me some intel: the Committee split their raid into three troops.
Three troops... Guess that tin can leads one.
And... The arbiter who made me see all those awful illusions... That's two.
Which makes the artillery camp out on the dunes the third.
When Angie asked for this talk, all three of her forces were compromised. Stuck in the mines, pinned down by you, or blindsided by Minova.
Makes sense. Her board was completely clear. She just needed time to piece her formations back together. The negotiation is a stall.
Then I am lost, my ==SEX11==. If you have already laid bare her scheme, why would you ever...
Because we need that time far more than she does.

Look at our situation back then. Fuyuka, Nazuna, and Allie had just barely shaken off No. 160's magic. I had no idea if the rest of you were still standing,==W== and the Daisy Orphanage was sitting right in the crossfire.
Taking her deal was my way of stalling, too.
But ... that's still too dangerous. Let's just run the clock and make a break for it! Boss, I can carry you and fly us straight out of Mirage!
Two hours won't cut it. Kasimira, how long does it take to evacuate the White Cats and empty the city of civilians?
We're out of capacity. Fifty White Cats shepherding over a thousand people is too much of an undertaking.
Not to mention the sheer amount of supplies we'd need for a desert march. I figure the earliest they'll be ready is tonight.
Allie is in the same boat. She and Benito are at the orphanage preparing to leave the city with the kids. But in two hours, they won't get far enough.
So, I'll try to stall them at the negotiation table and buy us some time.
It's Firenze. She must have an update on the Dusk Arbiter.
Good afternoon, Boss. I've been holding off on a direct line. I didn't want the Salvation Committee tapping our Heartlink.
But it's the 18th now. Nazuka's team must have found you. If you're picking up, you must already know about the raid and have it under control.
Not exactly under control, but it doesn't matter anymore. We've already clashed with them here in Mirage. If they're listening in, let them.
Heh. Fair enough. Judging by your tone, the Committee didn't walk all over you.
We barely held the line. They outmatched us in numbers, gear, and magic. Things are grim.==W== What's your status?
I diverted the Imperial Guard's grain convoy and hired some extra muscle out of Emor. Roughly two hundred fighters in total.==W== We'll hit Mirage in three days.
The Dusk Arbiter also threw in a few arbiters at the last minute.==W== Their leader looks formidable.
And Albedo is rallying any Sentinels of Dawn who don't believe you'll destroy the world.==W== They're marching for the desert, about a day behind us.
The point is, Boss, just hold the line for three days. After that, the Committee won't be able to touch you.
Got it. I'm counting on you. Stay safe out there.

You heard her. We just need to hold out for three days. Actually, make that two. Whether the Committee can listen in on our talks or not, their scouts are gonna spot Firenze's backup long before they get here.
Unless they're eager to wage war against United Harvest Philae, the Imperial Guard, the Dusk Arbiter, and the Sentinel of Dawn all at once, they'll pack up and leave early.
Alright, let's get to work. Nazuna, Fuyuka, head to the orphanage and help Allie move the kids.
You got it! Come on, Fuyuka, let's go.
Kasimira, I'm trusting you to find us a clear escape route through the mineshafts and to organize the civilian evacuation.
Mirage is home to the White Cats now.==W== We'll give it everything we've got.
Nazuka, you're the only one here who can take to the skies. Keep an eye on the Committee's movements.
Chitose, lock down the streets around Eureka Bar and Daisy Orphanage. Don't let anyone slip past.
Wait a minute... Chitose, where are Noya and the others? Weren't they with you?
We split up during the fight. They broke off to intercept more groups of enemies.
Put your mind at ease, my ==SEX11==. They are all highly capable. They will be fine.
Boss, I'm back!==W== We sent those Committee goons running for the hills!
Huh? Where did everybody go? Did we take too long getting back?
Noya, Iris, Amber! Where have you been? I was starting to panic.
Phew, Chitose called it. They're okay...==W== Wait,==W== is Noya...?
Hehe, we just plowed straight through their lines, so we had to take the scenic route back! But never mind that! We bumped into someone on the way and scored some insanely important intel!
Noya, forget the intel.==W== You're bleeding everywhere! What happened?!
<size=52>Wah!==W== Mom, easy! Go easy on me! Ow, ow, ow!</size>
Hold still. A gash this deep has to be cleaned and stitched properly.==W== Iris,==W== hand me the absorbable sutures.
You got extremely lucky. That magic bullet only sliced your skin. Bones and organs are fine.==W== I've stitched up the muscle layer, now let's seal the outside.==W== Amber,==W== skin adhesive.
What's that? It looks like some glue wished out of the Monolith.
It's from our basement stash. You can't wish this one out of the Monolith, no matter how hard you try. It seals the skin up tight without leaving a scar.
Boss, give me a hand. Pinch the wound closed so I can glue it.
Haha, that tickles! The spot you're pressing really tickles, ==PLAYER_NAME==...==W== Sss!==W== Ouch, I pulled the wound! Ow, ow.
Oh, so you do feel pain.==W== You absolute fool. Three of you charging an entire formation... Were you thinking at all?
O-Of course I was! At that moment, I was thinking...==W== Iris, what was I thinking again?
Well, Mom. We don't have the sheer power of Nazuka or Chitose. We can't just wipe out enemies instantly.
And unlike the White Cats, we can't just slip away and keep our distance.
But our teamwork is perfect.==W== No words. No signals. Just three of us moving as one.
Yeah, exactly! So charging in and fighting like crazy was the best way to stall them! Yep, that was my plan all along.
Besides, it's just a scratch!==W== It doesn't even hurt anymore. Watch, I can get up right now...
Sit. You are staying in this bed for thirty minutes. No moving. Or that wound will tear right back open.
What? Half an hour of no moving?!
And keep it dry. No heavy exercise for two days. Do not pick at the glue. And for a full week, absolutely no stretching that area.
Wait, so I can't fight for a week?! Mom, you know how tough I am! I fell off the Waterway as a kid and came out fine. A normal person might need a week to heal, but I'll be fine by tomorrow!
That's because you fell straight into the pond!==W== And Iris used magic to break your fall!
Do you know? A fraction deeper and you'd have had massive internal bleeding!==W== Mirage has no doctors. No hospitals. We could have lost you!
Eek! Mom, please don't be mad. I'll stay put, I swear.==W== B-But I really do have some crucial intel to share.
Just listen to Mom and rest, Noya. Amber and I will share Laru's intel. Boss already guessed most of it anyway. We just need to go over the combat data for those three Company Commanders.
I saved it on my phone. Sending over Heartlink now.
Phew. I need to check on the kids. We can't leave everything to Nazuka. Boss, keep an eye on Noya for me.
==PLAYER_NAME== is watching me? But ... ==PLAYER_NAME== has actual work to do.
Not at all. My schedule is wide open.
Because other than me, ==PLAYER_NAME== is the only one who can keep you in line.
Well, they're gone. Seriously though, is babysitting me for half an hour ruining your plans?
Nope. Everyone knows their assignments. I'd just be standing around anyway.
Mirage is surrounded. It's looking incredibly bleak. But when things get this dark, I have to stay calm and look on the bright side. You taught me that, Noya.
Plus, my friend got hurt. Sitting here with her is pretty important to me. But if you're really worried about delaying our battle prep, let's hear this intel.
Me? Honestly, Amber's notes are probably way more accurate...
Maybe. But your instincts are incredibly sharp. I want to hear your gut read on all this.
My gut read... O-Okay! Take a look at this.
What are these? Empty fry boxes?
Yeah. So, we totally smashed right through the Salvation Committee's line, but then some sniper ambushed us out of nowhere.
Luckily, they only fired twice before stopping.
Those shots came from the dunes miles outside Mirage. Of course you couldn't spot them.
They only fired twice because Minova and Kaede snuck into the enemy camp in disguise. They tried to jump Angie and failed, but they totally distracted the sniper.
Whoa, from that far out?==W== Oh, then I know exactly who it is! Hang on, let me look... Here, inside this box, it says...

Gunhild. Sentinel of Dawn gunner. Wields the ultra-long-range precision magic cannon, Piercer. Rumor says if Piercer hits you once, it remembers you. Next time, it just auto-aims and fires on its own.
It also engulfs other magic to temporarily boost its own damage. The more magic it swallows, the deadlier the shell... But the longer it takes to charge.
Fiercely loyal, respects authority, no bad habits. Top-tier marksmanship. Weakness: incredibly proud of her shooting, and easily irritated.
I get it! We'll just find a crack shot to provoke her, and she won't be able to aim straight!
This fry box is an absolute goldmine. How did you even get this?
It's nuts. You won't even believe me. It happened right after we ducked into the backstreets to dodge the sniper...
Where we ran into a total fry freak!

Look at our situation back then. Fuyuka, Nazuna, and Allie had just barely shaken off No. 160's magic. I had no idea if the rest of you were still standing,==W== and the Daisy Orphanage was sitting right in the crossfire.
Taking her deal was my way of stalling, too.
But ... that's still too dangerous. Let's just run the clock and make a break for it! Boss, I can carry you and fly us straight out of Mirage!
Two hours won't cut it. Kasimira, how long does it take to evacuate the White Cats and empty the city of civilians?
We're out of capacity. Fifty White Cats shepherding over a thousand people is too much of an undertaking.
Not to mention the sheer amount of supplies we'd need for a desert march. I figure the earliest they'll be ready is tonight.
Allie is in the same boat. She and Benito are at the orphanage preparing to leave the city with the kids. But in two hours, they won't get far enough.
So, I'll try to stall them at the negotiation table and buy us some time.
It's Firenze. She must have an update on the Dusk Arbiter.
Good afternoon, Boss. I've been holding off on a direct line. I didn't want the Salvation Committee tapping our Heartlink.
But it's the 18th now. Nazuka's team must have found you. If you're picking up, you must already know about the raid and have it under control.
Not exactly under control, but it doesn't matter anymore. We've already clashed with them here in Mirage. If they're listening in, let them.
Heh. Fair enough. Judging by your tone, the Committee didn't walk all over you.
We barely held the line. They outmatched us in numbers, gear, and magic. Things are grim.==W== What's your status?
I diverted the Imperial Guard's grain convoy and hired some extra muscle out of Emor. Roughly two hundred fighters in total.==W== We'll hit Mirage in three days.
The Dusk Arbiter also threw in a few arbiters at the last minute.==W== Their leader looks formidable.
And Albedo is rallying any Sentinels of Dawn who don't believe you'll destroy the world.==W== They're marching for the desert, about a day behind us.
The point is, Boss, just hold the line for three days. After that, the Committee won't be able to touch you.
Got it. I'm counting on you. Stay safe out there.

You heard her. We just need to hold out for three days. Actually, make that two. Whether the Committee can listen in on our talks or not, their scouts are gonna spot Firenze's backup long before they get here.
Unless they're eager to wage war against United Harvest Philae, the Imperial Guard, the Dusk Arbiter, and the Sentinel of Dawn all at once, they'll pack up and leave early.
Alright, let's get to work. Nazuna, Fuyuka, head to the orphanage and help Allie move the kids.
You got it! Come on, Fuyuka, let's go.
Kasimira, I'm trusting you to find us a clear escape route through the mineshafts and to organize the civilian evacuation.
Mirage is home to the White Cats now.==W== We'll give it everything we've got.
Nazuka, you're the only one here who can take to the skies. Keep an eye on the Committee's movements.
Chitose, lock down the streets around Eureka Bar and Daisy Orphanage. Don't let anyone slip past.
Wait a minute... Chitose, where are Noya and the others? Weren't they with you?
We split up during the fight. They broke off to intercept more groups of enemies.
Put your mind at ease, my ==SEX11==. They are all highly capable. They will be fine.
Boss, I'm back!==W== We sent those Committee goons running for the hills!
Huh? Where did everybody go? Did we take too long getting back?
Noya, Iris, Amber! Where have you been? I was starting to panic.
Phew, Chitose called it. They're okay...==W== Wait,==W== is Noya...?
Hehe, we just plowed straight through their lines, so we had to take the scenic route back! But never mind that! We bumped into someone on the way and scored some insanely important intel!
Noya, forget the intel.==W== You're bleeding everywhere! What happened?!
<size=52>Wah!==W== Mom, easy! Go easy on me! Ow, ow, ow!</size>
Hold still. A gash this deep has to be cleaned and stitched properly.==W== Iris,==W== hand me the absorbable sutures.
You got extremely lucky. That magic bullet only sliced your skin. Bones and organs are fine.==W== I've stitched up the muscle layer, now let's seal the outside.==W== Amber,==W== skin adhesive.
What's that? It looks like some glue wished out of the Monolith.
It's from our basement stash. You can't wish this one out of the Monolith, no matter how hard you try. It seals the skin up tight without leaving a scar.
Boss, give me a hand. Pinch the wound closed so I can glue it.
Haha, that tickles! The spot you're pressing really tickles, ==PLAYER_NAME==...==W== Sss!==W== Ouch, I pulled the wound! Ow, ow.
Oh, so you do feel pain.==W== You absolute fool. Three of you charging an entire formation... Were you thinking at all?
O-Of course I was! At that moment, I was thinking...==W== Iris, what was I thinking again?
Well, Mom. We don't have the sheer power of Nazuka or Chitose. We can't just wipe out enemies instantly.
And unlike the White Cats, we can't just slip away and keep our distance.
But our teamwork is perfect.==W== No words. No signals. Just three of us moving as one.
Yeah, exactly! So charging in and fighting like crazy was the best way to stall them! Yep, that was my plan all along.
Besides, it's just a scratch!==W== It doesn't even hurt anymore. Watch, I can get up right now...
Sit. You are staying in this bed for thirty minutes. No moving. Or that wound will tear right back open.
What? Half an hour of no moving?!
And keep it dry. No heavy exercise for two days. Do not pick at the glue. And for a full week, absolutely no stretching that area.
Wait, so I can't fight for a week?! Mom, you know how tough I am! I fell off the Waterway as a kid and came out fine. A normal person might need a week to heal, but I'll be fine by tomorrow!
That's because you fell straight into the pond!==W== And Iris used magic to break your fall!
Do you know? A fraction deeper and you'd have had massive internal bleeding!==W== Mirage has no doctors. No hospitals. We could have lost you!
Eek! Mom, please don't be mad. I'll stay put, I swear.==W== B-But I really do have some crucial intel to share.
Just listen to Mom and rest, Noya. Amber and I will share Laru's intel. Boss already guessed most of it anyway. We just need to go over the combat data for those three Company Commanders.
I saved it on my phone. Sending over Heartlink now.
Phew. I need to check on the kids. We can't leave everything to Nazuka. Boss, keep an eye on Noya for me.
==PLAYER_NAME== is watching me? But ... ==PLAYER_NAME== has actual work to do.
Not at all. My schedule is wide open.
Because other than me, ==PLAYER_NAME== is the only one who can keep you in line.
Well, they're gone. Seriously though, is babysitting me for half an hour ruining your plans?
Nope. Everyone knows their assignments. I'd just be standing around anyway.
Mirage is surrounded. It's looking incredibly bleak. But when things get this dark, I have to stay calm and look on the bright side. You taught me that, Noya.
Plus, my friend got hurt. Sitting here with her is pretty important to me. But if you're really worried about delaying our battle prep, let's hear this intel.
Me? Honestly, Amber's notes are probably way more accurate...
Maybe. But your instincts are incredibly sharp. I want to hear your gut read on all this.
My gut read... O-Okay! Take a look at this.
What are these? Empty fry boxes?
Yeah. So, we totally smashed right through the Salvation Committee's line, but then some sniper ambushed us out of nowhere.
Luckily, they only fired twice before stopping.
Those shots came from the dunes miles outside Mirage. Of course you couldn't spot them.
They only fired twice because Minova and Kaede snuck into the enemy camp in disguise. They tried to jump Angie and failed, but they totally distracted the sniper.
Whoa, from that far out?==W== Oh, then I know exactly who it is! Hang on, let me look... Here, inside this box, it says...

Gunhild. Sentinel of Dawn gunner. Wields the ultra-long-range precision magic cannon, Piercer. Rumor says if Piercer hits you once, it remembers you. Next time, it just auto-aims and fires on its own.
It also engulfs other magic to temporarily boost its own damage. The more magic it swallows, the deadlier the shell... But the longer it takes to charge.
Fiercely loyal, respects authority, no bad habits. Top-tier marksmanship. Weakness: incredibly proud of her shooting, and easily irritated.
I get it! We'll just find a crack shot to provoke her, and she won't be able to aim straight!
This fry box is an absolute goldmine. How did you even get this?
It's nuts. You won't even believe me. It happened right after we ducked into the backstreets to dodge the sniper...
Where we ran into a total fry freak!

strings.text: Angie's terms for peace remain unchanged: your life. Her deductions hit dangerously close to the truth of the Tyrant Development System. Though shaken, you still give Fuyuka the signal to spring the trap...
Just one guard. I admit, I'm a bit surprised.
Let's be real, Angie. You have no one left to send.
We have 160. Gunhild is tied down at the artillery. Greyhorn is the only backup you could scrape together.
Greyhorn is an honorable knight. She wouldn't stoop to a sneak attack.==W== And as for you...
Your Scepter of Death stands no chance against Chitose's blade.
So having Chitose with me is more than enough. The rest of my team has better things to do.
Oh my. Am I really nothing but a backstabbing coward to you?
Aren't you? You invited me to a hotel just to murder me with an Artifact I wished into existence.
Heh. I never denied being despicable. I'll do whatever it takes to save this world.
But sneak attacks are hardly my only tactic.
Enough talk. The fighting hasn't caused too much damage yet, and nobody has died.
Angie, order the Salvation Committee to stand down. I'll guarantee your safety, ensure a fair trial, and even plead your case.
Are those your terms? How merciful, considering we are trying to kill you.
But ...==W== where is all this confidence coming from?
We just steamrolled your Second Company in a head-on fight. And we captured 160.
Your companions are strong, and your tactics are sharp. But wars are won on logistics, not individual heroism.
Greyhorn. Give ==SEX4== the casualty report for the Second Company.
Zero fatalities. Forty minor injuries, ten severe. Aside from the critical cases, the rest can return to duty after a brief rest.
(Just like Nazuka said. The Committee has bottomless magic reserves. They're spamming defensive magic like it's free.)
(We tore right through their entire unit, but barely made a dent in their actual numbers.)
Your flawless assault only cost me ten soldiers. And I still have two completely untouched companies waiting in the wings.
You might pull off a few more beautiful victories. But how long will the Grace in your Soul Stones actually last?
We have an overwhelming advantage in both numbers and supplies.
You only called this meeting to pressure me. Riding the momentum of your recent win, hoping I'd panic and cave to your demands.
But you don't understand the Salvation Committee at all. Our only goal is to save the world. No matter how the battle turns, we will never accept your terms.
(She saw right through me. I really did want to put the pressure on her.)
(Changing the outcome for Noya and the Second Company means I can't predict what happens next. If the battle continues, the Committee definitely has the edge.)
(Then again, I never expected a few cheap words to fool her, let alone convince her army to surrender.)
(This whole conversation is just a stall. It gives the others time to get into position. I need to crush the Committee now, while my memories of the last loop are still useful.)
Well? Nothing to say?==W== I know you're waiting on Firenze and the Dusk Arbiters. They'll be here in about two days.
Looks like Angie has her own intel on Firenze and the Arbiters, even without my Heartlink calls.
But using this negotiation to stall for time only exposes your weakness.
The Salvation Committee just needs to keep up a relentless assault. Twenty-four hours is more than enough to take Mirage. Time is not on your side, Tyrant.
Then why aren't you attacking right now? When it comes down to it, you're using this negotiation to buy time to regroup too, aren't you?
We both know exactly where the other stands. Let's drop the act.
I'm just curious. Even if I really am the legendary Tyrant, what makes you so sure the Tyrant will destroy the world? Is it all based on that Book of Grace Prophecies?
Asking that proves you've read the diary in the White Cat's secret room.==W== You've accepted that you are the Tyrant.
You're right. We both need a little more time. So I'll share something the diary left out.
Tyrant,==W== do you know the basic principles behind Monolith wishes?
The wisher sacrifices their memories in exchange for an Artifact.
Exactly. Novians want the convenience of Artifacts, and the Monolith demands their vivid memories.
But I hear your companions... Or rather, the employees of the Boss Accord ... haven't lost any memories in quite some time.
Memories are also a form of information. Vita will replicate memories the Monolith demands during your wish-making, then hand over those copies while you keep your originals.
Can ...==W== it really work like that?
Tricking the Monolith...==W== No, technically we're not tricking it. The Monolith does get the memories, even if they're copies. Info is info, and a copy works just as well as the real thing.
That's ...==W== a feature created by the Tyrant Development System combining with the chess piece's authority. It feeds the Monolith copied memories during a wish.
To an outsider, it definitely looks like Boss Accord employees can wish without losing their memories.
"The arrogant Tyrant blinded the defenseless gods with false vows,==RT==stealing away their precious relics."
"From then on, the eternal tower began to decay,==RT==and the very foundations of the world began to shake."
Your actions mirror the Book of Grace Prophecies exactly. I believe that answers your question.
That system feature is going to destroy the world? How is that even possible...
Ever since I read that diary in the White Cat's secret room, I've been trying to prove I'm not the Tyrant. But the harder I try to escape this doomsday prophecy, the closer I get to fulfilling it.
Angie couldn't possibly know about the Tyrant Development System.==W== And she has no reason to lie to me right now. If she made that up, I could easily check the book myself.
No, no, no. I can't let her get into my head.
This woman in front of me is just trying to mess with my head.
Heh. Watching your expressions change is quite entertaining, Tyrant.
It's rare we get to negotiate like this. Allow me to present my terms.
Take this Scepter of Death and end your own life. Sacrifice yourself to save the world.
Do that, and I will guarantee the safety and freedom of your companions and the people of Mirage.
My ==SEX11==, you needn't listen to such absurdity. I should have cut this woman down at the Monolith in Philae.
Don't be so hasty. I know it's a difficult proposal to accept, so I will add an extra condition.
Your companions may join the Salvation Committee and stay by my side. If, after observing my actions, they decide I am not actually saving the world, they may kill me at any time.
Even if they spare me for now, in four years, when the world is truly safe from destruction, I will ask them to take my life as recompense for yours.
In other words, no matter what happens, I will pay for your life with my own. If you still doubt me, your companions can bind me with a magical contract. An unbreakable one.
How dare you compare my ==SEX11=='s noble life to a lowly ant like yourself?
She's offering the exact same terms as last time. I can tell that she definitely isn't killing me out of personal desire.
I'd love to squeeze more intel out of her, but time's up. I'll interrogate her properly once we catch her.
About your terms...==W== I need to contact my companions and see what they think.
Tyrant, you continue to surprise me. Are you truly willing to sacrifice yourself for the world?
Master! I'm right where you told me to be. I'm completely ready!
Angie suggested I take my own life with a Scepter of Death to save the world. If I do, she'll guarantee everyone's safety and freedom, and then forfeit her own life in four years.
What do you think of those terms, Fuyuka?
Master, what are you saying?!<size=45> No! <size=50>Absolutely, <size=55>unconditionally <size=60>NO!!!!
Wh-What's going on?! We haven't even fired yet, and the ground's caving in! The First Company hasn't even reached the mines yet, have they?!
What about them?! And what happened to Lady Angie?!
They're never getting to the Boss!
Ugh! When did you sneak up here? And disguised as one of us...
Ignore me! Hurry, launch your magic at Lady Angie's coordinates! That's a direct order!
Willing to sacrifice your own leader's life just to kill Boss? I admire that kind of dedication.
But I made a promise to ==SEX4==. I won't let ==SEX4== get hurt. Drop your staffs, you Salvation Committee lunatics!
Ignore the wounded! There're only two of them! Aim! Aim!
The dusk is looking quite bright all of a sudden,==RT==because a gentle rain is starting to fall—
Gah, where did all this sand come from?! I can't see a thing!
Let this rain of sand bury you! I'm not giving you the chance to aim at Boss!
Outside the city of Mirage,==RT==the swirling sand transforms into a torrential downpour,==RT==falling mercilessly upon the high dunes.

strings.text: You and the New Star have returned to the 50th floor, the place where it all began. As you reenact the prayer from long ago, the massive Stellaroid appears again. This time, it seems to recognize you...
Phew... Talk about a blast from the past. We actually made it back here.
Thinking back... How did the three of us manage to lug a Wishing Box that huge down fifty floors?
We ran on Iris's terrifying obsession with Artifacts.
Haha! When we cracked it open and saw ==PLAYER_NAME==, Iris thought ==SEX== was a humanoid Artifact. ==SEX1== was patting ==SEX4== down trying to find a power switch!
H-Hey, keep it down! We were out of Dorra for food back then!
Honestly, finding ==PLAYER_NAME== in there was way better than finding an Artifact. If we hadn't met ==SEX4==, Feagin would've eaten us alive when we got back to Emor.
Yeah. It feels like a dream. After all those adventures, here we are... Right back where it all began.
And facing another massive crisis, too!
But hey, if we made it back here, it means we can beat this. And when we set off again, we'll go even further.
Under the cover of our allies, the New Star Guild and I reach the top floor of the Desert Monolith in just over two hours.
Aside from the unique top floor, every level in a Monolith is a tangled web of nearly identical parallel floors.
Inside the Monolith, Floor 30 isn't a fixed location. It simply means a climber has reached the thirtieth floor's trial.
When the elevator doors open, there's no guarantee it's the same Floor 30 you saw last time. Two guilds entering back-to-back could climb all the way to the top without ever crossing paths.
We build our entire strategy against the Salvation Committee around this exact mechanic.
The Monolith's elevators only hold ten people at a time, naturally funneling the enemy into isolated squads that can't support each other.
By entering first and securing the right blessings, we use our advantage in power and terrain to ambush them.
Boss, the interceptions on each floor are going as planned. Iris's Monolith Blessing Combo Guide is a lifesaver. Syncing our setups to her strategies gave our magic and strength a massive boost.
We engaged over two hundred Committee members, crushed about a hundred and fifty, and the rest retreated outside. Only Fuyuka, Chaton, and Chitose took some minor hits, but nothing serious.
Great work. So there are under a hundred enemies left inside?
Yes, but they're the elites. And we still haven't caught any sign of Angie or Greyhorn.
Our spare Soul Stones are tapped out. Everyone's running on fumes.
No good. Theirs are rigged with magical seals. Cracking them would take way too long.
Understood. You've all done an incredible job. Let's move to Phase Two. You fall back, exit the Monolith, and resupply. Leave distracting the Committee to us.
Boss, what about the rest? Do we go on the offensive?
One swing of my sword shoots wind blades in eight directions now! The three of us can easily take on ten of them!
It won't be that easy. Angie and Greyhorn are still missing, and Captain Greyhorn is formidable. Dodging Nazuka's teams might not just be luck. They might be using a specific climbing technique.
We should play it safe. Stick to the plan and use the Monolith's terrain to outmaneuver them. We head to Floor 51: the Boss's Domain.
Ugh... Do we really have to go there?!==W== What if... What if that terrifying Stellaroid is still waiting for us?
Even if it is, we'll be fine. You said there's only one elevator up there, and the Stellaroid didn't attack until you stepped out of it.
Yeah. It only showed up when we tried to open the Wishing Box. Maybe it's just guarding it.
That's all we need. If we don't touch the Wishing Box, the Boss's Domain becomes a safe house that only we control.
We pop out to hit Angie. But she can't hit us.
Exactly. Even if Angie knows how to repeat history, it won't matter. With only one elevator in the Boss's Domain, choking them out will be effortless.
Nazuka's team keeps their blessings even outside the Monolith. We just hold the line until they resupply and return. Then, the Salvation Committee is completely out of options.
Let's head up and see if that giant Stellaroid is still around. We'll iron out the details after.
O God of Grace, please…==RT==Please let us find an absurdly huge Wishing Box!
Look! The elevator lights changed! We did it!
We're here, ==PLAYER_NAME==. Nobody move yet. Let me take a peek.
I recall... The giant Stellaroid threw a fit when we took the Wishing Box, and it wrecked the floor, right?
And we dumped the Wishing Box out in the desert, right?
Obviously. Loxy couldn't tow something that heavy.
<size=52>Then why ... is the Wishing Box sitting right in the middle of the Boss's Domain again?! And the floor is fixed?!</size>
Is this where ... the New Star Guild found me?
A pitch-black Wishing Box sits dead center in the Boss's Domain. With Amber's black strap secured around my waist, Noya and I inch toward it.
If anything happens, I yank ==SEX4== back.
You think the giant Stellaroid hauled the Wishing Box all the way back here? Did it repair the floor itself, too? Now that I think about it... Does it actually care about this room?
Following that logic, what was I to the Stellaroid when I was asleep in there? Some treasured Artifact it was hoarding?
Maybe it thought it was your personal maid! Just diligently guarding your beauty sleep this whole time.
That's a bit of a stretch.
Well? Did coming here jog your memory at all?
Not even a little. It honestly feels like my first time here. Even the texture of this Wishing Box ... is giving me nothing.
Wah! This rumbling... It's here! The giant Stellaroid!
Noya, Boss, get back here! Amber, pull back the strap!
Wait a sec. Something feels different this time...
The giant Stellaroid hovers above the room. It doesn't attack. It just floats there in silence.
We don't even know where its face is... Just be ready to yank the Boss back.
Don't tell me ... it actually remembers me.
Wait! The Stellaroid... It put its chest cannon away!
W-Wow, it actually did... But why?
I think it's because... You grabbed my hand.
It's flying away... It just left?
Y-Yeah, we're fine... It wasn't hostile?
More like, it's not hostile toward the Boss.
It was aiming at me earlier, so it remembers us taking the Wishing Box. But the second ==PLAYER_NAME== grabbed my hand, it stood down.
Doesn't that mean... What it's really guarding is ... ==PLAYER_NAME==? Grabbing my hand proved we're friends, so it backed off?
I-I don't know... But this is a good thing, right? At least ... it means we can use this floor as a safe house now.
Wait. If that's the case... I have an even bolder idea.
You took your sweet time, Angie.
Your companions put up quite a fight, Tyrant. They wiped out two-thirds of my forces. But this is where it ends.
Their Soul Stones are tapped out and they fled. My forces control every elevator on Floor 50.
Even if Monolith blessings multiplied your power five or ten times over, we didn't arrive empty-handed either.
Do you honestly plan to fight a hundred of us with just three people?
Let me correct you on one thing. My companions didn't flee. They just went to refill their Soul Stones.

Ridiculous. Every Soul Stone the Salvation Committee carries is magically sealed. You can't use them. Are you waiting on the White Cats? They couldn't scrape together enough to matter even if they pooled everything they had.
We aren't the only players in Mirage, Angie. Underestimating the insignificant factions will come back to bite you.
Yo, if it isn't Serena... Or should I call you Lady Angie now? Aren't you in a Monolith? How are you getting a signal?
Oh, right. There's a giant hole in that Monolith. Signal must be leaking through.
Hazana, cut the crap. What did you do?!
Nothing much. Just saw a bunch of boxes sitting out in the desert, and since nobody seemed to be claiming them, I brought the Scorpions out to pick them up.
Lady Angie! We... We can't hold them off! There are so many Desert Scorpions swarming us! It's terrifying!
You attacked the Salvation Committee's logistics squad?! How dare you! Didn't I promise you—
Sorry, Angie, but the Scorpions gotta eat. We go where the money is.
You can't match what the Boss offered. Even if you weren't a heretic and still ran the Sky Institute, you still couldn't afford it.
So, good luck with all that. See ya.
She's probably blowing a gasket right now, getting stung by the very Scorpions she always looked down on.
Keep it moving, everyone! Everything here is ours! As of today, we're company folks too!
Hey, miss. How did Boss know we were here? And how'd ==SEX== know we were just faking it with the Salvation Committee?
Hmm... I honestly have no idea how Boss knew you were here. ==SEX1== just seems to know everything. Even the special magic those Committee captains use.
Oh, is that right? Guess me wandering around with ice cream and fries without ever finding ==SEX4== didn't mess anything up then.
Question! Your lovely Bastelina has a question too!
What exactly did Boss bribe the Desert Scorpion with? That Hazana wanted nothing to do with this fight. Lady Angie tried pulling her in for ages and got nowhere.
Huh?! A Seal of Grace! No wonder... That's insanely rare.
Actually, the Seal wasn't what won her over. It was...
A Seal of Grace? That's a generous offer, sure. But I'm not gambling my crew's lives against the Salvation Committee just because you're paying top dollar.
Boss said this Seal of Grace isn't payment. It's just a bonus that comes with the real offer.

Here is what ==SEX== is really offering: Will you remain as sand blowing in the wind, or will you take this piece, lead the oppressed miners of Mirage, and forge a future where you are never bled dry by anyone else again?
Here is what ==SEX== is really offering: Will you remain as sand blowing in the wind, or will you take this piece and become the true masters of your own fate?
... Hahahaha! I don't know how the Boss figured it out, but you actually treats me like ... an equal partner.
With a Seal of Grace and a victory over the heretics, we finally have a real seat at the table in Nova. We aren't fighting for someone else. We're fighting for ourselves!
Myrsha! Run these Soul Stones to the Monolith entrance! Tell the Boss to go wild!
Let's move, Scorpions! Time to show that arrogant woman what we're made of!
My companions have already secured enough Soul Stones from the Desert Scorpions. They're heading up to Floor 50 right now and will be back before you know it.
You predicted every single step of this battle ... even the shifting loyalties of the Desert Scorpions? How on earth did you pull that off?
I am going to kill you right here, right now!
A full-body defensive ward layered directly onto clothing? How interesting, Iris. I didn't think you would ever waste magic so frivolously.
A spell like that drains an entire Soul Stone's worth of blessings in a single cast.
We only need to hold out a little longer anyway! We've got blessings to spare, so you're never going to catch us!
O God of Grace, please... Please let us find an absurdly huge Wishing Box!
Ooh, you just burned through two more Soul Stones. How many spares do you have left?
Run! It won't matter where you hide... I will hunt you down and kill the Tyrant!
I'm taking Iris. We'll hide on the cliff just below the floor.
Noya, open the Wishing Box! Judging by how calm Angie is, she probably knows how to "repeat history" too.
Heh. Not "probably," Tyrant. I know for a fact.
I've looked into every detail of your past. How could I overlook the place where it all began?
The Boss's Domain in the Desert Monolith. It only takes a light-blonde swordswoman and a purple-haired noble to unlock.
It's empty in here. An absolute dead end. Is this the grave you chose for yourself?
Looks like even the info brokers get it wrong sometimes. It's not empty in here.
Wh-What is that sound? According to the late Empress's records ... There shouldn't be any Archons in this Monolith!
Noya, get in the Wishing Box!
Angie's bullets shatter the final layers of defensive magic Iris cast on Noya and me, draining our last Soul Stones.
Noya and I leap into the Wishing Box, the heavy lid slowly shutting in front of us.
My final glimpse of the outside is the giant Stellaroid rising, its shadow swallowing the entire room.

Phew... Talk about a blast from the past. We actually made it back here.
Thinking back... How did the three of us manage to lug a Wishing Box that huge down fifty floors?
We ran on Iris's terrifying obsession with Artifacts.

Honestly, finding ==PLAYER_NAME== in there was way better than finding an Artifact. If we hadn't met ==SEX4==, Feagin would've eaten us alive when we got back to Emor.
Yeah. It feels like a dream. After all those adventures, here we are... Right back where it all began.
And facing another massive crisis, too!
But hey, if we made it back here, it means we can beat this. And when we set off again, we'll go even further.
Under the cover of our allies, the New Star Guild and I reach the top floor of the Desert Monolith in just over two hours.
Aside from the unique top floor, every level in a Monolith is a tangled web of nearly identical parallel floors.
Inside the Monolith, Floor 30 isn't a fixed location. It simply means a climber has reached the thirtieth floor's trial.
When the elevator doors open, there's no guarantee it's the same Floor 30 you saw last time. Two guilds entering back-to-back could climb all the way to the top without ever crossing paths.
We build our entire strategy against the Salvation Committee around this exact mechanic.
The Monolith's elevators only hold ten people at a time, naturally funneling the enemy into isolated squads that can't support each other.
By entering first and securing the right blessings, we use our advantage in power and terrain to ambush them.
Boss, the interceptions on each floor are going as planned. Iris's Monolith Blessing Combo Guide is a lifesaver. Syncing our setups to her strategies gave our magic and strength a massive boost.
We engaged over two hundred Committee members, crushed about a hundred and fifty, and the rest retreated outside. Only Fuyuka, Chaton, and Chitose took some minor hits, but nothing serious.
Great work. So there are under a hundred enemies left inside?
Yes, but they're the elites. And we still haven't caught any sign of Angie or Greyhorn.
Our spare Soul Stones are tapped out. Everyone's running on fumes.
No good. Theirs are rigged with magical seals. Cracking them would take way too long.
Understood. You've all done an incredible job. Let's move to Phase Two. You fall back, exit the Monolith, and resupply. Leave distracting the Committee to us.
Boss, what about the rest? Do we go on the offensive?
One swing of my sword shoots wind blades in eight directions now! The three of us can easily take on ten of them!
It won't be that easy. Angie and Greyhorn are still missing, and Captain Greyhorn is formidable. Dodging Nazuka's teams might not just be luck. They might be using a specific climbing technique.
We should play it safe. Stick to the plan and use the Monolith's terrain to outmaneuver them. We head to Floor 51: the Boss's Domain.
Ugh... Do we really have to go there?!==W== What if... What if that terrifying Stellaroid is still waiting for us?

Yeah. It only showed up when we tried to open the Wishing Box. Maybe it's just guarding it.
That's all we need. If we don't touch the Wishing Box, the Boss's Domain becomes a safe house that only we control.
We pop out to hit Angie. But she can't hit us.
Exactly. Even if Angie knows how to repeat history, it won't matter. With only one elevator in the Boss's Domain, choking them out will be effortless.
Nazuka's team keeps their blessings even outside the Monolith. We just hold the line until they resupply and return. Then, the Salvation Committee is completely out of options.

strings.text: A little earlier. Laru helps the New Star Guild escape the mines in disguise. Greyhorn notices but lets them go, since you alone are the target. Bastelina then passes you key intel on No. 160 in a box of fries.
Huff... Huff...==W== Amber... Is that sniper still on us?
No eyes on us. I think we lost her.
Ugh... Must've torn it open again when we made a run for it.
I'm sorry. You wouldn't have gotten shot if you hadn't covered me.
Don't say that, Iris. I was already hit.==W== If you went down too, Amber couldn't have dragged us both out of there.
Hehe, mind patching me up one more time? Oh, and help me scrub the blood off these clothes.
We can't let ==PLAYER_NAME== see this. ==SEX1=='ll worry sick and bench me.
Noya, you absolutely belong on the bench right now!==W==
Relax, I'm tough!==W== A little scratch won't stop me from swinging a sword. Watch!
Ow, ow, ow!==W== Okay... Maybe it stings a little.
Stop pushing yourself, Noya.==W== You're trying way too hard today... It's not like you.
Normally, you'd be the one saying it: if you're hurt, you rest.
Would I...?==W== Yeah, okay, I totally would.
But this time is different. It really is.
Different how?==W== Being trapped in Mirage by the Salvation Committee is our biggest crisis yet, sure,==W== but it's not like we have to beat them.
If we only need to escape, Boss will figure something out.
Don't panic, Noya. Even Iris isn't panicking yet.
It's not panic. It's my gut feeling.
You know my gut is never wrong. And this time just feels ...==W== different. I've only ever felt like this once before.
Shh. Keep your voice down.==W== The Salvation Committee up ahead.
It's the Imperial Guards that were trapped by Nazuna and Fuyuka in the mines! We need to turn back!
Oh no... The Committee is blocking this way too...
Silence who?!==W== Wait, huge misunderstanding! I'm with Boss too!
No time to explain!==W== Put these on and get behind me.==W==
Captain Greyhorn! And the brave souls of the First Company!==W== You must be exhausted hunting the Tyrant. Please, enjoy these special ice cream fries courtesy of Logistics!
We got pinned down in a mine by two measly Trekkers... Who has the appetite for fries?!
It's a disgrace. A stain on the Committee.
I'm sorry, that was my fault. The Tyrant's people hijacked my winds, and I didn't even notice. It's humiliating.
Same here. My scouting spell locked onto the wrong targets and dragged us all down.
Drop it. Wins and losses are part of war.
We took a beating in those mines, but the Committee still holds the advantage here.
Stick to Director Angie's deployment plan, and we'll capture the Tyrant!
Now, don't let Logistics' hard work go to waste. Eat up. We need the calories and salt.
Thanks for the rations, Laru. Pass my regards to your team.==W== Morale would be in the dirt without you.
You're too kind, Captain! Just doing our jobs.
Oh, them! The ice cream melts way too fast out of the cooler. I needed extra hands plating everything so you guys could enjoy the perfect fries!
So I hired a few locals to help out.
(What a sloppy disguise. One of them even reeks of blood. Going by Gunhild's latest report...==W== These must be ==PLAYER_NAME=='s Trekker companions, and they're injured.)
(Then again, I'm not with the Committee. I don't buy their rhetoric about saving the world for a second. I'm only here on the Grand Captain's orders.)

(Director Angie ordered us to only target the Tyrant. I have no reason to harass these Trekkers. What they did with ==PLAYER_NAME== in Philae was an act of justice. Arresting them now violates my honor as a knight.)
I'm full. Thanks for the food.
Thank you for covering for us.==W== You're Ms. Laru from the Sky Institute, right?
Ms? Save that for Albedo. It makes me sound ancient.
Call me the Fry Girl! Running into you three here must be the will of the Goddess of Fries!
Huh? Is this the time to talk about fries?!==W== We need to get out of here!
Never underestimate the fry!==W== Especially when it is perfectly coated in ice cream!
Mmm! This is so good I could pass out~~!==W==
Is it that good?==W== Let me try.
Why are you all eating?!==W== Noya, you're hurt! Drop the junk food!
One bite won't kill me! Here, Iris, try it...==W== Wait.
So that is what happened.==W== That Grace Imperium lady called herself the Fry Girl,==W== but honestly? Fry Weirdo fits way better.
But she's definitely on our side. After we finished the fries she sent us, we found a message written all over the inside of the boxes.
She even protected the ink from grease with rice paper.
No, she must have intended not to let the ink ruin her fries. Priorities.
Three flattened fry boxes sit on the table before me.==RT==The cardboard is packed with neat handwriting==RT==detailing troop counts, defensive layout, and key personnel.
At the very bottom sits a tiny signature: Bastelina.
This is what Bastelina and Laru gathered when they went undercover in the Committee.
It says ...==W== they got their phones confiscated and lost their contacts. They couldn't reach Albedo, so they smuggled this to us instead. They want us to make it out alive.
We already figured some of this out... The three divisions, the elite sniper with Angie, the artillery camp outside the city.
But there's still a ton of solid intel here. Take this one...

<alpha=#FF>Greyhorn. A Knight Commander of the Imperial Guard. She is not a Committee member. She is only assisting Director Angie on orders from a superior.==P====RT====RT==She gives it her all in battles, but she will not needlessly pursue you or your allies.

<alpha=#FF>No. 160, one of the Dusk Arbiters. She seemingly experienced severe childhood trauma and carries deep psychological scars.==P====RT====RT==She displays masochistic tendencies, but this is merely a trigger. She uses pain to recall her trauma, which freezes time itself all around her.==P====RT====RT==But this magic doesn't actually stop time. It just forcibly uses magic power to restrict the movement of anything within a certain range around her that she can see.

<alpha=#FF>The more pain and fear she endures, the further and longer she can freeze everything around her.==P====RT====RT==She's not much of a fighter physically, but that dagger of hers is the real threat. A single cut plants "Fear" in her victims, forcing them to confront their worst nightmares, leaving them defenseless.==P====RT====RT==Additionally, No. 160 is a former inter-city operator. She can intercept Heartlink comms within a certain radius. Please use your phones cautiously.
So her magic really is stopping time. The more she suffers, the longer it lasts... That explains why she took Fuyuka's punch on purpose.
Firenze is right to be cautious. Someone in the Salvation Committee really can tap into our Heartlinks. If Nazuka and Chitose give away their location, they won't be able to swoop in and bail us out.

<alpha=#FF>Director Angie is an amateur.==P====RT====RT==She lacks both tactical and magical expertise.==P====W====RT====RT==However, she commands loyalty from the Committee because she will sacrifice absolutely anything to save the world, which means killing you.
Sacrifice anything to kill me, huh?==W== Why is she so convinced the Tyrant will end the world?==W== I wonder if I can drag some answers out of her during the negotiations.
Anyway, this intel is huge. You did great.==W== Once we clear this mess, we owe Bastelina and Laru big time.
Hehe. See? Taking a hit had its perks.
Whoa, Noya, personal space! Your nose is practically touching mine.
And don't say that. There is zero perk to getting hurt. Just looking at that gash makes me wince.
If you mean the intel, Laru and Bastelina would've found a way to deliver it even if you were fine.
I wasn't talking about the intel.
It's been so, so long since I could just watch your profile while you're hard at work.
Wh-What's so great about my profile?
I don't know. I just like looking at it.
Here. Stare all you want. Special treatment for the patient.
Ah! If you sit right next to me, my angles are all messed up!==W== No, no, the whole vibe is gone!
Pfft...==W== You're sentimental today.==W== Iris was right. You're not acting like yourself at all.
Usually, if you wanted to stare, you'd just tackle me and press your face right against mine.
Hey! Stop making me sound like a puppy greeting its owner!
Sigh... It's all because of this awful gut feeling. It's making me anxious.
Huh? The overwhelmingly cheerful Noya is anxious?
What is this gut feeling telling you?
...==W== Ever since we left the White Cat's secret room... I've had this heavy premonition...
That today ... is the day you leave us.

Different how?==W== Being trapped in Mirage by the Salvation Committee is our biggest crisis yet, sure,==W== but it's not like we have to beat them.
If we only need to escape, Boss will figure something out.
Don't panic, Noya. Even Iris isn't panicking yet.
It's not panic. It's my gut feeling.
You know my gut is never wrong. And this time just feels ...==W== different. I've only ever felt like this once before.
Shh. Keep your voice down.==W== The Salvation Committee up ahead.
It's the Imperial Guards that were trapped by Nazuna and Fuyuka in the mines! We need to turn back!
Oh no... The Committee is blocking this way too...
Silence who?!==W== Wait, huge misunderstanding! I'm with Boss too!
No time to explain!==W== Put these on and get behind me.==W==
Captain Greyhorn! And the brave souls of the First Company!==W== You must be exhausted hunting the Tyrant. Please, enjoy these special ice cream fries courtesy of Logistics!
We got pinned down in a mine by two measly Trekkers... Who has the appetite for fries?!
It's a disgrace. A stain on the Committee.
I'm sorry, that was my fault. The Tyrant's people hijacked my winds, and I didn't even notice. It's humiliating.
Same here. My scouting spell locked onto the wrong targets and dragged us all down.
Drop it. Wins and losses are part of war.
We took a beating in those mines, but the Committee still holds the advantage here.
Stick to Director Angie's deployment plan, and we'll capture the Tyrant!
Now, don't let Logistics' hard work go to waste. Eat up. We need the calories and salt.
Thanks for the rations, Laru. Pass my regards to your team.==W== Morale would be in the dirt without you.
You're too kind, Captain! Just doing our jobs.
Oh, them! The ice cream melts way too fast out of the cooler. I needed extra hands plating everything so you guys could enjoy the perfect fries!
So I hired a few locals to help out.
(What a sloppy disguise. One of them even reeks of blood. Going by Gunhild's latest report...==W== These must be ==PLAYER_NAME=='s Trekker companions, and they're injured.)
(Then again, I'm not with the Committee. I don't buy their rhetoric about saving the world for a second. I'm only here on the Grand Captain's orders.)

(Director Angie ordered us to only target the Tyrant. I have no reason to harass these Trekkers. What they did with ==PLAYER_NAME== in Philae was an act of justice. Arresting them now violates my honor as a knight.)
I'm full. Thanks for the food.
Thank you for covering for us.==W== You're Ms. Laru from the Sky Institute, right?
Ms? Save that for Albedo. It makes me sound ancient.
Call me the Fry Girl! Running into you three here must be the will of the Goddess of Fries!
Huh? Is this the time to talk about fries?!==W== We need to get out of here!
Never underestimate the fry!==W== Especially when it is perfectly coated in ice cream!
Mmm! This is so good I could pass out~~!==W==
Is it that good?==W== Let me try.
Why are you all eating?!==W== Noya, you're hurt! Drop the junk food!
One bite won't kill me! Here, Iris, try it...==W== Wait.
So that is what happened.==W== That Grace Imperium lady called herself the Fry Girl,==W== but honestly? Fry Weirdo fits way better.
But she's definitely on our side. After we finished the fries she sent us, we found a message written all over the inside of the boxes.
She even protected the ink from grease with rice paper.
No, she must have intended not to let the ink ruin her fries. Priorities.
Three flattened fry boxes sit on the table before me.==RT==The cardboard is packed with neat handwriting==RT==detailing troop counts, defensive layout, and key personnel.
At the very bottom sits a tiny signature: Bastelina.
This is what Bastelina and Laru gathered when they went undercover in the Committee.
It says ...==W== they got their phones confiscated and lost their contacts. They couldn't reach Albedo, so they smuggled this to us instead. They want us to make it out alive.
We already figured some of this out... The three divisions, the elite sniper with Angie, the artillery camp outside the city.
But there's still a ton of solid intel here. Take this one...

<alpha=#FF>Greyhorn. A Knight Commander of the Imperial Guard. She is not a Committee member. She is only assisting Director Angie on orders from a superior.==P====RT====RT==She gives it her all in battles, but she will not needlessly pursue you or your allies.

<alpha=#FF>No. 160, one of the Dusk Arbiters. She seemingly experienced severe childhood trauma and carries deep psychological scars.==P====RT====RT==She displays masochistic tendencies, but this is merely a trigger. She uses pain to recall her trauma, which freezes time itself all around her.==P====RT====RT==But this magic doesn't actually stop time. It just forcibly uses magic power to restrict the movement of anything within a certain range around her that she can see.

<alpha=#FF>The more pain and fear she endures, the further and longer she can freeze everything around her.==P====RT====RT==She's not much of a fighter physically, but that dagger of hers is the real threat. A single cut plants "Fear" in her victims, forcing them to confront their worst nightmares, leaving them defenseless.==P====RT====RT==Additionally, No. 160 is a former inter-city operator. She can intercept Heartlink comms within a certain radius. Please use your phones cautiously.
So her magic really is stopping time. The more she suffers, the longer it lasts... That explains why she took Fuyuka's punch on purpose.
Firenze is right to be cautious. Someone in the Salvation Committee really can tap into our Heartlinks. If Nazuka and Chitose give away their location, they won't be able to swoop in and bail us out.

<alpha=#FF>Director Angie is an amateur.==P====RT====RT==She lacks both tactical and magical expertise.==P====W====RT====RT==However, she commands loyalty from the Committee because she will sacrifice absolutely anything to save the world, which means killing you.
Sacrifice anything to kill me, huh?==W== Why is she so convinced the Tyrant will end the world?==W== I wonder if I can drag some answers out of her during the negotiations.
Anyway, this intel is huge. You did great.==W== Once we clear this mess, we owe Bastelina and Laru big time.
Hehe. See? Taking a hit had its perks.
Whoa, Noya, personal space! Your nose is practically touching mine.
And don't say that. There is zero perk to getting hurt. Just looking at that gash makes me wince.
If you mean the intel, Laru and Bastelina would've found a way to deliver it even if you were fine.
I wasn't talking about the intel.
It's been so, so long since I could just watch your profile while you're hard at work.
Wh-What's so great about my profile?
I don't know. I just like looking at it.
Here. Stare all you want. Special treatment for the patient.
Ah! If you sit right next to me, my angles are all messed up!==W== No, no, the whole vibe is gone!
Pfft...==W== You're sentimental today.==W== Iris was right. You're not acting like yourself at all.
Usually, if you wanted to stare, you'd just tackle me and press your face right against mine.
Hey! Stop making me sound like a puppy greeting its owner!
Sigh... It's all because of this awful gut feeling. It's making me anxious.
Huh? The overwhelmingly cheerful Noya is anxious?
What is this gut feeling telling you?
...==W== Ever since we left the White Cat's secret room... I've had this heavy premonition...
That today ... is the day you leave us.

strings.text: Angie is finally captured, while Greyhorn takes the chance to retreat. You gather at Eureka and refute Angie's claims. Before anyone could celebrate, an injured Bastelina arrives with terrible news...
The ground gave way. Looks like an abandoned mineshaft.
Get behind me. The Tyrant must have set an ambush down here.
H-Hello! Um... I hope my punch didn't hurt you too badly. I held back as much as I could!
M-Master is not the Tyrant! Stop making things up!
Greyhorn, go. Leave before the rest of the Tyrant's forces arrive. I grant you full command of the Salvation Committee.
Ma'am, what are you saying? I am not even a Committee member. How can I take command?
Your Grand Captain's orders were to follow my commands, right?
Then this is my command. You are the only one left who can lead the Committee. You must kill the Tyrant.
None shall leave. For the safety of my ==SEX11==, this shaft will be your tomb.
Be careful, Chitose. That knight knows her way around a sword.
What a ferocious battojutsu stance. The scouts mentioned a black-clad Trekker guarding the Tyrant. That must be her.
My blade ... slipped right off her armor?
The curvature of that plating... It's forged specifically to deflect slashes?
Then I must aim for the gaps.
Even with a rapier, I can't match her speed. At this rate... I'll have to risk it.
She stepped into the strike? Taking the blow on her breastplate to force a counter?!
To think such a technique exists.
The armor held, but I still can't land a hit. Is this going to be a war of attrition?
A mere bullet. If I can see it, I can sever it.
Chitose, fall back! Your blade can't pierce that armor. Secure Angie!
Dammit, the Tyrant saw through my defense. Fuyuka... Is that the timid Trekker from earlier?
Step aside. I don't want to hurt you.
My ribs... I think they're broken. Imperial plate is useless against heavy blunt force.
Forgive me, Lady Angie. I will come back for you.
My ==SEX11==, her tendons are severed. She can no longer wield the Scepter.
I haven't heard a single cannon shot. Was my Committee on the dunes ambushed as well?
I brought a little "rain" down on the dunes. Your Third Company should be busy struggling in the sand right now.
Chitose, stop her bleeding. We're moving out.
The battle for Mirage is over.
==PLAYER_NAME==! You actually caught her! That's amazing!
Chitose and Fuyuka did all the heavy lifting.
Heheh, great job, Fuyuka! That's our Petal Bloom captain for you.
You both worked really hard too, Nazuna, Nazuka! Master told me you buried their artillery in sand?
Ugh, don't even get me started.
Boss, I might know a little Terra magic, but I'm no Hazana! Sand isn't exactly my specialty!
But you did fine, didn't you? You pulled enough sand into my cyclone to dump a literal storm on their camp. They were completely buried.
I was pushing myself to the absolute limit! I couldn't drag you down. But pulling all that sand left my brain feeling fried.
I'm not casting a single spell for three days. No, make that a week!
I need a plushie... A big, soft, nice-smelling plushie to recover.
Thanks, Nazuna. You're our only Terra mage, so I had to lean on you. I'll buy you a life-sized plushie once we leave Mirage.
Yo, Boss. It's been a minute.
Good to see you, Minova. How are the kids in the Ashwind Clan doing?
The Boss Accord carries a lot of weight now. With me officially on the payroll, the street gangs don't dare mess with us.
A few of the older ones are even sitting for the Platinum Academy entrance exams next year.
Hell of a tactical call, by the way. We hit them right as they were priming the cannon. They couldn't turn it around in time.
That captain, Gunhild, was stubborn as a mule, though. I beat her until she couldn't even stand, and she was still trying to swing at me.
I had to jam my bat down her cannon barrel and snapped it off. That'll take her half the day to dig out.
You snapped it? Then what's that in your hand?
Haha, come on, Boss. Who brings just one bat to a street fight?
Anyway. This woman with the busted hands... This is Angie, right?
Minova, of the Ashwind Clan... Heh. You even have street urchins from the Ash District traveling all the way for you, Tyrant.
Just how many people have you beguiled? How many souls have you bound?
I figured a big shot like you would have something profound to say after getting caught.
Turns out, you're completely full of it.
We didn't rush out here because of some soul control. We came because Boss actually looked out for us.
That was simply ... a calculated move. ==SEX1== needed to buy your loyalty.
What's your little group called again? The Salvation Committee?
Cute name. But let me ask you:==W== when Feagin was running rampant in the Ash District, beating kids and running sweatshops, where were you?
When that massive Stellaroid broke out of the Monolith, and boulders from the Waterway crushed countless homes, where were you then?
If you claim that Boss was just buying loyalty, why didn't you step up and buy us first?
The Salvation Committee has limited resources. We must prioritize what is essential to saving the world.
Bull. You ignore the suffering right in front of your faces. You won't even lift a finger when it's easy.
And now we're supposed to believe you're out here saving the world? Only a fool would buy that!
I don't need to understand your twisted logic!
You think killing Boss is going to save the world?
I say putting a round through your skull is what'll really save the world!
We're not here to be executioners. The battle is over. We just hold her until Firenze and the Dusk Arbiters arrive to put the Committee on trial.
Heh... Hahaha. You are truly naive, Tyrant.
Did you honestly believe capturing me would end this?
Your ambush in the mineshaft surprised me. But it also proved something.
Anticipating my artillery was one thing. But using the mineshaft to lay a trap... That was a tactic I had only ever formed in my mind. And yet, you knew it.
At that moment, it all made sense.
What are you getting at, Angie?
Tell me, Tyrant. Can you see the future? Or ...==W== did you travel back from it?
That expression says it all. I must have won in the future you saw. You had absolutely no counter to my final card.
I will kill you, and I will save this world.
Master, what... What is she talking about? Has she lost her mind?
She's just throwing a tantrum because we beat her.
What does Angie mean? Seeing the future? Traveling back?
Does she know about the White Room?
No. That's impossible. I countered too many of her moves, so she's just grasping at theories.

Wait, think about it. I initiated the parley this time. She had zero time to prepare. That means ... her goal for the negotiation was different from last time. She wasn't trying to lure me into a trap.
She came to the table while setting up an artillery strike.==W== Was it a suicide mission? Or does she ... actually have an unplayed trump card?
Huff... Huff...==W== I finally found you! Boss, why are you still here?!
Bastelina? What are you doing here?
The battle is over. Why would we run?
It's not over! Without Lady Angie to maintain discipline, the Committee's ranks broke. They abandoned the order of only targeting the Tyrant!
What's coming next isn't just a strike team hunting one target. It's an all-out war!
Blood! She's hurt... Her back is soaked in blood!
