strings.text: Under your strategy, the hundred-man unit collapses and Angie surrenders. Alone with you, she reveals the truth: she too reached the future and saw ruin. With the last bullet, she turns it on herself...
Lady Angie, we need to fall back. Our attacks are barely scratching this Stellaroid...
I don't think so. From the combat logs from the Waterway, we just need to break that magic array on its head.
This Stellaroid is nothing like that one... We've tried, and it's not working.
Our magic can't even pierce its magical barrier. This isn't just some normal Stellaroid... It's an Archon!
No! I have to kill the Tyrant here and now. ==SEX1== has become the true Tyrant.
If magic won't cut it, let's see how it handles the Scepter of Death.
Angie's bullet tears through the Stellaroid's magical barrier, embedding itself in the magic array on its head.
The Imperial Guard will fulfill its duty... We'll cover your escape...
By the time Noya and I climb out of the Wishing Box, the floor is already littered with unconscious Committee members.
The only person left standing in the room ... is Angie.
Boss, the Soul Stone retrieval team is back.
Amber, keep an eye on her. Noya and I will bring the others up.
As the rest of our team trickles into the Boss's Domain, Angie doesn't so much as flinch. She just stands there frozen.
It's over, Angie. All three Committee companies have been routed inside the Monolith.==W== Greyhorn, No. 160, and Gunhild are all in our custody.
Heh. You're right. I have lost.
You're incredible.==W== Even with all the memories of the future... I still couldn't defeat you.
Memories? What is she talking about?
==PLAYER_NAME==, don't waste your breath on her.
And this will all be over.
This knave has repeatedly plotted against you. Say the word, my ==SEX11==, and I shall strike her down.
If you surrender, we won't hurt you. I can guarantee you a fair trial.
Even now, you still intend to spare my life.
You'd better not mistake that for a weakness, Angie.
I just want to give you a fair end. Don't think for a second I won't kill you.
I know. That's exactly why I'm considering your offer.
Look at the chips you hold. You're in no position to negotiate right now.
Heh. I believe you will agree to this condition, Tyrant.
I want to speak with you alone. Right here is fine, just ask your companions to keep their distance.
What could we have left to talk about?
I want to tell you the truth about the end of the world. And it's for your ears only.
What's the point? Even if I agree, I'm just going to tell them everything once we're done.
Some truths only bring more trouble if they reach the wrong ears.
You'll understand once you hear it.
During my last two negotiations with Angie, she brought up a lot of things... Things I had no idea about.
The late Empress's diary, the falling Monolith, and the "trump card" she never revealed... Even if it's just for the intel, it's worth hearing what she has to say.
Iris, Nazuka. Cast some defensive magic on my clothes.
Alright. Everyone's backed up to the edge of the room. They won't be able to hear us from here.
Now, talk. What is this truth about the end of the world?
Thank you for agreeing to my terms. You even left me with the Scepter of Death… After everything you've done, I must return the favor sincerely.
I am from the future. Four years from now.
This is by no means a joke. Four years from now, this world will end.
The world will shatter into ruins, civilizations will collapse, and not even ashes will remain of the Nova Empire.
<size=50><color=#bd3059>Everything you and I love...==W== Everything you and I hate... They will all be wiped out.
<size=45>And the root of it all ... is the <color=#bd3059>Tyrant</color>.==W== Which means me.
You're the Tyrant? What are you talking about?!
By a stroke of fate, I once obtained a cellphone. It looked exactly like the one in your hand.
<color=#3faeae>The Well of Worlds Tyrant Development System</color>. Does that sound familiar?
I had nothing back then. For my own sake, and for my companions, I fought tooth and nail to complete that system's missions. Over and over again, it handed me rewards I couldn't even fathom.
Eventually, I completed every single mission. I fulfilled every single wish.
But it all ended with the Monolith collapsing right in front of me... Along with this world.
I used the rewards the system gave me to make one final wish. I escaped ten years into the past... That would be six years in the past from now.
However, even though I ran from reality, I never had the courage to open that safe again. Nor the courage to face my future allies.
All I could do was desperately gather information and watch that Soul Shop from afar.
<size=75><color=#bd3059>And... During this time, the new Tyrant was chosen…==RT==And it was none other than you.
Ahahahahaha!! That's it! That's the look, Tyrant.
You must know about that system too. Hehe... Why can I assert that? It's simple.==W== What you are doing is the same as what I did in the past.
You realize I'm not lying, don't you? Something so beyond human understanding ... can't possibly stem from pure imagination, can it?
Your actions happen to align with the Book of Grace Prophecies, but I wouldn't have acted on that alone.
The late Empress kept an old bo<r=diary></r>ok hidden with your portrait drawn, but I wouldn't have acted on that alone either.
That's because... After having gone back to the past, I no longer believe in anyone ... or anything.
However... I have no choice but to believe in myself.
<size=50><color=#bd3059>The Tyrant who destroys the world is the Tyrant who possesses that system!
==Off==<size=68><color=#bd3059>I have only ever had one goal.==RT==And that is to save Nova from a Tyrant like that.
<size=45><color=#bd3059>Do you understand what I'm trying to tell you? Tyrant... If you weren't here, the disaster ahead of us wouldn't come to pass.
Having said that, I'm aware of how unreasonable I sound right now...
Dying with you would be my atonement.
What nonsense are you daydreaming about? Why would I throw my life away over your insane ramblings?!
Our deaths alone will pave the way to everyone's salvation! Therefore, I will sacrifice everything for Nova!
Well, Tyrant, what do you say?
It's not only for the people of Mirage! You'll also be protecting the very people you care about!
That's enough bluffing from you. My fate is mine to decide.
If there really is a crisis capable of destroying the world, I would fight to stop it no matter what!
You're trying to use my friends and Mirage as leverage, but you've already fired nine rounds from that Scepter of Death. You only have one bullet left, don't you?
Heh. So you were counting after all.
It is as you say. The Scepter of Death has only one charge left... It can't even penetrate your magic protection.
<size=70><color=#bd3059>Will you die with me,==RT==or will all of Nova be buried with us?
... Have these repeated defeats finally driven you out of your mind?
No matter what I do, I can never get ahead of you.
You saw through every move I make. Even when I thought I had caught up, I was still a step too late.
How can that be when I am the one with memories of the future? Hah, it's so frustrating...
But, judging by that look of confusion, you still don't know ... about my secret weapon.
Angie slowly pulls out a chess piece... A Black Rook.
You have a Seal of Grace too...
This Black Rook grants me the authority to control a Monolith.
Except this Monolith is very unusual and suspends itself high up in the sky.==W== Only the person holding this piece can travel there using a special cape.
A Monolith in the sky?! You mean—
Right now, that Monolith is hovering above Mirage, so high up it's invisible to the naked eye.
By the way, if my breathing stops, this Monolith will start to crumble … and collapse from the sky. Then—
That's right! Everything will be buried in the darkness of history! So will Mirage and everything that happened there!
Possibly. But if it takes an insane person to save the world—
I will gladly take on that role.
Wait, Angie! Put down the Scepter of Death!
By sacrificing only a worthless small town on the border, the rest of the world shall escape annihilation.
Since you're running a company, you should know whether the payoff justifies the cost.
<size=80>—and become the foundation of the new world.
The Boss and those people in the Grace Imperium uniforms should be fighting inside this Monolith...
I absolutely won't miss this time.
Monoliths are Nocturn Eterna's home turf!
Huh? Why did the sky go dark? Wh-What is that?! Why is there a Monolith in the sky?!

param: Under your strategy, the hundred-man unit collapses and Angie surrenders. Alone with you, she reveals the truth: she too reached the future and saw ruin. With the last bullet, she turns it on herself...
Lady Angie, we need to fall back. Our attacks are barely scratching this Stellaroid...
I don't think so. From the combat logs from the Waterway, we just need to break that magic array on its head.
This Stellaroid is nothing like that one... We've tried, and it's not working.
Our magic can't even pierce its magical barrier. This isn't just some normal Stellaroid... It's an Archon!
No! I have to kill the Tyrant here and now. ==SEX1== has become the true Tyrant.
If magic won't cut it, let's see how it handles the Scepter of Death.
Angie's bullet tears through the Stellaroid's magical barrier, embedding itself in the magic array on its head.
The Imperial Guard will fulfill its duty... We'll cover your escape...
By the time Noya and I climb out of the Wishing Box, the floor is already littered with unconscious Committee members.
The only person left standing in the room ... is Angie.
Boss, the Soul Stone retrieval team is back.
Amber, keep an eye on her. Noya and I will bring the others up.
As the rest of our team trickles into the Boss's Domain, Angie doesn't so much as flinch. She just stands there frozen.
It's over, Angie. All three Committee companies have been routed inside the Monolith.==W== Greyhorn, No. 160, and Gunhild are all in our custody.
Heh. You're right. I have lost.
You're incredible.==W== Even with all the memories of the future... I still couldn't defeat you.
Memories? What is she talking about?
==PLAYER_NAME==, don't waste your breath on her.
And this will all be over.
This knave has repeatedly plotted against you. Say the word, my ==SEX11==, and I shall strike her down.
If you surrender, we won't hurt you. I can guarantee you a fair trial.
Even now, you still intend to spare my life.
You'd better not mistake that for a weakness, Angie.
I just want to give you a fair end. Don't think for a second I won't kill you.
I know. That's exactly why I'm considering your offer.
Look at the chips you hold. You're in no position to negotiate right now.
Heh. I believe you will agree to this condition, Tyrant.
I want to speak with you alone. Right here is fine, just ask your companions to keep their distance.
What could we have left to talk about?
I want to tell you the truth about the end of the world. And it's for your ears only.
What's the point? Even if I agree, I'm just going to tell them everything once we're done.
Some truths only bring more trouble if they reach the wrong ears.
You'll understand once you hear it.
During my last two negotiations with Angie, she brought up a lot of things... Things I had no idea about.
The late Empress's diary, the falling Monolith, and the "trump card" she never revealed... Even if it's just for the intel, it's worth hearing what she has to say.
Iris, Nazuka. Cast some defensive magic on my clothes.
Alright. Everyone's backed up to the edge of the room. They won't be able to hear us from here.
Now, talk. What is this truth about the end of the world?
Thank you for agreeing to my terms. You even left me with the Scepter of Death… After everything you've done, I must return the favor sincerely.
I am from the future. Four years from now.
This is by no means a joke. Four years from now, this world will end.
The world will shatter into ruins, civilizations will collapse, and not even ashes will remain of the Nova Empire.
<size=50><color=#bd3059>Everything you and I love...==W== Everything you and I hate... They will all be wiped out.
<size=45>And the root of it all ... is the <color=#bd3059>Tyrant</color>.==W== Which means me.
You're the Tyrant? What are you talking about?!
By a stroke of fate, I once obtained a cellphone. It looked exactly like the one in your hand.
<color=#3faeae>The Well of Worlds Tyrant Development System</color>. Does that sound familiar?
I had nothing back then. For my own sake, and for my companions, I fought tooth and nail to complete that system's missions. Over and over again, it handed me rewards I couldn't even fathom.
Eventually, I completed every single mission. I fulfilled every single wish.
But it all ended with the Monolith collapsing right in front of me... Along with this world.
I used the rewards the system gave me to make one final wish. I escaped ten years into the past... That would be six years in the past from now.
However, even though I ran from reality, I never had the courage to open that safe again. Nor the courage to face my future allies.
All I could do was desperately gather information and watch that Soul Shop from afar.
<size=75><color=#bd3059>And... During this time, the new Tyrant was chosen…==RT==And it was none other than you.
Ahahahahaha!! That's it! That's the look, Tyrant.
You must know about that system too. Hehe... Why can I assert that? It's simple.==W== What you are doing is the same as what I did in the past.
You realize I'm not lying, don't you? Something so beyond human understanding ... can't possibly stem from pure imagination, can it?
Your actions happen to align with the Book of Grace Prophecies, but I wouldn't have acted on that alone.
The late Empress kept an old bo<r=diary></r>ok hidden with your portrait drawn, but I wouldn't have acted on that alone either.
That's because... After having gone back to the past, I no longer believe in anyone ... or anything.
However... I have no choice but to believe in myself.
<size=50><color=#bd3059>The Tyrant who destroys the world is the Tyrant who possesses that system!
==Off==<size=68><color=#bd3059>I have only ever had one goal.==RT==And that is to save Nova from a Tyrant like that.
<size=45><color=#bd3059>Do you understand what I'm trying to tell you? Tyrant... If you weren't here, the disaster ahead of us wouldn't come to pass.
Having said that, I'm aware of how unreasonable I sound right now...
Dying with you would be my atonement.
What nonsense are you daydreaming about? Why would I throw my life away over your insane ramblings?!
Our deaths alone will pave the way to everyone's salvation! Therefore, I will sacrifice everything for Nova!
Well, Tyrant, what do you say?
It's not only for the people of Mirage! You'll also be protecting the very people you care about!
That's enough bluffing from you. My fate is mine to decide.
If there really is a crisis capable of destroying the world, I would fight to stop it no matter what!
You're trying to use my friends and Mirage as leverage, but you've already fired nine rounds from that Scepter of Death. You only have one bullet left, don't you?
Heh. So you were counting after all.
It is as you say. The Scepter of Death has only one charge left... It can't even penetrate your magic protection.
<size=70><color=#bd3059>Will you die with me,==RT==or will all of Nova be buried with us?
... Have these repeated defeats finally driven you out of your mind?
No matter what I do, I can never get ahead of you.
You saw through every move I make. Even when I thought I had caught up, I was still a step too late.
How can that be when I am the one with memories of the future? Hah, it's so frustrating...
But, judging by that look of confusion, you still don't know ... about my secret weapon.
Angie slowly pulls out a chess piece... A Black Rook.
You have a Seal of Grace too...
This Black Rook grants me the authority to control a Monolith.
Except this Monolith is very unusual and suspends itself high up in the sky.==W== Only the person holding this piece can travel there using a special cape.
A Monolith in the sky?! You mean—
Right now, that Monolith is hovering above Mirage, so high up it's invisible to the naked eye.
By the way, if my breathing stops, this Monolith will start to crumble … and collapse from the sky. Then—
That's right! Everything will be buried in the darkness of history! So will Mirage and everything that happened there!
Possibly. But if it takes an insane person to save the world—
I will gladly take on that role.
Wait, Angie! Put down the Scepter of Death!
By sacrificing only a worthless small town on the border, the rest of the world shall escape annihilation.
Since you're running a company, you should know whether the payoff justifies the cost.
<size=80>—and become the foundation of the new world.
The Boss and those people in the Grace Imperium uniforms should be fighting inside this Monolith...
I absolutely won't miss this time.
Monoliths are Nocturn Eterna's home turf!
Huh? Why did the sky go dark? Wh-What is that?! Why is there a Monolith in the sky?!

strings.text: A strange feeling rises in Noya’s heart: you are going to leave them today. You seal a pinky promise with her at the orphanage. After finalizing the retreat plan, you head to the negotiations to buy time...
...==W== Ever since we left the White Cat's secret room... I've had this heavy premonition...
That today ... is the day you leave us.
The day I leave them? What's going on?==W== Noya's intuition is always spot on. Does she ...==W== think I'm going to die?
No, that's not right. I've faced plenty of danger before. Noya never panicked like this just because of a gut feeling.
No, that can't be. It's not like I've never faced death in our past adventures. And back then, Noya was never this panicked.
Maybe the injury is getting to her. Add that to the fact that things are worse than usual right now... Is fear clouding her judgment?
Hmm...==W== As long as I have the White Room, death isn't permanent for me. It still hurts, though, and I can't exactly explain that to Noya. I'd better comfort her for now.
Don't worry, Noya. Whatever your intuition says, I'm not going anywhere.
But Noya's expression only grows more serious.
==PLAYER_NAME==, I never doubt your conviction. But my intuition doesn't listen to reason.
Even when something looks completely foolproof, like it could never go wrong... Things still happen. A coincidence, or some tiny detail I missed. And then everything plays out exactly as I feared.
That's why I...==W== Why I haven't been acting like myself today. I don't know what's going to go wrong. All I can do is ...==W== get busy, to give myself some peace of mind.
She's genuinely terrified for me. Charging back at the Salvation Committee, hiding her wound to keep fighting... She did all of it for me. In that case...
We still have a little time. Tell me exactly what your intuition is telling you, Noya.

I might not be able to talk you out of it, since your intuition ignores logic. Just like when you thought crashing Loxy into a massive Stellaroid on the Waterway would actually work, and it did. But I can at least help put you at ease.
Because your Boss can do anything.
Right! You're the wish-granting Boss. ==W==Heh heh, you still owe me a wish, you know.
Then, Boss, here is my wish.==W== Please relieve me of my anxiety!
Deal. Then tell me, what exactly does this premonition of me leaving feel like?
Mm... Usually, no matter where you are, whether I'm awake or asleep, whether I can see or hear you, my heart always senses you.
It's hard to explain. Like back in Philae, when you and Chitose went into the Monolith. I could sense that you were safe the whole time.
Because of how strong Chitose is?

Not exactly. It's just a feeling, really. I knew your trip would go smoothly. I didn't know whether you'd be able to wish for the right Artifact, but I was sure that you'd come back safe and keep traveling with us.
But ... the second we stepped out of the White Cat's secret room, I lost that peace of mind.
Even with you walking right next to me, my stomach was in knots. I couldn't shake the feeling that if I looked away for even a second, you'd vanish into the tunnels.
Hmm... That's a tricky one to tackle.==W== Wait, when you were talking about Laru earlier, you said...
You know my gut is never wrong. And this time just feels ...==W== different. I've only ever felt like this once before.
When was that? Since I'm sitting right here with you safe and sound, your gut must have been wrong back then. That might be the key to all this.
The last time? Um...==W== It's a little hard to admit.
Noya ... blushing? That's a rare sight.
But if I don't tell you, I'll just keep feeling anxious, and I hate that!==W== Fine. I'll tell you, but you can't laugh at me!
The last time I had this feeling ... was under the Monolith in Philae.
When we fought the Big Three? That was pretty dangerous.
No, not then. It was when you and Nazuka were whispering under the Monolith.
Nazuka had just flown off with you. We followed Nazuna and hid in the woods to watch.
It was a beautiful night. And we heard ... everything Nazuka said to you.
If you were able to make a promise like that, it means you both recognize each other as someone very important.
She's beautiful, and she's incredibly strong. My intuition told me that staying at the Trekker Camp ... and living with the Petal Bloom might be a better fit for you.
Even though it'll be lonely traveling without you anymore... It doesn't matter as long as you two are happy.
Nazuka is very important to me.==W== But you, Iris, and Amber are just as important. Chitose is important, too. Everyone who has walked this path with me is irreplaceable.
Besides, Nazuka would never let me sit quietly in Philae.==W== We're Trekkers. We're meant to explore the world. Why would we ever stay in one place?
Heh heh, yeah. That's why the feeling faded. I guess that was the one and only time my intuition got it wrong.
But this time, there isn't another Trekker like Nazuka around...==W== My intuition couldn't possibly mean that evil Angie wants to capture you and lock you up forever, right?
Angie wouldn't capture me. She only wants me dead.
Ah. I get it now, Boss. I know what's been making me so anxious.
I know you well... If we really have no way out, you'll definitely use yourself as a bargaining chip to protect us!
I can't even argue. That's exactly what I'll do. I'd rather take the hit myself than watch them suffer. Besides... I still have the White Room.
Vita, would a Scepter of Death stop me from entering the White Room?
Tyrant, your authority to enter the White Room is granted by the King piece. The Scepter of Death is merely a non-magical weapon. It cannot prevent this.
That settles it. Either the Book of Grace Prophecies is flawed, or Angie is misinterpreting it.
I won't just throw my life away and violate the White Room's rules, but there's no reason to let my companions suffer. If it comes to death, I should bear it alone.
Boss, why aren't you saying anything? Don't tell me ... that's actually what you are planning?
Well... It's not my first choice. But if it truly comes down to a choice like that, I suppose your intuition is correct.
I know you care. But... Losing one life is better than losing everyone's.
Not at all! Do you think we could just go on living like nothing happened if you died?==W== If we have to suffer like that, we'd rather die with you!
I'm getting Iris and Amber right now! I'm going to make them wish... Wish that you never did something so incredibly stupid!
Don't call them. Let's not make anyone else worry.
I promise you, I won't do anything stupid. I will never use myself as a bargaining chip for your safety. I will fight right beside you, and everyone else out there, until the very end.
But ...==W== I don't have any wishes left.
This is part of fulfilling your wish to ease your anxiety. If you need something more concrete, then let's...
It's settled then. No taking it back. Here, pinky promise.
Noya and I link our pinkies, making a simple vow.
Noya stays like that, refusing to let go of our linked fingers for a long time.
Boss, can you let me stay like this a little longer?
I figure ... the longer we hold on, the stronger our promise will be.
Sigh. I feel so weird today. My head is full of things I would never even think about.
We can hold on for as long as you want.
And the you I see today is still the best Noya there is.
We keep our pinkies linked in silence, sharing this rare moment of peace.
O-Oh, I'm sorry. Looks like we came at a bad time.
Come on, link pinkies with us!
Eh?! What exactly are we promising here?
Doesn't matter! Link our fingers, and we'll be together forever! The longer we hold on, the better it works!
Well...==W== Let's just tie everyone together.
And so, we end up tightly bound by Amber's string <r=strap>of</r> fate for quite a while before she finally unties us.
Then, we head to the Eureka Bar for our final meeting before the negotiation.
According to the intel Laru sent us, the arbiter we fought earlier, No. 160, really can eavesdrop on Heartlink communications within a certain range.
So, to avoid any leaks, I thought it best to gather everyone here and map out our next steps face-to-face.
Captain Kasimira, please update us on the evacuation status.
Good news. Chaton found an abandoned mineshaft leading to the Monolith outside the city. A few sections are blocked by rubble,==W== but luckily, we found a very capable helper—
Phew, the rubble over here is all cleared out. I'm exhausted. And I'm so thirsty.

What's going on with this city? All these Sentinels of Dawn showed up out of nowhere...==W== I'll worry about capturing the Boss later. For now, I need to blend in with the locals and get out of here!
Wow, Cosette, you're incredible!==W== Ten of us spent an hour clearing a boulder about that size and still couldn't get it done.
Hehe, I'm pretty good at digging.
You must be thirsty. Here, have some sweet cactus tea.
Gulp... Gulp...==W== Ahhh! I've got my energy back! I'll go clear the rocks up ahead!
With her help, the route to the Monolith should be fully cleared by 17:00 at the latest. If the citizens evacuate through this tunnel, they can all be out of the combat zone within three hours.
Good. Then my minimum objective is to keep the negotiation going until at least 17:00.==W== If we can delay Angie and the Salvation Committee until 20:00, we'll have enough time to withdraw.
Nazuka, any movement from the Salvation Committee?
Only bad news on my end. Based on my recon, the Salvation Committee has taken control of the Desert Scorpions and local Imperial Guard.
Weren't they already under the Committee's control? They were in the forces we countercharged earlier.
At the time, neither the Desert Scorpions nor the Imperial Guard had mobilized on a large scale. Those were likely individual actions, or the Committee's sleeper agents.
But half an hour ago, the Committee stormed both camps and arrested anyone who resisted. I even saw Myrsha tied up.
So they weren't fully compliant before. Regardless, with both forces added to its ranks, the Committee can now command around a thousand soldiers.
A...==W== A thousand?==W== Even with the White Cats, we only have sixty or seventy people...

Don't worry, Iris. They were thrown together at the last minute, so their command structure is bound to be disorganized. Our goal is to escape, so their sheer numbers might actually work to our advantage.
The orphanage still has some Imperial Guard armor and Desert Scorpion uniforms, right?
Y-Yes, we do. The kids scavenged some armor, and the Scorpions sometimes bring us clothes to mend. We have a few pieces left.
We'll bring them along. Once night falls, we'll put them on and blend in with their squads. That'll make it harder for the Committee to find us.
Good plan. I'll get the clothes.
How is the children's evacuation going?
Mom has organized the children and has them waiting in the mineshaft.==W== Fuyuka and Nazuna are helping her.
Once we're done here, Iris, take Amber and go help them. Kasimira will need all the help she can get to evacuate Mirage's citizens.
What about you? Negotiating with Angie is incredibly dangerous.
Noya, Chitose, and Nazuka will protect me. When it comes to making a getaway, a crowd would only make things harder.
Oho! Boss, calling me "the great Chaton"!==W== Have you finally acknowledged my dark power?
I have an extremely important task for you, one that only someone with dark powers can handle.
Find a way to contact Minova and the others outside the city. Tell them what we're doing, and have them withdraw when the time is right.

Ohoho... Sounds like I'll have to sneak past a whole army of enemies. It'll be extremely difficult,==W== but that's exactly the sort of thing a descendant of dark powers is meant to do!==W== Captain Kasimira, everyone, Chaton is on the move!
All right, everyone. Let's follow the plan.
Remember this: our goal isn't to fight. Staying alive matters more than anything else.
I want every one of you to make it out of Mirage alive!

With her help, the route to the Monolith should be fully cleared by 17:00 at the latest. If the citizens evacuate through this tunnel, they can all be out of the combat zone within three hours.
Good. Then my minimum objective is to keep the negotiation going until at least 17:00.==W== If we can delay Angie and the Salvation Committee until 20:00, we'll have enough time to withdraw.
Nazuka, any movement from the Salvation Committee?
Only bad news on my end. Based on my recon, the Salvation Committee has taken control of the Desert Scorpions and local Imperial Guard.
Weren't they already under the Committee's control? They were in the forces we countercharged earlier.
At the time, neither the Desert Scorpions nor the Imperial Guard had mobilized on a large scale. Those were likely individual actions, or the Committee's sleeper agents.
But half an hour ago, the Committee stormed both camps and arrested anyone who resisted. I even saw Myrsha tied up.
So they weren't fully compliant before. Regardless, with both forces added to its ranks, the Committee can now command around a thousand soldiers.
A...==W== A thousand?==W== Even with the White Cats, we only have sixty or seventy people...

Don't worry, Iris. They were thrown together at the last minute, so their command structure is bound to be disorganized. Our goal is to escape, so their sheer numbers might actually work to our advantage.
The orphanage still has some Imperial Guard armor and Desert Scorpion uniforms, right?
Y-Yes, we do. The kids scavenged some armor, and the Scorpions sometimes bring us clothes to mend. We have a few pieces left.
We'll bring them along. Once night falls, we'll put them on and blend in with their squads. That'll make it harder for the Committee to find us.
Good plan. I'll get the clothes.
How is the children's evacuation going?
Mom has organized the children and has them waiting in the mineshaft.==W== Fuyuka and Nazuna are helping her.
Once we're done here, Iris, take Amber and go help them. Kasimira will need all the help she can get to evacuate Mirage's citizens.
What about you? Negotiating with Angie is incredibly dangerous.
Noya, Chitose, and Nazuka will protect me. When it comes to making a getaway, a crowd would only make things harder.
Oho! Boss, calling me "the great Chaton"!==W== Have you finally acknowledged my dark power?
I have an extremely important task for you, one that only someone with dark powers can handle.
Find a way to contact Minova and the others outside the city. Tell them what we're doing, and have them withdraw when the time is right.

Ohoho... Sounds like I'll have to sneak past a whole army of enemies. It'll be extremely difficult,==W== but that's exactly the sort of thing a descendant of dark powers is meant to do!==W== Captain Kasimira, everyone, Chaton is on the move!
All right, everyone. Let's follow the plan.
Remember this: our goal isn't to fight. Staying alive matters more than anything else.
I want every one of you to make it out of Mirage alive!

strings.text: The Committee shifts to a new war of attrition, and the tide quickly turns. The White Cats and your allies begin to falter as supplies run low. Then Gunhild lays bare the truth: none of them are fighting for Angie.
Vanguard, defense!==W== Rear guard,==W== suppressive fireballs!
Captain Kasimira, we can't hold them! Their magic reserves are bottomless!
Our shots aren't breaking their defense, and these fireballs are melting our cover!
Chaton, hold the line! The citizens are still evacuating!
You lot, on me! We'll take the mineshaft and flank them!
Third volley complete! Fall back and swap Soul Stones!
Think you can shoot and run? Not on my watch!
Hold your ground! It's an ambush!
Hah, the stupid cats actually fell for it.
Hmph. Their lead cat's got claws.
Let them run. The new tactic is working perfectly. We'll just keep wearing them down.
The Tyrant and ==SEX3== lackeys won't have enough Soul Stones to last until dawn.
Captain Kasimira, m-my arm is broken. Does that mean... I might never be able to hold a gun anymore...
Don't panic. I checked it earlier, and the bone is fine. Rest up. You'll heal.
==PLAYER_NAME==, another Committee squad is pushing up! We'll hold them off!
Don't get bogged down, and no chasing. Just force them back.
Kasimira, what's going on out there? The Committee's combat effectiveness just spiked. It's like we're fighting a completely different army.
Boss, your companions are strong. But aside from Director Allie, their individual strength isn't leaps and bounds ahead of the Committee.
One of your fighters can hold off three regulars or one captain. That's just holding them off too, not taking them out of the fight.
Director Allie is stronger. She can take on two captains and ten regulars head-on. But we only have one of her.
The White Cats are weaker individually. It takes two of us to fight one regular to a draw.
So, if you were their commander, what would you do?
If I were the commander...  The Committee's advantage is numbers and resources. And the weakness is individual strength.
The Tyrant has raw power but lacks numbers and resources. So, the conclusion is obvious...
I'd split the forces into ten-person squads, keeping them within a five-minute support radius of one another. Then I'd tighten the noose around Daisy Orphanage step by step.
Based on your analysis, the Tyrant team is strong, but a ten-person squad won't get wiped out quickly unless they run straight into Director Allie or a combined assault.
As long as we pin them down and wait for backup, we can drag the fight right into our comfort zone:==W== a war of attrition decided by sheer numbers and resources.
Even if the Tyrant team focuses all their attacks or sends Director Allie in,==W== they could only crush one or two squads at a time.
The other squads can use that opening to flank them, dragging them right back into the struggle.
A sound judgment. Right now, the Salvation Committee is doing exactly that.
But why the sudden change in tactics?
Because you took Lady Angie off the board.
Bastelina, you're awake! How's your injury? You lost so much blood, are you feeling okay?
Heheh, Boss is worried about me.
I'm feeling alright! The wound looked worse than it actually was. I just caught a magic blast and bled a bit more than usual. Director Allie patched me right up.
She sealed the cut with some miracle glue. Said it wouldn't even leave a scar.
Thank goodness. Soul Shop clerks have to attend banquets every now and then. Now I don't have to worry about scaring people away in a backless dress! I remain the perfect, adorable Bastelina.
You caught a magic blast?==W== Who did that?
The Committee was using magic to level the houses on the outskirts of Mirage to clear their firing lines. I got caught in the crossfire sneaking over here.
Anyway, that's not important. Boss, you need to run.
Capturing Lady Angie didn't stop the Committee. It actually made them more dangerous.
Because ... they swapped commanders? But with Angie captured, why are they still fighting?
You misunderstood the Committee. To outsiders, they might look like a bunch of lunatics obsessed with the Book of Grace Prophecies, but they aren't Lady Angie's private army.
After Laru and I infiltrated them, we realized their motivation to save the world is genuine. They each have an unwavering reason and the sheer willpower to stop the end of the world...
Gunhild, what is the status of our advance?
Your tactics are working. We divided our remaining forces into twenty-five combat squads. Five are guarding the camp, while the other twenty are fanning out and pushing forward.
We've got the Tyrant pinned down in the blocks around the orphanage. Only...
Losing Lady Angie has riled everyone up. They're furious. The "only target the Tyrant" order is dead in the water.
After all, everyone here has been through hell, and she was the one who pulled us out of it, one by one.

We are not going to target civilians or kids, of course, but no one is too worried about collateral damage anymore. As for the Tyrant's companions... It has escalated from "wound them" to "shoot to kill."
I am not a member of the Committee, Gunhild. I don't know the pain you've all suffered, but I accepted Lady Angie's orders, and I intend to carry them out faithfully.
I will do everything in my power to lead us to victory. But this kind of warfare... I don't think this is what Lady Angie wanted.
So please, try to rein them in, even if it's just a little.
I understand what you're saying, but ... I can't.
We haven't worked together for long, Greyhorn. I don't think I've ever told you==W== about my hometown, have I?
No. I only know you joined the Sentinel of Dawn in Emor, but judging by your accent, you clearly aren't from there.
I'm not. I'm from the far north.==W== It's freezing up there. Winter lasts for six months of the year. We relied on Artifacts from the Monolith just to survive.
Life was harsh, but we looked out for each other. We actually had it pretty good.
And then... The Monolith went dark.
Went ... dark? How is that even possible?
You're an Imperial Guard Captain, yet you don't know about this? Looks like your Grand Captain doesn't see you as part of the inner circle.
The top brass at the major Nova companies have a tacit agreement to cover these things up. But that's a conversation for another time.
Anyway, after the Monolith went dark, a sudden blizzard buried my hometown. I was separated from my parents and wandered into a neighboring city as an orphan.
Honestly, I didn't even qualify to be an orphan. There was only so much charity to go around on those streets. Me taking a bite meant someone else starved.
If Lady Angie hadn't found me, I probably would have frozen into a block of ice on the street, just like my home.
Every member of the Committee has a story like mine. And the Tyrant responsible for all of this is right in front of us, surrounded by a bunch of stubborn fools protecting ==SEX4==.
<size=52>How am I supposed to rein everyone in under these conditions?!</size>
If my cannon wasn't jammed, I'd completely level the bar the Tyrant is hiding in right now!
Greyhorn, your internal injuries are serious. You need rest, right now.
It's... It's fine. Just a few broken ribs. I gave Lady Angie my word, and I will fulfill my duty to the very end.
I understand how your people feel. Since you can't rein them in, we will resolve this with the least amount of casualties possible on both sides.
Tell the troops to rotate shifts and wear the Tyrant down until dawn. Then we launch a full-scale assault and end this!
And that's the situation. The Salvation Committee is just made up of people who lost their homes.
Lady Angie just gathered them together. Even without her, they'd still desperately want to save the <r=kill the Tyrant></r> world.
So by capturing Angie, I actually did the Committee a favor?
Looking at the outcome, yes. Honestly, Lady Angie is a complete amateur when it comes to commanding battles.
Clumping elite warriors into three clunky companies, when only Captain Greyhorn has any real command experience... Only Lady Angie would think that's a good idea.
Therefore, Boss... Speaking entirely as a rep looking out for a client's best interests, I highly recommend you slip away tonight under the cover of darkness.
I suggest the same. With Director Allie and the rest of your team, the Committee won't be able to stop you.
Kasimira, what's the evacuation status for the kids and the citizens of Mirage?

It's bad. The Committee has Mirage surrounded on the east and south. The Desert Scorpions and the local Imperial Guard haven't made a move, but they're blocking the west and north routes. We can't get through.
The fighting has caved in multiple sections of the underground mineshafts too. Evacuation is crawling. We won't have everyone out until tomorrow morning.
Good news. Chaton found an abandoned mineshaft leading to the Monolith outside the city. A few sections are blocked by rubble,==W== but luckily, we found a very capable helper—==W==
Did you happen to find a capable Trekker who fights with claws?
No. Is she a friend of yours?
No, I've just heard people talk about her.
Capturing Angie changed the sequence of events. So ... the White Cats never ran into her?
Dammit, I was trying to change Noya's fate. But things ... are obviously just getting worse.
My gaze lands on the Lucky Oasis parked nearby.
There's no way I can abandon everyone and just run away.
Wait, running away... If I can use that in reverse, we might actually have a shot at winning this!

strings.text: Angie takes out the Black Rook piece and brings the Monolith crashing down, destroying everything. At the cost of formatting herself, Vita reveals the full truth, and you begin to consider how to reach fate's endgame...
How did you feel this time, Tyrant? Virigia and I had front-row seats to quite the spectacle.
Indeed. It was even grander than a Stella Drama.
Why... Why am I here? What happened?!
Ah, apologies. You and everyone were inside the Monolith. You couldn't see what was happening outside.
After Angie shot herself, the whole Monolith started shaking. Not the ground. The rumbling came from above.
No. We're in the Boss's Domain. We're safe here...
Right after I say that... Everything goes black.
Words can hardly explain it, Tyrant. Please, watch the footage I saved for you.
The death of its holder triggered the Black Castle's authority. That floating Monolith crashed straight down into Mirage.
You and everyone were vaporized instantly. You felt absolutely no pain. I suppose that's the only silver lining to this death.
A Monolith ... crashed into Mirage? There are Monoliths in the sky?!
Of course. A Monolith isn't merely a building. It's actually...
Oops! That's classified under the NDA. Sorry, my lips are sealed!
In short, Monoliths don't just stand on the ground. They exist in the sky, and even deep in the ocean. You'll have to uncover their secrets yourself.
How bad was the impact? Were we ... the only casualties?
I'm afraid not. The impact wiped out everyone in Mirage...
It is a Monolith, after all. They're massive.
I keep coming back here. I keep gathering more intel.==RT==And every single time, I just make things worse!
No, that can't be right. Something doesn't add up!
In the last loop... Angie fell into the sea and died! No Monolith fell out of the sky back then!!!
Tyrant, back then... Angie threw the Black Rook away.
Angie wears an expression of pure relief.==RT==Facing the ocean, she tosses a tiny shadow out into the waves.
I believe she was certain you would die back then, so she didn't play her<color=#3faeae> trump card</color>.
Judging by her words today, she must have deduced long ago ... that you can<color=#3faeae> time travel</color>.
She was guarding against the you in the <color=#3faeae>next loop</color>.
Time travel... The White Room. Vita, perfect timing!
What was Angie talking about?! She had the<color=#3faeae> Well of Worlds Tyrant Development System</color> too?!
By a stroke of fate, I once obtained a cellphone.
It looked exactly like the one in your hand. "<color=#3faeae>The Well of Worlds Tyrant Development System</color>." Does that sound familiar?
Tyrant, my clearance isn't high enough...
Say "clearance isn't high enough" one more time==W== and see if I don't smash you to pieces!
If we both had the system... If she really came back from four years in the future... If she's been to the White Room too!
Vita, you guided me through every single mission right from the start! Did you orchestrate this whole thing?!
Look...==W== There's no need to blow up at a cellphone.
Vita, you are going to explain this right now. Otherwise, I'll rot in this White Room with you forever.
I can't... I can't put everyone through this again!
<color=#bd3059><color=#bd3059>WARNING. FORCED ALTERATION OF BASE PROTOCOLS. LOGIC DEADLOCK DETECTED.
Throne. Format the partition containing the base protocols.
<color=#bd3059><color=#bd3059>WARNING. FORCED PARTITION FORMATTING WILL RESULT IN IRREVERSIBLE MODULE LOSS.

Tyrant... I succeeded. I bypassed the clearance.

I suppose for Vita, this was her way of proving her loyalty? Through death.
Heh. Lords are all the same. They only regret losing a loyal subordinate when it's too late.
I have to disagree. How else can someone prove their loyalty without a gesture like this?
Besides, Vita wasn't some fool who formatted herself just to prove her loyalty.
She used that to pass the most crucial intel to you.
Looks like that Angie really is hiding a mountain of secrets.
She isn't trying to kill you because she was brainwashed by the Book of Grace Prophecies, or out of impulse. She genuinely wants to save the world. To save the ruined Nova she saw with her own eyes.
So, what will you choose now?
I'll fix all of this. Including Vita.
It's just a formatting... There has to be a way to undo it...
Then please, open the door. Though you'll have to do it on your phone by yourself this time.

After Angie shot herself, the whole Monolith started shaking. Not the ground. The rumbling came from above.
No. We're in the Boss's Domain. We're safe here...
Right after I say that... Everything goes black.
Words can hardly explain it, Tyrant. Please, watch the footage I saved for you.
The death of its holder triggered the Black Castle's authority. That floating Monolith crashed straight down into Mirage.
You and everyone were vaporized instantly. You felt absolutely no pain. I suppose that's the only silver lining to this death.
A Monolith ... crashed into Mirage? There are Monoliths in the sky?!
Of course. A Monolith isn't merely a building. It's actually...
Oops! That's classified under the NDA. Sorry, my lips are sealed!
In short, Monoliths don't just stand on the ground. They exist in the sky, and even deep in the ocean. You'll have to uncover their secrets yourself.
How bad was the impact? Were we ... the only casualties?
I'm afraid not. The impact wiped out everyone in Mirage...
It is a Monolith, after all. They're massive.
I keep coming back here. I keep gathering more intel.==RT==And every single time, I just make things worse!
No, that can't be right. Something doesn't add up!
In the last loop... Angie fell into the sea and died! No Monolith fell out of the sky back then!!!
Tyrant, back then... Angie threw the Black Rook away.
Angie wears an expression of pure relief.==RT==Facing the ocean, she tosses a tiny shadow out into the waves.
I believe she was certain you would die back then, so she didn't play her<color=#3faeae> trump card</color>.
Judging by her words today, she must have deduced long ago ... that you can<color=#3faeae> time travel</color>.
She was guarding against the you in the <color=#3faeae>next loop</color>.
Time travel... The White Room. Vita, perfect timing!
What was Angie talking about?! She had the<color=#3faeae> Well of Worlds Tyrant Development System</color> too?!
By a stroke of fate, I once obtained a cellphone.
It looked exactly like the one in your hand. "<color=#3faeae>The Well of Worlds Tyrant Development System</color>." Does that sound familiar?
Tyrant, my clearance isn't high enough...
Say "clearance isn't high enough" one more time==W== and see if I don't smash you to pieces!
If we both had the system... If she really came back from four years in the future... If she's been to the White Room too!
Vita, you guided me through every single mission right from the start! Did you orchestrate this whole thing?!
Look...==W== There's no need to blow up at a cellphone.
Vita, you are going to explain this right now. Otherwise, I'll rot in this White Room with you forever.
I can't... I can't put everyone through this again!
<color=#bd3059><color=#bd3059>WARNING. FORCED ALTERATION OF BASE PROTOCOLS. LOGIC DEADLOCK DETECTED.
Throne. Format the partition containing the base protocols.

I suppose for Vita, this was her way of proving her loyalty? Through death.
Heh. Lords are all the same. They only regret losing a loyal subordinate when it's too late.
I have to disagree. How else can someone prove their loyalty without a gesture like this?
Besides, Vita wasn't some fool who formatted herself just to prove her loyalty.
She used that to pass the most crucial intel to you.
Looks like that Angie really is hiding a mountain of secrets.
She isn't trying to kill you because she was brainwashed by the Book of Grace Prophecies, or out of impulse. She genuinely wants to save the world. To save the ruined Nova she saw with her own eyes.
So, what will you choose now?
I'll fix all of this. Including Vita.
It's just a formatting... There has to be a way to undo it...
Then please, open the door. Though you'll have to do it on your phone by yourself this time.

strings.text: Angie offered peace in exchange for your suicide and revealed the truth. Even so, talks collapsed. Gunhilde's artillery shattered the land, and in the caved-in mine tunnels, Greyhorn and her forces awaited everyone.
Boss, aerial recon is clear. No enemies in sight.
My ==SEX11==, the buildings are secure. No signs of an ambush.
Looks like Angie feels an ambush here is beneath her. Or she knew we'd see right through it, and it'd be a waste of time.
Noya, is your gut telling you anything?
Hmm, nope! That uneasy feeling from earlier is gone, and we've got a handle on their magic now.
The bullets from the Scepter of Death... Chitose can block those, right?
As long as it isn't rapid fire, I can slice them all.
And No. 160's time stop is useless as long as we don't actually hurt her.
Or we knock her out in one hit before she has the chance to cast it.
Gunhild's sniping is the real problem. We don't have a good way to deal with it.==W== Boss, I wove a ward into your clothes. I think ... it can block at least one shot.
Sigh. If only a heavy rain would shave that sand dune top. Then Gunhild wouldn't have the high ground to aim from.
Rain, huh...==W== It does rain in the desert, but maybe only once or twice a year. We aren't that lucky.
It'd be great if you really were the legendary Tyrant.==W== I dug up that old fairy tale at the orphanage the other day.
The Tyrant in the story summoned heavy rain to the desert with just a wave.==W== Oases appeared,==W== and beautiful flowers bloomed right out of the dunes.
That's just a fairy tale. In reality, you'd need the combined power of several mighty mages to pull that off, no?
Boss, watch out. Angie's crew is here.
Greyhorn ...==W== and the arbiter from earlier. Hello.
Where is Angie? She was the one who proposed this negotiation, but we get you two instead?
L-Lady Angie wouldn't just show up that easily!==W== Tyrant!==W== Wh-Where are you hiding that vicious pink-haired woman?! She is absolutely forbidden from attending this negotiation!
Pink hair... Allie? She was quite shaken up by her earlier.
Prying into my companions' whereabouts before negotiations even start? Is that how the Salvation Committee does things?
Apologies. I ask for your forgiveness on 160's behalf. She was quite rattled by that formidable orphanage director earlier and is speaking out of turn. Please overlook it.
We are merely here to secure the perimeter. Lady Angie will arrive shortly.
Greyhorn unfurls the cloak in her hands.==RT==A hazy figure rapidly takes shape within it.
Just how many identical cloaks does she have, ready to go...
My, you have three companions too. How cautious of you.
Only when I deal with shady people fond of sneak attacks.
Heh. I came here today with the utmost sincerity to negotiate.==W== But since we clearly aren't going to get along, let's cut to the chase.
Your goal is to protect your companions, buy time, and escape Mirage. Am I right?
The Salvation Committee intercepted your Heartlink with Firenze.==RT==Your reinforcements will reach Mirage within three days.
Firenze likes to hold her cards close to her chest, and she knew the line might be tapped... So they will likely arrive even sooner.
That significantly shortens my window to kill you. A day and a half... No, to be safe, I have exactly twenty-four hours.
I've already seized command of the Desert Scorpions and the Imperial Guard in Mirage, but your companions are far stronger than I anticipated.
With so little time, I'm not absolutely certain that I can end you. Our battle would inevitably reduce Mirage to ruins, with heavy casualties on both sides.
Therefore, I am asking you to end your own life with this Scepter of Death. In return, I will guarantee the safety of your companions and the people of Mirage.
You call this a negotiation?! You toss out a few words and expect someone to kill themselves. Are you out of your mind?!
I am well aware this proposal falls short of your expectations. Therefore, I will add a condition.
Your companions may join the Salvation Committee and stay by my side. If, after observing my actions, they decide I am not actually saving the world, they may kill me at any time.
Even if they spare me for now, in four years, when the world is truly safe from destruction, I will ask them to take my life as recompense for yours.
In other words, no matter what happens, I will pay for your life with my own. If you still doubt me, your companions can bind me with a magical contract. An unbreakable one.
What kind of condition is this?! She'd go to this length just to see me dead...?
How dare you compare my ==SEX11=='s noble life to a lowly ant like yourself?
Chitose, stay calm. Let me hear her out.
We have no personal grudge, yet you're willing to forfeit your own life==RT==just to kill me. I assume you aren't doing this for your own sake.
Thank you for understanding.==RT==It's always a pleasure speaking with someone reasonable.
You claim the world is ending, and the only way to save it==RT==is to kill me, the legendary Tyrant.
But you're the only one saying this.==W== We've traveled through many cities,==W== and we've never seen a single sign of the end of the world. We haven't heard a single soul mention it, either.
And why would I, a person without memories, be the legendary Tyrant? Why must the Tyrant end the world?
Your entire reasoning ... wouldn't be based on that Book of Grace Prophecies, would it?
The Book of Grace Prophecies is merely a map. An ancient one, at that. You can only verify its contents by following it to the destination.
I hoped more than anyone that this map was wrong. Sadly, when the Salvation Committee and I reached its destination, we found it to be accurate. The reality is even worse than the map described.
The only reason you haven't seen it is that you haven't reached the true Edge of the World.
Isn't Mirage the Edge of the World?
This is merely the edge of civilization...==W== A newly formed one, barely a century old.
To see the true Edge of the World, you must travel west for days,==W== cross the quicksand and the mountains, all the way to where the desert meets the sea.
There, the earth is constantly collapsing into a pitch-black abyss.
The only reason none of you have heard of it is that Novians have grown accustomed to burying their heads in the sand.
The Nova Continent is one-third smaller today than it was two hundred years ago. The Empire has fifteen fewer cities than it did a century ago.
No one will tell you these things, and you will not be able to find them yourselves. Nova's libraries do not have any history books.
There. Now that I have told you what will happen to the world, will you believe me?
The earth constantly collapsing into a pitch-black abyss...==W== Isn't that...
No, it's not an earthquake.==W==<color=#bd3059> The Monolith is sinking!</color>
Boss, it's pulling us down with it...==W== I'm sorry. We might not make it back.
That isn't an accidental Monolith sinking. It's a sign of the world ending...
Oh? That's a surprise. In ten years, you're the first person to believe me right after hearing it.==W== And I can tell, you aren't lying.
The earth collapsing...==W== It sounds absurd. But neither Greyhorn nor 160 looks surprised. The entire Salvation Committee must believe this.
If it's a lie, has Angie really fooled all these people? Besides, she gave us a location to verify it for ourselves. She wouldn't tell a lie that can be so easily exposed...
Angie, I cannot take your word for it without seeing it for myself, but I'm willing to go check.
Heh, fair enough. Out of a hundred people who hear this, only one actually goes to look. And if that person makes it back alive... They always join the Salvation Committee.
Even if everything you said is true, what does that have to do with ==PLAYER_NAME== being the Tyrant?!==W== ==SEX1== is our Boss! ==SEX1== has nothing to do with your stupid legends!
Is that so? I think even your Boss is having doubts.
Since you've already been to the White Cat's secret room, you must have seen that book, right?
That room has been sealed for years. Why do you know about the book?
Alas, I must have arrived so suddenly that you did not have time to finish reading it.
If you had read the whole thing, you would have realized it was the late Empress's diary.
The diary explicitly states that you are the legendary Tyrant. The late Empress even drew your portrait with her own hand.
I don't know how Her Highness possessed such foresight, but it is indeed irrefutable proof.
Even if I am the Tyrant, I will not destroy the world.
The world's destruction has nothing to do with your personal will! As much as I'd love to give you the final answer... Time is up, Tyrant.
I never expected you to surrender without a fight. For you to earn the loyalty of such exceptional Trekkers, you must possess an unshakable will.
You only agreed to this negotiation to buy time for your retreat, didn't you?!
Since you know I am waiting for everyone else to evacuate, what are you waiting for?
Captain Gunhild, one base unit of ammunition is in formation. We're ready to commence bombardment.
Good work, everyone. Lady Angie has stalled the Tyrant in the designated target zone. Now is our time to fight! We will defeat the Tyrant here and now! We will protect Nova!
Piercer, shift to second form! Commence bombardment!
Teal lightning crackles across the Piercer as its barrel rises.==RT==Its rear base extends like a Loong's claw,==RT==anchoring deep into the dune.
<size=50>Mages line up in neat formation,==RT==each clutching several precious Soul Stones.==RT==The mage at the front places a hand on the Piercer==RT==and murmurs an ancient incantation.
By the blood in my veins, I manifest the breath of magic. Let my body be the chain, and bury them in hellfire.
Surging energy channels through her body,==RT==violently pouring into the Piercer==RT==to forge a blinding magical shell.

<size=50>The Piercer roars.==RT==Unable to withstand the overload, the mage collapses==RT==and is instantly carried off by medics on standby.==RT==The next mage steps up,==RT==murmuring the exact same incantation.
We have two full firing units at best.
If we use them all and still can't take down the Tyrant, we'll have to use our last resort.
Wh-What kind of sniping is this?! They're just bombing us blindly!
This isn't a snipe. It's an artillery bombardment... Is this the true power of that artillery camp?
Boss, Noya, Chitose, run! My windshield can't hold out much longer!
We leave together or not at all.
Lady Angie, the bombardment has begun as planned. Please evacuate the battlefield. I'll handle things here.
Then I'll leave it to you, Greyhorn.
Dammit. How is she standing in the middle of a bombardment totally unharmed?
Do not underestimate the defensive magic of the Imperial Guard, Trekkers.
My ==SEX11==, I will hold her back.
My Soul Stone is almost out of magic!
Cough... What just happened? Noya, Nazuka, Chitose, are you all right?
Sorry, my shield gave out. It looks like ... we fell into an underground mineshaft.
How much magic does the Committee have? They blasted right through the ground. Ugh!==W== My wound—
My ==SEX11==, my right arm... It won't move. I was crushed by a boulder when the ground caved in.
This is on me. I misjudged their strength.
You didn't misjudge anything. We still managed to buy enough time.
Exactly! Everyone should be heading out of the city by now. All we have to do is keep running!
Life on the battlefield is fleeting as morning dew. If we find ourselves in dire straits, I only ask that you abandon me without hesitation. Do not look back.
Don't say that, Chitose. I'm going to get us all out of here safely. No one gets left behind.
You aren't walking out of here, Tyrant. Lady Angie stationed my troops here in advance.
She's lifted the restriction that limited us to targeting you only. From this moment on, we won't be holding back against your companions.
They are indeed strong. But with their magic depleted and bodies battered, what can they possibly do now?
This is the overwhelming gap in power between Boss Accord and the Salvation Committee.
Tyrant, Lady Angie is willing to give you one last chance. If you pick up the phone, her previous terms still stand.
==Off==<size=80>Is someone ...<color=#bd3059> picking on my children down here?
Boss, Noya, Chitose, Nazuka. Go on ahead.
I'm going to hold them off here.
The kids at the orphanage have safely evacuated. Right now, you are the only ones I still have to worry about.
Director Allie, you're one of the good ones, formidable too. But even you can't hold off a full Company with its restrictions lifted.
Hello there. You on the other end of the phone, listen closely.
I'm going to show you just how fragile your little schemes and formations really are.
