Surging energy channels through her body,==RT==violently pouring into the Piercer==RT==to forge a blinding magical shell.

<size=50>The Piercer roars.==RT==Unable to withstand the overload, the mage collapses==RT==and is instantly carried off by medics on standby.==RT==The next mage steps up,==RT==murmuring the exact same incantation.
We have two full firing units at best.
If we use them all and still can't take down the Tyrant, we'll have to use our last resort.
Wh-What kind of sniping is this?! They're just bombing us blindly!
This isn't a snipe. It's an artillery bombardment... Is this the true power of that artillery camp?
Boss, Noya, Chitose, run! My windshield can't hold out much longer!
We leave together or not at all.
Lady Angie, the bombardment has begun as planned. Please evacuate the battlefield. I'll handle things here.
Then I'll leave it to you, Greyhorn.
Dammit. How is she standing in the middle of a bombardment totally unharmed?
Do not underestimate the defensive magic of the Imperial Guard, Trekkers.
My ==SEX11==, I will hold her back.
My Soul Stone is almost out of magic!
Cough... What just happened? Noya, Nazuka, Chitose, are you all right?
Sorry, my shield gave out. It looks like ... we fell into an underground mineshaft.
How much magic does the Committee have? They blasted right through the ground. Ugh!==W== My wound—
My ==SEX11==, my right arm... It won't move. I was crushed by a boulder when the ground caved in.
This is on me. I misjudged their strength.
You didn't misjudge anything. We still managed to buy enough time.
Exactly! Everyone should be heading out of the city by now. All we have to do is keep running!
Life on the battlefield is fleeting as morning dew. If we find ourselves in dire straits, I only ask that you abandon me without hesitation. Do not look back.
Don't say that, Chitose. I'm going to get us all out of here safely. No one gets left behind.
You aren't walking out of here, Tyrant. Lady Angie stationed my troops here in advance.
She's lifted the restriction that limited us to targeting you only. From this moment on, we won't be holding back against your companions.
They are indeed strong. But with their magic depleted and bodies battered, what can they possibly do now?
This is the overwhelming gap in power between Boss Accord and the Salvation Committee.
Tyrant, Lady Angie is willing to give you one last chance. If you pick up the phone, her previous terms still stand.
==Off==<size=80>Is someone ...<color=#bd3059> picking on my children down here?
Boss, Noya, Chitose, Nazuka. Go on ahead.
I'm going to hold them off here.
The kids at the orphanage have safely evacuated. Right now, you are the only ones I still have to worry about.
Director Allie, you're one of the good ones, formidable too. But even you can't hold off a full Company with its restrictions lifted.
Hello there. You on the other end of the phone, listen closely.
I'm going to show you just how fragile your little schemes and formations really are.

strings.text: You take Angie with you and become the bait yourself, driving Loxy out of the encirclement with the help of the Desert Scorpion. But then this inexplicable "ocean" completely cuts off your last path to survival…
Boss, I have one Soul Stone left. Take it.
Thanks, Benito.==W== But don't you need to keep a few?
You're gonna push the Lucky Oasis to the limit! Stop being so polite and take it!
That's not the issue.==W== If the Committee attacks again and you're out of stones, can you actually hold them off?
Relax. Allie just evacuated the kids into the White Cats' secret room. It's secure and well-ventilated. Even the Committee isn't getting in without that nursery rhyme.
Don't worry about the kids. Once you break through, we'll have a lot more room to breathe.==W== We can just play hide-and-seek with the Committee through the streets and mineshafts.
Hehehe. The great Chaton has never lost a game of hide-and-seek.==W== Just watch me run circles around them with my dark power!
Boss... Are you seriously still worrying about us at a time like this?
You and the New Star Guild are the ones taking on the most risk here.
Honestly, you always come up with these reckless plans without a single thought for your own safety!==W==<size=50> I really don't know how your brain works!</size>
Because this gives us the best chance of getting everyone out alive.
If we stay in Mirage, the Committee will bleed us dry before morning.
Bastelina suggested I just make a run for it. I'd never do that, of course, but it did give me an idea.
Kasimira and I went over our advantages, but there's one major thing we overlooked:==W== the Lucky Oasis's mobility.
The Committee has mages who can fly or enhance their speed, but we didn't bring a single Artifact vehicle into the desert.
The Committee only wants my head and Angie. As long as we're in the same vehicle, they have no choice but to chase us.
And a high-speed desert chase is exactly where we shine.
But an entire army hunting you down...==W== Just let me go with you!
My ==SEX11==, please allow me to accompany you, too.==W== If I cannot be by your side to protect you, my heart ...==W== will simply not know peace.
I know you're worried.==W== But Nazuka, the others still need to hold the line here in Mirage. They need your aerial recon.
And Chitose, you're one of the few fighters here who doesn't rely on magic. They need your blade. Please, keep everyone safe for me.
You...==W== You always have a million perfect reasons to convince us.==W== Come on, Chitose. There's no point arguing with ==SEX4==.==W==
Once ==SEX== breaks out and Mirage is secure, I'll fly us out to find ==SEX4==.
You are correct, Lady Nazuka. I will sever the remaining enemies in Mirage with all haste, and then we shall seek out my ==SEX11== together.
When did those two get along so well...?==W== Well, I guess that's a good thing.
Just ... promise me you won't push yourselves too hard. Every single one of you is important to me.
We know, we know. If things really go south, we'll figure out a way to surrender to that tin can with drafty armor.
Captain Greyhorn is an honorable knight. She won't mistreat any of you.
All right, we're moving out.==W== Iris, get Angie in the car.==W==
Iris shoves a bound Angie into Loxy.==W== I face the setting sun and slam the pedal to the floor.
Captain, we caught someone sneaking around the mineshafts.
A kid? Is she with the Tyrant?
We ...==W== don't think so.==W== She's not on Lady Angie's list, but her magic looks a lot like Nocturn Eterna's.==W== We weren't sure what to make of it, so we brought her to you.
Hmm, she's definitely just a kid at this height.
Hey there, little one. What's your name?==W==
Too scared to speak, huh?==W== Well...==W== Sorry about this, but let me just check your head.
No horns.==W== And the magic is Grace drawn from a Soul Stone.
Oh, come on, look at those innocent eyes. She's not with Nocturn Eterna. She's just a Trekker terrified by you.
Apologize to her, then escort her somewhere safe.
Gunhild, over here. We have a situation.==W== Cough...
Greyhorn, you really need to rest. What could possibly be more important than your health right now?
The Tyrant is fleeing north out of Mirage in a green RV. ==SEX1=='s about to exit the city and pass right by our artillery camp.
I'm only allowed a few sentences. You must stop the Tyrant. Save the world.
It will. I didn't actually expect you to be this cooperative.
A suggestion, if I may. I should sit by the window. That way Gunhild spots me in her scope, and the entire Committee will come after you.
Fine. But don't try anything funny.==W== I have a Scepter of Death pressed right against your spine.
You're doing exactly what I want you to do. Why would I run?
From the very beginning, the only person I've wanted to kill is the Tyrant.

That's exactly why I tried to ambush ==SEX4== in Philae.==W== This way,==W== the only casualties would have been just the two of us.==W== Don't you agree that would have been far better than letting the flames of war consume Mirage?

What twisted logic is that?!==W== None of this would be happening if you weren't so obsessed with that Book of Grace Prophecies!==W== I've looked into it. No one even knows who wrote that book! You have zero proof it's actually real.
I don't base my judgment of ==PLAYER_NAME== solely on the Book of Grace Prophecies.
I've spent days reading every single book on Tyrant legends I could get my hands on!
Go ahead and lay out whatever other reasons you have! I'll debunk every single one of them!
How diligent. I'd genuinely enjoy debating this with you if we had the time.==W== But ...==W== look out the window. My comrades have caught up.
All units, attention! The Tyrant is in that green RV! Blow out the tires!
M-My staff is frozen solid?!==W== How is an ice spell covering this much ground?! Just who the hell is in that car?!
Phew... I haven't actually cast that spell since I learned it. Didn't expect it to work so well.
Wait, why is my Soul Stone empty?!==W== That one spell drained an entire stone's worth of Grace?!
Th-That's such a waste! I've... I've never cast a spell this expensive!
Barreling straight at us just to drop a massive area spell? They're underestimating the Salvation Committee.
Surround them! We're getting Lady Angie back!
Raise the sand walls! Block their path!==W==
Dammit, where did these two Trekkers come from?!==W== Block her shots!
We... We made it through! Thank goodness Noya and Amber cleared a path, or we would've slammed right into that sand wall.
Cough, cough...==W== Well played, Tyrant. You found the fatal flaw in our tactics immediately.
Between the vehicle's speed and their allies running interference, a formation like ours that relies on mutual support gets torn to shreds.
All combat squads, listen up! Raise sand walls on my mark! Don't rush in to attack, box them in first!
Gunhild, those two Trekkers are yours.
Amber leaps from the dune with Noya into the air.
The black straps on her wrists shoot through Loxy's open sunroof, wrapping around the seat handles and pulling themselves into the speeding vehicle.
==PLAYER_NAME==, we're back! We talked to the Desert Scorpions, just like you asked.
And Loxy lured the whole Committee right to us! Now all we have to do is smash through those sand walls, and we win!
Don’t say it like it's no big deal. Looks like they're trying to link those sand walls into a circle to trap us inside.
Which way should I steer, Noya?
Follow your heart! Just steer in the direction you want to go most!
What are you talking about, Noya?! I don't have your intuition!
Noya's warm palm covers my hand, helping me grip the steering wheel tight.
I noticed it the second we left the White Cats' secret room.
You've been ... especially protective of us today.==W== Or, more selfishly, especially protective of me.
I don't know what's going on, but I can feel how anxious you are. Every time we fight, you always make sure we're in the safest possible spot.
But for this final "great escape," you still chose to rely on us.==W== You haven't forgotten ...==W== the promise the four of us made our first night in Mirage.
How am I supposed to say this? How do I explain what happened last time without mentioning the White Room?
Hehe, you don't have to give me an answer right now, ==PLAYER_NAME==. I can wait.
Do you remember that massive Stellaroid we fought at the Waterway?
Of course I do. That was our first time fighting together. Our first real battle.

Facing a monster like that on our first team-up... We were totally reckless.==W== With a power gap like that, anyone else would have said we had zero chance.==W== It was the kind of despair you're never supposed to overcome.
But we had your brains, Iris's caution, Amber's agility, and my intuition!
To hell with despair! We turned the impossible into the possible!
And today won't be any different!
Cap, is doing this actually gonna help the Boss?
Hahaha! Beats me! But that Trekker, Noya, was it? She made a damn good point.
The Scorpions need this turf war over, like yesterday.==W== And if they can't finish it, they need to take it somewhere else. If this keeps up, our crystal diamond mine is gonna cave in.
But earlier, you helped the Committee cast a sandstorm...
That was then, this is now.==W== I thought the Committee was gonna score a quick win, so I tossed a little support their way. I didn't expect the Boss to see right through their whole setup.

Good thing none of the Boss's crew got hurt, so there's no bad blood.==W== Now it's time to flip the script and help them.==W== Of course, we can't let the Committee catch us doing it, or they'll come knocking.
Heads up, here comes the RV!
Golden sands beneath the setting sun, heed my call! Rise and form the dune!
A giant forged of golden sand rises in front of the Committee's sand walls,==W== then immediately collapses, as if the caster had lost control.
I see! The Committee has plenty of magic, which makes breaking those walls impossible. But if someone dumps enough sand to create a makeshift ramp...
Then we can just fly right over them!
Launching off the crest of the dune, the Lucky Oasis traces a perfect arc through the air,==W== sailing right over Greyhorn and Gunhild's heads before touching down in the boundless desert.
Boss, the Dusk Arbiters and I have captured almost the whole Salvation Committee.
Thanks to you running them ragged across the desert, we barely took any casualties. Everyone is safe.
That's a relief.==W== We're running low on Grace, though. Can you send someone to pick us up?
Mistique, Nazuka, and Chitose headed out a few days ago. They brought plenty of Soul Stones.==W== Honestly, you went incredibly far.
We didn't have a choice. We meant to head east and meet up with you after breaking out of Mirage,==W== but Greyhorn cut us off, so we had to gun it northwest.
Judging by the distance, we're practically at the edge of the Nova Continent. Another day or two of driving, and we'd probably hit the ocean.
We've turned back. We should run into the others soon. I'll get in touch with them now.==W== Talk later, Firenze.
We'll be waiting for you, Boss.
We hit a lot of bumps along the way, and even accidentally gave the Committee a "combat boost"...==W== But it's over now.
Once we hand Angie over to the Dusk Arbiters, we can finally go back to our normal lives.
Even now, I haven't given up on killing you.==W== In fact, I remain absolutely certain that I will.
Did I? You'll find out soon enough.
Noya? What's wrong? Why are you braking?
Y-You need to see this...==W== The desert... It's gone.
Is this ...==W== the ocean?! What is an ocean doing in the middle of the desert?
The sea at the end of the desert? But that should be to the west! Noya, are you sure we didn't go the wrong way?
I wouldn't make a rookie mistake like that! Look at the sun. We've been heading east this whole time, tracing our exact route back!
Hey, Nazuka. Where are you all?==W== We hit a snag on our end. It's going to take a while longer to meet up.
Boss, where did you go? We've reached the coastline, and we still haven't found you.
To see the true Edge of the World, you must travel west for days,==W== cross the quicksand and the mountains, all the way to where the desert meets the sea.
There, the earth is constantly collapsing into a pitch-black abyss.
Angie did say that during the negotiation last time...==W== Don't tell me this ocean is...==W== No, it can't be!
Amber, fire a shot straight up. Maximum output.
Boss, I see ... a flash of red light on the horizon. Was that you?==W==
Is my ==SEX11== ...==W== on the other side of the sea?
You did defeat the Salvation Committee, Tyrant. But to think you'd end up trapped here, doomed by the end of the world itself!
It's obvious just looking at it. This strait formed because the earth collapsed while you were deep in the west, and the ocean simply rushed in to fill the void.

The northwest corner of the Nova Continent has no Monolith. It's where the destruction is most severe.==W== You were so focused on leading the Committee to their graves, you never realized you were digging your own.
What are you babbling about? A strait this narrow? We can just fly right over it!
Exactly.==W== Mistique,==W== let's go get them.
No, we can't!==W== We can't fly over the water at all. There is way too much magic in the air here. I can't even steer my broom!
Careful! Don't force it. This ambient magic will just warp your spells.
Don't waste your breath. A collapsing landmass creates massive magical turbulence. It usually lasts for years. Trying to cast a spell in this kind of maelstrom is basically suicide.
If you want to save your Tyrant, you'll have to sail a ship that doesn't run on magic.
Unfortunately for you, there isn't a single port in northwestern Nova.
No! I have to try again!
<size=50>Quick, get in the car! The ground on our side is giving way too!</size>
Heh... Farewell,==W== Tyrant.==W== To meet an end like this... I am satisfied.
Angie wears an expression of pure relief. Facing the ocean,==RT==she tosses a tiny thing out into the waves.
The next second, the violent tides swallow her whole,==RT==along with the very sand beneath her feet.
Loxy frantically reverses, but by the time its tires finally stop spinning, even==RT==Mistique and Nazuka high above can no longer see Amber's second signal flare.
The days blur together. When our last magic runs dry, we are forced to press on==RT==by foot, dodging the collapsing earth and the encroaching sea.
Albedo pleads with the Sentinels of Dawn and the Dusk Arbiters to mount a rescue.
The Trekker Association rallies every seafaring Trekker they can find.
Firenze and Matilda even track down the United Harvest headquarters,==RT==trying to dispatch ships from southern Nova.
Yet, all their struggles are meaningless.
==Off==<color=#000000>The magical turbulence spawned by the fracturing earth==RT==forms a violent barrier, severing the fragment of desert we're on==RT==from the rest of Nova.</color>
==Off==<color=#000000>Nova's transport thrives, but seafaring has long been abandoned.==RT==Even at full speed, the nearest ship would take a month to reach us.
==Off==<size=70><color=#000000>Our supplies will never last that long.
My lips move, but no sound comes out. My parched throat went numb days ago. The slightest vibration of my vocal cords feels like swallowing glass.==W==
Using the last of my strength, I squeeze Iris's hand, just to prove I am still breathing.
Noya and Amber... They've gone cold.
Boss, I don't think I have much longer, either.
You passed out earlier... So you missed their last words.==W== I'll... I'll say them for you. Cough...
We're going to be rescued. And when we are…==RT==Let's rebuild Loxy together ... and set off again.
Talking with Boss is fun. But we haven't had a real talk ... in a long time.
I'm so glad we found you in that Monolith. Even if...
Sitting here with you... Turning into a beacon for other Trekkers…==RT==It's not a bad way to go, Boss.
Iris's fingers go limp, slowly slipping from my grasp. And I ... can't even shed tears of grief.
I have some water for you. Would you like to soothe your throat?
Cough...==W== Ugh...==W== My throat doesn't hurt anymore. I... I can speak again?
The White Room harbors your soul, not your physical body. The injuries your body sustained will not manifest here.
You truly suffered this time.==W== Scorched by that blazing sun while water slowly drains from your body... I understand how terrible that feels.

Still, getting buried in the same desert with your most cherished companions and your "home" on wheels? That might be a blessing.==W== There are plenty of people out there who couldn't beg for an end that sweet.
I...==W== I failed again.==W== And I dragged even more of my friends into this ordeal with me.
And... The end of the world...==W== It's actually real...
Bernina, Virigia... Do you know anything about this "end of the world"?
I am sorry. As Monolith staff, our only news comes from chatting with passing Trekkers. They have never mentioned anything about the world ending.
Even if we did know, our NDA would prevent us from saying a word about it.
I see.==W== Vita, what about you? Did you know?==W== No, wait, even if you did, you'd just say...
Tyrant. I lack sufficient permission to disclose information regarding this matter.
You're even beating me to the punch now.
Open the door. With everything I've learned this time around, I know exactly how to win this war.
I'm going to save everyone, and no one will get hurt!
Even Ashwind is here... Are we really doing a final showdown with the Salvation Committee right here? Ugh... There's no way we win this.
Boss, what do we do next?
Running is useless. The decapitation strike is useless.
If I want to protect everyone, I have to utilize absolutely every piece of intel I gathered from the last two attempts.
I need to leave Angie in charge of the Committee, pick a battlefield that keeps the kids and citizens out of the crossfire, and force a showdown.
No wars of attrition. I'm going to wipe them all out in one fell swoop!
Running away is shameful but useful
The best defense is a good offense
Return to where it all began
Listen up. We are going to utterly crush the Salvation Committee.
Huh? Boss, what are you talking about?==W== We only have...
It's more than enough.==W== As long as we get inside <color=#3faeae>that Monolith</color>, we can overcome their numbers and turn this entire war around.

I don't know what's going on, but I can feel how anxious you are. Every time we fight, you always make sure we're in the safest possible spot.
But for this final "great escape," you still chose to rely on us.==W== You haven't forgotten ...==W== the promise the four of us made our first night in Mirage.
How am I supposed to say this? How do I explain what happened last time without mentioning the White Room?
Hehe, you don't have to give me an answer right now, ==PLAYER_NAME==. I can wait.
Do you remember that massive Stellaroid we fought at the Waterway?
Of course I do. That was our first time fighting together. Our first real battle.

Facing a monster like that on our first team-up... We were totally reckless.==W== With a power gap like that, anyone else would have said we had zero chance.==W== It was the kind of despair you're never supposed to overcome.
But we had your brains, Iris's caution, Amber's agility, and my intuition!
To hell with despair! We turned the impossible into the possible!
And today won't be any different!
Cap, is doing this actually gonna help the Boss?
Hahaha! Beats me! But that Trekker, Noya, was it? She made a damn good point.
The Scorpions need this turf war over, like yesterday.==W== And if they can't finish it, they need to take it somewhere else. If this keeps up, our crystal diamond mine is gonna cave in.
But earlier, you helped the Committee cast a sandstorm...
That was then, this is now.==W== I thought the Committee was gonna score a quick win, so I tossed a little support their way. I didn't expect the Boss to see right through their whole setup.

Good thing none of the Boss's crew got hurt, so there's no bad blood.==W== Now it's time to flip the script and help them.==W== Of course, we can't let the Committee catch us doing it, or they'll come knocking.
Heads up, here comes the RV!
Golden sands beneath the setting sun, heed my call! Rise and form the dune!
A giant forged of golden sand rises in front of the Committee's sand walls,==W== then immediately collapses, as if the caster had lost control.
I see! The Committee has plenty of magic, which makes breaking those walls impossible. But if someone dumps enough sand to create a makeshift ramp...
Then we can just fly right over them!
Launching off the crest of the dune, the Lucky Oasis traces a perfect arc through the air,==W== sailing right over Greyhorn and Gunhild's heads before touching down in the boundless desert.
Boss, the Dusk Arbiters and I have captured almost the whole Salvation Committee.
Thanks to you running them ragged across the desert, we barely took any casualties. Everyone is safe.
That's a relief.==W== We're running low on Grace, though. Can you send someone to pick us up?
Mistique, Nazuka, and Chitose headed out a few days ago. They brought plenty of Soul Stones.==W== Honestly, you went incredibly far.
We didn't have a choice. We meant to head east and meet up with you after breaking out of Mirage,==W== but Greyhorn cut us off, so we had to gun it northwest.
Judging by the distance, we're practically at the edge of the Nova Continent. Another day or two of driving, and we'd probably hit the ocean.
We've turned back. We should run into the others soon. I'll get in touch with them now.==W== Talk later, Firenze.
We'll be waiting for you, Boss.
We hit a lot of bumps along the way, and even accidentally gave the Committee a "combat boost"...==W== But it's over now.
Once we hand Angie over to the Dusk Arbiters, we can finally go back to our normal lives.
Even now, I haven't given up on killing you.==W== In fact, I remain absolutely certain that I will.
Did I? You'll find out soon enough.
Noya? What's wrong? Why are you braking?
Y-You need to see this...==W== The desert... It's gone.
Is this ...==W== the ocean?! What is an ocean doing in the middle of the desert?
The sea at the end of the desert? But that should be to the west! Noya, are you sure we didn't go the wrong way?
I wouldn't make a rookie mistake like that! Look at the sun. We've been heading east this whole time, tracing our exact route back!
Hey, Nazuka. Where are you all?==W== We hit a snag on our end. It's going to take a while longer to meet up.
Boss, where did you go? We've reached the coastline, and we still haven't found you.
To see the true Edge of the World, you must travel west for days,==W== cross the quicksand and the mountains, all the way to where the desert meets the sea.
There, the earth is constantly collapsing into a pitch-black abyss.
Angie did say that during the negotiation last time...==W== Don't tell me this ocean is...==W== No, it can't be!
Amber, fire a shot straight up. Maximum output.
Boss, I see ... a flash of red light on the horizon. Was that you?==W==
Is my ==SEX11== ...==W== on the other side of the sea?
You did defeat the Salvation Committee, Tyrant. But to think you'd end up trapped here, doomed by the end of the world itself!
It's obvious just looking at it. This strait formed because the earth collapsed while you were deep in the west, and the ocean simply rushed in to fill the void.

The northwest corner of the Nova Continent has no Monolith. It's where the destruction is most severe.==W== You were so focused on leading the Committee to their graves, you never realized you were digging your own.
What are you babbling about? A strait this narrow? We can just fly right over it!
Exactly.==W== Mistique,==W== let's go get them.
No, we can't!==W== We can't fly over the water at all. There is way too much magic in the air here. I can't even steer my broom!
Careful! Don't force it. This ambient magic will just warp your spells.
Don't waste your breath. A collapsing landmass creates massive magical turbulence. It usually lasts for years. Trying to cast a spell in this kind of maelstrom is basically suicide.
If you want to save your Tyrant, you'll have to sail a ship that doesn't run on magic.
Unfortunately for you, there isn't a single port in northwestern Nova.
No! I have to try again!
<size=50>Quick, get in the car! The ground on our side is giving way too!</size>
Heh... Farewell,==W== Tyrant.==W== To meet an end like this... I am satisfied.
Angie wears an expression of pure relief. Facing the ocean,==RT==she tosses a tiny thing out into the waves.
The next second, the violent tides swallow her whole,==RT==along with the very sand beneath her feet.
Loxy frantically reverses, but by the time its tires finally stop spinning, even==RT==Mistique and Nazuka high above can no longer see Amber's second signal flare.
The days blur together. When our last magic runs dry, we are forced to press on==RT==by foot, dodging the collapsing earth and the encroaching sea.
Albedo pleads with the Sentinels of Dawn and the Dusk Arbiters to mount a rescue.
The Trekker Association rallies every seafaring Trekker they can find.
Firenze and Matilda even track down the United Harvest headquarters,==RT==trying to dispatch ships from southern Nova.
Yet, all their struggles are meaningless.
==Off==<color=#000000>The magical turbulence spawned by the fracturing earth==RT==forms a violent barrier, severing the fragment of desert we're on==RT==from the rest of Nova.</color>
==Off==<color=#000000>Nova's transport thrives, but seafaring has long been abandoned.==RT==Even at full speed, the nearest ship would take a month to reach us.
==Off==<size=70><color=#000000>Our supplies will never last that long.
My lips move, but no sound comes out. My parched throat went numb days ago. The slightest vibration of my vocal cords feels like swallowing glass.==W==
Using the last of my strength, I squeeze Iris's hand, just to prove I am still breathing.
Noya and Amber... They've gone cold.
Boss, I don't think I have much longer, either.
You passed out earlier... So you missed their last words.==W== I'll... I'll say them for you. Cough...
We're going to be rescued. And when we are…==RT==Let's rebuild Loxy together ... and set off again.
Talking with Boss is fun. But we haven't had a real talk ... in a long time.
I'm so glad we found you in that Monolith. Even if...
Sitting here with you... Turning into a beacon for other Trekkers…==RT==It's not a bad way to go, Boss.
Iris's fingers go limp, slowly slipping from my grasp. And I ... can't even shed tears of grief.
I have some water for you. Would you like to soothe your throat?
Cough...==W== Ugh...==W== My throat doesn't hurt anymore. I... I can speak again?
The White Room harbors your soul, not your physical body. The injuries your body sustained will not manifest here.
You truly suffered this time.==W== Scorched by that blazing sun while water slowly drains from your body... I understand how terrible that feels.

Still, getting buried in the same desert with your most cherished companions and your "home" on wheels? That might be a blessing.==W== There are plenty of people out there who couldn't beg for an end that sweet.
I...==W== I failed again.==W== And I dragged even more of my friends into this ordeal with me.
And... The end of the world...==W== It's actually real...
Bernina, Virigia... Do you know anything about this "end of the world"?
I am sorry. As Monolith staff, our only news comes from chatting with passing Trekkers. They have never mentioned anything about the world ending.
Even if we did know, our NDA would prevent us from saying a word about it.
I see.==W== Vita, what about you? Did you know?==W== No, wait, even if you did, you'd just say...
Tyrant. I lack sufficient permission to disclose information regarding this matter.
You're even beating me to the punch now.
Open the door. With everything I've learned this time around, I know exactly how to win this war.
I'm going to save everyone, and no one will get hurt!
Even Ashwind is here... Are we really doing a final showdown with the Salvation Committee right here? Ugh... There's no way we win this.
Boss, what do we do next?
Running is useless. The decapitation strike is useless.
If I want to protect everyone, I have to utilize absolutely every piece of intel I gathered from the last two attempts.
I need to leave Angie in charge of the Committee, pick a battlefield that keeps the kids and citizens out of the crossfire, and force a showdown.
No wars of attrition. I'm going to wipe them all out in one fell swoop!
Running away is shameful but useful
The best defense is a good offense
Return to where it all began
Listen up. We are going to utterly crush the Salvation Committee.
Huh? Boss, what are you talking about?==W== We only have...
It's more than enough.==W== As long as we get inside <color=#3faeae>that Monolith</color>, we can overcome their numbers and turn this entire war around.

strings.text: Thanks to Allie's fierce stand, you break past Greyhorn's blockade. You are able to stop No. 160's spell, but not Gunhilde's barrage. Though badly wounded, Noya tries to shield you, yet both of you fall.
Is Allie ... going to be okay?
Don't worry. Mom's tough. You told us yourself, that she and Narida took down hundreds of Sentinels of Dawn and Imperial Guards without breaking a sweat.
That was a guerrilla fight, sure. But it's way too tight in this shaft. The Salvation Committee can't swarm her.
I'm fine. But my Soul Stone is out of magic.
I can still fight with my left hand.
Let's not waste the time Allie bought us. Keep moving. We regroup at the Monolith.
Half of the first unit fired. Everything's right on schedule.
The strikes blew right through the surface, driving the Tyrant straight down into the abandoned mineshafts.
Our First Company was waiting for them.==RT==They've already linked up with Captain Greyhorn.
The Second, along with the Desert Scorpions and the Imperial Guard,==RT==are moving in to flank.
There are only so many exits in that mine. We're getting the Tyrant this time. Guaranteed.
Nothing in this world is guaranteed. Director Allie has already stopped Greyhorn dead in her tracks.
I just spoke with her. Turns out, Allie is Taffett, the missing ace of the White Cats.
The Tyrant really does surround ==SEX8== with hidden talents.==W== Gunhild, no holding back. Unload the rest of your payload.
Even through the ground, you can still track 160 and Noya, right?
My ==SEX11==, the tunnel ahead is blocked. The collapse is fresh.
Same here.==W== The Salvation Committee boxed us in on purpose.
Tch... So Angie chose this spot just to set this trap. She played me...
No, the gap in manpower is just too huge. It's like playing chess with ten pieces against a hundred. I couldn't possibly block every single move.
Boss, over here! I feel a draft coming from this wall. There must be a way through! Stand back,==W== I'm busting it open!
Heehee... And just where do you think you're going, Tyrant?
Noya, watch out! Someone's behind the wall!
You again? You're such a pain. Are you a stalker or something?!
A stalker? Maybe!==W== But right now... I'm the beacon for heavenly fire.
Ugh, enough with the riddles. Nazuka, Chitose, you go on ahead. I'll tie this freak down.
Heehee, too scared to hit back? Well, I'm not holding back! Your wound is right there, Trekker. Way too easy to poke!
Not that playing it safe matters anyway. I swallowed plenty of pain before I even came looking for you.==W== Getting shot through by a magic cannon feels ... freaking amazing! So amazing!
And now I'm giving all that amazing pain right to you!
God of Grace, please stop the clock! Make it stop!
... Tyrant! Hey, what are you doing covering my eyes?!
==RT====RT==<size=47>But this magic doesn't actually stop time. It just forcibly uses magic power to restrict the movement of anything within a certain range around her that she can see.
You can only freeze what you can see. So, by blocking your vision, your magic is completely useless.
H-How is this possible?! I can see your hand! You should be frozen...
Phew, that takes care of her.==W== Nazuka, Chitose, tie this arbiter up and drag her along. I've got Noya. We'll be right behind you.
Lady Angie, thanks to No. 160 buying us some time, I've already found the location of Noya.
Open fire. 160 made her peace with death before she deployed.
I'm sorry, Boss. I really dragged you down this time.
What are you talking about? We won. The Salvation Committee couldn't hold us, and everyone got out safe.
My final sight is the tunnel caving in, and Noya turning around to shield me with her own body.
<size=50>Whoa!</size>==W== You startled me...==W== What is it?
It just popped into my head! I figured out how to make it rain in the desert!
First, Iris freezes the oasis lake into a giant block of ice.==W== Then, if we can get Mistique to lift it up into the air,==W== the melted ice will fall like rain!
Uh...==W== That would technically make it "rain," sure.==W== But if you're hauling ice all the way up there, wouldn't it be better to just drop it on the enemies on the dune?
Enemies on the dune?==W== What's that?
That's... Uh, I thought you were trying to figure out a way out of this mess...
Ahaha! No, no!==W== I was just thinking about how to make flowers bloom in the desert.
Just think! If we could really pull it off, we might get to see a scene==RT==straight out of a fairy tale, don't you think?
Scene out of a fairy tale... Just for that?
Not "just for that."==W== It's my dream to see all of the world with you, Boss!
But I'm more interested in star plucking than fighting monsters!
Yep! I heard it from someone, too. They say if you defeat the boss-class Stellaroid in the Monolith and find the Wishing Star it guards, then any wish you make will come true ♪
... Hm?==W== But I thought your dream was ...==W== to defeat the powerful Stellaroid in the Monolith ... and pluck a star, right?
Yes<size=53>♪</size> But==W== there's no rule saying you <r=·>can't </r><r=·>have </r><r=·>more </r><r=·>than </r><r=·>one </r><r=·>wish</r>!
Okay, okay, let's not talk about that right now. Boss, look!
... Rain?==W== Noya, what are you talking about...==W==
This is it... The most beautiful flower in the desert.
Warm droplets fall onto my face.
Just as she said, the desert witnesses rain.
Boss, open your eyes...! Look at me!!
There are still so many places we haven't seen together...!
Boss? Thank goodness... I thought you weren't going to wake up.
It's so dark I can barely see. Are you okay...? Are you hurt ... anywhere?
Y-Yeah. The rubble's got me pinned down, so I can't really move... I don't seem to be injured though.
That aside... What happened? Did the mineshaft collapse?
Yeah. That explosion just now... Looks like it caved in completely.
Oh... But don't worry, I know that Nazuka and Chitose are fine.
That's good to hear. But what about you, Noya?==W== You seem really out of breath...
M-Me? I'm... Haha... I'm fine, really. I just got a few scrapes when I fell, that's all...
In a situation like this, if all we got were a few scrapes, we should count ourselves lucky. By the way, have you seen my phone? I need to get in touch with everyone soon...
Huh? Is that your phone I'm touching right now? I think it's caught on something. I can't pull it out. I might be able to turn on the screen, though...
What wet my cheek was not the warmth of rain ... but crimson drops falling from Noya's chest.
She's held back the collapsed rubble just to carve out a tiny pocket of space for me.
Oh... Did it get a little brighter?
So that means... You found the phone, right?
But... Huh? Th-that's weird... It should be brighter now, but... I can't really see your face...
That's enough, Noya. Don't push yourself any further...
No... I can't. If I don't hold on... You'll get crushed under the rubble...
And besides... You don't have to worry. Being tough is ... kind of my saving grace. You know that too... Right?
So... Once we get out of here, and pull out the stake stuck in me... A wound like this ... will heal up in just a few days...
And then... Boss? Let's go for a drive ... together ... with Loxy...
Yeah, we will. We'll go. I'll go with you anywhere you want! So stop wasting your strength talking anymore!
No... This might be my last chance, so let me finish it properly...
What!? Don't be silly, Noya! Don't say something like that!!
S-sorry... but... I can barely see anymore... And I don't think I'll be able to talk much longer...
Ahaha... Even though I promised ... that I'd never lie to you...
If it goes on like this... I'll be a liar forever in your memory... And I couldn't ... bear that... Not even in death... So... Please... Will you listen?
Mm... Thank you. Um, you know, what I told you back at the orphanage...
That moment when you and Nazuka made your vow beneath the Monolith... I really ... really thought it was beautiful. That's how I truly felt.
And ... the fact that you made a vow like that... It made me think ... you two really do have a wonderful relationship. That's how I truly felt, too.
But... But, when I said I was fine as long as you two were happy... I'm sorry... Maybe that was a lie after all...
When all of us were secretly watching you two... The truth is... I wished it were me standing there with you...
To be honest... My heart tingled a little. Haha... Doesn't sound like me at all, right?
Well... because of all that, I didn't know how to tell you how I felt...
But I thought we'd still have a long, long way to go... So I never thought I had to rush... I'm sorry. Looks like... Time's up...
...No, there's no need to apologize. But if that's how you really felt, I wish you'd told me sooner...
Mm... I don't really know how to put it, but...
When I found you in the Wishing Box, I felt like ... my wish had already come true.
Because of that, I figured I shouldn't ask for anything more...
Just traveling with you every day, seeing new sights... I thought I should be grateful for days like that, but...
I guess I was not as cheerful as I thought...
Well... Then let's make sure we both get out of here alive, so we can go see all kinds of new sights together.
It's just... I'm sorry. Now that I've gotten it all out... I feel so relieved, and I'm getting sleepy...

Noya's arms slowly give out. Under the crushing weight of the rubble, our bodies are pressed tightly together.
From the day I awoke in the desert until this very moment... Never once had I longed so desperately for death.
This is the White Room. Your companions cannot reach you here.
Right, right! The White Room! That means I still have a chance. I can still go back and save Noya, right?!
Please compose yourself, Tyrant. This isn't like you.
Noya bled out for me. She went cold right in front of me, bit by bit!
And right up until the very end, she was holding up that rubble to protect me!
Calm down?! How the hell am I supposed to calm down?!
We fully understand your pain. But you need to stay calm, now more than ever.
If you rush back completely hot-headed, do you really think you'll make the right call?
You'll just drag your companions into another tragic end. It'll only add to their suffering and yours.
I'm sorry. You're right. I was being impulsive.
I completely misjudged the situation. I thought we could make a clean getaway, but the Salvation Committee threw far more at us than I expected.
Even if Allie, Chitose, and Nazuka can each take down dozens of Committee members on their own...
Against their sheer numbers and organization, our individual strength meant nothing.
It is good that you can think rationally again. Then, please remember this final image.
As you gaze at the distant scenery, do not forget that someone is silently gazing at you, too.
If only you had noticed her feelings sooner, perhaps she would have been much happier.
Vita, open the door! I'm going to change all of this!

param: Thanks to Allie's fierce stand, you break past Greyhorn's blockade. You are able to stop No. 160's spell, but not Gunhilde's barrage. Though badly wounded, Noya tries to shield you, yet both of you fall.
Is Allie ... going to be okay?
Don't worry. Mom's tough. You told us yourself, that she and Narida took down hundreds of Sentinels of Dawn and Imperial Guards without breaking a sweat.
That was a guerrilla fight, sure. But it's way too tight in this shaft. The Salvation Committee can't swarm her.
I'm fine. But my Soul Stone is out of magic.
I can still fight with my left hand.
Let's not waste the time Allie bought us. Keep moving. We regroup at the Monolith.
Half of the first unit fired. Everything's right on schedule.
The strikes blew right through the surface, driving the Tyrant straight down into the abandoned mineshafts.
Our First Company was waiting for them.==RT==They've already linked up with Captain Greyhorn.
The Second, along with the Desert Scorpions and the Imperial Guard,==RT==are moving in to flank.
There are only so many exits in that mine. We're getting the Tyrant this time. Guaranteed.
Nothing in this world is guaranteed. Director Allie has already stopped Greyhorn dead in her tracks.
I just spoke with her. Turns out, Allie is Taffett, the missing ace of the White Cats.
The Tyrant really does surround ==SEX8== with hidden talents.==W== Gunhild, no holding back. Unload the rest of your payload.
Even through the ground, you can still track 160 and Noya, right?
My ==SEX11==, the tunnel ahead is blocked. The collapse is fresh.
Same here.==W== The Salvation Committee boxed us in on purpose.
Tch... So Angie chose this spot just to set this trap. She played me...
No, the gap in manpower is just too huge. It's like playing chess with ten pieces against a hundred. I couldn't possibly block every single move.
Boss, over here! I feel a draft coming from this wall. There must be a way through! Stand back,==W== I'm busting it open!
Heehee... And just where do you think you're going, Tyrant?
Noya, watch out! Someone's behind the wall!
You again? You're such a pain. Are you a stalker or something?!
A stalker? Maybe!==W== But right now... I'm the beacon for heavenly fire.
Ugh, enough with the riddles. Nazuka, Chitose, you go on ahead. I'll tie this freak down.
Heehee, too scared to hit back? Well, I'm not holding back! Your wound is right there, Trekker. Way too easy to poke!
Not that playing it safe matters anyway. I swallowed plenty of pain before I even came looking for you.==W== Getting shot through by a magic cannon feels ... freaking amazing! So amazing!
And now I'm giving all that amazing pain right to you!
God of Grace, please stop the clock! Make it stop!
... Tyrant! Hey, what are you doing covering my eyes?!
==RT====RT==<size=47>But this magic doesn't actually stop time. It just forcibly uses magic power to restrict the movement of anything within a certain range around her that she can see.
You can only freeze what you can see. So, by blocking your vision, your magic is completely useless.
H-How is this possible?! I can see your hand! You should be frozen...
Phew, that takes care of her.==W== Nazuka, Chitose, tie this arbiter up and drag her along. I've got Noya. We'll be right behind you.
Lady Angie, thanks to No. 160 buying us some time, I've already found the location of Noya.
Open fire. 160 made her peace with death before she deployed.
I'm sorry, Boss. I really dragged you down this time.
What are you talking about? We won. The Salvation Committee couldn't hold us, and everyone got out safe.
My final sight is the tunnel caving in, and Noya turning around to shield me with her own body.
<size=50>Whoa!</size>==W== You startled me...==W== What is it?
It just popped into my head! I figured out how to make it rain in the desert!
First, Iris freezes the oasis lake into a giant block of ice.==W== Then, if we can get Mistique to lift it up into the air,==W== the melted ice will fall like rain!
Uh...==W== That would technically make it "rain," sure.==W== But if you're hauling ice all the way up there, wouldn't it be better to just drop it on the enemies on the dune?
Enemies on the dune?==W== What's that?
That's... Uh, I thought you were trying to figure out a way out of this mess...
Ahaha! No, no!==W== I was just thinking about how to make flowers bloom in the desert.
Just think! If we could really pull it off, we might get to see a scene==RT==straight out of a fairy tale, don't you think?
Scene out of a fairy tale... Just for that?
Not "just for that."==W== It's my dream to see all of the world with you, Boss!
But I'm more interested in star plucking than fighting monsters!
Yep! I heard it from someone, too. They say if you defeat the boss-class Stellaroid in the Monolith and find the Wishing Star it guards, then any wish you make will come true ♪
... Hm?==W== But I thought your dream was ...==W== to defeat the powerful Stellaroid in the Monolith ... and pluck a star, right?
Yes<size=53>♪</size> But==W== there's no rule saying you <r=·>can't </r><r=·>have </r><r=·>more </r><r=·>than </r><r=·>one </r><r=·>wish</r>!
Okay, okay, let's not talk about that right now. Boss, look!
... Rain?==W== Noya, what are you talking about...==W==
This is it... The most beautiful flower in the desert.
Warm droplets fall onto my face.
Just as she said, the desert witnesses rain.
Boss, open your eyes...! Look at me!!
There are still so many places we haven't seen together...!
Boss? Thank goodness... I thought you weren't going to wake up.
It's so dark I can barely see. Are you okay...? Are you hurt ... anywhere?
Y-Yeah. The rubble's got me pinned down, so I can't really move... I don't seem to be injured though.
That aside... What happened? Did the mineshaft collapse?
Yeah. That explosion just now... Looks like it caved in completely.
Oh... But don't worry, I know that Nazuka and Chitose are fine.
That's good to hear. But what about you, Noya?==W== You seem really out of breath...
M-Me? I'm... Haha... I'm fine, really. I just got a few scrapes when I fell, that's all...
In a situation like this, if all we got were a few scrapes, we should count ourselves lucky. By the way, have you seen my phone? I need to get in touch with everyone soon...
Huh? Is that your phone I'm touching right now? I think it's caught on something. I can't pull it out. I might be able to turn on the screen, though...
What wet my cheek was not the warmth of rain ... but crimson drops falling from Noya's chest.
She's held back the collapsed rubble just to carve out a tiny pocket of space for me.
Oh... Did it get a little brighter?
So that means... You found the phone, right?
But... Huh? Th-that's weird... It should be brighter now, but... I can't really see your face...
That's enough, Noya. Don't push yourself any further...
No... I can't. If I don't hold on... You'll get crushed under the rubble...
And besides... You don't have to worry. Being tough is ... kind of my saving grace. You know that too... Right?
So... Once we get out of here, and pull out the stake stuck in me... A wound like this ... will heal up in just a few days...
And then... Boss? Let's go for a drive ... together ... with Loxy...
Yeah, we will. We'll go. I'll go with you anywhere you want! So stop wasting your strength talking anymore!
No... This might be my last chance, so let me finish it properly...
What!? Don't be silly, Noya! Don't say something like that!!
S-sorry... but... I can barely see anymore... And I don't think I'll be able to talk much longer...
Ahaha... Even though I promised ... that I'd never lie to you...
If it goes on like this... I'll be a liar forever in your memory... And I couldn't ... bear that... Not even in death... So... Please... Will you listen?
Mm... Thank you. Um, you know, what I told you back at the orphanage...
That moment when you and Nazuka made your vow beneath the Monolith... I really ... really thought it was beautiful. That's how I truly felt.
And ... the fact that you made a vow like that... It made me think ... you two really do have a wonderful relationship. That's how I truly felt, too.
But... But, when I said I was fine as long as you two were happy... I'm sorry... Maybe that was a lie after all...
When all of us were secretly watching you two... The truth is... I wished it were me standing there with you...
To be honest... My heart tingled a little. Haha... Doesn't sound like me at all, right?
Well... because of all that, I didn't know how to tell you how I felt...
But I thought we'd still have a long, long way to go... So I never thought I had to rush... I'm sorry. Looks like... Time's up...
...No, there's no need to apologize. But if that's how you really felt, I wish you'd told me sooner...
Mm... I don't really know how to put it, but...
When I found you in the Wishing Box, I felt like ... my wish had already come true.
Because of that, I figured I shouldn't ask for anything more...
Just traveling with you every day, seeing new sights... I thought I should be grateful for days like that, but...
I guess I was not as cheerful as I thought...
Well... Then let's make sure we both get out of here alive, so we can go see all kinds of new sights together.
It's just... I'm sorry. Now that I've gotten it all out... I feel so relieved, and I'm getting sleepy...

Noya's arms slowly give out. Under the crushing weight of the rubble, our bodies are pressed tightly together.
From the day I awoke in the desert until this very moment... Never once had I longed so desperately for death.
This is the White Room. Your companions cannot reach you here.
Right, right! The White Room! That means I still have a chance. I can still go back and save Noya, right?!
Please compose yourself, Tyrant. This isn't like you.
Noya bled out for me. She went cold right in front of me, bit by bit!
And right up until the very end, she was holding up that rubble to protect me!
Calm down?! How the hell am I supposed to calm down?!
We fully understand your pain. But you need to stay calm, now more than ever.
If you rush back completely hot-headed, do you really think you'll make the right call?
You'll just drag your companions into another tragic end. It'll only add to their suffering and yours.
I'm sorry. You're right. I was being impulsive.
I completely misjudged the situation. I thought we could make a clean getaway, but the Salvation Committee threw far more at us than I expected.
Even if Allie, Chitose, and Nazuka can each take down dozens of Committee members on their own...
Against their sheer numbers and organization, our individual strength meant nothing.
It is good that you can think rationally again. Then, please remember this final image.
As you gaze at the distant scenery, do not forget that someone is silently gazing at you, too.
If only you had noticed her feelings sooner, perhaps she would have been much happier.
Vita, open the door! I'm going to change all of this!

strings.text: After long being trapped in the White Room, you awaken once more from the Wishing Box to find two familiar yet unfamiliar faces. You assume the role of an Acolyte, but cannot escape her scrutiny…
Farewell. And now... Join me, and become the foundation of the new world!
Sitting here with you... Turning into a beacon for other Trekkers... It's not a bad way to go, Boss.
Boss, stay awake! Keep your eyes open and look at me! There's so much of the world we haven't seen yet!
So please, my Tyrant, don't become a star once more.
The same old road leads to the same old ends.
Huh? This voice... It's from back then?
Did I go back?==RT==Back to when the New Star Guild first found me?!
It seems your companion is awake.
Iris... Noya... I'm so glad to see you again.
Iris? Noya? Listen here, sinner. Neither of those is the name you gave me earlier. Is this person truly your "Master"?
Huh? What are they talking about? Master?
Hmph. What does a backwater Night Watcher know? This is a perfectly normal side effect of magic practice.
Master, you've mistaken me for Iris again! It's me, Elis. Iris's older sister. Your loyal, humble slave.
Yes, Elis! It's the lovely name you bestowed upon me.
Your head must be spinning. But don't worry. It just proves your resurrection magic was a success.
<size=50><r=·>Don't</r><r=·> try</r><r=·> to</r><r=·> speak</r></size>. Just rest. You'll recover shortly.
What's going on? She looks exactly like Iris, but claims to be her older sister... Elis?
And Noya's tone is completely off. Sinner?==W== Wait. This isn't the Lucky Oasis... Is this a prison cart?
You're desperately trying to keep ==SEX4== quiet. Struck a nerve?
Let me guess. You don't even know this person. And ==SEX== certainly isn't your "Master."
Ugh, talking to a simpleton like you is exhausting. Fine. Wash out your ears and listen closely.
My Master is a servant of Goddess Trivia, the favored of Demigod Lucilla, and the most promising Acolyte in Emor.
In Emor, anyone seeking to become a full Priest must offer an original spell at Goddess Trivia's temple.
But crafting magic is dangerous. It's incredibly easy for an unrefined spell to corrupt the caster's mind and scramble their memories.
To keep others safe, my merciful Master locked ==SEX8== away in a tower in the Wilds to attempt the impossible:
<size=50><color=#3faeae>Resurrection ... magic...</color></size>==W== Liar. Magic like that doesn't exist.
Exactly! That's why it had to be created from scratch! And thanks to my Master's sheer genius, ==SEX== has perfected it!
You saw it yourself over the past few days.
My Master had no heartbeat, no breath, no body heat. Yet look at ==SEX4== now. Completely alive!
Doesn't that prove the magic worked?
I don't buy it. You obviously used a spell to put ==SEX4== in a state of suspended animation.
Step aside. I have a few questions for your "Master."
Watch your place, Night Watcher! You have no authority to interrogate a noble Acolyte.
So the knight who looks like Noya is hunting down Iris...
No. She's hunting Elis, who just looks exactly like Iris.==RT==And I somehow got dragged into it, which is why we're sharing a cage.
One: Elis is lying through her teeth. That entire monologue was just feeding me my lines.
She wants me to play along as this noble Acolyte so we can pull rank and shake our captor.
Two: Elis is telling the truth. She really has a sister named Iris, and she actually knows an Acolyte who studies resurrection magic and looks exactly like me.
Like a coincidence that massive even exists!
Come to think of it... Where exactly are we? Goddess Trivia? Demigod Lucilla? Emor is the only name I recognize.
Does that mean I'm still in Nova?==W== No. There have been no slaves on Nova for ages.
Did walking through that door in the White Room drop me into a parallel world?
Maybe... I'm still dreaming? Or could it be ... this is all just a hallucination from the moment I was beheaded?
... Right. What am I doing? Vita broke trying to save me.
Ugh, enough spiraling. Wherever I am, priority one is getting out of this cage. Time to chat with the Night Watcher.
Elis, ask the Night Watcher to step over here.
Master? You don't need to entertain the whims of a lowly Night Watcher.
She threw us in this cage without a shred of proof! She's completely barbaric.
Once we reach the city, I'll find her Patron and ensure she is severely punished.
Honorable ==SEX12== Acolyte.==W== I am Alina Colossi, a Night Watcher of Filanis. I serve under Archon Olympia.
For your own safety, I need to ask you a few questions. If it turns out I've misjudged your identities, I will apologize and accept Lady Olympia's punishment.
Go ahead. I just woke up, and my head is still spinning, but I'll answer whatever I can.
A misunderstanding obviously landed us in this cage. Hopefully, we can clear the air now.
Tell me. Are you familiar with the Missing Saintess Incident from three years ago?
Elis gives me a meaningful look. Looks like she wants me to say yes.
This Night Watcher clearly respects the title. If we want out of here, I need to lean hard into this Acolyte persona.
... Looks like I'm playing along with Elis for now.
I need to keep my answers vague. Give her nothing to poke holes in.
Three years ago... That rings a bell. But what does that have to do with locking us in a cage?
Take a look at this portrait.
A word in private, if you would.
Alina leads me out of the cart to a tree several meters away... Just far enough to keep Elis from eavesdropping.
Your slave looks very much like the missing Saintess.==W== If I may ask, when and where did she become your slave?
So Elis might be the missing Saintess. That explains the pursuit.
But I'm already committed to this Acolyte act. Elis and I sink or swim together. I'll just have to play along.
Elis and I met in Emor four years ago. The timeline doesn't match your missing Saintess. She just happens to look like the portrait.
I see. I understand.==W== It appears I was mistaken. I apologize for confusing your slave with the Saintess.
Once we reach Filanis, I will explain this to my Patron. You will be compensated, and I will accept my punishment.
No need for punishment. I recently fell into a deathlike slumber while researching magic anyway.
It's an easy mistake to make. Just don't treat us as suspects anymore.
You are as humble as you are merciful, ==SEX12== Acolyte. Thank you for your forgiveness. I'll release your slave from the cart at once.
By the way, I grew up in Emor. I really miss the Grand Arena. On match days, the crowds were massive, and tickets were almost impossible to get. Did you ever catch a match?
Emor has an arena...? That's news to me.==W== Matches sound like a huge deal there. If I say yes, she'll quiz me on the details.==W== I need a believable excuse to brush her off.
As an Acolyte, my studies leave me with little free time. And ... tickets are practically impossible to get, just as you said.
Yeah. We cleared the air. She's letting you out.
==SEX12== Acolyte, there is something you should know. The rumors about the missing Saintess aren't entirely accurate.
The public believes a Saintess mysteriously vanished during a ritual at Emor's tower three years ago. Supposedly abducted by a powerful mage.
But as a Night Watcher of Filanis,==W== I was told the truth behind it.
There was no abduction. The Fallen Saintess staged the whole thing.==RT==She abandoned her sworn god and fled the ritual.
To hide her tracks, she has been roaming between cities for the past three years,==RT==silencing anyone who found out. Fifteen people are dead because of her.
Her specialty is bewitching innocents to act as her shields. Her victims unknowingly defend her and lie to cover her tracks.
Elis is the Fallen Saintess? And I'm under her spell?==W== No. I am immune to magic. I can't be bewitched.
Your elegant bearing and fine clothes tell me you are indeed an Acolyte, or at least someone of equal standing.
Your eyes are clear. You aren't under any spell. Which begs the question: why are you covering for a sinner and willingly lying for her?
When speaking of Elis, you never once called her your slave. You don't view her as property. A true master would never carry ==SEX8== that way.
It seems to me there's no master-servant relationship between the two of you.
Of course, that alone wasn't enough to condemn you. But your next slip proved you are definitely not from Emor.
The Grand Arena doesn't sell tickets. There are no tickets. Spectators get in using free clay tokens.
The woman before you is extremely dangerous. She calls herself your slave for a reason.
M-Master... Don't listen to her, I'm your most loyal...
Sinner! No sudden movements. Take your hand off the stone on your chest.
Heh. Who knew a backwater like Filanis bred such a sharp Night Watcher.
God of Magic,==W== blanket the earth in the mists of the underworld.==W== Blind my foes,==W== that I may walk unseen.
Let spark become flame.==W== Reveal the unseen!
Heh heh. Just because the chant says unseen doesn't mean it makes you invisible.
Thanks for the assist, "Acolyte." If you hadn't led her ten paces away, I never would have had time to prep my magic circle.
Well then, until next time. Sharp Night Watcher, kind Acolyte.
... Did she just animate the abandoned puppets in the forest?
Acolyte. Shut the cart door and stay inside. It's the safest place for you right now.

strings.text: Elis saves you from the dolls, easing Alina's suspicions. Over the following days, you and Elis grow closer through palm-written chats. Reaching Filanis, you feel a faint familiarity…
These puppets are relentless. Alina hacked them to pieces before she ran off, but...
Now they're actually tearing off their own limbs and slapping together five new bodies.
Thank goodness for sturdy bars. Mindless bashing won't leave a dent.
At this rate... I'll be perfectly safe right here until I starve.
But unless someone rescues me, I'll end up starving forever.
Alright, panicking won't help. Time to retrace my steps.
I remember...==W== I tried to use my ability to "undo a move" and beat Angie. To find a way out where nobody had to die.
But that meant throwing my own life away. I'd be dead if Vita hadn't blocked the shot with the Throne.
The Throne shattered. I woke up locked in the White Room, with no Monolith staff in sight. It was just an endless void.
I walked and walked ... until my mind went numb. Then I heard a familiar voice and pushed open another door.
Which dumped me here.==W== It feels like waking up on the Lucky Oasis all over again, except...
Noya is a Night Watcher,==W== Iris is the Fallen Saintess,==W== and Amber ... is nowhere in sight.
... Is this a dream? No, you can't dream up things you don't know.
An illusion inside the White Room? Another world entirely? I have no idea.
Doesn't matter. I found an exit in the White Room, which means I haven't lost yet.
Getting my head chopped off wasn't ideal, but I still squeezed through the door of fate.
Dead end or not, there's a way out of here. For the others, and for Vita... I have to get back!
What is going on? Why is the carriage shaking?
Wait, why are they all crowding one side of the cart?!
They're trying to tip it! If it falls, they can reach me through the bars!
Alina! Get back here! The cage is giving way!
God of Magic, grant me your blazing holy fire...
F-Fire magic?! Hey, don't roast me alive!
See, my dear Master? You always end up needing me. That Night Watcher is completely useless.
She saw those bars and figured brute force wouldn't cut it. But she forgot these things have half a brain. An iron wall means nothing if the enemy can just climb over it.
Why are you here? Alina is close. If she sees you, she'll arrest you. You should go.
Oh? My Master actually worries about me. I'm flattered.
I'm a murderous Fallen Saintess, remember?
You've seen my face and heard my voice. Aren't you afraid I'll silence my only witness?
If you came to silence me, you wouldn't have saved me. Letting the puppets do it would be much easier.
Besides... You might be the Fallen Saintess, but I don't think you'll kill to cover your tracks.
Fascinating. You woke up half an hour ago, and we just met. Where is this trust coming from?
Don't tell me ... you fell for my looks, or do you just enjoy hearing me call you Master?
Because==W== I refuse to believe anyone with Iris's face is a murderer...==W==Heh. Good luck saying that out loud.
Ahem. It's not your looks. It's how you operate.
Not my looks, huh? I get it. You are charmed. You just have other reasons to trust me.
Now I'm curious. What exactly did my actions give away?
Well... This cheeky attitude is nothing like Iris. I'd better just spell it out for her.
You're a powerful mage. If you're a ruthless killer, there is no need for you to drag a groggy amnesiac into a fake identity.
Alina is a veteran. She poked holes in my answers in seconds. Against someone like that, a magical ambush would've been your best bet.
When we stepped outside, you did lay down a magic circle. But it was a haste spell, non-lethal.
Habits are hard to break. You avoid hurting people, and you clearly tried to keep me out of the crossfire. You're no ruthless killer.
Tsk. What a day. First a sharp Night Watcher, and now a Master bending over backward to prove my innocence.
Enough about me. We need to move.
Exactly. Let's see that Night Watcher catch us now. She can stay in this forest and play with those junk piles all night.
God of Magic, grant me your blazing holy fire... Burn away these wicked woods!
Right magic, wrong chant. She has some bizarre casting habits...
Wait, did the puppets' faces just change color?
The wind blades ... disappeared?! Do they have anti-wind wards on them?!
God of Magic, let the swiftest wings of the forest heed my command. Cleanse this clamorous world!
H-How is that possible? No one wastes two different wards on scrap!==W== Wait... Not just wards. They're feeding on my magic!
Ugh... My magic is useless. We're surrounded.
Get inside! The cage will hold them!
I can't. If I open the door now, they'll flood inside,==W== and we're both dead...
Upon the foundation of my soul, with my spirit as the mortar... I seal my Master's cage. Weather the storm, stand firm against the gale, endure the searing flame...
I finally met someone who understands me. I'm not letting you die today, Acolyte. This is all the magic I have left. Take it.
This ward should hold... At least until the Night Watcher returns...==W==
They suddenly got tougher. I don't recognize the magic warding them...
Alina, cut off the magic! They are absorbing it from your blade!
Ah, I see.==W== Then I will cut them down with pure steel!
Just as I thought. This is much easier.
Incredible... She cut through fifty,==W== no, at least a hundred puppets on pure swordplay alone?!
==SEX12== Acolyte, are you alright? Any injuries?
I was safe in the cart. Go find Elis! The puppets just buried her!
Don't worry. Your <color=#3faeae>slave</color> had the good sense to duck beneath the wreckage for cover while I was swinging.
You are one to talk! That last swing nearly took my head off!
Wait. What did you just call me?
I checked the puppets in the forest. Your magic did not animate them.==W== Furthermore, I saw what you did...
You used your last reserves of magic shielding the Acolyte just as you were about to be overrun. A Fallen Saintess would never do such a thing. A fiercely loyal slave would.
You may still be the Fallen Saintess hiding behind a clever disguise, but this truth lies beyond my mortal judgment now.
I am taking you both to Filanis. My Patron,==W== the great Archon <color=#3faeae>Olympia</color>, will judge your identity and decide your fate.

==A-2==After Alina abruptly ceased her interrogation, we resumed our journey.==P====RT====RT====A-1==On paper, Elis remains a sinner and I her suspect accomplice. Yet Alina treats us exactly like an Acolyte and ==SEX3== attendant, affording us all the respect the titles carried.==P====RT====RT====A-1==Even our three daily meals are leagues better than her own rations.
Bouncing along in the cart, Elis and I grow closer,==RT==developing a highly unorthodox method of conversation.
(Trace it with me again, ==PLAYER_NAME==! An Acolyte who cannot even write ==SEX3== own name is a fatal flaw.)
(Understood. One more time. Is this right?)
(I will handle all the writing from now on. It perfectly fits the personal slave disguise anyway.)
(Why did Alina abandon the interrogation the other day? Any thoughts?)
(A few. She is sharp. She likely noticed the same discrepancy you did. My behavior is nothing like the Fallen Saintess she knows about.)
(Plus, you look the part of a noble. Wrongfully arresting your personal slave would land her a severe reprimand from her Patron.)
(But you really are the runaway Saintess, right?)
(There's no point hiding it from you. I fled the ritual, but I've just been studying magic in a tower near Emor for three years.)
(I know nothing of those crimes. When we get out, I'll show you my daily journals in the tower. They'll prove my innocence!)
(I was fast asleep a few days ago in the tower.)
(Then that Night Watcher just burst in with a portrait and tried to arrest me.)
(I ran through the Monolith.==RT==Just as I was about to collapse, I spotted an ornate coffin.)
(I went to hide inside, but surprise, you were already in it.)
(You were dressed like royalty, so I claimed you were an Acolyte==RT==in a resurrection trance, and I was your slave standing guard.)
(Volunteering to be a slave... Is that really necessary?)
(You really don't remember anything. Slaves are property. If she wants to arrest me, she needs your permission first.)
(As long as I claim to be yours, she has to verify your ownership before dragging me away, Fallen Saintess or not.)
(So she loaded you and the coffin onto the cart for an investigation. She even warned me that if our identities didn't match, she'd charge me with desecrating a corpse.)
(Thanks to you, I bought some time. Otherwise, I'd be in shackles with no way to draw a single magic circle.)
(Speaking of which, who are you? And why were you in a coffin at the top of that Monolith? I never saw anyone go up there in three years.)
There is no possible way I can explain crossing into this world through the White Room... I'll just have to give her the abridged version.
(I'm no Acolyte, and I'm from far, far away. As for why I ended up in the Monolith with that coffin, I honestly have no idea.)
(Doesn't matter. You look the part anyway. No one will doubt the Acolyte disguise. Just let me do the talking in <color=#3faeae>Filanis</color> so we don't blow our cover.)
(I'll keep playing your slave.==W== But seriously, be a bit more ruthless with me. Show some authority! Nobody treats a slave as gently as you do.)
(The same applies to the Night Watcher. Drop the polite facade. It breaks character. But if she serves you well, offer a suitable reward.)
(Speaking of which... Is this palm-writing trick actually fooling Alina?)
(Undoubtedly. She is preoccupied with the horses. And even if she suspects conspiracy, I have other ways to divert her attention.)
Crap, we were so focused I didn't even notice the cart stop.==W== We're busted!
When you rub it like that, it feels ...==W== strange. Could you be ...==W== a little gentler with your fingers?
What kind of insane cover story is this?!
Ahem. Intimate eccentricities between master and slave are to be expected,==W== but you have lingered quite long enough. It is time to disembark.
Considering your presumed status, parading you into the city in a prisoner cart before the facts are clear would be a disgrace.
Ahem. How exceptionally thoughtful of you. My Master is a distinguished Acolyte. ==SEX1== absolutely cannot present ==SEX8== to the Archon in such filth.
Indeed. Considering your situation, I specifically chose a bathhouse closed to the public today. We are the only ones here.
How thoughtful. Though this place hardly looks fit to house a bathhouse. Is Filanis really this backwater?
This is not Filanis proper. It is merely a spontaneous settlement erected on the outskirts.
Behold. The city gleaming in the sunlight on the lake island, built around that tower.
A Monolith on a lake island ...==W== and this exact street layout.
That is the true Filanis.==W== The great City of Perfection.
