Calling me "==SEX12==" is a violation of the terms. Just call me ==PLAYER_NAME==, and call her Elis.
And you can stop calling me "Master." We need to blend in. It's about time I restore my slave to the status of a free woman.
We don't have a physical contract, so let's just have Alina act as our witness.
I ...==W== understand.==W== I will bear witness to ==PLAYER_NAME== freeing the slave, Elis.
Hah...==W== I really don't get you.==W== What is going on inside that head of yours?
Good. No one is using titles anymore. I like this.==W== So...==W== Captain Alina, give the order.
As the newest recruits of the Night Watchers, what's our first move?
Well...==W==Then let's discuss the connection between the Fallen Saintess and the recent disappearances in Filanis.

strings.text: Children vanish across Filanis, and many blame the Fallen Saintess. Alina no longer suspects you and Elis, and reveals why she is so desperate to know about the resurrection magic.
Under Archon Olympia's rule, Filanis has long been a peaceful, orderly city-state. Its people lived in harmony, and serious crimes were almost unheard of.
For years, we Night Watchers had little to do beyond catching thieves, putting out fires, and driving off monsters that strayed too close to the city.
A month ago, that peace was shattered.==W== A young girl vanished from her home,==W== and despite all the searching her family and I did, we found no trace of her.
At first, I thought she might have fallen into the water and been swept away from Filanis.==W== But then...==W==
A week later, a second child disappeared,==W== this time outside Filanis.==W== According to the family, the child had only gone out to buy bread and never came back.

All Filanian children know how to swim, so the odds of two of them accidentally falling into the water were far too low. Lulu and I searched every cellar and abandoned house in Filanis, but found nothing.
Kidnapping? But no one ever came to demand a ransom. Could it have been trafficking?
That was my thought as well, so I widened the search and kept a close watch on foreign travelers. Around the same time, rumors of the Fallen Saintess began to spread.
Many people were convinced the Fallen Saintess had slipped into Filanis==W== and taken those poor children away to devour them.
Come on, ==W==no matter how wicked the Fallen Saintess is supposed to be,==W== she wouldn't eat children!
Of course, it was a ridiculous rumor. In fact...==W== I don't believe the Fallen Saintess was responsible for those crimes,==W== or for any of those deaths.
Hm? Why do you think that?
If she were really on the run, moving from city to city would be the worst choice. She'd be better off disappearing into some remote place and waiting until people forgot about her.
A Saintess who managed to escape a sacrifice can't be a fool. I don't think she'd do something as stupid as killing people to hide her identity, only to expose herself in the process.
But ... those crimes really did happen...
I read about a case like that in Filanis's library.
A serial killer who was blamed for thirty deaths had actually only killed five. The other twenty-five were copycat crimes, pinned on the still-unidentified killer.
You mean ... the Fallen Saintess was framed.==W== Then why did you try to arrest Elis in the forest under that name?==W==
The so-called Fallen Saintess may not even exist. It could just be a name people made up as the rumors spread.
But the criminals using that name as cover for all kinds of crimes… They're very real.
Captain Alina,==W== another child has gone missing.
Another one? That's the third now...==W== Lulu,==W== have you found out anything about that Fallen Saintess rumor?
Well, if I had to name one lead...==W== A strange man showed up at the bathhouse yesterday.
A traveler with money to burn. They say he even holds the title of knight.==W== But he kept staring at people's teeth and skin, sizing them up...==W== Like he was inspecting merchandise.
That habit... Don't tell me he's a slave trader?
He was going around the bathhouse telling people stories about the Fallen Saintess. But he's an outsider...==W== How does he know our local rumors so well?

Very suspicious. He may be the one who took the children. I've heard that in some distant city-states, nobles don't care for ordinary slaves. They prefer abducted ones, especially those who once came from respectable families.
Stop right there. I'm Alina of the Filanis Night Watch. I'm inspecting your wagon.
Hah, Filanis really does like to overreach.==W== We're out in the wilds now, not in your city.
Captain Alina, those wagons...==W== No, they're cages. There are several slaves inside.
Hah. We never brought slaves into Filanis, so we haven't broken any of Archon Olympia's laws.==W== Wait. You look familiar.==W== Ah, you're that bathhouse girl!
No matter where it happens, treating people like toys or merchandise is evil. And you're also suspected of kidnapping and spreading panic. I'm taking you back for questioning.
Ridiculous. There are only two of you, and you think you can haul us back?==W== Boys, looks like we're adding two prime new goods to the cart. Draw your weapons!
Know your place!==W== Lulu, keep them alive. We still need them to tell us where the children are.
We defeated the slavers, but the missing children weren't among the slaves in the cages.

There was a tower in the forest on their way. I feared they might be hiding the kidnapped children there, so I sent Lulu back to the city and drove one of the prison wagons to the tower myself...==W== And that's where I ran into you.

So that's what happened. You'd just taken down a group of slavers, and they were spreading rumors about the Fallen Saintess. Then you saw me, looking just like the wanted sketch, so of course your mind went there. Totally makes sense.

Actually... I never really thought you were the Fallen Saintess. For one, you don't have the eyes of someone who's killed before. And for another, I've always believed the Fallen Saintess was just a figure exaggerated by rumor.
I only said it to see how you'd react...==W== Just a little trick we Night Watchers use when questioning thieves: start with a bigger accusation and see if they flinch.
Then what did you think I'd done?
That you might've been working with the slavers. Or maybe ... a grave robber.
Hey, come on, use your eyes!==W== I'm this cute and charming, and you thought I was a slaver or a grave robber?
Uh... Because you were standing next to an absurdly lavish coffin, and inside was the breathless ==PLAYER_NAME==.
Yeah, I can see how that would've looked like grave robbing. Heh.==W== So you threw both me and the coffin into the wagon as evidence of Elis's "crime."
No need to apologize. In that state, anyone would've thought I was a corpse.
So that's why your attitude changed later... I "came back to life," and Elis protected me on her own. Which meant she couldn't have been a grave robber, or a slaver.
Right. But I still had doubts about who you really were...==W== So I brought you back to Filanis.

Elis acted perfectly natural for a slave. But you, as her master...==W== You had none of that air of superiority. And the way you treated her wasn't like a slave at all. It was more like ...==W== a friend.
(I'll keep playing your slave.==W== But seriously, be a bit more ruthless with me. Show some authority! Nobody treats a slave as gently as you do.)
Elis did warn me about that, but I just couldn't do it... No matter how hard I try, I can't treat a living person like a sl<r=object></r>ave.

So I started to wonder if maybe both of you were slaves. The high-ranking kind, the ones who serve Archons or Demigods.==W== You escaped together, and pretending to be master and slave was simply the easiest cover.
So...==W== You brought us to Filanis to protect us, and to help us start over there with new identities.
Yes. If Archon Olympia discovered you were slaves, she would most likely set you free.
You're almost so kind it doesn't even feel real.

Your Patron Olympia, ruler of Filanis, may forbid the people of Filanis from keeping slaves, but that doesn't mean you have to leave the city and rescue slaves out in the wilds, does it? Wouldn't that just bring trouble to her?

Archon Olympia always said that anyone who steps into Filanis should do so as a free person. She supports us in freeing slaves by peaceful means whenever possible, and punishing those who profit from selling them.
And ... I used to be a slave too. I know what it feels like to be treated like an object. So I'll help you however I can.
... Why do slaves even exist? Why can't people just live peacefully together?
Of course it's because...==W== Everyone has wishes they want fulfilled, and some people can only get what they want by sacrificing others.
Hmph, don't go thinking everyone is as naive as you two<r=good people></r> idiots. You keep being this gullible, and one day it'll get you killed.
Thanks for the warning.==W== But...==W== After you tried to escape from the bathhouse and Saintess Leita caught you, I started to rethink who you really were. You probably aren't slaves.
Elis, you're the runaway Saintess, aren't you? And ==PLAYER_NAME== is a noble of some standing who, for reasons I don't know, chose to help you.
Huh!? What nonsense are you talking about? How could I possibly be a Saintess?
That's a pretty sharp guess. No wonder she is a Night Watcher... Aside from one thing she couldn't possibly know, that I'm from another world, she's basically right.
When Saintess Leita was trying to determine who you were... She looked like she recognized you, and even deliberately helped cover for you.
Normally... An innocent person would have no reason to flee through the sewers like that. But when it came to you hiding under the carriage, she brushed it off by mocking you.
So I looked into it...==W== Into Saintess Leita's past before she became a true Saintess, and found that she was from the same class as the runaway Saintess.
Everyone in that class had a clear record, except for the runaway Saintess. None of the others could possibly have ended up in Filanis as a slave,==W== which leaves only one possibility...
Even if I did know that Saintess, it doesn't prove anything...==W== We didn't have to meet during training. Maybe we were just neighbors back in Emor...==W== Yeah, neighbors!

How could a Saintess possibly be neighbors with a slave? If you're saying she was neighbors with ==PLAYER_NAME== instead, then at the bathhouse...==W== Saintess Leita looked like she didn't know ==PLAYER_NAME== at all.
I... I can explain that too...
Elis, stop struggling.==W== I think Alina isn't saying all this to turn us in. After all, she never brought up any of these doubts during the bathhouse test.
Archon Olympia has never issued a warrant for the runaway Saintess in Filanis. Lord Coppelius once told me that he didn't believe the runaway Saintess did anything wrong.
And during all this time, even after being locked in a prison cart, the two of you never did anything dangerous. As one of Filanis's Night Watchers, I have no reason to arrest Elis.
I don't think that's the whole story though. Back at the bathhouse entrance...
Could you tell me about the <color=#3faeae>resurrection magic</color>?
<size=50>Name your price...==W== I'll give you anything I have!
T-==W==Truly...?==W== May I ask about the tower and wishes?
You clearly had something you wanted to ask me.==W== If our identities were exposed, we'd either be arrested or forced to run.==W== And then you'd never get the answer you were looking for, right?
It's shameful, really. I was fortunate enough to be granted noble status, and though I bear the title of "Knight," my heart is still full of selfish desires.
==PLAYER_NAME==, you're right. I do have my own motives in this matter.==W== I really do want ... to learn that knowledge from you.
So please, don't think of me ... as some selfless good person who's only trying to help you.
Everyone has desires.==W== As long as those motives don't harm anyone else, I don't think there's anything wrong with them.
Do you want to continue our earlier conversation? About the tower and wishes?
Yes... Only Saintesses and Priests can enter Filanis's tower to make wishes, but a knight like me can also earn a once-in-a-lifetime chance after accumulating enough merit.
I want to make a wish for my companions, but I don't know ... how should I do it to bring about the result I want.
So I was hoping to ask you how wishing actually works.
Make a wish for your companions? You only get one chance in your whole life. Shouldn't you think about yourself too?
I... I owe them. No matter what, I want to repay them.
There are other ways to repay someone... This is a wish we're talking about. A wish that can grant anything!
Yes... I think this is the only way I can repay them. Please, come with me. I'll take you to them.
Elis and I follow Alina out through the back door of the Insula.
We trek through the forest for more than ten minutes. Only when even Filanis's Monolith has vanished behind the trees does Alina finally stop.
These are the companions I spoke of.
This is ... a graveyard? Sorry, we didn't know...
No need to apologize. I should have told you sooner.==W== A year ago, this Night Watcher of Filanis, Alina ... was still a gladiator in Emor.
What? A gladiator? The kind of famous star who fights in the Grand Arena and basks in the crowd's cheers?
Those kinds of gladiators do exist, yes. But I had nothing to do with that world.
Back then... I was nothing more than a gladiator slave without even a name...

strings.text: Alina reveals her past as a gladiator who lived among slaves. She won freedom by defeating magic puppets, but failed to save her companions who had fought and died beside her, and that regret turned into her wish.

Listen. The more blood spilled, the more the crowd goes wild, especially when it's a dainty girl like you. Doesn't matter if it's your blood or your opponent's... They'll be overjoyed either way. Understand?
Well, if you could fight your way to fame, then you can say goodbye to this filthy place forever.
You would live in a mansion that smells of myrrh and frankincense. Lounge on silk cushions stuffed with swan feathers by a crystal-clear pond, sipping chilled mead like some fine young lady…
Haha! Now that's what I call living. Bet you dream of a life like that too, huh?
...Jeez. "Yes, yes"… Is that the only word you know? Are you a puppet or something?
Ugh, fine. Forget it. Go on. A wimp with that empty look like yours would probably just die and get dragged out right away.
In the heart of Emor stands a theater where the curtains never fall.
With towering walls as its curtains and yellow sand as its stage. The lavishly dressed audiences sit in the sunlight, while the slaves in chains stand there in a daze, never seeing the light of day.
People call the Grand Arena "the heart that pumps life into Emor."
But it is never glory that keeps that heart beating... It is the blood that paints the sand red.
I was born beneath those high walls, and I inherited my parents' shackles without ever taking a name.
No one asks a slave's child what they want to be when they grow up. From the moment they are born, their master decides their role and attaches strings to them like a puppet.
The only choice I was ever allowed to make ... was the weapon to fight with. I chose the sword.
The arena is run by twin Archons. The elder sister leases out the venue and the slaves, while the younger one sells tickets and hosts the event they market as "gladiator fight"...
Masters would control the slaves,==W== commanding them to struggle, scream,==W== then fall to please the crowd.
Um... Thank you for going easy on me earlier.
Put some honey on your wound. It'll help keep it from festering.
R-Really? Oh, I'm Yonon... What's your name?
That's your number, right? I have one too—103. But I'm not asking for your number…
I don't have a name, nor do I need one.
Come on, Yonon. Come here so I can patch you up.
Yonon, you sure it's safe to talk to that kid? Who knows what she's thinking? You better stay away in case she stabs you in the back...
Stab? But she's a kind girl...==W== I don't think she would harm me…
Gladiators don't have proper names like the audience members do.
Of course, some gladiators would give themselves names based on their fighting style, hoping the crowd would remember them...
Even so, I never thought of taking a name for myself. After all, we were objects, the masters' property.
To a gladiator, a "name" is nothing more than a price tag, something to make you worth more on the market.
I'd rather hone my swordsmanship than waste time on that.
Every time I brought down an opponent in the arena, the crowd would clench their fists, raise their thumbs, and urge me to end the show with a finishing blow.
But ... I wasn't interested in following their orders, let alone killing in their favor.
So in my bouts, I would cut my opponents' skin open with the tip of my sword, but avoid all the major blood vessels or tendons.
That way, blood would spray a lot, but no one would lose their life.
But little did I know... In that arena with no way out, all hope would only lead to more devastating despair...
One year ago,==W== the Archon of Filanis arrived with a huge batch of magical puppets. That lady with kind heart intended to have them replace the slaves.
But she did not know. The audience couldn't care less about the skills or showmanship. It was the shedding of blood of the living that they craved.
To welcome the Archon of Filanis, the twin Archons who run the arena set up a grand fight: a duel between gladiators and magical puppets.
But it was never a stage to test the puppets' abilities. It was a slaughterhouse for the magical puppets to get rid of the "old puppets" who no longer obeyed their masters religiously.
Yeah. We're about to fight the magical puppets, right?
Your sword is falling apart so... We put our money together and bought you a new one.
Um... As a thanks for all the help, I guess? Ahaha... If it weren't for you, we'd probably all be long dead by now.
A-Anyway, the sword's yours now. Hehe… And good luck with the fight. If anyone is to defeat those puppets, it's you, 18. So we're counting on you.
Oh, of course we'll do our best, too. But those puppets probably won't go easy on us like you do, so I'm a little worried...
I contemplated whether to tell her, that I wasn't fighting for anyone's sake, and that I was only resisting the fate the arena had decided for me.
But ... the weight of the sword in my hand touched my heart, and words failed me. It was the first gift I had ever received in my life.
<color=#bd3059><size=75>Not a reward, but an actual gift...</color>
A few days later, the arena's master sent the ones==RT==whose lives I had saved, their wounds not yet healed,==RT==into the battle against the magical puppets.
The fight began at the sacred hour of midnight. The great arena lit over a thousand bonfires for the grand spectacle.
At first, the puppets only moved stiffly, and seemed helpless against our teamwork.
However, their magically reinforced bodies and insane mimicry made them tougher opponents than we'd expected.
The puppets soon absorbed our techniques and tactics ... and turned the tide of battle. My allies, already injured, fell one by one.
Spattered blood hissed harshly in the bonfires... But even that sound was drowned out by the roaring cheers.
The audience's bloodthirsty eyes at that moment were more terrifying than those puppets.
Fortunately, what the puppets had copied was my swordsmanship. So my fallen comrades hadn't suffered fatal wounds. At the same time, I saw a chance to win in their mimicry.

<color=#bd3059>==Off==Puppets that feel no pain... Let's settle this.==RT==See if your magic will run out before my sword breaks!!
How I managed to hold out...==W== I no longer remember.
In the end, as dawn broke, amid cheers loud enough to shake the arena, I collapsed alongside the last remaining puppet to the blood-soaked sand.
And … when I next awoke, I was in a carriage bound for Filanis.==W== Archon Olympia, the Archon of Filanis, had bought me, set me free, and granted me the rank of Knight.
Archon Olympia told me she would advance her research into magical puppets that could replace and one day, free all slaves.
That was also when the name "Alina Colossi" was born into this world.
To repay my debt to Archon Olympia, I became a Night Watcher of Filanis. And I swore to protect the perfect city she had built—a city with no slaves.
When I joined the Night Watch, Archon Olympia even paid me ten years' wages in advance... I had lived as a slave and had no idea what to do with money.
So I returned to Emor with a great sum of gold coins. I wanted to buy the freedom of my wounded companions.
Just as I had made it through that night and seen the dawn, I wanted my companions to see that light too.
Yonon? Sorry, never heard that name before.
...Oh, wait a minute. I think the previous 103 did go by that name...
Just what I said. Slaves who die in the Arena get their numbers passed on, right? Everyone who fought the puppets was dead. Naturally, all their numbers got reassigned to new slaves.
Wh-Don't lie to me...! Those puppets shouldn't have killed anyone!
Wh-Whoa, Knight lady, please calm down...! I ain't lying to you or nothing, see?
Most of the fighters in that match were severely wounded anyway, and the arena doesn't feed idlers... Some of them lasted half a day... And the toughest ones a few days longer... That's all.
Some of 'em only got minor injuries, but... They got thrown right back into the arena, including 103. Used to test the puppets' skills, or so I hear.

So anyway, right now I can get you a gladiator slave of much finer quality than those. And if you want a memento of that match, I've got the ID tags of two fighters... Heh heh, buy a slave and I'll throw 'em in as a gift.
The familiar ID tag slipped through my fingers and fell into the pool of blood beneath the arena that never dries.
==Off==<color=black>The magical puppets did take the stage in the arena...==RT==But they never saved any slaves.
I'm sorry... I came back too late...
I'm sorry... We were supposed to have already won...
I'm sorry... I couldn't save a single one of you...
In the waves of deafening cheers from the arena, I wandered aimlessly through the streets of Emor.
The most popular show now features slaves fighting magical puppets instead of each other. It's just a one-sided massacre, more to the audience's liking.
And it's all because... I proved in that match that slaves and magical puppets could fight each other...
I... I stripped everyone of their way out with my own hands...
... No, not yet. It's not over yet. It can't be.
It was then that I remembered the story about the tower that Yonon once mentioned.
Hey, 18, did you know?! They say if you go into that tower and make a wish, then any wish will come true!
Hmm… "Please don't let me be born a slave ever again in my next life..." Do you think this would work?
No use thinking about it. It's only for Senators, Priests, and Saintesses. Gladiators have no place there.
I know, I know. A little wishful thinking doesn't hurt. If we ever survive this, maybe one of us would get lucky someday?
And if one of us does make it into the tower... They could wish on our behalf! "Please don't let any of us be born a slave in our next lives"!
If gold coins can't bring you back... I'll offer anything more precious than gold. I'll do whatever it takes.
Since death has taken you away, I'll go to that tower to make a wish. I'll bring everyone back myself.
With this sword from you, I swear... I will climb the ranks until I earn the right to enter that tower.
That blood-soaked sand will not be where your stories end.
This is how No. 18, a former gladiator,==W== has become Alina, a Night Watcher.
No. 18 once took up the sword simply to survive.
But that is no longer the only reason "Alina" wields this sword. I want to see everyone again... To properly apologize.
To tell them I'm truly sorry for failing them... For not being with them when they were suffering. I'm really ... truly sorry.

param: Alina reveals her past as a gladiator who lived among slaves. She won freedom by defeating magic puppets, but failed to save her companions who had fought and died beside her, and that regret turned into her wish.

Listen. The more blood spilled, the more the crowd goes wild, especially when it's a dainty girl like you. Doesn't matter if it's your blood or your opponent's... They'll be overjoyed either way. Understand?
Well, if you could fight your way to fame, then you can say goodbye to this filthy place forever.
You would live in a mansion that smells of myrrh and frankincense. Lounge on silk cushions stuffed with swan feathers by a crystal-clear pond, sipping chilled mead like some fine young lady…
Haha! Now that's what I call living. Bet you dream of a life like that too, huh?
...Jeez. "Yes, yes"… Is that the only word you know? Are you a puppet or something?
Ugh, fine. Forget it. Go on. A wimp with that empty look like yours would probably just die and get dragged out right away.
In the heart of Emor stands a theater where the curtains never fall.
With towering walls as its curtains and yellow sand as its stage. The lavishly dressed audiences sit in the sunlight, while the slaves in chains stand there in a daze, never seeing the light of day.
People call the Grand Arena "the heart that pumps life into Emor."
But it is never glory that keeps that heart beating... It is the blood that paints the sand red.
I was born beneath those high walls, and I inherited my parents' shackles without ever taking a name.
No one asks a slave's child what they want to be when they grow up. From the moment they are born, their master decides their role and attaches strings to them like a puppet.
The only choice I was ever allowed to make ... was the weapon to fight with. I chose the sword.
The arena is run by twin Archons. The elder sister leases out the venue and the slaves, while the younger one sells tickets and hosts the event they market as "gladiator fight"...
Masters would control the slaves,==W== commanding them to struggle, scream,==W== then fall to please the crowd.
Um... Thank you for going easy on me earlier.
Put some honey on your wound. It'll help keep it from festering.
R-Really? Oh, I'm Yonon... What's your name?
That's your number, right? I have one too—103. But I'm not asking for your number…
I don't have a name, nor do I need one.
Come on, Yonon. Come here so I can patch you up.
Yonon, you sure it's safe to talk to that kid? Who knows what she's thinking? You better stay away in case she stabs you in the back...
Stab? But she's a kind girl...==W== I don't think she would harm me…
Gladiators don't have proper names like the audience members do.
Of course, some gladiators would give themselves names based on their fighting style, hoping the crowd would remember them...
Even so, I never thought of taking a name for myself. After all, we were objects, the masters' property.
To a gladiator, a "name" is nothing more than a price tag, something to make you worth more on the market.
I'd rather hone my swordsmanship than waste time on that.
Every time I brought down an opponent in the arena, the crowd would clench their fists, raise their thumbs, and urge me to end the show with a finishing blow.
But ... I wasn't interested in following their orders, let alone killing in their favor.
So in my bouts, I would cut my opponents' skin open with the tip of my sword, but avoid all the major blood vessels or tendons.
That way, blood would spray a lot, but no one would lose their life.
But little did I know... In that arena with no way out, all hope would only lead to more devastating despair...
One year ago,==W== the Archon of Filanis arrived with a huge batch of magical puppets. That lady with kind heart intended to have them replace the slaves.
But she did not know. The audience couldn't care less about the skills or showmanship. It was the shedding of blood of the living that they craved.
To welcome the Archon of Filanis, the twin Archons who run the arena set up a grand fight: a duel between gladiators and magical puppets.
But it was never a stage to test the puppets' abilities. It was a slaughterhouse for the magical puppets to get rid of the "old puppets" who no longer obeyed their masters religiously.
Yeah. We're about to fight the magical puppets, right?
Your sword is falling apart so... We put our money together and bought you a new one.
Um... As a thanks for all the help, I guess? Ahaha... If it weren't for you, we'd probably all be long dead by now.

strings.text: The Chill of the Blade, the Warmth of Your Grip (Part I)
After countless trials, Chitose's training journey has begun. Her aura, which supposed to be her mastery, however, begins to spiral out of control...
A stream murmured, weaving through the chirps of insects.
A cool breeze brushed my cheeks.
In a flash, my blade sliced clean through the bamboo stalk before me.
With a soft plunk, the severed top fell into the pond.
No answer came, but I looked to the empty air and asked all the same. An old habit.
Since I was a child, I was taught to become a "useful blade."
That is my task, my mission ... my very reason for being.
For as long as I could remember, I had lived within the walls of this grand estate.
And yet... I had never been truly alone.
Gentle voices were heard from behind the wall.
Though we had never met, they had always watched over me in this way, a reassuring presence.
We ... will always be here to protect you, Chitose.
Just dedicate yourself to your Master's training, and you will become a "useful blade."
So I had lived my life by their guidance from beyond the wall.
My peaceful life of training continued, until the day I was finally forged into a truly sharp blade.
(So many years ... and the moment is finally here.)
(The final lesson... I finally did it. Can I truly become the blade now?)
Beyond swinging a sword or commanding the water's flow, my most vital training—
—had been to forge my magic into a sharp edge.
The power to cut with nothing but focused magic.
The moment I mastered this "bladeless blade" was the moment I became the blade itself.
Chitose... How goes your training on the final lesson?
I stood alone on the empty dojo floor.
As always, my Master's steady voice guided me from behind the screen.
An apple was placed before me.
To slice this apple clean in half without a sword...
(... Steady my stance. Hold my breath. Focus...)
A sharp pulse of magical energy tore through the air. The apple fell with a soft thud.
It rolled to a stop at my feet. For once, the cut was perfect—
Not ragged, crooked, or crushed. All my training... It'd finally paid off.
You honor me. I owe all my success to your guidance, Master.
And with that, you are now a blade that can stand on its own. Your training here is over.
Your next trial is to find your wielder. Go. Your journey begins now.
After that, no matter how relentlessly I asked, I was met with only silence.
Hey! Watch where you're going! You just gonna walk away?
What was that?<size=45> Speak up! Can't hear you!</size>==W====RT==<size=47>Hey—</size><size=52>wait a sec. My pauldron's cracked! You're gonna pay for this!</size>
(I've made someone mad again... How many times has it been?)
(But I've trying so hard ... to hold this power back.)
It wasn't until I was well into my journey that I realized my training to control my aura was far from enough.
I'd only ever managed it in total solitude. But out here on the road, people were everywhere...
(I lose control of my aura when there are others around? My training is far from complete...)
Hey—I'm talkin' to you! Pay up!
—C'mon, you can't take her! Forget it, let's just go!
I watched them hurry off, then my gaze drifts toward the glowing tower on the horizon.
The Monolith... Could there be someone powerful?
Agh—! Ow!==W== My hand—how did it get cut?!
Mine too—! My weapon's cracked! Did your blade hit me again?!
... Forgive me. The fault is mine.
... I must ... step away from the party.
Huh? It wasn't that bad! We couldn't have won that last fight without you.
What about the Artifact? You're just gonna walk away from the reward and bounty?
Yes. I seek not Artifacts or rewards,==W== but a wielder.
I turned and walked away, head held high, toward the next place my wielder might be.
The books I'd read mentioned that once I found a worthy wielder, everything would fall into place.
... When I am alone, at least, I must regain control of my aura...
"Master... Mother... Father... Are you watching me?"
I asked my three blades. But on the day I set out, they became mere swords once more—so as always, I was met with only silence.
I looked to them, but there was only silence.
I focused on the apple before me, and with a breath, unleashed my aura.
But the apple wasn't split in two halves like it did during my final trial.
I've failed once again... Why is it not working anymore?
Was leaving the estate a mistake? Was it wrong to be around others? No, but ... how am I to find my wielder...?
Doubt, regret, sorrow. The chaos of it all floods my mind, stealing my breath.
If this goes on... I will be nothing but ... an unworthy, dull blade.
To become a truly sharp blade...
It was like I was sinking into bottomless water... or maybe I was back at the edge of that pond.
At least I felt safe there. Perhaps it'd be better to just go back...
Tears blurred my vision. When I awoke, a deep ache from hunger had settled into my bones.
I was still dwelling on that smashed apple from my dream—but an aroma pulled me back to reality.
Unmistakably, someone has left food beside me. As if it's beckoning me to eat.
(... Who left this? Are they already gone?)
I looked to the distance and saw a few small figures talking, then they vanished down a path from this level of the Waterway.
The hunger gnawed at me, and my hands moved on their own, reaching for the food...
I am a blade... I shouldn't have such worldly desires ... and yet.
These bread and fish... How have I never realized how flavorful they are?
Master would surely not approve of me now.
I knew this, and still... I couldn't stop shoving food in my mouth.
A soothing warmth spread from my stomach through my chest. At last, I felt my edge returning—I was sharp once more.
... A small kindness should be repaid a thousandfold.==W== I am honor-bound to repay this debt.
Remembering the saying, I gathered my belongings and fixed my gaze on the path where they disappeared.
It had been a long time since my purpose felt so clear.
I must keep up with my lifesaver.
(... Will you be the one to wield me?)

strings.text: The Chill of the Blade, the Warmth of Your Grip (Part II)
Having received a single meal of kindness, Chitose followed her lifesaver's steps, and along the way, took it upon herself to do good and stop evil.
(The city feels... much rowdier than usual today. I need to find my lifesaver fast.)
Hey—you! Haven't seen your face around here before.
What's on your back? Think you can just waltz through our turf without payin' the toll?
What, you think you're better than us?!
Please, step aside. If you were hurt, I...
Damn it! It's been ages since we had a good scrap. And this one's pickin' a fight!
I had no choice...==W== My apologies.
(Now that I've eaten, my body feels so light... So this is what starving does to you...)
(It seems this sort of street wisdom is vital when traveling alone.)
Ah! My drink! You sliced it in two halves!
My deepest apologies for the intrusion... But I am in the midst of battle.
The silver-haired girl's hand clamped down on mine. An incredible magical power crackled at her fingertips.
YOU SLASHED MY DRINK! I barely touched it!
The situation is dire... We can settle this later—
Hey! Where d'you think you're goin'?
Yeah, pay the toll! Unless you want trouble!
Who are you? Wait... If I wreck these goons for you, will you buy me a drink?
Buy? So... if I were to treat you to a beverage, you would forgive my offense?
Understood. I shall compensate you for the lost drink.
(Those claws... So that's where the strange magical power I felt was coming from!)

strings.text: The Chill of the Blade, the Warmth of Your Grip (Part III)
It seems that Chitose's lifesaver is in danger. She decides to step in and help. This will be the beginning of a strange and unforgettable relationship...
(It's so late... What business could they have here?)
(They were arguing with someone... Then that person fled.)
(... The side who looked stronger ran. Does that mean ... my lifesaver's squad is even more powerful?)
That shadow is blocking our magic.
I heard Feagin. She contacted the Imperial Guard.
We're gonna be surrounded any minute. No time to hunt them down.
Let's get Loxy out of here first!
(They're leaving ... but it looks like they're about to have company.)
Hear about that? Creta's old miser put a bounty on five Trekkers—a million Dorra a head.
Feagin coughing up that much? Those five must've really messed with Creta Trading. Almost makes you not wanna go after 'em.
Look at you, getting all sympathetic!==W== Bag this bounty, and we can kick back for months.
Yeah, you're right.==W== Roof's leaking, and gotta pay back that weapon loan...==W== If we run into those Trekkers, guess it's just their bad luck.
They gotta be using the Waterway to get around. We'll set up an ambush right here.
Apologies.==W== I'm afraid I can't let you do that.
Hey, you just split my damn sword!
Dammit, see? This is why I didn't wanna mess with them...
Hey, get up! This is no time to be resti—
(My lifesaver is here... Let me hide somewhere.)
(Hmm... Is this enough to repay the debt?)
Oh! You must mean those Trekkers! They just got back to Emor recently. Right now, they're helping the Ashwind Clan fight back against Creta Trading.
They've got a real fight on their hands...==W== I heard some knights took commissions from Creta Trading. Looks like the company's ready to play dirty.
(It sounds like ... more enemies await them.)
(... Should I continue to follow them?)
The area ahead is blocked. Do not go any further.
It's very dangerous. This is for your own safety.
(This aura... The work of a seasoned warrior.)
(... If I just identify myself as a "Trekker" in the city, I should avoid suspicion.)
Thank you for the warning, but there is no need for concern. I am merely a Trekker passing through.
I see. After the bounty, are you?
I'm the Imperial Knight assigned to this incident. The targets are on the run. If you intend to join the hunt...
Speak of the devil. There they are now. Those Trekkers are a tenacious bunch.
(Those people on the skateboards... Wait, isn't that my lifesaver and ==SEX3== squad?!)
(Then this person before me ... must be their pursuer.)
"Bother," you say...? I see...You're not here to hunt the bounty. You are the bounty.
If you don't know them, what's with the overflowing hostility?
Forgive me. I bear you no ill will...
Hmph. You've got some moves.==W== But don't you dare underestimate an Imperial Knight!
(She saw right through me... She's the real deal.)
And that is exactly why I cannot let you pass!
Not backing down? Fine.==W== The gloves are coming off!
(... Lightning!? This is going to be tough to counter.)
(... But I can't let that stop me...)
Hah, that's some unique magic you have. It's quite sharp.
(Did my uncontrollable aura deter her?...==W== Well, at least I stop her, then—)
Your magic is very powerful, but—
Young Trekker, in a fight, relying on brute force alone is useless.
No more fooling around—the big catch’s here!
No! She's aiming at ...==W== my lifesaver—!
I'm afraid I can't let you do that!
(If my blade can't keep up with her spear, I shal use my body to stop—)
(Huh? I can... control my aura again.)
The books I'd read mentioned that once I found a worthy wielder, everything would fall into place.
(Could it be that ... ==SEX== is not only my lifesaver, but also...)
My apologies for the delay, my ==SEX11==.
Hmm... Your magic has suddenly become so smooth... Were you holding back just now?
But swords and guns have no mercy. If you don't want to lose your life, then stop rambling about lifesaving and all!
My apologies, but for me, ==SEX== is not merely a lifesaver;==W== ==SEX=='s also my wielder...
To put it in common words, ==SEX=='s my ==SEX11==.
So you have your reasons. But I have my orders...
All units! While she's distracted, capture the target!
(I'm still holding up, but barely... There are too many of them. If this keeps up...)
==PLAYER_NAME==, and that righteous Trekker who helped us. All of you, run! I'll hold them off here!
Are you okay? You're not hurt?
Leave this to Ashwind. We'll retreat together.
Un-Understood. Oh, my ==SEX11==, please don't stand so close to me...
Argh—! My pauldron's cracked! What did you do?!
Agh—! Ow! My hand—how did it get cut?!
No, my ==SEX11==! If you touch me... You'll get hurt—
(==SEX1=='s holding my hand ... but ==SEX3== hand is unharmed...)
In the underground clinic in Ash District, Chitose lays out her bedroll and lies down beside the hospital bed.
She isn't actually asleep, but merely fulfilling the duty of a blade—
As your blade, my ==SEX11==, I must naturally remain close at hand.
For Chitose, the person beside her had already become her ==SEX11==.
(The apple beside me was somehow sliced in half ... without me noticing.)
(But you ... you can hold my hand without getting hurt... It's incredible.)
I never knew ... that holding a hand could feel so warm and comforting.
Chitose, carve your own path with your own two hands... That is your next trial.
Will you hold me in your hand?
(I know... There's no answer for now.)
(But you are the only one, the wielder, who can touch me without getting hurt.)
Please allow me to take the liberty of addressing you in this way.
I only hope that when you wake up ... you'll give me your answer.

strings.text: Your Name, Unknown to My Heart (Part I)
Boss and the New Star Guild embark on their first joint ascent of the Monolith. Before entering, everyone is busy with their preparations.
This all happened right after they pulled me from the desert, before we even made it to Emor...
Noya! Eyes on the road when you're driving!
Aww, but you were having such a great time chatting! I felt left out!
Look, helping us search is great...==W====RT==But not if you get us all killed in a wreck, yeah?
What are you looking for out there?
The entrance?==W== But ... isn't the Monolith over there?
I peer out the window. A huge Monolith shoots up from the deep woods,==B== crowned with a cross-shaped star. It's like a beacon, pulling every Trekker toward it.
The Monolith is separate from its entrance.
The entrance isn't actually on the Monolith, just somewhere near it? That's a weird design.
Hehe, looks like this is our lucky day!
This is the entrance? Incredible. We're nowhere near the Monolith itself.
I know, it's wild! The first time I saw it, I couldn't believe it either. It's just a door on a rock, not connected to anything. You'd never guess it's the way in.
Open the door. Step in. Close it. Open it again. You're there.
How in the world does that work?
The Monoliths are full of mysteries.==RT==It's not confirmed, but we think it's some form of teleportation magic...
There's no door at the base of the Monolith. The only way in is to find one of these elevators blended into the terrain. They link up with the elevators inside the Monolith.

These elevators vanish the second you use them, only to pop up somewhere else around the Monolith. It's probably just like the legends say—==W==a trial from the God of Grace for anyone who dares to climb the Monoliths.
It usually takes some time to find an entrance. Today was actually really fast. One time, we roamed around a Monolith for two whole days and still couldn't find its entrance...
No wonder it felt like we were just driving in circles.
When that happens, it just means your luck's out. Probably shouldn't attempt a climb! Even if you force it, your wish will probably be a dud.
There's no actual evidence connecting the two...==W== That's just a hunch of yours, Noya.
Who cares! We found it this fast, so we must be on a roll! C'mon, let's get ready and dive in!
You've got a point...==W====RT==Okay, let's start prepping.
What about you? If you don't wanna climb, you can just wait out here for us.
Come with us! It's way too dangerous to be out in the Wilds alone. Don't worry if you're not much of a fighter. Just stick right behind us.
I want to go with you. I still can't remember anything. Maybe I'll find some clues inside the Monolith.
After stashing the Lucky Oasis out of sight, we start preparing for the climb.
I have no idea how to prepare for it, though...==W== Guess I'll see what they're up to.
Stretching! Gotta get a good warm-up in before a real adventure.
You should stretch too. C'mere, I'll help.
Like this—back to back with me...==B== Now hook your arms with mine.
My bones... I can hear them cracking...
'Kay, now sit down, legs out straight. Lean forward and try to touch your toes.
Noya gets right behind me, her body close as she gently pushes my torso forward.
Her breathing is soft. A warmth radiates down my spine. I should be feeling relaxed, but my heart is pounding.
Wait, hold on...==W== Ow! Ow, ow, OW!
Hahaha!==RT==Oh, stop being so dramatic! Just a little longer!
It's gonna break! I swear my spine is gonna snap!
Ugh... We haven't even started climbing, and my body's already falling apart...
But you feel a lot looser after stretching, don't you?
Now that you mention it, I do feel a little more limber.
Hehe, that's great!==W== You never know what you'll run into in a Monolith, so always remember to warm up before going in!
I say goodbye to Noya and walk over to someone else who's caught my eye.
The view is definitely better from up high, but...
Coming down, elastic strap caught on a branch. Tangled my feet...
"Elastic strap"? You mean that black one on your back?
Right. It allows me to hang from tricky spots, and tie up enemies.
So its two functions combined to create a new problem...
I can catch you from down here. How about you break the branch and just drop?
I'll leave it to you then... Keeping balance, is hard.
Amber drops into my arms. She's small and soft, and instinctively curls up like a kitten.
If... I get tangled up again, I'm counting on you.
Happy to help,==W== but maybe try not to get tangled up so often?
C-==W==Could I borrow your hand for a second?
I reach out to Iris. A moment later, she takes my hand in both of hers and squeezes it tight.
Her palms are soft, and a pleasant coolness spreads from her fingers to mine.
Just a little ritual I have before entering a Monolith. Hope it's not too weird...
Oh, I see.==RT==You just grabbed my hand out of nowhere, so I thought something was up.
No need to apologize. It makes me feel like I'm already part of the crew. It's kinda nice.
Thank you. It's a huge relief.
A little while later, we're all geared up and ready to go.
Once we're inside, you have to stick with us. Don't wander off.
The space inside is chaotic. The only way forward or out is through elevators that pop up at random. If you get separated, you could be lost in here for good.
Also ...==W== the Monolith is full of magical things—all creations of the God of Grace. You can look, you can touch, but never take anything. And most importantly, do not eat a single thing.
If we can't take anything, how are we supposed to get Artifacts?
The rules say only things from a Wishing Box are ours to keep. You have to be extremely careful about that.
Yup! Break the rules, and the Monolith sends you a bill!
Don't listen to her... It's not a bill.==W== Whatever you eat, the Monolith just takes it back when you leave.
... No, just taking it back would be getting off easy. The more you eat in here, the more you forget who you are ... until you fade away completely.
Okay, that's kinda terrifying...==W====RT==But sure, I'll be careful.
We have to get an Artifact this time... We need the money to get by...
The four of us step into the elevator as it radiates an eerie glow.

Ugh... We haven't even started climbing, and my body's already falling apart...
But you feel a lot looser after stretching, don't you?
Now that you mention it, I do feel a little more limber.
Hehe, that's great!==W== You never know what you'll run into in a Monolith, so always remember to warm up before going in!
I say goodbye to Noya and walk over to someone else who's caught my eye.
The view is definitely better from up high, but...
Coming down, elastic strap caught on a branch. Tangled my feet...
"Elastic strap"? You mean that black one on your back?
Right. It allows me to hang from tricky spots, and tie up enemies.
So its two functions combined to create a new problem...
I can catch you from down here. How about you break the branch and just drop?
I'll leave it to you then... Keeping balance, is hard.
Amber drops into my arms. She's small and soft, and instinctively curls up like a kitten.
If... I get tangled up again, I'm counting on you.
Happy to help,==W== but maybe try not to get tangled up so often?
C-==W==Could I borrow your hand for a second?
I reach out to Iris. A moment later, she takes my hand in both of hers and squeezes it tight.
Her palms are soft, and a pleasant coolness spreads from her fingers to mine.
Just a little ritual I have before entering a Monolith. Hope it's not too weird...
Oh, I see.==RT==You just grabbed my hand out of nowhere, so I thought something was up.
No need to apologize. It makes me feel like I'm already part of the crew. It's kinda nice.
Thank you. It's a huge relief.
A little while later, we're all geared up and ready to go.
Once we're inside, you have to stick with us. Don't wander off.
The space inside is chaotic. The only way forward or out is through elevators that pop up at random. If you get separated, you could be lost in here for good.
Also ...==W== the Monolith is full of magical things—all creations of the God of Grace. You can look, you can touch, but never take anything. And most importantly, do not eat a single thing.
If we can't take anything, how are we supposed to get Artifacts?
The rules say only things from a Wishing Box are ours to keep. You have to be extremely careful about that.
Yup! Break the rules, and the Monolith sends you a bill!
Don't listen to her... It's not a bill.==W== Whatever you eat, the Monolith just takes it back when you leave.
... No, just taking it back would be getting off easy. The more you eat in here, the more you forget who you are ... until you fade away completely.
Okay, that's kinda terrifying...==W====RT==But sure, I'll be careful.
We have to get an Artifact this time... We need the money to get by...
The four of us step into the elevator as it radiates an eerie glow.

strings.text: Your Name, Unknown to My Heart (Part II)
The four faced a troublesome enemy, and although Boss found a way to defeat it, the enemy launched a final counterattack just before its death...
Amber, watch out! It's taking aim at you!
Huh? Whatcha doin' in the corner?
These Crispy Hooves sometimes overshoot their charge and get stuck in corners. Just checking for stragglers.
Really? First I've ever heard of that.
You're knowledgeable.==W== You've been calling out the Stellaroids' weak points this entire time. Our combat is significantly more efficient today.
How ... are you so good at this?
I can't really explain it.==W== I still don't remember anything else,==W== but the moment I see a Stellaroid, facts about them just ... come to me.
You're such a natural with Stellaroids! Bet you were an incredible Trekker before you lost your memory!
I have to agree. Only a seasoned Trekker would have that kind of insight.
It seems that even without your memories, your combat experiences have remained.
You handled them just fine on your own.
Seriously, things went smoothly because your teamwork is on point. You take 'em down so cleanly.
If it were just me, I couldn't beat them even if I knew all their weaknesses.
Hahahaha! Looks like we're all thinkin' the same thing!
Uh... Did I say something wrong?
Not at all! Hearing you say it just made us realize how much better we've gotten at fighting together!
We were an absolute disaster when we started...
Remember when we first started climbing? I was about to unleash this awesome sword skill, and before I even hit the Stellaroid, bam! Iris froze me solid.
I wasn't used to it yet, so I failed to calculate your position.==W== Besides, I specifically aimed away from you. You're the one who leaped right into it!
Good thing Amber was there to blast that block of ice apart a second later!
Don't sweat it, Amber! It's all those little mishaps that helped us finally click as a team!
You have really been through it. Frozen solid, taking bullets...==W== Seriously, Noya, how are you even still on your feet?
Heh, I'm tougher than I look! Little scrapes patch themselves up in no time!
Joking and teasing, we press onward.
Now that's a Stellaroid I haven't seen before.
Me neither...==W== I've got no data on its combat patterns... A head-on attack would be suicide. We need to...
Let's just jump it and find out!
Wait! What if it flattens us and no other Trekkers make it this far? We'll be stuck! No one's coming to help!
But look how tough it is! Take it down, and a Wishing Box is bound to appear!==W== Plus, with an expert like you around, we're golden!
Yeah. You know things about Stellaroids that aren't in any books. Having someone with your expertise here is a huge relief.
We have to get that Artifact, finish this commission ...==W== and finally get paid so we can EAT!
Okay, she just went from zero to a hundred.
Yeah, you get used to it!
C'mon, let's wreck this thing and get our Wishing Box!
Whoa! Where'd these things come from?!
They just ... materialized. Right behind us.==W== I felt nothing.
I've never seen a Stellaroid pull a move like that!==W== Iris, any ideas?
I think it's a Space Walker. Intel's almost nonexistent. All I know is that it teleports.
This isn't good. They're getting pinned down...
If I really was an experienced Trekker, I must've fought one of these before. It has to have a weak spot... I just need to remember it...
I'm fine.==W== You got here just in time.
The attack pattern of this thing is insane! Our squad's about to break... We're not gonna make it...
No, you've all done great. Just holding it back this long was more than enough.
Its attacks seem unstoppable, but there's a rhythm to them.
It can teleport, but not endlessly. Each time, it takes aim at a target, then warps its attack right on top of them.
It's frozen in place while it channels that. It can neither move nor stop the attack. That's its moment of weakness. That's when we strike.
Hold on...==W== Was that me from the past?
The Stellaroid in my memory was bigger, far more dangerous... But it looked and moved just like this Space Walker.
They must be the same type of Stellaroid. If that's the case...
Amber, keep your distance, stay nimble. Draw its fire.
Iris, prep an area magic. Use your ice magic to lock it down.
Noya, once it's locked on Amber, you rush it.
You got it! Leave it to me!
The Space Walker has to channel energy to teleport. That's our opening.
As long as we're in sync, we can't lose!
Following my lead, the three of them move as one, systematically breaking down the Space Walker's defenses.
Brace yourself!==W== This is gonna hurt!
The Wishing Box! Where's the Wishing Box?!
I have a bad feeling... Something is wrong...
The Stellaroid is fading! Lord, we've won!
Good work. Have the intel team move in for final data collection.
Space is... It's buckling around it! It's sacrificing itself to cast one last teleportation magic!
When this type of Stellaroid dies, it...
I lunge, shoving Noya clear.==W==In the last second before the world vanishes, light itself bends and shatters around me. My body feels like it's being torn apart as I plummet into an endless void...

strings.text: Your Name, Unknown to My Heart (Part III)
Lost in Monolith, Boss stumble into a "convenience store." After eating a delicious pork cutlet rice bowl, Boss's body seems to undergo some unusual changes.
How did I wind up back here?
Still no sign of Noya or the others. I've been shouting my lungs out, but no one's answering.
Once we're inside, you have to stick with us. Don't wander off.
The space inside is chaotic. The only way forward or out is through elevators that pop up at random.==W== If you get separated, you could be lost in here for good.
Iris was right... I'm completely turned around.
A Space Walker's teleportation can't be infinite. He must've just zapped me somewhere close by... But I'm definitely still inside the Monolith.
I need to find the others, fast.==W== But how...?
I pull out the dinner knife I found and carve a message where it can't be missed.
Everything here looks untouched. If other Trekkers had been through, they would've left some kind of mark.
So either some "entity" is maintaining this place, or the Monolith repairs itself.
If that's the case, leaving marks is pointless. But with all these Stellaroids around, staying put is a death wish.==B== Gotta find a safe spot, now.
Ugh, all this walking is making me hungry...
Yeah, didn't get a chance to eat before coming in.
I spin around—a massive Stellaroid is looming right behind me. It didn't make a sound.
No way... There is no way that's edible!
Er...==B== On second thought, I'm not that hungry anymore.
Huff... Huff...==W== Why is it still chasing me?!
I'm lying. I'm so hungry I could pass out! Damn it, can't run anymore... My vision's ... getting blurry...
Why.==W== Won't.==W== You. Eat.==W== My. Food!
Relax. He can't get in here.
Thanks, you're a lifesaver...==W== Who are you?
Portia. I work at the convenience store. And you?
I... I don't know. I've lost my memory.
Hmm? Oh well. A name isn't important for you, anyway. Here. You must be starving after all that running.
The store's specialty—pork cutlet bento. Crispy, tender... way better than anything that thing out there makes.
Want me to heat it up?
It smells incredible...==W== I think it's just making me hungrier...
This... this pork cutlet...!==RT==It's... amazing! How can anything taste this good?!
Heh, look at you go.==RT==If you like it that much, you should stay. You can have delicious pork cutlets every single day.
Yeah, stay. Work for your meals. We've got room and board covered. How 'bout it?
Besides, you can't leave anyway. Clinging to false hope would just make you miserable, wouldn't it?
... No, just taking it back would be getting off easy.
The more you eat in here, the more you forget who you are...
Don't eat anything in the Monolith...
If I do... What happens again?
Gotta hustle and drum up some business.
C'mon, customers... I've gotta keep my sales numbers up.
If I bring in a crowd, the boss'll definitely give me a bonus.
When is my break? I'm craving some pork cutlet...
Wh-what the—?! How did I end up like this?!
Can't talk ... and I can barely move.
If you like it that much, you should stay. You can have delicious pork cutlets every single day.
That's right... I ate that pork cutlet from the convenience store, and then everything went black.
Next thing I know, I woke up like this. How much time has passed...
I wonder if the others have wished for the Artifact and left the Monolith by now.
Even if they haven't... There's no way they'd recognize me like this.
Am I going to be trapped here, working around the clock forever?!
Oh no...==W== My head's getting ... fuzzy again...
Probably 'cause the promotion hasn't started yet.
Can't slack off! I've gotta drum up some business!

strings.text: Your Name, Unknown to My Heart (Part IV)
The New Star Guild successfully rescued Boss from the Monolith. To celebrate, everyone held a welcome party. However, this "welcome party" turned out to be—
The signal's weak...==W== but I'm still picking it up. It feels like it's coming from high up.
I just hope ==SEX=='s all right...==W== It's way too dangerous to wander the Monolith alone.
As long as we keep climbing, we'll find ==SEX4==.
The desert. When we got separated.
Ugh... I thought I was going to be buried in the sand and just forgotten...
You were only a five-minute walk ahead of me.==W== Nothing to worry about! Besides, even if we were miles apart, our bond would bring us back together!
"Relying on our bond" is not a plan!==W== That's precisely why I made this locator magic. Just didn't expect we'd need it so soon—==W==hey, why are you staring at me?
It just hit me how lucky we are to have you!
Wh-What's all this all of a sudden...?==W== C-Come on, let's just go. We need to find ==SEX4==, fast.
Huh? This stuff's all expired! Seriously, Miss Portia's slacking off again.
Okay ...==W== toss the old stuff, put out the new...
Done! Everything's restocked and tagged for discount.
Time to stand by the door and bring in some customers...
<size=35>I'd really love to keep ==SEX4== here, working for me forever.
A pity... ==SEX1== hasn't had enough of the food yet. If ==SEX3== consciousness awakens, ==SEX== can still be taken back.
And those little friends of ==SEX5== should be here any minute. Heh heh... What to do?
Kinda getting tired of pork cutlets...
Miss Portia did say the chow mein here is good too. Maybe I'll try that next.
Right! Gotta work even harder for that yummy chow mein!
Huh? Sounds like customers. Better get to it!
My magic is picking something up. ==SEX1== is close.
The convenience store...==W== I remember that clerk. She looks like she hasn't slept in a week.
What are these customers even talking about?
Aren't they gonna buy anything? What's with the poking...?==W== Oh, maybe they want a photo? Better strike a friendly pose.
That's ... weird.==W== Why does a hug from her feel so warm?
Hey, Iris, this mascot... It wasn't here the last time we came by, was it?
It's definitely suspicious. My magic is...==W== Wait, my magic just linked to the mascot!
Trekker from the Wishing Box! Are you in there?
Trekker from the Wishing Box... Who's that?
What's a Wishing Box? What's a Trekker? And is it almost lunchtime?
Hey, snap out of it! I still owe you one. You saved me, remember?
Saved...==W== Who did I save? Who saved me?
We don't even know your name! C'mon, you can't just blow us off!
The nameless Trekker with memory loss ... the one they rescued from the Wishing Box! And they're—
==SEX1== talked! ==SEX1=='s really the Trekker from the Wishing Box!
We gotta get outta here. Ugh, what is this weird suit? Let's get it off ya.
It's soft. Like it's your own skin. It won't come off.
Hold on. Where do you think you're going with my employee?
Employee? This is our companion! See the water ring on ==SEX3== hand? That's a locator magic I cast right before we came in.
Doesn't matter who ==SEX== was. ==SEX1=='s a clerk at this convenience store now.
So what'll it take for you to let ==SEX4== go?
Isn't it obvious? This is a store. You buy stuff.
In fact, buy out my entire stock, and I'll throw the employee in as a freebie.
I dunno how many Stella Coins you're asking for ... but will this do?
Noya heaves a massive, overflowing bag of Stella Coins onto the counter with a loud thud.
Noya?! Where'd you get all these Stella Coins? When did you even...?!
All those Stellaroids we fought? They dropped a ton of Stella Coins. Figured they might come in handy, so I scooped 'em all up.
So, is this enough? If not, we can just go farm some more.
... You've got to be kidding me.
Well now, my reliable employee... These customers have made quite a purchase. How about you give them a hand?
Under Portia's instructions, I stagger out of the store after Noya, Iris, and Amber, barely managing the mountain of goods in my arms.
Ugh... My head's clearing...==W====RT==What was I just doing? How did I end up working as a clerk?
Hehe! Welcome back to the land of the living!
Hey, that's what we're here for! The New Star Guild never leaves a companion behind!
We've been in this Monolith for almost two days. We need to get out now, before it gets too dangerous.
I glance back at Portia. She's just tidying up behind the counter like nothing happened.==W== Without even looking over, she gives a casual wave.
Whoa, the second I step out of the Monolith, I become overwhelmed by hunger.
We were in there for thirty-five hours. It's no wonder we're hungry.
And that meal from the convenience store? Anything not from a Wishing Box gets reclaimed by the Monolith when you leave. It's like you never ate at all.
It just... vanishes?==W== So what would happen if someone stayed in there for a month?
The Monolith takes away everything you've eaten. The moment you step outside, you suddenly turn into skin and bones and starve to death~
Don't describe such a terrifying scene so vividly!
Well... That's just her theory. Nobody's ever lasted that long in a Monolith. The longest on record is one week. When that Trekker was pulled out, they've lost their mind...
I've heard about that. That person also said they saw legendary heroes walking around them!
On second thought...==W== Compared to ghosts, starving to death is still scarier...
Alright, alright, I'll drop it.==W== (yawn) It's getting late. Isn't it time we brought out that?
Ta-da! Pajamas, just for you! We got 'em from a Wishing Box while we were out looking for you.
You can't be comfortable sleeping in your outdoor clothes.
They're cute. It was Noya's idea.
Wow, they're so soft... You are amazing. I don't know how to thank you.
Hey, you saved me from that Stellaroid, remember? Consider us even!
Besides, there's something else we wanted to talk to you about.
Amber pulls me over to sit with them.
Trekker from the Wishing Box, come travel with us!
We, uh... We'd like to invite you to join the New Star Guild.
You want me to join? Why?
W-We talked it over. Your memory loss' pretty severe, and ... it doesn't look like it's coming back anytime soon. We'd just be so worried if you left on your own...
I mean, an experienced Trekker like you would be fine no matter where you go, I'm sure of it! But ... maybe you could stay with us, at least until you've figured things out?
Okay, my turn! The first time I saw you, lying right there in the Wishing Box, I just knew we were meant to cross paths.
Plus, we worked together really well back in the Monolith. You're a natural fit for our guild!
We like you. We want you to stay.
Thanks...==W== No, that's not what I should be saying.
I'm happy when I'm with all of you.
I want to be on your team, too.
Heh heh, told you ==SEX=='d say yes!
Then, it's official! Welcome to the New Star Guild!
Yeah. I'm glad to be part of the team.
Don't be so stiff! You're one of us now, so let's get this party started!
Whoa—==W====RT==Hey! What's with the surprise pillow attack?!
'Cause it's time for a pillow fight!
Who has a pillow fight at a welcoming party...?
Heh! First one to strike wins!==W====RT==Your turn! Think fast, Amber!
Whoa! Nice moves, Amber! You actually dodged that!
Oh yeah? Well, watch out! I'm bringing out my special move!
You're all out. My turn. Hi—yah!
You two... Could you please act your age...==W== Ouch!
Hahaha... Uh oh, now you've done it...
Heh heh... I assume you two are prepared for what's coming next?
W-Wait! Amber, Noya...==RT==Stop using me as a shield—!
Warm, orange light spills out from the window, lingering long into the night. And just like that, our journey begins.
